### A second arm is registered on the same corpus, and it is not in the queue

The arm above reads the corpus as it stands. **A second arm on the same carrier asks
a different question: if a template is propagating, countries under a conditional
programme should cluster on the block count, and the position of the spike is the
position of the template.** It is registered here and it has not been opened.

**It is one arm of this station rather than a station of its own.** The carrier is
the same published survey, the parser is the same and carries its own known-answer
check, and the positions are the same. What differs is where the treatment comes
from: the first arm's treatment is a property of the schedule itself, and the second
arm's treatment sits outside the carrier entirely, in a published list of programmes.

**That is also why the second arm has to pass a gate the first one does not.** The
first arm's treatment variable is the structure of a tariff schedule, so the ceiling
on how many values a treatment can take in the world does not bind it. The second
arm's treatment is a country attribute, binary, over the 53 schedules recovered, and
that is the shape where the ceiling does bind. **The way out, if there is one, is
that the survey publishes five customer-class annexes rather than one, roughly three
hundred schedules in total, while a programme condition can name residential tariffs
without naming industrial ones.** Positions would then be country-and-class pairs
rather than countries, and the ceiling would not be the binding constraint.

**A second and prior question is whether the treatment should be binary at all.**
Being under a programme is a level, and the discipline that applies here asks for a
gradient instead: the count or the strength of conditions naming utility tariffs,
which a published programme database records line by line.

**So two counts have to be produced before this arm opens**: how many of the 53
countries were under a conditional programme in the survey's year, and how far apart
the two ends of the condition-count are. Both are one query against a public
database. **Until both exist the arm stays registered and unqueued**, and if the
first count kills it the disposal is that the arm does not open, not that it opens
under a different station number: a station number does not change how many values a
treatment takes in the world.

**One overlap is recorded here so it is not discovered twice.** Programme
conditionality is already registered elsewhere in this repository, in the carrier
ranking for a different question, with the note that the condition is itself an
instruction to change a procedure and is published in a dated letter. That ranking
asks whether a shared procedure can be told apart from a shared environment; this arm
asks whether a counting law's object propagates. **Same treatment variable, two
questions**, and the availability work already done there should be read before any
is repeated here.

### The second arm ran, and it returns a negative reading with the treated group named

`experiments/tariff_blocks_conditionality.py`, record
`results/tariff_blocks_conditionality.json`. The programme and condition data are the
IMF conditionality dataset of Kentikelenis and Stubbs, one country-year panel and one
row-per-condition file, downloaded by hand and not redistributed here. The three
outcomes were fixed before the pull.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **TB-11** print the block-count distribution for schedules whose country was under an arrangement in 2015 or 2016 and for those whose was not, cell by cell, no threshold on either | **23 under, 30 not.** Block counts `1..8`: under `4 4 7 2 2 2 2 0`, not under `7 4 8 3 2 2 3 1`. **Means 3.35 against 3.40** | the same shape on both, which was registered as a negative reading · `own_reading` |
| **TB-12** print the count of conditions naming an electricity price against the block count, as a gradient, with the treated countries named | **21 conditions over 8 countries**, out of 723 conditions falling on these 53 in the window. Rank correlation of blocks against the SOE condition count `+0.11`, against months under an arrangement `+0.02` | printed · `own_reading` |
| **TB-13** every schedule resolves to a name in the panel, and any country absent from the condition file is named rather than silently read as having none | **0 unmatched.** 7 named as absent from the condition file: Australia, Austria, Germany, Iran, Japan, Lebanon, Malaysia | PASS · `instrument` |

**The negative reading is the registered one and is reported as it came.** Two
distributions of the same shape was written down before the pull as one of the three
outcomes, and it is what came back.

**What the arm learned about its own treatment variable is worth more than that.**
Being under an arrangement is not the treatment this arm wanted; having one's tariff
schedule rewritten by an external condition is. Those are not the same set. Of the 53,
23 were under an arrangement, and **the conditions that name an electricity price fall
on 8 of them**: Pakistan 9, Jordan 4, Haiti 2, Madagascar 2, Guinea 1, Honduras 1,
Kyrgyz Republic 1, Yemen 1. **Read one by one, seven of those eight name a price
level**; the Yemen condition rolls out prepaid meters, which is metering rather than
pricing. Both numbers are in the record and the full text of all 21 is printed there.

**So the treatment group is seven or eight countries spread over eight block-count
values, and no distribution reads off that.** This is not a sample that came out
small. It is the number of times the mechanism occurred in this window on this
corpus, which is what the count on the treatment variable is supposed to establish
before anything is bought.

**One expectation formed from the codebook did not survive the data.** The
classification puts price rises for basic-needs goods, electricity and gas included
when explicitly for households, in the social-policy area, so that area looked like
the one to read. Across these 53 countries and these two years it carries **four
conditions and none of them is about a price**: two on tertiary education policy, one
on payroll system integration, one on a social-fund beneficiary survey. **Every
electricity-price condition sits in the state-owned-enterprise area instead.**

**The conditions themselves are a carrier for a different question, and that is this
arm's net product.** Each is a dated public instrument in which a third party
instructs a government to rewrite a published price schedule, several with the
percentage in the text: Guinea `+20`, Madagascar `+15`, Honduras `+2.5`, and Jordan an
automatic adjustment mechanism with a stated commencement date. The carrier ranking
for the shared-procedure question already names programme conditionality as its
strongest channel on the ground that the condition is itself an instruction to change
a procedure and is published in a dated letter. **It had no instance attached. These
21 are instances, with country, year, condition type and source document.**

### A third arm: the time-of-use columns of the other annexes

The residential annex is the only one that draws blocks. The other four carry a
time-of-use column, which states a charge per period and so states how many
periods a schedule writes and how many distinct values they carry. The text of
all five annexes was already on disk, so this arm collected nothing.

Across the three annexes that carry the column: **125 rows, 42 with a time-of-use
column, writing 112 periods and 105 distinct values, 7 collisions**.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **TB-14** the same column splitter on the residential annex against the counts already on disk | `179` blocks, `156` values, `23` collisions, reproduced digit for digit | PASS · `known_answer` |
| **TB-15** periods against distinct values, per annex and per colliding schedule | commercial `44 -> 42`, industrial `54 -> 49`, agricultural `14 -> 14` | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **TB-16** collisions split by whether rounding could have produced them | 7 total, **2 exact**, 5 resolution-limited | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **TB-17** the survey's structure column against its own time-of-use column | 7 name it and print nothing; 4 print charges without naming it | PASS · `known_answer` |
| **TB-18** periods per customer class across annexes | 12 countries, 8 the same in every annex | PASS · `own_reading` |

**Two of the seven collisions are exact, which the block arm has none of.** Every
block-arm collision is bounded above by the survey rounding to two decimals.
India prints `0, 0, 0.01, 0.02` for both its commercial and its industrial
schedule: two periods charged nothing, and no pair of distinct positive charges
rounds to two zeros. Those two are one country writing one rule into two tables,
and the record counts them as one country.

**TB-17 reads the document against itself.** Eleven of the forty-two schedules
disagree with the survey's own typing of them, four printing time-of-use charges
under a structure column that does not name it and seven the reverse. The rows
are named rather than counted, because a count does not say whether the
disagreement is in the typing or in the collection.


## B30 — the propagation chain, arm by arm, and what each one returned

**Entered 2026-09-03. The readings are in
[`docs/b30_results.md`](docs/b30_results.md) and the
registrations are in [`docs/b30_prereg.md`](docs/b30_prereg.md). Until now only the
two B30-5 sections above were in this file, so this index is the missing half of
discipline 18a: every arm's state, including the ones that returned nothing.**

**This section is an index and not a second copy.** Each row carries the arm's
state and the headings of its blocks; the numbers, the limits and the corrections
live in the results file and govern.

**The third column names headings and not line numbers, and that is `D24`'s rule
applied to this table.** It carried line numbers until 2026-09-16, and `20` of the
`55` of them pointed into another arm's block by then, because every chunk inserted
in the middle of the results file moves every address below it and none of them
errors when it moves. **A heading does not move**: the results file's `73` top-level
headings are all distinct, its `65` `<arm>, chunk <word>` pairs are all distinct, and
no sub-heading repeats inside a single chunk, so `chunk three` under an arm is an
address that stays an address and `grep -c` settles it. **The check is a script and
not a claim**: `scripts/check_b30_index.py` resolves every address in this column
against the results file and reports any that does not land on exactly one heading.

| arm | what it returned | block |
|---|---|---|
| **B30-1** | **Two carriers, two recorded negatives, and a better instrument found on the second.** On the quotation graph the maximum hop distance is one, so there is no hop gradient and the arm cannot run. On ATPCO the registered criterion asked whether the public record yields dated "A initiated, B followed on day N" pairs; **it does not, and the negative was recorded on the spot**. What the record supplied instead is the adjacency authored by both parties and entered into a court record, plus a **court-ordered, dated, staggered deletion of edges lying in `G_I` alone**, with `G_T` untouched | results file, chunks one to two, headed `B30-1 and B30-5` |
| **B30-2** | **Carrier condition worked out 2026-09-03, the obvious candidate closed on arithmetic, census unbuilt.** The count is Menger's: edge-disjoint routes between two regions, minus one, is the number of independent checks available, and a region joined by a single intermediary has zero. **On a dense network that count degenerates into degree**, and degree in international merchandise trade tracks economic size, so the arm would read size and report checkability. **The census can only exist on a sparse network whose edges are physical**: inland waterway, pipeline, single-port islands and landlocked states are recorded as directions, not choices | results file, chunk one |
| **B30-3** | **First branch, with the alternative measured at its strongest rather than assumed away.** The matrix carries two named cars with opposite origins (Volkswagen Golf, Toyota Corolla). **Freight acts through origin and predicts they separate; they correlate `+0.8639`, third of all 1,378 item pairs, against a median pair of `-0.0376`.** Duty was then pulled from UNCTAD TRAINS (HS 870323, MFN applied, 133 of 149 countries, 1,231 of 1,280 cities, spread 0 to 167 per cent). **It enters and is not an income proxy** (Spearman `+0.6011` on the car rows against `-0.4315` on rent as control), **and it does not carry the co-movement**: one world rate takes `+0.8606` to `+0.8471`. **Chunk three then rebuilt the control in duty's favour** — each car on its own origin's schedule, the uncertain EPA step swept across its whole plausible range, both schedules entered for both rows, plus squares and interaction, six regressors. **Strongest point of the entire sweep `+0.8241`; the six-regressor case `+0.8032`, still above the matrix's 99th percentile of `+0.7064`.** Uncontrolled and named: registration tax, excise, dealer margin; tariff year 2020 against a late-2022 price vintage | results file, chunks one to three |
| **B30-4** | **Carrier settled on paper, availability gate run across six source classes, arm not opened, total collection cost zero.** Chunk one closed a city-by-item matrix without collecting anything (how many items a city carries is a property of the survey, not the market) and settled on the subscription-platform class, where a category's creator count is structural. **Chunk two then ran the gate and it returns a constant, not a shortage**: Substack's API works and its own description puts every category's leaderboard at the **top 25**, because a leaderboard is a display rule and not a market size. **So the treatment variable takes one value, which is gate zero (`D18`) answering one.** Graphtreon has no category and no entry tier; industry, press and trade-press classes give platform totals and never a per-category distribution. **What would open it is one published number, the count of creators in a category**, and none of the six classes contains it. Named as an instrument limit rather than a finding: Patreon's own directory was unreachable from this session and was never read. **Chunk three, 2026-09-16, read a seventh class chunk two had not enumerated: third-party aggregate directories that publish a creator count per category.** Six were read and **the count does vary there**, from 33 to 248 on a 1.8K index and from 155 to 25,418 on a 68,409 index, so the top-25 constant does not carry to this unit. **They disagree with each other on the same category name, and the test needs no denominator**: blonde against brunette reads `1.89` at one site and `1.01` at another, and solo is `58.5%` of one site's classified creators against `6.4%` and `3.7%` at two others; on the seven categories two of them share, the ratio of index shares spans `0.16` to `3.17`, a spread of **`20.4`**. **That disagreement does not close the single-site route**, since one site holds one rule and its count can still be monotone in true category size; what it shows is two unseparated components, different crawls and different labelling rules, and reading the published rules confirms at least three kinds are in play (third-party keyword match on bio words, creator-declared tags, and unpublished curation). **The registered word sorts them at zero cost**: the arm reads the density of *asserted* comparables, a creator-declared tag is an assertion and a keyword match is the indexer's inference, which leaves two of the six, **and neither states where the declaration lives**, the next step of this gate. **Two obstacles hold whichever site is chosen**: none of the six publishes a within-category spread, only a mean or median, so the outcome variable is not in the published layer (`D45`) and reading it means an enumeration whose size moves with the treatment; and one site truncates the treatment at the thin end by its own rule, `a listing only appears here once it has enough creators behind it to be worth browsing`, which is the same display-rule family as the top-25 finding. **Prior to all of it**, one index states there is no public API, directory or registry to enumerate, so whether a seller can perceive category size at all is a `D23` question that decides the carrier and is unsettled. **Chunk four then closed the seventh class on a structural reason rather than a shortage, for two page reads.** The two sites claiming creator-declared tags were read to the bottom. SearchOnly's own submission form takes a name, an email, a username and a free-text box with **no category selector anywhere**, and indexes `based on your content and profile information`, so the label is the site's. OnlySeek's FAQ is the one genuine case, `Categories are built from the tags creators wrote on their own profiles`, with removal as the creator's only interface, **and OnlySeek publishes no per-category count**: its category index prints none and two category pages print only the site-wide `201,447+`. **So across all six the count and the assertion are disjoint, and that is what the class is made of**: printing a count per category requires the directory to own a closed taxonomy, and owning the taxonomy is what removes the seller's assertion, while creator-written tags are an open vocabulary with no fixed buckets to count against. By `D27` the class needs no seventh site. **Chunk four's structural claim and the sorting behind it were withdrawn the same day, in a `作废栏` at the end of that chunk, and the record is worth carrying because nothing new was measured to overturn it.** Two rows were wrong: OnlySpotlight's rule IS published, on its report page (`Attributes are self-declared and unverified`, plus a CC BY 4.0 CSV), and the SearchOnly row was an inference from a submission form with no category selector written in the shape of a reading (failure mode 177). **And the claim itself breaks in both directions**: a platform can own the tag list, let the seller pick, and count (itch.io); a directory can harvest seller-declared attributes and still count over its own crawl. **The requirement was in chunk one all along and is about the count rather than the label**: `the count of a category is the count of the market, not the count of what anyone collected`. Failure mode 176 now carries that form. **So Patreon returns**: its own help centre says `You can't manually change the category in which you're featured. Patreon automatically categorizes creators based on their content, descriptions, and taglines`, which is the platform's own operative taxonomy and the surface a creator is actually found on; whether it publishes a per-category count is the open question. **One reading survives and is sharper**: five directories crawl one platform, uniform samples would agree in share, and on seven shared categories the ratio of shares runs `0.16` to `3.17`, so at most one of the five is uniform and nothing identifies which. **And the two sites are second carriers rather than rejects**: SearchOnly publishes per-category counts with a price-band breakdown (`Free 107.5K` / `$1-9 134.2K` / `$10-19 92.2K` / `$20+ 44.7K`, thirteen categories, smallest `281`), the same published shape itch.io carries, which turns the sampling objection into something measurable (`D49`). **Chunk five then closed Patreon out of Patreon's own documentation, with the site never opened.** Its classification qualifies under chunk one's requirement and is a field in its own data model (`Creators are grouped into hundreds of different genres and niches based on their content type and descriptions`; Campaign v2 carries a `categories` relationship). **The count is published across none of five source classes**: Explore is `personalized` and `curated` per viewer so there is no fixed listing to count; the help docs name the genres and print no number; **the API states `No endpoints exist for listing or counting campaigns across the platform or within categories`** and needs each campaign's own authorization; the blog and newsroom carry no per-category statistics; Graphtreon gives platform totals (`344,097` paid creators, `18,424,335` paid memberships) with no per-category count and no per-creator tier price. **So this is `D45`, published at no resolution, rather than `D26` or an instrument limit**: the per-genre count exists inside Patreon by construction and is exposed nowhere. The class-1 item registered in chunk two is closed. **Live carrier after five chunks: itch.io** (platform register, counts from `127` to `505k`, published price-band counts, tags the creator picks from a suggested list), **with SearchOnly as a second arm for measuring the sampling objection.** **Chunk six then moved the carrier and registered the split before any price was pulled.** The move is recorded as a carrier change rather than as the old carrier passing: itch.io prices one-off, so chunk one's link back to the first arm's grid finding does not carry, and the registered sentence names no subscription. **The platform draws the axis split itself**: a closed genre list of eleven values spans Sports `13,769` to Action `242,113`, **`17.6` times with no thin end**, while the open tag vocabulary spans `127` to `505k`; the live branch reads the thin end, **so tags carry the treatment and genre becomes a free stratifier** that removes price-level differences between kinds of game. **By `D49` the reading is declared to depend on three features of a label and nothing else** (it names a kind a buyer substitutes within; its members are visible to a seller, which holds for every tag here; its size is set by how many make that kind rather than by price), and the split rule follows from the third: `2D` at `430k` and `No AI` at `505k` fail it. **Order of work registered: pull names and counts, classify on names alone and record, only then join the price bands.** **Step one ran 2026-09-16 and step two the same day, in that order, with no price fetched by either.** Step one parsed `616` directory cells, none skipped, ten of ten verified against direct reads, and **one wrong parse bought three shapes**: the register prints tags, genres and one bare feature, so the genre axis arrived free rather than as a second fetch. Step two split the `516` games-scope tags into **`151` market, `292` not a market, `73` third state, the market side spanning `161` to `114,000`, a factor of `708`**, which is the treatment variable the criterion registered. **Three of the classifier's own hand-written set entries matched nothing in the vocabulary and every total stayed right** (an engine's name standing in for its jam, a truncated console name, an escaped form left from before names were unescaped); a set difference against the vocabulary found them, printed entry by entry, and that check now runs in the self-test with a seeded dead entry asserting it fires. **The third state came back holding two different things and was amended once, with the discriminant written down and reading no count**: a form of play is a market tag, a subject a work is about stays unsettled, a purpose claim is neither; twenty-one names moved and they land at both ends (`Card Game` `24,400` and `Nonogram` `161`), so it is not a move that fattens one end. **Scanning the market side for nesting returns `15` pairs of three kinds, and only one of them is a threat**: nested pairs (`Horror` over `Lovecraftian Horror`) are the design, since the subject is held by construction and the density varied; **one market under two names** (`LGBT` / `LGBTQIA` / `Queer`, `Runner` / `Endless Runner` / `infinite-runner`, `Picross` / `Nonogram`) splits the treatment while leaving the outcome whole, **which flattens the relationship in the direction of branch B**, and it is not detectable from names, so step three reads nested pairs. Open and named: the resolution of a dispersion read off four or five published bands (`D24`), the paid count as the real `n` (`4,318` of `92,386` on the thickest tag, `13` of `127` on the thinnest), whether the thin end is read tag by tag or in bins, and whether the genre axis is used at all, since tag by genre is about `15,000` requests. **Chunk seven, 2026-09-16, opened step three and settled the unit of the axis.** **The page's published resolution is three bins above zero, not four or five**: the site's price controls are `free`, `store`, `5-dollars-or-less` and `15-dollars-or-less`, cumulative and in the path, so subtracting gives `(0,5]`, `(5,15]` and an open `(15,+)`, with On Sale a discount state rather than a band. **Whether those filters count from zero was measured rather than assumed**: the derived top bin is non-negative and the filters monotone on all `151` tags, so they count from the first cent. **The bins are not the reading, because the prices are**: each listing cell carries the project's own posted price, `36` to a page, so a distribution with no binning costs what the bins cost and the bins become a cross-check. **The counts ran, `5` per tag, `755` requests, every tag returning a full set, and they turned up an instrument failure**: `free + paid = total` holds exactly on `135` tags, misses by one on `7` and by more on `9`, the sharpest being a tag whose free page alone reports `4,760` against `3,377` unfiltered, **which no consistent filter can do**; the two pages carry the same games in the same order (`34/36`, `33/36`), **so the populations agree and the counters do not**, and since all nine are market tags the walk settles them by construction (`11d` known_answer). The seven that miss by one match the signature of uploads landing between requests, are `+1` and never negative, and move no reading. **The same attribute order cost five matchers in one file, each silently**: a third of the paid pages parsed to zero cells and `26%` of a paid listing carried no price with nothing complaining; rewritten with lookaheads the same cached pages give `5,137` cells, zero parse misses and `0.10%` without a price, **recovering `1,319` prices for zero new requests**. This is the third time this site's attribute order has cost the station, and the guard now asserted per page is the one the shape asks for: on a paid listing a cell with no price is not a plausible object, and a cell count taken independently of the parser is asserted against the parse. **The site does not price only in dollars**: `USD 4,941`, `EUR 133`, `GBP 55`, `BRL 3`, symbol before the number for some and after for others, so the currency is carried with the value and conversion is decided against a measured `3.7%`. **The free-to-paid boundary is a commitment threshold and not a point on a price scale**, measured: the free listing's `5,436` cells carry `14` price tags all reading a zero floor, the paid listing's `5,132` price tags include `116` reading zero **and all `116` are on sale, `115` at a hundred per cent off**, so a paid project has a positive regular floor and name-your-own-price with no floor posts no number at all and is correctly outside a dispersion of posted prices; flagged for other users of this carrier because purchase-rate readings meet a break there that is not a price effect. **The unit of the axis is the tag**: a project tagged survival and strategy substitutes for a buyer who came for either, those buyers overlap only partly with survival-and-horror buyers, and the site makes it literal by serving one tag page at a time; counting per project instead would need an assignment rule, which is a degree of freedom this design does not otherwise spend. **The finer partition is countable rather than a rabbit hole**: `/games/tag-horror/tag-lovecraft` returns `725` and `/games/tag-picross/tag-nonogram` returns `92`, so combination markets are destinations with their own densities, thinner than either parent, available for one request each. **How much the multiple counting amounts to was measured**: one genre per project and never two across `9,218` cells, so ten genre counts sum to `1,314,500` against `5,473,909` tag slots, **`4.16` slots per project on the raw vocabulary and `1.12` on the market side**, the split done in step two for another reason being what makes it small; `1.12` is an upper bound because `5.6%` of projects set no genre and the directory lists ten of the seventeen genres the upload form offers, seven of which share a name with a market tag, so `genre-survival` and `tag-survival` are different populations and every count here used the tag form. **Chunk four's surviving reading was qualified the same day, original text unchanged**: the `20.4` spread of index shares assumes the shares are comparable, which holds only if each site files the same number of categories per creator, and a site reporting solo at `58.5%` of its classified creators is filing one; **so part of the spread measures the filing rule rather than the sampling, and it also identifies a subset, since a site permitting several categories is structurally closer to a population where a creator does one thing among others**. The class stays closed on coverage alone (`68,409` against a population in the millions, failure mode 176), **which is a closing reason that does not depend on filing rules**. **The walk then ran, `1,660` requests, median `0.65` s, `26,353` distinct paid projects, `223` notes all of one kind and no repeated page, page cap or missed cell.** **It settles the counter**: the walk matched the printed count on `146` of `151` tags and the five that differ differ by one, four up and one down, which is churn (an upload adds, a delisting or an author removing a tag subtracts) and is recorded with its direction rather than smoothed. **On all nine tags whose counts failed `free + paid = total`, the walk matched the printed `paid` exactly, to zero**, so the paid counter is sound on every tag and the fault sits in `free` or `total`; since the treatment is drawn from `total` this locates rather than removes it, and one tag's walk (about ninety pages on Furry) would say which. **The denominator was asked for rather than summed**: the unfiltered games page prints `1,546,536`, so the ten-genre floor was `15%` low and the ratios correct to **`3.54` tag slots per project and `0.95` on the market side**, less than one. **On the paid population it is `2.17`, which is `2.3x` the population rate**, so the treatment is counted over one population and the outcome over another and the two do not tag alike; the distribution is `39.1%` in one market, `29.1%` in two, `17.1%` in three, `14.8%` in four or more, which is the shape counting per tag predicts and counting per project would have to flatten with a rule. **The overlap was measured and it corrects the earlier reading in both directions**: pairs called synonymous overlap less than that word implies (Runner and Endless Runner `0.29`, LGBT and Queer `0.49`, Picross and Nonogram `0.77` of the smaller side) while pairs called nested overlap more (Horror and Survival Horror `0.87`, and Lovecraftian `0.65`), **so the flattening bias is smaller than it was written to be and the subset relation the nested design rests on mostly holds**; the heaviest overlaps on the axis are neither, being a romance cluster (Otome and Romance `0.80`) and an idle cluster (`0.71`). **How much the clustering costs is a number that moves on a knob, so the ladder is printed rather than a point** (`11f`): `14` groups at Jaccard `0.02`, `128` at `0.15`, `142` at `0.25`, `151` at `0.60` where no pair survives, **so at any test of `0.15` or above the axis keeps at least `128` of its `151` points and the multiple counting does not collapse it**. **What has no usable posted price is counted rather than imputed**: `26,188` priced (`99.37%`), `153` with no price element at all (`0.58%`, cells otherwise complete, so a paid project may post no single number), `12` in a fifth currency that cannot be converted (`Pay ¥N`, titles both Japanese and Chinese, and the symbol is shared by two currencies about twenty times apart), `293` discounted to nothing and `1,144` on sale at all. Non-dollar is `6.7%` of priced projects, wider than the `3.7%` the first pages showed. **Chunk eight, 2026-09-17, ran the sweep before choosing a statistic, and it took three passes to get a number that stayed put.** `360` settings, all returning a value, **sign the same in every one**, positive, `+0.058` to `+0.631`, which is neither registered branch. **The first pass was the sample size**: a tag's dispersion was read off however many prices it carried, six to nearly four thousand, and a shuffle that deals prices across tags with the sizes held reproduces almost the whole correlation (`sd_log` null `+0.218` against observed `+0.250`; across the five measures the artefact runs `-0.199` to `+0.649`), **so the same data read five ways gives a size artefact anywhere from minus a fifth to plus two thirds**. Picking the measure with the smallest artefact would be picking the answer, so **the size is held by design instead**: every tag contributes exactly `12` prices, keeping `148` of `151` tags, after which the five nulls read `-0.022`, `-0.003`, `-0.018`, `-0.018`, `-0.021`. The self-test plants the confound and requires its removal, **using the real prices with synthetic sizes, because a synthetic price distribution does not reproduce it** (a lognormal plant reads near nothing, since the bias lives in the real shape: `590` distinct values piled on a dollar, five dollars, `$4.99`). **The second pass was breadth**: a thicker tag is also a coarser label, so the control is a pair whose smaller side sits inside the bigger, with containment measured from memberships not names, giving `101 / 58 / 37 / 23 / 16` pairs at `0.30` to `0.70` over `37 / 25 / 17 / 9 / 7` distinct bigger sides. **The third pass was `D51`**: the pair count at `0.50` moved between `7` and `16` of `37` across five seeds, **a swing wider than the distance to the halfway mark, so it was not a measurement**; the draws needed to settle it were measured (`25` gives sd `3.4`, `100` gives `0.8`, `400` gives `1.6`, `1200` gives `1.3`) and the pair tests now run at `400` draws with every count printed over five seeds. **The controlled comparison: not one cell of the ladder has the thinner side wider**, every count at or below half, and **the five measures split along what they measure rather than along noise** — the three that read tails (`sd_log`, `gini`, `cv`) put the thicker side wider at `0.30`, `0.40` and weakly at `0.50`, while the two that read the middle (`iqr/median`, `mad/median`) read a coin flip at every level. **The floor was measured by planting it**: at containment `0.50` a `1.10x` widening of the thinner side is caught by three of five measures (`p 0.02 / 0.00 / 0.00`) and none is there. **So on the middle of the distribution the comparison is flat against a design that resolves ten per cent, which is the branch registered as anchoring not being what sets the entry price; branch A is unsupported at every level by every measure; and the tails are a third outcome neither branch enumerated**, a thicker market carrying a wider upper tail with an unchanged centre, recorded as a finding rather than pressed into a branch (`11c`, `D15`). **Chunk eight's containment control was withdrawn the same day in that chunk's `作废栏`, and the reason is mechanical**: a containment pair sets a tag against a subset of itself (`87%` of Survival Horror's paid projects carry Horror too), so the bigger side's price pool contains the smaller side's plus everything else, **a mixture is at least as spread as its own component under almost any width measure, and that is set theory rather than a market**; the numbers stay in place with the bias direction stated, and what stands is the sweep, the size-confound diagnosis, the equal-n design, the `D51` finding and the resolution ladder, none of which use containment (failure mode 181). **Chunk nine, 2026-09-17, then registered a reading.** The registered word is dispersion and **the mechanism under it is anchoring, which is copying a number rather than narrowing a range**: across `24,159` dollar-priced projects there are `590` distinct price points with a dollar carrying `4,774`, five dollars `1,944`, `$4.99` `1,831`, **so width and pile move independently and here they do**. Four families of measure were swept and **the shuffle picks among them without appeal to taste**: at equal `n` the nulls are `cv +0.649`, `gini +0.501`, `sd_log +0.215`, `top1_share +0.150`, `mad/median -0.199`, and only two sit at zero, **`iqr/median +0.011` and `price_point_entropy -0.031`, and they are in different families**. `price_point_entropy` reads `-0.291` to `-0.260` over five seeds against its null, **z `-2.7`**, which is **branch A in the registered words: the price points scatter where the comparables thin out, so there is no anchor to attach to**. **Breadth is held by a measure rather than a pair**: genre entropy over a tag's paid projects, `0.10` on Sokoban to `2.39` on Sci-fi, nearly unrelated to the pile (`-0.064`) while related to density (`+0.366`); inside thirds of it the sign holds everywhere, `-0.19 / -0.42 / -0.23` on the project count and `-0.05 / -0.21 / -0.09` on the paid count, **both defensible since a seller browsing a tag sees every project while only the paid ones carry a number to copy**. **The two clean measures disagree and they disagree about something real**: `iqr/median` reads flat, `price_point_entropy` reads scatter, and both are true, since a thick market and a thin one have about the same spread between their quartiles while the thick one has more of its mass on the same few numbers. **Ruled 2026-09-17: the criterion registers `price_point_entropy`**, with the width reading printed beside it at every setting. **Five passes, each finding a different thing between the data and a number** (the sample size, the breadth of the label, the draws, the control itself, the family of measure), **and not one of them announced itself**. **Chunk nine's own argument was then corrected in its `作废栏`, the same day, from the record**, and the reading did not move. Two errors: the null table quoted the **pre**-equal-n values under an equal-n heading, so **eight of nine nulls are at zero rather than two** and the shuffle eliminates exactly one measure (`top1_share`, `+0.150`) rather than picking the measure; and the section reading `iqr/median` as flat rested on the withdrawn containment control. **Put through the breadth measure, every width measure turns over between one third and the next** (`sd_log +0.20/-0.09/-0.00`, `iqr +0.23/-0.08/-0.04`, `cv +0.25/+0.08/+0.14`) and all five carry a breadth correlation near `+0.17` against `-0.08` to `+0.10` for the surviving pile measures, **so the width family is not flat on this carrier, it is unreadable**, which is a stronger statement and removes the supposed disagreement between branches. **What separates the measures once the size is held is two things**: whether the family answers the mechanism, and whether the sign holds across the breadth thirds. **Three measures survive both** and all three read the anchoring direction: `top3_share` (`+0.216` to `+0.295`, z `+2.0`), `distinct_per_n` (`-0.285` to `-0.216`, z `-2.5`) and `price_point_entropy` (`-0.303` to `-0.257`, z `-2.8`). **The registration stands and is now the representative of three concordant measures.** The sixth pass is recorded as failure mode 182: **this chunk was written from the runs rather than from the record, and a figure does not carry the stage that produced it**. **The price itself was then checked, three ways.** **Currency is the seller's and not a display conversion**: `83%` of euro prices land on a round euro point and `81%` of pound prices on a round pound point against a `90%` dollar baseline, and no rate between `0.70` and `1.10` explains them better than one (a first look at `2.51€ / 3.35€ / 4.19€`, each `0.8395` of a round dollar point, suggested otherwise and did not survive: **the roundness test had been written to accept only `.00`, `.99` and `.95`**). **It is stable**: of `16,057` projects appearing on more than one tag page, two print a different price and both are a sale starting mid-walk. **And it is the project's own**: a sample of `24` stratified across four price bands found the listing price on `22` of the pages with **none carrying a lower option**, so the listing is not showing the cheapest of several, and the two without a purchase control a day later are corroborated at band resolution by the page's own breadcrumb. **The sample answered the multi-market question from the other side for free**: project pages declare `2` to `10` tags each, median `7`, and **in all `24` the count of those that are market tags equals the count derived from the tag pages, exactly**, with `48` market, `83` non-market, `4` third-state and `23` outside the census vocabulary across `158` declared tags. **Closed 2026-09-17.** The station carries two numbered criteria in `results/b30_4_knob_sweep.json`, both computed from the objects and both flipped by a seeded wrong input: `B30-4-1` `instrument`, the equal-n nulls of all five width measures at zero; `B30-4-2` `own_reading`, the sign of `price_point_entropy` against the destination's project count the same in every third of breadth and across seeds, **which is branch A**. The design file carries the registered measure and the ground for it. **The records are published with a provenance block and a `SOURCES.md` entry** naming what each row is, what it is not (a posted minimum, not a transaction price), and what is deliberately absent (no descriptions, no markup; the `222 MB` of fetched HTML stays off the repository because a description is text its seller wrote while a title and a price are facts). **And the registered measure was then run across its own settings, which it had not been**: the sweep of chunk eight covered the width family, while the pile family had only ever run at one setting, **and a measure run at one setting has not been checked**. Six settings over the sale knob, the currency knob and a third option that **restores a discounted project to the level it was discounted from, which is the number its seller set**; three seeds; the whole axis and each third of breadth. **Every value is negative**, `-0.316` to `-0.260` on the whole axis, **and the two settings closest to what a seller set (dropping the sales, or restoring them) read strongest**. The account from dual listing is refuted in both directions by arithmetic alone: **double counting has the wrong sign on eight of the nine**, and on the ninth **an overlap cannot exceed the smaller bin**, which holds 208 against a gap of 1,591. **The listing stops at 200 pages of 36 rows, found by a 404 on page 201**, so this check is structurally unavailable on 45 of 151 tags; the largest paid listing is 120 pages, **so the walk that vindicated the `paid` counter on all 151 tags ran untruncated**, and that is the counter the reading uses. **The shared symbol is `JPY` on all twelve pages**, and the twelve were outside every setting already because the parser declined their price strings. **The one broken counter that does enter a density definition was measured against the rank it enters** rather than argued away: replacing `total` by `free + paid` across 151 tags moves 43 ranks of which 39 move by one, moves two materially (`furry` 17 places, `gay` 16), and leaves the two orderings correlated at `+0.9989`. **And the combination-market axis was then gated and did not clear, which closes the arm.** The account the single-tag axis cannot rule out is that prices scatter at the thin end because those sellers are less practised, and a destination made by intersecting two established tags is thin without being obscure. **719 such destinations exist and 49 of them share no project at all**, density `12` to `1,233`, `0` of `1,176` pairs touching, **so that axis is independent as a fact about its sets rather than as an estimate**.
