got two. That count came from a rule rather than from the energy sector, so this
station writes the rule out in full, applies it outside energy, and checks it
against the one set of answers already on disk. Nothing is fetched: the whole
station is four questions asked of seventeen candidates, plus one comparison
against a record.

The screen, in order. **Q0, one commodity**: are the two classes buying the same
thing? **Q1, no transfer**: can a holder pass it to the other class cheaply?
**Q2, two posted prices**: does each class have a published price? **Q3, imposed
split**: is the division set by a third party rather than chosen by the parties?

**Q0 is new, and it was implicit in Q1 all along.** "The two prices cannot be
arbitraged against each other" presupposes that they are two prices of one thing.
Written out, it removes fixed broadband and cable television, where a business
package carries a service level, a static address and symmetric capacity, so the
gap between the two prices contains product specification. One kilowatt hour is
one kilowatt hour, and that is why electricity survives. Both of those two fail
Q3 as well: the operator defines the packages, so the split is chosen.

**Q1 has two sources, and until B53 only the first had been used.** Either the
commodity cannot be transferred, arriving over a fixed network with nothing
moving past the meter, or the entitlement cannot be transferred, with the
commodity moving freely and identity checked at the point of consumption. The
second covers tuition at a resident against a non-resident rate, named concession
fares, resident admission pricing and prescription copayment. It is the larger
family, and it was out of view because Q1 was read as a rule about commodities
when it is a rule about whether a channel exists between two classes.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B51-1** the screen passes every carrier whose class difference has been measured | electricity, piped natural gas and resident tuition, all three carry | PASS · `known_answer` |
| **B51-2** the screen's Q2 answer agrees with the paired-cell count in the record, product by product | **8 of 8 agree**: `179`, `102`, `122`, `48`, `17` and `22` paired cells against a yes, `0` and `0` against a no | PASS · `known_answer` |
| **B51-3** every candidate answers all four questions and every answer carries a ground | 17 candidates, 4 questions each | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B51-4** every candidate that does not pass names which questions it failed | 8 named, by question | PASS · `bookkeeping` |

**B51-2 is the only thing here that data could have broken.** The screen reads a
rule; the record counts rows. Two paths to the same eight answers, and they
agree at every product.

**What the station does not do.** It confirms no new carrier at the moment it
runs. Eight fail, each at a named question, and the rest are open. **Resident
tuition was one of the open ones and B53 settled it**: Q2 by 5,605 published
schedules from one cross-institution source, and Q3 by measurement rather than
by reading one statute, since private schedules write one value 3,424 times in
3,439 while public ones write two or three 1,973 times in 2,166. Three candidates
now carry and six are open, each with the specific thing that has to be read
before it can be settled: a cross-country source of household against commercial water and
sewerage tariffs; whether district heating publishes a separate non-household
price at all; a fare table
carrying both the full and the concession rate; whether a resident admission
price is imposed or offered at the operator's discretion, which may fail Q3
outright; and whether what is published against a prescription is a price or a
reimbursement rate, since the second would make the two numbers
incommensurable. An answer whose ground has not been read against a source
leaves its candidate open rather than passing it, and the printed table marks
which answers are read and which are carried.


## B52 — the same class square across Europe and across time, and a reading of B49's withdrawn

Station documents: [`b52_prereg.md`](docs/b52_prereg.md) and [`b52_results.md`](docs/b52_results.md).

B49 read this square in 13 countries at 3 years. B50 read it in one country over
37 semesters. This station puts both dimensions together on the Eurostat panel:
every geography the source carries, 38 semesters, three tax bases. Nothing new is
collected; the same four legs are pulled without a country filter.

Carrier: Eurostat bi-annual energy prices, the standard reference bands Eurostat
itself publishes against, `KWH2500-4999` and `MWH500-1999` for electricity,
`GJ20-199` and `GJ10000-99999` for gas. `experiments/b52_europe_class_square.py`
fetches and scores; responses are cached under `data/cache/eurostat/` so a rerun
goes to the network zero times. Criteria are written into the script that
produces the record, the record carries their wording, and every quantity this
run produced is reported.

**Counting the independent loops, because a panel invites inflation here.** Four
vertices and four edges give `b1 = 4 - 4 + 1 = 1` per country. Each country is one
independent square and the semesters are that square moving, not new squares. The
independent count is **33, one per country, not 1076**. The script prints that
line and writes it into the record.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B52-1** panel completeness, country by country | 33 countries, 38 semesters, 1076 cells, 33 independent loops; two cells dropped because a price is zero, which is an absence and not a price | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B52-2** the square does not move with the currency the prices are quoted in | floor `1.579e-03`; of 1076 comparisons **546 are the identity**, because a euro-area country already quotes in euro, and the floor comes from the rest | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B52-3** no readable cell matches the rival's point prediction of exactly zero | **0 of 1069**; the 7 cells at or below the floor cannot separate zero from non-zero and carry no verdict | PASS · `rival` |
| **B52-4** cells at or below the floor are named and carry no verdict | 1069 of 1076 above; median `103x` the floor, largest `2.1802` | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B52-5** the sign drift is one-directional, each country over its own first and last semester | 6 one way, 5 the other, 22 unchanged | **FAIL** · `own_reading` |
| **B52-6** the same, on one window every country shares for its whole length | `2008-S1..2025-S2`, 22 countries: 5 against 2 | **FAIL** · `own_reading` |
| **B52-7** the same, stopped before the 2021-2023 energy interventions | `2008-S1..2021-S1`, 23 countries: 3 against 2 | **FAIL** · `own_reading` |

**What is stronger here.** The rival is a scalar price field over positions, which
predicts every square sum is exactly zero whatever the level of prices. B49 read
39 cells with 13 independent loops and a median at 56 times its floor. This reads
1069 with 33 independent loops and a median at 103 times.

**What is withdrawn.** B49 also read a moving sign, 5 positive cells of 13 in
2000, 2 in 2010, 1 in 2025, with five countries turning one way and none the
other. That shape does not survive: 6 against 5 with each country's own window, 5
against 2 on a shared one, and **3 against 2 in a window stopping before the
energy crisis**. One direction being empty is not there in any window. That
withdraws a registered open item rather than a claim: the framework predicts a
non-zero square and says nothing about which way the sign goes, and the reading
was recorded as an open question and not as a result.

**Three things the panel separates that were running together.** The crisis
enlarged this quantity's movement by ten to twenty-five times: one Dutch semester
moves `1.325` where thirteen German years move `0.07`. It contributed almost
nothing to the first-to-last change: 14 down and 9 up before it, 15 down and 7 up
across the whole window, because the jumps come back. And the bias itself is weak
in both windows and one-directional in neither.

**Dates.** The largest moves are at `2021-S2` to `2022-S1`. The Nord Stream 1
reductions and halt run from June to September 2022 and the ruptures are 26
September 2022, all inside `2022-S2`. European gas was already climbing in the
autumn of 2021, so that halt is a step inside the episode rather than its start.
The episode is one common shock with very different downstream responses, which
is why it is not treated as one common design.

**A negative reading on Germany, and the instrument limit it exposes.** The German
electricity class gap moves `0.07` between 2008 and 2021 while the renewables
surcharge on electricity bills rose about sixfold over the same years, with
electricity-intensive industry paying a reduced rate. The two are consistent, and
checking the statute says why: the reduced rate requires **more than 1 GWh a year,
membership of a listed sector, and an electricity cost intensity of at least 14 or
20 per cent** depending on the list. **The standard non-household reference band is
0.5 to 2 GWh.** Its lower half cannot meet the consumption threshold at all, and a
firm meeting the intensity test consumes far more than the band's upper edge. **So
the reference band cannot see that exemption, and a class difference of that
family is invisible to this instrument.** What is checked here is the threshold
against the band, not a count of firms inside the band.


### B52 second arm — the readable form of D48's fourth shape, and three versions of its null

`33 countries` `38 semesters` `nothing collected` `read from this station's own record`

**D48 says the fourth shape, "there is no restoring force here", is itself a
prediction, and the register said what was missing: that statement has to be
separable from "a restoring force we failed to see". This writes the reading, and it
took three nulls to get one that holds.**

**Version one wrote the null at one half and the file's own self-check killed it.** A
deviation is measured against the series' own median, estimated from the same
realised path, so **a pure random walk through this pipeline reads 0.7031 back** at a
floor of 0.0727. Regression toward a sample-estimated centre is mechanical and large.

**Version two used shuffled first differences, and a self-check found that too weak
the same day.** Shuffling keeps the step distribution and destroys the step order, so
it removes any autocorrelation the steps carry — and **negatively autocorrelated
steps produce reversion in the level on their own**, which is where averaging or
measurement error in a semi-annual series lands. Measured: **the differences carry a
median lag-one autocorrelation of −0.2046, negative in 25 of 33 countries, as low as
−0.75.** The shuffled null was standing on the wrong side of that.

**Version three: a circular block bootstrap of the differences, which keeps the local
step structure and still integrates to a level with no restoring force in it.** Block
length is load-bearing, so the whole ladder is printed rather than chosen:

| null | reads |
|---|---|
| Gaussian walk | 0.6614 |
| shuffled differences | 0.6747 |
| block 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 | 0.6773 / 0.6774 / 0.6961 / 0.7103 |
| **block 8, strictest eligible** | **0.7199** |
| block 12 / 16, not eligible | 0.7320 / 0.7383 |

The usual block length at a median series of 37 points is `L^(1/3) = 3.3`; the ladder
is carried to 8, more than twice that. **Beyond it the resampled series is mostly one
contiguous run of the original and the null degenerates into the observation, so
those lengths are printed as a trend and do not adjudicate.**

**The reading: observed 0.7667 (back 276, away 84, n = 360), gap +0.0468 against a
floor of 0.0355. Separated at every eligible block length.** At the ineligible block
16 the margin falls to +0.0284, below the floor; that is stated as scope.

**The half-life ladder is built on the same steps**, with the force applied on top of
the same block-bootstrapped differences and compared one-sided against `phi = 1`.
H = 1 produces 0.8552, H = 2 produces 0.8180, H = 4 produces 0.7884, **H = 8 produces
0.7670, which is where the observation sits**, and H = 16 and beyond are not
separable. **Moving to the stricter null pushed this quantity from about two
semesters to about eight, four years.** Version two's ladder used Gaussian steps
against a real-step null, which compared step structure rather than force: the sixth
category error.

**Seasonality is measured and only half excluded.** Inside one semester half,
consecutive points are a year apart and an S1-to-S2 alternation cannot act. S1 reads
0.8162 against 0.7615, gap +0.0547 on a floor of 0.0517, separated. **S2 reads 0.7892
against 0.7509, gap +0.0383 on a floor of 0.0475, not separated.** The main reading
is held to that scope: neither "seasonality is excluded" nor "this is seasonality".

**The energy shock is the obvious alternative and it is not excluded.** A shock that
rises and falls back is by itself large deviations followed by moves back. Cut at this
station's own fixed pre-crisis end, 2021-S1, the reading gives observed 0.7849 against
0.7557, **gap +0.0293 on a floor of 0.0416: not separated.** `n` falls from 360 to 279
so the floor rises, and the gap itself falls by 37 per cent; both moved and neither
dominates. **That is the middle of the three states, undecidable, not a reading of no
restoring force.** Resolving it needs a carrier without that shock, not more cuts of
this panel.

**The tax candidate is excluded, and what excludes it is the direction.** One of the
three registered candidates was administratively set tax rates. If the force lived in
the tax, removing tax would weaken it. **It strengthens: I_TAX gap +0.0468, X_TAX
+0.0821, X_VAT +0.0601, all three separated.** It lives in the price.

**What this says, with the two readings stated apart.** The counting law counts how
many class values a programme writes and does not order them, so the framework has no
reason to pin that sign, and that stays true. What is measured is that on the full
window the sign's deviation **does** revert at a half-life this panel can see, **and
that this cannot be told apart from the 2021-23 energy shock.** So "something pins it"
now carries a qualifier: that something may be the shock. Either way it is not the
counting law. No score: an object nobody has a reading for, and one open alternative.

| | criterion | kind | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | B52-R1 the pipeline reproduces the artefact and can see a planted force | known_answer | matched walk reads 0.6614, not 0.5; a planted H = 4 separates from it |
| PASS | B52-R2 print every country's length and the steps that entered | instrument | 33 countries, 360 steps, 200 sims per null |
| PASS | B52-R3 the observed proportion against a measured null | own_reading | 0.7667 against 0.7199, gap +0.0468, floor 0.0355 |
| PASS | B52-R5 a null carrying the panel's own step autocorrelation | instrument | step acf1 median −0.2046, negative in 25 of 33; block ladder printed |
| PASS | B52-R6 the reading repeated inside each semester half | own_reading | S1 separated, S2 not; seasonality half excluded |
| PASS | B52-R7 the reading on a window stopping before the energy shock | own_reading | gap +0.0293 on a floor of 0.0416, not separated; the alternative is not excluded |
| PASS | B52-R8 the reading on the other two tax bases | own_reading | X_TAX +0.0821, X_VAT +0.0601, both separated; the force is in the price, not the tax |
| PASS | B52-R4 which half-lives this panel could have seen | own_reading | separable 1, 2, 4, 8 semesters; not 16 and beyond |

`experiments/b52_restoring_force.py`, `results/b52_restoring_force.json`


## B53 — the counting law where the collisions are exact

Station documents: [`b53_prereg.md`](docs/b53_prereg.md) and [`b53_results.md`](docs/b53_results.md).

A published tuition schedule writes three classes, in-district, in-state and
out-of-state, and produces however many distinct dollar figures those three
carry. That is the counting law's object. What this corpus adds is that the
figures are whole dollars: every collision the tariff corpus reports is bounded
above by that survey rounding to two decimals and is stated as an upper bound at
the published resolution, and no rounding turns two different dollar amounts into
one. **B53-3 reads that premise off the corpus rather than assuming it**, and
finds no non-integer figure over 5,605 schedules. What it reports is the format
the comparison needs, and it cannot fail on a corpus published in whole dollars.
It says nothing about what an institution summed before publishing a number: the
counting law counts written values, and a whole-dollar figure is the written value
whatever produced it.

Carrier: the Urban Institute Education Data API over IPEDS, public and keyless,
2020, fetched state by state and cached per endpoint and state so an interrupted
run resumes. Institution control comes from a separate endpoint and is not
derived here. `experiments/b53_tuition_class_values.py` fetches and scores.
Criteria are written into the script that produces the record, the record carries
their wording, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B53-1** every private institution writes one value across the three classes; the control code comes from a separate endpoint, so this is a check and not a restatement | 3,439 private schedules, **15 write more than one value**, each one named | **FAIL** · `known_answer` |
| **B53-2** how many schedules write 3 → 1, 3 → 2 and 3 → 3, by control and level | `3 → 1` 3,617; `3 → 2` 1,738; `3 → 3` 250 | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **B53-3** the premise that makes the comparison exact: every figure a whole dollar amount, so two figures are equal or they are not | 0 non-integer figures over 5,605 schedules. **Reports the corpus's format, not the institutions' arithmetic**, and cannot fail on a corpus published in whole dollars | PASS · `premise` |
| **B53-4** coverage state by state, states returning nothing named rather than absent | 56 requested, 56 returned; 124 rows dropped for a negative code, counted per state | PASS · `bookkeeping` |

**The reading.**

| control | level | 3 → 1 | 3 → 2 | 3 → 3 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| public | undergraduate | 136 | **1,227** | **243** |
| public | graduate | 57 | **500** | 3 |
| private nonprofit | undergraduate | **1,510** | 6 | 3 |
| private nonprofit | graduate | **1,246** | 2 | 1 |
| private for-profit | undergraduate | **480** | 1 | 0 |
| private for-profit | graduate | **188** | 2 | 0 |

Of 3,439 private schedules 3,424 write one value; of 2,166 public schedules 1,973
write two or three. **The collisions total 8,972**, and every one of them is
exact. The tariff corpus reports 23 in its block arm, all resolution-limited, and
7 in its time-of-use arm, 2 of them exact.

**Independent counts, both reported.** 5,605 schedules across 3,861 institutions.
Undergraduate and graduate are two separate schedules and can each be counted as
a procedure, and they are set by one institution, so the institution count is the
ceiling and the schedule count is not. This run covers one year; the corpus runs
1986 to 2023, and the independent count has to be recomputed before it is
extended across years, since an institution across years is one object moving.

**The failing criterion is the useful one.** The known answer is that a private
institution has no in-state and out-of-state distinction. Fifteen schedules
break it, and they are named rather than counted. Four institutions do it in
both the undergraduate and the graduate schedule, which is not the signature of
a filing error; most take the form in-district equal to in-state and below
out-of-state, and three carry three distinct figures. The claim registered is
that fifteen named schedules were written this way in 2020, not that private
institutions in general price by residence.

## B54 — enumerating the carriers where eligibility is checked at the counter

Criteria are written into the script that produces the record, the record
carries their wording, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

A class difference shows up in a price only where the good is one good, the
entitlement cannot be handed on, two prices are posted, and the split is imposed
by someone other than the parties. B51 wrote those four questions down. One of
the two ways to satisfy the second question, the good moves freely while the
buyer's standing is checked at the point of sale, had produced one carrier. This
station enumerates that family: nineteen named candidates on seven axes,
residence, income test, nationality, age, enrolment or occupation, disability,
and registration. `experiments/b54_eligibility_carrier_enum.py` records one row
per candidate with each of the four answers, whether that answer stands on a
document, and the document.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B54-1** every answer says whether a document stands behind it, and an answer that does not is never counted as an answer | 19 candidates, 76 answers, 0 unmarked | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B54-2** the verdict map is written out cell by cell, and the undetermined cell maps to neither carrying nor failing | 4 cells printed, undetermined maps to no verdict | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B54-3** print the object: every candidate's four answers and its verdict | **carries 12, undetermined 0, fails 7** | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **B54-4** every candidate names the instrument that would be read | 19 candidates, 0 without one | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B54-5** the band and the Q3 answer agree in every row: band 1 answers no, bands 2 and 3 answer yes | 19 candidates, 0 disagreements; bands 1:2, 2:13, 3:4 | PASS · `instrument` |

Ten candidates carry and thirteen sit in this family.

**The fourth question changed on 2026-09-07 and that is what moved the count.**
It asked whether a third party rather than the parties drew the line. That is a
proxy. What D30's second clause actually bars is a split the disfavoured side can
escape, and it bars it because the disfavoured side then exits and leaves no price
difference to read. Where the class is an attribute of a person rather than a form
the seller may restructure, nobody exits, and the question that carries is whether
the attribute can be acquired at near-zero cost. The question now asks that, in
three bands: crossing costs nothing, crossing is possible and costs, crossing is
impossible by construction.

The change is not a loosening. **No candidate that failed now carries**, and two
of the four failing rows already had their reasons written in crossing language,
enrolment is free and open and anyone may cross by paying the membership, while
the question text still said who drew the line. The answers were using the new
discriminant before the question did.

What it bought: the old question needed a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction reading of
statutes, and the new one is answerable from the axis itself for residence, age,
enrolment, income, nationality and disability. Candidates blocked on it went from
eight to none. The ones that remain undetermined are blocked on whether two
published numbers are commensurable, on a posted board not yet read, and on
whether a residence test is actually verified, which are questions that need
documents.

**The tariff that was not yet read has since been read, on 2026-09-08, and it
moved that candidate out of the undetermined cell and into the failing one.** The
guess in the instrument was that the discounted schedule and the standard
schedule are two lines on one filed tariff. The filed tariff is titled LINE-ITEM
DISCOUNT FOR CALIFORNIA ALTERNATE RATES FOR ENERGY (CARE) CUSTOMERS and prints no
per-kWh charge of its own. It prints one multiplier, 35.000 per cent off the
otherwise applicable rate schedule, and a second, 50.000 per cent off the delivery
minimum bill. A price and a published constant that converts it are one price, so
the second question fails. This is the same verdict a discount announced as a
percentage off gets, reached from the opposite direction: here the discounted
figure is filed with a regulator to three decimals, and it is still one price,
because what is filed is a multiplier.

That failure is about prices and says nothing about class values. The same tariff
writes 35.000, 18 and 50.000, and those are class values, filed at a higher
resolution than any transit table this project has read. B57 reads them as a row
and the line separates. One carrier, two questions, two answers, both correct.

**A third candidate failed the same question on the same day, from the hardest
source of the three.** Japan's Health Insurance Act art. 74(1) makes the patient
charge the amount computed for the treatment multiplied by the ratio the relevant
item names, 30 or 20 or 30 per hundred, and the Elderly Medical Care Act art.
67(1) does the same at 10, 20 and 30. The statute prices once, for everyone, and
then writes a ratio per case, so there is no second price. The earlier note on
this candidate guessed the obstacle was that a reimbursement rate and a price are
not commensurable. The statute says the obstacle is the same one the utility
tariff has, and the difference matters: the guess sends the next reader looking
for a health system that posts prices, and the statute says this family does not
post a second price by construction. Those ratios are class values, and B57 reads
them as two rows, at 2 of 3 and 3 of 3.

**The two membership rows were re-read on 2026-09-23, each against one named seller,
and both still fail.** The crossing cost now counts soft resistance as well as fees
and statutes, and a band-one row is asked one more question: can someone else cross
for you. For both sellers the seller's own terms answer yes.

- **Costco (United States).** The card is *"not transferable"* and carries a
  *"recognizable, unobstructed full-face photo"*, but *"Only Costco members may
  purchase items"* in the warehouse, and online a non-member pays *"a 5% surcharge
  over posted prices for members"*. That is one price and a published constant, so
  the second question fails. The goods pass: the terms provide for merchandise
  *"purchased for resale"* with a resale licence on file, and Shop Cards let
  non-members buy.
- **Safeway forU.** Member prices need *"your forU account number at checkout or
  the phone number you used when registering"*; the program *"is a free customer
  loyalty program"* with *"No purchase ... required"*; and the terms provide for
  someone else's use: *"If a Program Member's account number is used by any other
  person, all Points relating to purchases made by such other person will be
  credited to the Program Member's account."* Whether both prices are shown at the
  shelf is not in the terms, so that answer stays unchecked; the failure rests on
  the two checked answers.

Counts unchanged: 12 carry, 0 undetermined, 7 fail. B54-4 was one cell wider than
its rule: it counted a failing row as a leak whenever the row carried any unchecked
cell, including cells the failure does not rest on. It now counts a verdict as leaked
only when it rests on an unchecked or unknown cell. No row had such a cell before, so
no reading moved; with a verdict function that ignores the checked flag, the new form
flags a seeded unchecked yes and a seeded unchecked no.

## B55 — a fee schedule where 104 cells carry 45 figures

Criteria are written into the script that produces the record, the record
carries their wording, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

Virginia's hunting and fishing licence fees, `4 Va. Admin. Code 15-20-65`, taken
from the state code, one section at a time, with every row carrying the
sub-heading it was read under. The class lines are drawn by the legislature in
`Code of Virginia 29.1-319`; the Board sets the figures. Amounts are exact to the
cent, so no rounding turns two different figures into one.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B55-1** every priced row an exact cent amount, the premise that makes the collisions exact | 104 priced rows, 0 inexact | PASS · `premise` |
| **B55-2** cells, distinct figures and collisions satisfy collisions = cells − figures | 104 cells, 45 figures, 59 collisions | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B55-3** the residency line counted on its own, across pairable activity, age and term cells | 41 pairs, 1 carrying the same figure on both sides | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **B55-4** every row carries its sub-heading | 106 rows, 0 without one, 9 sub-headings | PASS · `bookkeeping` |

The largest single block of the difference has a name: one lifetime age ladder,
265 / 215 / 165 / 115 / 65 / 25, is reused across hunting, freshwater fishing and
trout, so eighteen cells carry six figures.

Read in the direction that can fail: forty-five figures means the programme wrote
forty-five distinct class values on classes that have members. That reading fails
when the figure count exceeds the number of bands the text writes, which would
say a class line was drawn outside the text or a band was left to discretion.
This run does not exceed it.

Comparing corpora by their collision rate does not hold, and the station says so:
the rate moves with how fine a granularity the pricing party chose, which is a
property of that party. The quantity that does carry across carriers is per line
rather than per table, whether drawing a class line separates any pair of cells
that would otherwise carry the same figure. On this schedule the residency line
separates 40 of 41 pairable cells.

Read 2026-09-13. That pair list stood at 26 until B57 added a coverage check
which walks the schedule and prints every fee row whose figure no pair uses.
Thirty-one rows came back, and fifteen of them were the resident side of the
lifetime age ladder above: 45-50, 51-55, 56-60, 61-64 and 65 and over, on each of
hunting, freshwater fishing and stocked trout, standing against one non-resident
lifetime licence that carries no age band at all. Whether those count as pairable
is a reading and not an arithmetic fact, and this station reads them as pairs,
since the age bands exist on one side of the line only and that is part of what
the line does. The remaining sixteen rows have no counterpart at all and B57-3b
names every one: multi-year terms, a senior annual licence, a combined sportsman
licence, and several non-resident lines with nothing resident opposite them.

## B56 — three named class lines, and the schedules that write fewer figures

Criteria are written into the script that produces the record, the record
carries their wording, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

Two carriers where the class line is nationality or age and the entitlement is
checked at the gate: monument admission in India, and the reduced transit fare
that `49 U.S.C. 5307(c)(1)(D)` conditions federal assistance on. The federal
condition names three classes, people 65 and over, people with a disability and
Medicare cardholders, and caps their off-peak fare at half the peak fare. It does
not require the three to pay the same as each other.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B56-1** every figure an exact integer in the smallest currency unit | 2 carriers, 10 amounts, 0 inexact | PASS · `premise` |
| **B56-2** collapse = lines named − distinct figures, split into the eligibility step and the pricing step | monuments 3 → 2, collapse 1 at pricing; transit 3 → 1, collapse 1 at each step | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B56-3** the two steps recorded separately | both recorded for both carriers | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B56-4** every carrier names its instrument and its retrieval | 2 carriers, 0 without provenance | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B56-5** the rival's point prediction, that a seller which has paid to sort gives each sorted block its own price, so figures equal blocks | 3 operators read, **0 hit it**; Boston 11 blocks → 3 figures, Maryland 4 → 2, New York 4 → 2 | PASS · `rival` |
| **B56-6** the same pair of segments, drawn and credentialed by two operators under the same federal condition, gets the same verdict | Boston merges school students with seniors, Maryland prices them apart; 3 nominal pairs, **1 independent** | PASS · `own_reading` |

**Where the line is drawn and where it is used are two steps.** On the current
Agra schedule the SAARC and BIMSTEC line is checked at every counter and carries
its own figure at two monuments of eight on a weekday and none of seven on a
Friday. The same operator, the same day, the same line: used in one place and
empty in another.

**The rival, and why it has standing here.** Third-degree price discrimination
asks for market power, sorting by elasticity, and blocked resale. All three hold
on a transit network without argument: the operator is a price maker on its own
lines, it issues a distinct photo credential per class and checks it at the
farebox, and the credential is not transferable. The sorting cost is paid in
full. Its point prediction is not that every named line carries its own figure,
since it is silent where elasticities coincide. The half that can be read without
measuring an elasticity is that elasticity belongs to the rider rather than to
the operator, so one pair of segments cannot be merged in one city and priced
apart in another. Boston merges school students with seniors, its page saying
that all reduced fares are the same whichever card is held; Maryland prints
Student as its own column at 1.50 against 1.00 for senior and disability and 2.00
full. The federal condition says nothing about students.

The reading that the cost of issuing one card rather than three explains the
merge is closed by the same page: Boston conditions on which card is held on
another good, admitting the senior and income-eligible cards to a reduced RIDE
fare and not the disability, Medicare or student cards. The merge on the fare
table is a choice and not a limit of the farebox.

What is registered is that the rival's point prediction does not hold on the
three operators read and that its remaining route out, an elasticity ordering
that reverses between cities, has not been measured. That is not the same
statement as the rival being wrong, and it is not the same statement as neither
side being decidable.

**Reading the criteria.** They do not all ask the same kind of question, so they
do not add. Four of the six ask whether this run's instrument and its inputs are
sound; one asks what this station's own registered reading says; one asks whether
a rival's point prediction holds. Only the last of those bears on the framework.

## B57 — whether drawing a class line separates anything

Criteria are written into the script that produces the record, the record
carries their wording, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

The counting law with the word distinct in it is an identity: what a published
programme produces is the number of distinct class values it writes. Nothing is
learned by scoring an identity. The quantity that can fail sits one level down
and is per line rather than per table. A programme's cells are indexed by a
class-line value and a context, where the context is every other attribute the
cell is indexed by. Two cells that share a context and differ in the line value
form a pairable pair, and the line separates that pair when the two values
differ. The use rate is separated over pairable.

It is comparable across carriers where a collision rate is not. A collision rate
moves with how fine a granularity the pricing party chose, which is a property of
that party; the use rate is a proportion, per line, and moves with neither the
cell count nor the precision the values are written to. It asks whether the edge
exists.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B57-1** the general pairing rule reproduces the hand pairing B55 reported on the same table | B55's own pair list gives 41 pairs with 1 carrying the same value; the rule returns **41 and 1** | PASS · `known_answer` |
| **B57-2** separated plus same-value equals pairable, in every row | 24 rows, 0 violations | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B57-3** every recomputed cell an exact integer in the unit its own source files: the smallest currency unit for a fare, thousandths of one per cent for a filed discount | **324 cells walked**, 0 inexact, 3 carrying no published number because a rule forbids the line | PASS · `premise` |
| **B57-3b** print the coverage of the pairing: how many rows the fee schedule has, how many distinct resident figures the registered pairs use, and every row whose figure no pair uses | 106 rows, 41 pairs using 18 distinct resident figures, **16 rows uncovered and each named** | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B57-4** print the object: per row and per line-pair, pairable, separated, rate, and the contexts where the line separates nothing | 24 rows printed, every pair broken out | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **B57-5** every row names its source and whether it was recomputed from cells on disk or carried | 24 rows, 23 recomputed, 1 carried, 0 without provenance | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B57-6** the rival's point prediction, that a line drawn and credentialed separates somewhere, so the rate is above zero | 23 non-degenerate rows read, **six return zero** | PASS · `rival` |
| **B57-7** every row names the partition the source itself draws, which its line values are taken from | 24 rows, 0 without one | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B57-8** a row whose table has absent cells reports them rather than dropping them in silence, since an absent cell is a reachability fact and not a rate | one row has an incomplete table: 9 of 15 cells present, 6 absent, each named | PASS · `bookkeeping` |
| **B57-9** every row says whether its partition's own label already fixes the value, and a row where it does is excluded from the rival reading | 24 rows, 0 without the field; **one degenerate** | PASS · `instrument` |

**The family does not fix the rate; the pair does, and one row shows it inside
itself.** On the monument schedule, one operator, one table, one nationality
partition: Indian against other foreign nationals separates 15 of 15, SAARC and
BIMSTEC against other foreign nationals separates 15 of 15, and **Indian against
SAARC separates 2 of 15**. Averaging those to the row's 71.11 % produces a figure
that denotes nothing. The comparable unit is the pair of line values, not the
row and not the family. The thirteen contexts where that line separates nothing
are named in the record.

**The set the line values are drawn from has to be one the source names, and
that clause was added before the sixth row was built rather than found in a
later audit.** Whether a child line counts as used depends entirely on what it
is paired against: against the paying classes it separates every time, and
inside the free list, where every entry is zero, it separates never. Both are
true and neither is the reading, because neither set is a partition the page
draws. What the page draws is the free list, and inside it the child line does
nothing. Criterion B57-7 checks every row records the named partition it takes
its line values from. A use rate whose partition is not named is not a reading,
because whoever chose the set chose the answer.

**The sharpest case for that clause is one operator's own table read twice.**
The three classes the statute names sit inside a single column headed
Senior/Disability on that operator's published table, and read 0.00 per cent. The
column headers of the same table, less a paratransit column that is not the same
commodity, read 100.00 per cent. Same operator, same table, two partitions, both
named by a source, and the two readings sit at opposite ends of the range. The
difference is real rather than a choice: the statute names disability and
Medicare separately and the table combines them. Without naming the partition,
that table can be reported at zero or at one and both figures are true.

**An absent cell is not a zero and not an agreement.** That table prints 9 of 15
possible cells: no student price on the day, weekly or monthly pass, no senior
price on the weekly pass or the student season pass. Dropping such a context from
the pairing is right, since there is no pair to read, but dropping it in silence
is not: a class that cannot reach a product at all is a reachability fact, which
is the first question of the square screen and a different object from a rate.
The two ways a line can do nothing are kept apart on the record — both cells
present and equal, which costs the rate a numerator, against the other cell not
existing, which does not enter the rate.

**A partition whose own label already fixes the value is degenerate, and its
rate reads the label back rather than the cells.** A heading reading Free Fare
Eligibility fixes the value at zero, so every entry under it carries zero by
construction; a heading reading Riders Eligible for Reduced Fares does not fix
which reduced fare, and another operator's table prints three different reduced
columns under the same idea; a statute that caps a fare at half the peak fare
does not fix it either, and says nothing about the three classes paying the same
as each other. Criterion B57-9 records the answer and its reason for every row
and keeps a degenerate row out of the rival reading. This is the degenerate
square of the square screen in another setting: a zero the construction forces
carries no claim.

**One operator's own page settles the degeneracy question by printing four
different figures under one heading.** A third operator was read on 2026-09-08
because its published price page gives an income-qualified class its own figure
beside the others, which is what the income line needed: at the two operators
already read it sits in two separate tables, and two tables are not a partition
any one source draws. Under the heading Types of fares that page prints 300, 100,
0 and 175, so no argument is needed about whether the label permits different
values. Two entries are excluded under the one-commodity question with the reason
recorded, a paratransit service and an annual pass.

Broken out pair by pair, that row says something narrower than its 70 per cent.
Every pair involving the adult class separates, four of four. Every pair involving
the youth class separates, three of three. **Every pair inside the reduced block
is identical: senior against disability, senior against income-qualified,
disability against income-qualified.** The operator distinguishes adult, reduced
and youth, and inside reduced it draws three lines with three eligibility tests
and three credentials that produce one figure.

**Across the four operators now read, the merging is not indiscriminate, and the
narrower statement is the one worth registering.** Three of the four price a young
class apart from the reduced block, at 150 against 100, at 0 against 100 and at 0
against 135. **None of the four separates within senior, disability, Medicare and
income-qualified.** That is a much narrower claim than operators merging
everything, and one operator read can still end it.

**The fourth operator was chosen because it looked most likely to end it**, since
it runs a separately branded income programme alongside a separate senior and
disability programme. It confirms instead, and its own footnote is the plainest
statement of the merge in the corpus: discount fares apply to seniors 65 and over,
individuals with disabilities, Medicare recipients, and customers enrolled in the
income programme. Four classes in one sentence, one column, proof of eligibility
required for each, and the page presents the consolidation as policy.

**The closest thing to a refutation is on the same page and is reported rather
than smoothed.** On that operator's paratransit service the income line does
separate from the disability line, 450 against 225 for a one-way trip: an
income-qualified rider with a disability pays half what a rider with a disability
pays. Paratransit fails the one-commodity question of the carrier screen, and that
question was fixed long before this page was read, so it does not enter the row.
The statement therefore stands on the commodity the screen admits, and the single
place the income line separates is a commodity the screen excludes. **That is
worth more than a clean confirmation, because it says where to look next.**

**Half of that question is settled by reading the rule rather than more tables.**
49 CFR 37.131(c) caps a paratransit fare at twice the fare charged to someone
paying full fare, and the regulation puts the decisive words in a parenthesis:
without regard to discounts. The ceiling is therefore one number for every
paratransit rider and blind to every discount class, so it can neither require nor
forbid a split among them. **The split that operator makes on paratransit is its
own and not a rule following through.** Checking the corpus against the ceiling
tests the reading and the fares together: four paratransit fares on disk, none
over, sitting between 0.292 and 0.818 of their own ceilings. It also disposes of
an observation left open earlier, that one operator's paratransit fare sits above
its full fare, which breaks nothing because the ceiling is twice and that fare is
at 0.550 of it.

**The two products sit under different rule sets, and that is structural.** On
fixed route a federal grant condition names three classes and caps their off-peak
fare; on paratransit the only federal rule is a ceiling that does not mention
classes at all. One consequence for scope: the row built on the statute's
partition has no paratransit counterpart, because that partition does not reach
there, so this corpus cannot put the same question to both products.

**The other half is why that operator chose opposite ways, and it is not answered
here.** That is a question about purpose, and purpose has no independent indicator
in a fare table, so reading it off the pricing would take the thing to be
explained as the explanation. One structural account was drafted and this corpus
refuted it immediately: that a discount block, once it exists, absorbs new classes
without producing a new value, while its absence forces one. A second operator
has such a block and still gave students a column of their own. The account is
recorded as refuted so that it is not drafted again. Settling the question needs
that operator's own rate filing or board papers, which is a document rather than a
measurement, and it has not been fetched.

**Four named partitions return zero, across fifty-four pairs**, and in both the label
permitted other values. The three classes one sentence of the statute names, read
across three operators and six goods; the four entries under one operator's
reduced-fare heading; and the income-qualified class against the senior class at
the two operators that price both. The lists are not the same, since the statute
names disability and Medicare separately and the operator's list combines them.

Before that clause was added this read as three partitions and fifty pairs. The
third row was the free list, and its zero was in its heading. The clause was
added by auditing this station's own rows the day after they were built, and the
audit is why the count moved. What it also removed was an apparent pattern:
before it, every row that read zero was a list of who qualifies and every row
that read high was the columns of a price table, which looked like a finding.
Half of that was the degenerate label. **The half that survives is the sharper
one: where the label permitted several values, three operators chose the same
one.**

**The row that returns zero on the statute's own list.** `49 U.S.C. 5307(c)(1)(D)` names three classes,
people 65 and over, people with a disability, and Medicare cardholders. Three
operators each issue a distinct credential per class and check it at the farebox,
so the sorting cost is paid in full, and across three operators and six goods
every one of the eighteen pairs carries the same value. Eighteen nominal pairs,
**three independent facts**, one per operator.

What is registered is that the rival's point prediction does not hold on that
row. It is not that third-degree price discrimination is refuted: three operators
is three, and a route out that has not been measured is recorded alongside.

**The self-check is what this station bought.** The use rate was proposed with a
limitation attached, that it does not move with value granularity but does move
with which two cells count as pairable, and that the pairings were written by
five separate hands. This station writes the rule once as a function, applies it
to every row, and puts it against the pairing B55 had done by hand on the same
table. Both integers come back identical.

**The twelfth row is a different family, and it is here to block a
generalisation.** Every row above that reads an income line reads zero: income
against senior across three operators, and a fourth operator's income programme
against its own Medicare, disability and senior lines. Eleven rows of that would
support a sentence about income lines. The twelfth is a tariff filed with a
regulator rather than a fare table, and its two filed income schedules take
different values, so the sentence does not survive. **One counterexample is what
that costs, and the reason to spend it is that this station has already had to
correct a family-level generalisation once.**

Two more rows arrived the same day on the age axis, which had read zero
everywhere until then, and they came from two statutes. One of them writes the
merge itself: its first case, a patient under 70, and its third, a patient over
70 whose income reaches a cabinet-order amount, both take 30 per hundred, so
crossing the income threshold after 70 returns the patient exactly to the ratio
of someone under 70. An age line and an income line meeting on one number, inside
one article. What is registered is that the two are equal, not why.

The utility row arrives with two contexts and so restates the correction inside a
single document. On bundled volumetric charges the two schedules file 35.000 and 18 per
cent, and the line separates. On the delivery minimum bill they file 50 and 50,
and it does not. The merge this station keeps reading in transit tables happens
here too, one line item away from a split made by the same two classes. **The
family does not fix the rate and neither does the row.**

That carrier fails B54's question about two posted prices, because what is filed
is a multiplier and a price with a published constant that converts it is one
price. That is a fact about prices. This row counts class values, and the
programme wrote 35.000, 18 and 50.000. One carrier, two questions, two answers,
and both hold.

**Three further rows, read the same day, close off the two cheapest explanations
of the zeros.** The age line reads 0 of 18, 0 of 12, 0 of 18 and 0 of 6 at four
transit operators, and every one of those rows is in the public service pricing
family. A municipal pool in that same family publishes an admission table whose
three columns are Resident, Corporate and Guest and whose three rows are Youth,
Adult and Senior, and both partitions separate all nine of their pairs. So the
zeros are not produced by the line being an age line, and they are not produced
by the seller being a public operator. The two statutes make that point from
outside the family; this makes it from inside, on a table of the same shape as a
fare table.

What survives as a candidate is the federal grant condition that names the three
classes together, which is what the row on that condition already records. It is
a candidate and not a finding, because two of the transit merges also swallow
classes the condition does not name, a student line and an income line. What is
registered is the narrowing: neither the family nor the axis explains those zeros.

That pool's table also gives the second instance of one table read under two
partitions. The first was a transit table whose two named partitions read 100 and
0 per cent, at opposite ends of the range. These two read 9 of 9 and 9 of 9. The
two instances together say the reading follows the partition rather than the
table, which is stronger than either alone.

The city rental schedule that came with them reads 7 of 11, and it carries a
choice this project declines to make for the reader. Six further items on the
same schedule are printed with a single fee column, so every buyer pays the same
and the line is not drawn there at all. Counting those as contexts where the line
separates nothing gives 7 of 17. Both figures are in the record, and the rate
reported is the one over the rows the page itself prints in two columns.

**Two cinemas were read to answer the one objection the four zeros cannot answer
themselves.** Every zero row is a public transit operator and three of them take
a federal grant whose condition names three classes together, so a defender of
third-degree price discrimination can say those operators are not maximising
profit and are following a grant condition. That objection is fair and it needs a
seller outside that regime. A cinema is the textbook's own canonical example of
third-degree price discrimination, and the three conditions the standard survey
states are met: market power over a showing, direct segmentation by asking for ID
at the box office, and no arbitrage, since a ticket cannot be resold into another
showing.

One cinema's published price page prints Adults at 14.00 and then Senior Citizens
age 65 and over with ID, Children, Students with valid student ID, and Federally
Disabled with valid ID, all four at 10.00. Three separate verification routes are
maintained and they produce one number. The other prints Adults at 14.00 and one
further row reading Seniors, College Students, Children at 13.00, while the same
page prices Senior Wednesdays at 7.00 and College Tuesdays at 8.00, so separate
values are demonstrably available to that operator for the same two labels.
Neither cinema's tax status was read. What is load-bearing is that no grant
condition and no statute groups these classes.

**Those rows hold the rival's prediction at the row grain while containing a block
of pairs that read zero, which is why the same prediction is now also read per
pair.** The row rates are 40 and 50 per cent, and inside them six pairs and three
pairs separate nothing. This station had already ruled, before those rows existed,
that the comparable unit is the line-value pair rather than the row. Read at that
grain: 64 pairs across the non-degenerate rows, 29 of which separate nothing, and
they no longer sit inside one family. Nine are at the two cinemas, seventeen at
five transit operators, one inside a statute. Changing the grain changes no
reading, since both grains are computed by the same function; the two criteria are
the same prediction at two resolutions and both are kept.

The pair grain also surfaces two things the row grain hid. One transit row reading
70 per cent contains three pairs that separate nothing, disability against income,
disability against senior, and income against senior. One statutory row reading
66.67 per cent contains the pair where a patient under 70 and a patient over 70
above the income threshold both pay 30 per hundred.

What a defender can still say is that the segmentation is two-way, full price
against discount, and that the four categories are four eligibility routes into
one segment rather than four segments. That splits into two branches and neither
requires reading anyone's motive. If they are segments, the rival predicts
different prices and the reading is one number. If they are not segments, the
rival's theory says nothing about why they exist or why each is separately
verified.

**A twentieth row settles something the earlier rows only asserted in prose: a
line that separates is not the same object as a line that files a multiplier.**
Two state park systems post camping fees under column headers reading RESIDENT
and NON-RESIDENT, sixteen sites between them, and all sixteen separate. The ratio
is not constant: one system runs from 1.40 to 1.67 and the other from 1.50 to
2.00. So these are sixteen separately set prices rather than one base with a
published constant on top, which is what the utility tariff and the two statutes
are, and what makes those one price rather than two. The contrast had been stated
in words and no single row had put both sides on the page.

Read down the residence axis the four rows on it run 100.00, 100.00, 97.56 and
63.64 per cent across four families. There is no family-level answer on that axis
either.

**The last defence those zeros face is cost, and it is now answered from the
sellers' own pages rather than argued.** The defence is that segmenting more
finely is not worth paying for. One transit operator's reduced-fare page issues
four separate credentials for its four classes: a Senior CharlieCard, a
Transportation Access Pass for disability and Medicare, an S-Card or M7 Card for
students, and a reduced fare card for income-eligible riders aged 18 to 64. Four
applications, four sets of eligibility documents, one number: $1.10 on the subway
and $0.85 on the bus. A second operator runs four programmes with four separate
applications, one of them verified through the state benefits website, and prints
one discount of fifty per cent. **The sorting was not skipped. It was bought four
times, and the step the seller declined to take is a line in a fare table.**

Five operators have now been read. Of the 29 zero pairs, **18 are separately
credentialed on the seller's own page**, 1 shares one credential, 3 are mixed
across the operators their row spans, and 7 are not read.

**The hardest single instance is one operator's disability card.** Its
application must be filled out by the applicant and the applicant's health care
professional, takes up to two weeks to review, and ends with the rider coming in
to be photographed. The fare it buys is the one a senior at the same operator gets
by showing a motor vehicle administration photo card, and the one a Medicare
holder gets by showing a Medicare card. Three verification routes of wildly
different cost, one number.

**One pair goes the other way, and that is where this framework explains a zero the
rival cannot.** At one operator Medicare recipients are served through the
disabilities card. One credential, so there is no point of sale at which those two
classes can be told apart, and the shared value is forced rather than chosen. The
general statement is that the number of distinct class values is bounded by the
number of separately issuable credentials, and that the bound sits on the issuing
side rather than the buying side. It binds on one pair here and is slack on
eighteen.

Read again 2026-09-13. A second pair sat in that cell until this round, a single
Regional Reduced Fare Permit at a third operator, which that operator's own page
describes as one application covering senior riders, riders with disabilities and
Medicare holders alike. The fare system the permit is loaded onto lists two named
card types under Card type, Senior and Disability, each with its own eligibility
documents, and both take the same $1.00 fare. What this criterion asks is whether
the seller can tell the two classes apart where the price is set, and two named
card types in the fare system is that. The pair therefore moves from forced to
chosen. The correction costs one mechanical account and buys back an instance of
what the station counts, a seller that can tell two classes apart, checks two sets
of documents, and writes them the same number.

**The mixed state is the sharpest reading of the three.** The three classes a
federal grant condition names together are separately credentialed at two
operators and share one card at a third, and all three operators write one value.
So the merge has two different causes, and only one of them is mechanical. The
rival gives both cases the same sentence. This framework gives two and says which
operator is which.

What is not written is that public operators tend to merge. Two of the five cannot
tell the classes apart at all, and the three that can merged the classes they
could have separated. Those are two findings and running them together loses the
half that carries.

The criterion can fail, and how it fails is worth stating: had the merging
operators turned out to issue one card each, the cost defence would stand and
every zero would have a mechanical account. One pair is that way. Eighteen are
not. What is read is that the machinery for telling the classes apart is built
and the output is one number; no intent is inferred from that.

**A zero of a third kind turned up on 2026-09-08, and it is the one neither
account owns.** A national health ministry publishes hospital subsidy by ward class
and residency status, three columns, five rows, and all fifteen pairs separate. The
same announcement then says emergency department fees will not discriminate between
nationality or citizenship. **A published rule bans the line in one context while
the same document draws it in five others.** Until then every zero here came from
one of two places: the seller could have written two numbers and wrote one, or its
credentials gave it no place to tell the classes apart. This is neither. The
subject of that sentence is not the seller.

Those three pairs are outside the rival's reach and the screening station puts them
there, alongside the statutory row: a prediction about how a profit-maximising firm
prices has no referent where a ministry is forbidden to price at all. What they
enter instead is the count of how a zero can arise, which is this framework's
question rather than the rival's.

The cells of that row are not figures. What was read is that they are equal; their
shared level is not on that page, so they carry a marker and the row is held out of
the exact-integer premise for that reason. This quantity uses only equality and
inequality between cells and never their level, so nothing turns on it.

**Reading the criteria.** They do not all ask the same kind of question, so they
do not add. Four ask whether this run's instrument and inputs are sound, one asks
what this station's own registered reading says, and three ask whether a rival's
prediction or defence holds. Only the last three bear on the framework.

## B58 — whether the rival's own conditions hold where this project scored it

Criteria are written into the script that produces the record, the record
carries their wording, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

B56 and B57 score third-degree price discrimination against published class
tables. Neither checks what the rival itself says has to be true before it
applies. The standard survey states three: the firm has short-run market power,
consumers can be segmented directly or indirectly, and arbitrage across
differently priced goods is infeasible. This station runs that screen over every
carrier that contributes a zero pair to B57-11, and it was built so that it could
subtract.

**The rival needs a fourth thing that is not on its own list.** The inverse
elasticity rule is a first-order condition of profit maximisation, and the cost
argument B57 scores is a profit argument. Separating that fourth requirement from
the three feasibility conditions is the one structural act here; the rest is
bookkeeping.

| criterion | reading | |
|---|---|---|
| **B58-1** every element of the rival's construction carries the source it was read from | 13 elements, 0 without a source | PASS · `premise` |
| **B58-2** the cell to verdict map is written out, and an unchecked or unestablished feasibility answer never lands on an admitting verdict | 7 cells printed, 0 leaks; 2 carriers still carry an unchecked answer, both named | PASS · `instrument` |
| **B58-3** print the object: every carrier, its four answers, whether each stands on a document, and its verdict | 8 carriers printed | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **B58-4** B57-11's zero pairs partitioned by whether the rival's own conditions admit the carrier | **39 pairs: 7 admissible, 19 objective contested, 9 objective open, 4 inadmissible** | PASS · `own_reading` |
| **B58-5** coverage: which parts of the rival carry a reading and which carry none | 13 elements, **first and second degree carry no reading at all** | PASS · `bookkeeping` |

**The reading.**

| | zero pairs | what the screen says |
|---|---:|---|
| five transit rows | **19** | the three feasibility conditions hold and are checked, and a named document constrains the seller's objective: the federal grant condition names the three classes together and caps the reduced fare at half the peak fare |
| two cinema rows | **9** | the three hold and are checked, and no document speaks to the seller's objective either way |
| one statutory row | **1** | **inadmissible.** The seller is a statute. There is no firm, and it does not maximise profit, so the rival's prediction has no referent there |

**One pair comes out of the count, and it should.** The earlier reading carried
29 across three families, and one of those rested on an article of a health
insurance act. A prediction about how a profit-maximising firm prices has no
purchase on a statute.

**And one pair now sits in the cell where all four conditions hold.** The Marcus
Corporation, NYSE: MCS, announced in its own release that moviegoers 11 years old
and under and 60 and over may buy tickets for $7 for all shows before 4 p.m. Two
named age classes, one number, from the seller. Its objective stands on a release
filed with the SEC: it identifies itself by exchange and ticker, reports total
revenues, Adjusted EBITDA and net earnings per diluted common share, and
management states it is focused on driving performance at every level. That is
the weakest of the four answers on that carrier and the record says so: no filing
states an objective of maximising profit, and the Business and Strategy sections
of the 10-K read carry no objective sentence at all. What is recorded is the
closest readable thing to the rival's own assumption, not the assumption itself.

**A second carrier joined the admissible cell the same day, and its document is
harder than an exchange listing.** A national rail carrier publishes six named
classes with a figure on one everyday-discounts page: children two through twelve
at 50 per cent, students seventeen to twenty-four at 15, and seniors, active duty
military with their dependents, veterans, and members of a passengers'
association all at 10. Nine of the fifteen pairs separate; the six among the four
tens separate nothing. **One of those four is a membership a rider buys**, so on
that figure the class value tracks nothing about the person at all. What is
recorded is that reading and not a reason for it.

Its objective is a statutory command rather than an inference: 49 U.S.C.
24301(a)(2) says the carrier shall be operated and managed as a for-profit
corporation, and (a)(3) says it is not a department, agency, or instrumentality of
the United States Government. The section imposes no route or service obligation
and subsection (g) preempts state law on rates, routes and service. What was not
looked at is whether any appropriations legislation attaches fare conditions to
these classes, and that is named as a gap.

**So the number to carry depends on which question is asked.** Seven pairs have
all four conditions. Sixteen have no document against the objective. Nineteen have
a named document constraining it. One is inadmissible. A single headline figure
across those is what the screening station exists to prevent.

Three sellers were checked the same day and found not to be carriers of this kind
at all, and that is recorded so the next reader does not retry them: a single
large venue, a listed cinema chain, and a listed ski operator all price by date
through a booking flow and publish no static table of class prices.

**Market power and absence of arbitrage are granted on the rival's own
classification rather than established from a document, and that is recorded as
what it is.** The rival's definition of third degree is pricing based on limited
observed characteristics, naming age and student status among them, so a seller
posting senior, student and child prices is an instance of that definition. A
defender who denies market power at these sellers denies that this is price
discrimination, which removes the carriers from the rival's domain and removes
its claim to account for why the classes exist. Segmentation is checked per
carrier from the published pages.

**An unchecked yes on a feasibility condition does not buy admissibility, and the
direction is why.** A carrier is admissible only where the rival's conditions
hold, so asserting that they hold is this project writing itself strong. The rule
is in the verdict function rather than in prose, and B58-2 checks it.

**What this station does not do is re-judge anything.** B56-5, B57-6 and B57-11
keep their verdicts. What it adds is that a headline count cannot be carried
without the screen behind it.

**Two parts of the rival carry no reading at all**, and naming them is the least
visible and most useful thing here: first-degree price discrimination has none,
and second-degree has its premises located to source without a single quantity
scored against it. Two cells of the verdict map are reachable and empty this run,
and the one that matters needs a document stating a cinema's objective.

### B58 second arm — the second degree, scored on fifty-three published tariff schedules

`53 national residential schedules` `nothing bought` `read from a record already on disk`

**The station's own coverage criterion had recorded the second degree as premises
located to source with no quantity scored. This arm scores one.**

Two of the four located premises can be read off a published schedule. `v` taking
only `(q, theta)` says the optimal tariff is a function of quantity alone. Single
crossing plus optimality says the marginal charge falls with quantity. **The second
one needs profit maximisation, which this station already separated out for the
third degree because it is not in the rival's own feasibility list**, so the
direction is printed as an object and not scored, and the per-schedule objective is
registered as not done.

**B58-10, the rival's point prediction that a residential tariff prices quantity and
nothing else: 7 of 53 schedules price a second argument, by the survey's own type
label.** Three IBT/TOU (Iran, Mongolia, Pakistan), two Linear/TOU (Guatemala,
Turkey), two voltage-dependent (China, Nigeria). Quantity-only 39, unresolved 7.
**The unresolved seven are labelled "Multiple" and the survey does not say what it
multiplies over**, so they score for neither side.

**Both outcomes were reachable.** The survey's own vocabulary carries pure IBT and
pure Linear, which are quantity-only, and those are thirty-nine of the fifty-three.

**Grid B, and the two readings are stated apart.** The counting law indexes values
by whatever the programme writes down, so a time band or a voltage level is a class
line it counts; that reading is scored separately in the TB- family, 179 blocks and
156 distinct values. The rival's reading is that there is no such argument. On seven
schedules the rival's does not hold and ours does.

**Scope.** The located premises are the one-dimensional model, and these schedules
were measured to lie outside it, so the premise is false on the ground measured
rather than silent about it. Rochet-Chone 1998 records that the one-dimensional
two-step solution fails outside one dimension, because `one does not know the
direction of the (local) incentive compatibility constraints that will be binding`.

**B58-9, the direction, printed and not scored:** increasing 39, single block 11,
flat 2, non-monotone 1, **decreasing 0**. **The survey's label and its own printed
charges disagree on one schedule and it is printed:** Australia is labelled DBT, a
decreasing block tariff, and prints `0.26 / 0.26 / 0.26`, which is flat.

|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | B58-6 the four premises carry their source and profit maximisation is listed apart | premise | all four verbatim from MIT 14.271 lec3; the fifth is not among Stole ch.34's three |
| PASS | B58-7 every cell maps to a named outcome and the unresolved cell maps to no verdict | instrument | three values, only two enter B58-10 |
| PASS | B58-8 print the object | own_reading | 53 schedules printed whole, 1 label-versus-charges disagreement printed |
| PASS | B58-9 print the direction and do not score it without the objective | own_reading | increasing 39, decreasing 0; the objective partition is registered as not done |
