## B59 — the class line on reserve balances, and what the excluded class recovers

The gross gap is read off a rule and needs no data. 12 CFR 204.2(y) is a closed
list of four kinds of eligible institution and a Federal Home Loan Bank is not
among them, so an FHLB's balance at a Federal Reserve Bank is unremunerated while
an eligible institution's earns IORB. Same obligor, same instrument, same
continuous availability, no collateral either way, no maturity either way: only
the holder differs, and the weight differs by the whole policy rate.

The excluded class does not exit, it routes, lending federal funds at EFFR. What
is measured here is the second half, the net gap, and it does not adjudicate a
scalar price field on positions: a Fed balance and a fed funds loan are different
positions with different obligors. It adjudicates a narrower and named
expectation, that interest on reserves would floor money market rates.

Integer basis points throughout. Both series publish on a 1 bp grid, so that is
the resolution floor, and a day whose gap sits at or inside it is mapped to no
verdict rather than to a sign. IOER and IORB are different definitional bases and
never share a column.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`instrument` 1 pass · `known_answer` 2 pass · `rival` 1 pass 1 no verdict · `own_reading` 2 pass

| | criterion | detail |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B59-1 `instrument` both administered series parse and align to EFFR, and a blank cell is skipped rather than read as a zero | IORB era 1,281 paired days, IOER era 3,217; blank rows skipped IORB 0, IOER 0, EFFR 257 |
| PASS | B59-5 `known_answer` the 2021 redefinition was a rename and not a rate change | IOER 2021-07-28 = 15 bp, IORB 2021-07-29 = 15 bp |
| PASS | B59-6 `known_answer` the run reproduces counts read independently in a browser before the script could reach the endpoint | reproduced, every integer |
| PASS | B59-4-IORB `rival` the stated expectation that interest on reserves would floor money market rates | floor_broken. Above the floor 1,171 days, below it 0, inside the 1 bp floor and mapped to no verdict 110 |
| **no verdict** | B59-4-IOER `rival` the same expectation on the older definitional basis | both_signs, which is a determinate description and not a verdict. Above the floor 2,714, below it 152, inside the floor 351 |
| PASS | B59-3-IORB `own_reading` the net gap printed, no line drawn on it | n 1,281; min 1, q1 7, median 7, q3 7, max 9 bp; 9 distinct values. 2024 reads exactly 7 bp on all 251 days. The 110 days inside the floor are all 2025 and 2026 |
| PASS | B59-3-IOER `own_reading` the net gap printed, no line drawn on it | n 3,217; min −65, q1 5, median 9, q3 13, max 89 bp; 65 distinct values. 171 days exactly zero, in 2009, 2018, 2019 and 2020; 175 strictly negative, of which 162 are 2019 and the three largest are the first fortnight of October 2008 |

**The scope reading.** The price of this barrier is not a constant. It tracks how
abundant reserves are: when they are abundant the excluded class holds a surplus
with nowhere else to put it and pays, and when they are scarce banks bid for
funds and the gap closes or reverses. The zeros and the negatives cluster in the
balance-sheet runoff of 2018 to 2020 and in the first fortnight the mechanism
existed. That is a conditional statement with a mechanism, not an intermittent one.

Data: FRED, `IORB`, `IOER`, `EFFR`, retrieved 2026-09-08.

**The 2026-09-16 rate decision, and a hypothesis written down before its data
exists.** The FOMC raised the target range to 3.75–4.00 percent effective
2026-09-17, its first increase since 2023-07-27. Three quantities move with it
and none of the three is a reading here.

The gross gap, the administered rate against the zero an ineligible holder
earns, goes from 365 to 390 bp. 12 CFR 204.2(y) is unchanged, both classes are
still there, and the count of distinct class values is still three. What moved
is the level of the common field, and the level was never the object: the gross
half is read off the rule, and the rule prints a source, not a number.

The primary credit rate less IORB is still 10 bp. On disk that difference takes
exactly one value, 10.0 bp, on all 1,334 paired days from 2021-06-17, across 17
changes in IORB, 11 of them increases, with single steps as large as 75 bp. This
is the eighteenth such change and the twelfth increase, so it confirms and does
not measure.

IORB less the ON RRP offering rate is still 15 bp, and those are not two prices.
The primary credit rate has sat at the top of the target range since 2020-03-16
and the ON RRP offering rate sits at the bottom, so the difference is
(top − 10) − bottom = 15 by published rule and one subtraction.

What the decision does open is the net gap. Read by month from the series on
disk, IORB − EFFR sits at exactly 7 bp on all 167 days from 2025-01 to 2025-08,
falls through 4 in 2025-10 and 2 in 2025-11, and then sits at 1 bp on all 105
days from 2025-12 to 2026-04, every one of them inside the resolution floor. It
reads 2 bp from 2026-06 to 2026-09-04. The three cuts of 2025-09-18, 2025-10-30
and 2025-12-11 fall inside that collapse, so two accounts of it are observably
the same so far: the scope reading above, registered 2026-09-08, says the gap
tracks how abundant reserves are and not the level, and therefore predicts no
response to this increase; a co-moving account says it tracks the level of the
administered rate, and therefore predicts a return toward 7 bp.

The hypothesis, written before any post-increase day exists: the increase
effective 2026-09-17 does not change IORB − EFFR. Window, the first ten trading
days with an EFFR print from 2026-09-17; statistic, the ten-day median; cells
and the verdict each maps to, with the undetermined cell mapped to no verdict:
median in [1, 3] bp, the scope reading holds and the co-moving account does not;
median at or above 5 bp, the scope reading is withdrawn; median exactly 4, or
fewer than 8 days with a print, no verdict and the window is extended. The band
[1, 3] is the full set of values observed from 2026-05 to 2026-09-04 and the 5 bp
threshold is that band's top plus twice the 1 bp floor; neither is read off a
post-increase run. The two accounts stand 5 bp apart against a 1 bp floor, and
within-regime monthly dispersion on this series is 1 bp, so ten trading days
separate them. Cost is two CSV files and one scan, no resampling and no repeats.
All three outcomes are reachable: 7 bp was the reading before 2025-09, 2 bp is
the reading now, and the older definitional basis printed 152 strictly negative
days.

Board implementation notes, read in full: 2026-03-18 directs the Desk to
`Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of securities ... to maintain
an ample level of reserves`, while 2026-07-29 and 2026-09-16 both read `When
appropriate, increase ...`. The change in that sentence falls between 2026-03-18
and 2026-07-29 and the gap collapsed in 2025-10 to 2025-12, so the two do not
line up and this is recorded, not read. A quantitative reserves series, H.4.1
reserve balances, was not retrieved this round.

**The same hypothesis as a series, because what separates the two accounts is
sign and not sample size.** The three administered-rate moves of 2025-09-18,
2025-10-30 and 2025-12-11 were all cuts and all fall inside the collapse from 7
to 1 bp, so level and gap moved together and the two accounts are not separated
by that stretch. The increase of 2026-09-17 turns the sign once. The projections
published with this decision put the median at one further increase within 2026
and, with the second year below the first, a turn to cuts in 2027, so the family
of events ahead alternates in sign. A gap that tracks the level must rise on an
increase and fall on a cut; a gap that tracks how abundant reserves are does
neither.

Registered before any of those days exist, and stated conditionally because how
many such changes occur is decided by a committee and not by structure: for each
change in IORB effective after 2026-09-17, with E its effective date and d its
signed size in basis points, take the ten trading days with an EFFR print ending
before E and the ten from E, and let the reading be the difference of the two
ten-day medians. Cells, with the undetermined cell mapped to no verdict:
absolute difference at or below 1 bp, the scope reading holds on that event and
the co-moving account does not; same sign as d and at least 5 bp, the scope
reading is withdrawn on that event; opposite sign and at least 5 bp, neither
account predicted it and it opens a line toward a wider reading rather than
counting against either; between 2 and 4 bp, or fewer than 8 days with a print
in either window, no verdict and the numbers are printed. The 1 bp and 5 bp
figures are the ones already stated above and are not read off any later run.
The series closes once there are at least two events of opposite sign, or at
2027-12-31, whichever comes first.

Two features of this reading are worth stating positively. EFFR is a
volume-weighted median of actual overnight transactions and IORB is
administered, so neither prices a future path and guidance about that path
cannot enter an overnight spread; what the projections change is how many events
there are and in what order of sign, not what any one of them reads. And each
change is a single step on a published effective date, `Effective September 17,
2026` in this instance, with the rate moving from one value to another that day
and no stages in between, so a step statistic has the same shape as the
treatment here.

No p-value, no permutation and no standard error are reported: the administered
spread is highly autocorrelated day to day and the count of independent
observations is far below the count of days, so this station prints objects.

## B59, size arm: what banks of each size pay for overnight fed funds, over the balance the expense accrued on

`experiments/b59_size_spread.py`, record `results/b59_size_spread.json`, flagged
`diagnostic_only`: no size class named in rule text is where the gradient that
reads lies (the FDIC's $10 billion line and the banker's bank class, both below),
so no grid is assigned to any reading here. Public bulk Call Report archives, 2009Q1 to 2026Q2; every arm on
the RC-K average starts in 2010, since the one-year product used for 2009 carries
no Schedule RC-K.

**The instrument.** One expense line, `RIAD 4180`, covers fed funds purchased and
repo sold, filed year to date and differenced to a quarter. Schedule RC-K files
the quarter's average of the two liabilities together, `RCFD`/`RCON 3353` (QTLY
AVG OF FED FUNDS PCHD&SEC RP), which is the balance that expense accrued on. An
earlier reading of this arm divided by the quarter-end fed funds balance instead.

**What the quarter-end balance does.** Among filers with no repo at either
quarter end, the median quarter-end balance over the RC-K average is 1.01 in the
largest band and 1.34 in the smallest when fed funds were also carried at the
previous quarter end, and 3.2 to 4.6 in every band when they were not. Those
filers read far under the rate, and they are about half of the smallest band and
a fifth of the largest, which is enough to turn the band comparison around
between rate environments.

| | quarter-end balance | RC-K quarterly average |
|---|---|---|
| slope of yearly median cost on yearly mean EFFR | 0.59 | 0.96 to 1.00, four RC-K arms |
| largest band minus smallest: zero bound, off the floor, 2023-26 | −26, +43, +143 bp | −73, −51, −49 bp |
| 2023-26 band medians against EFFR, largest to smallest | −22, −171, −179, −164 bp | +16, +33, +62, +73 bp |

Standard errors resample filers with all their quarters, not filer-quarters: the
largest band in 2023-26 is 51 filers on the RC-K average and 20 on the first
reading's rows, and one bank's quarters are not independent draws.

**Across arms.** On the RC-K average the largest band's gap to the smallest is
negative in all sixteen cells of four arms by four environments, and the band
medians against EFFR rise with every step down in size in every environment for
three of the arms. Its size depends on who is
in the arm: −23 to −39 bp for filers carrying fed funds at both quarter ends, −46
to −89 bp for filers with none at the previous end, −1 to −30 bp for the small
set whose two quarter-end balances both sit within a quarter of the average.
Dropping the no-repo filter, a least-absolute-deviations fit of cost on the repo
share among filers carrying both liabilities gives a fed funds gap of −54, −54,
−53 and −52 bp, against −59, −65, −49 and −49 bp on the no-repo filers; the fit is
at 5.9 to 8.1 filer standard errors except 2023-26, where its standard error is 58.
The fit's levels inside a band are not read: repo-only filers price 155 to 242
bp under EFFR in 2023-26 with interquartile ranges over 200 bp, which is
customer sweep repo priced by the bank, so the fit's common-repo-price
assumption does not hold off the floor. Its gap is read, and it agrees.

**The FDIC size line.** 12 CFR 327.8 makes an insured institution small below
$10 billion in assets and large at or above it, and moves a filer across only
after four consecutive quarterly reports on the other side; on the RC-K arm that
class differs from the quarter-end side of the line on 54 of 31,485 rows. What the
rule writes on this position is a formula term and not a value per class: the
total rate schedules overlap (2.5 to 18, 4 to 32 and 13 to 32 bp for small
institutions by CAMELS group, 2.5 to 42 bp for large, 12 CFR 327.10, since 2023),
and federal funds purchased and repurchase agreements are named in the large
scorecard's balance sheet liquidity ratio, and for highly complex institutions
in an average short-term funding measure taken from Schedule RC-K, while none of
the seven small-institution ratios names them (12 CFR 327.16 and Appendix A).
Both classes have counted them in the assessment base since 1 April 2011 (76 FR
10672). Read against the data, the step across the line is small and never
resolved, while the step inside the small class is resolved in every era:

| era | 10bn-20bn minus 5bn-10bn | 1bn-5bn minus under 1bn |
|---|---|---|
| 2010Q1-2011Q1 | −0.8 bp (se 9.0) | −43.9 bp (se 7.6) |
| 2011Q2-2015Q4 | −11.7 bp (se 7.1) | −39.6 bp (se 6.8) |
| 2016Q1-2019Q4 | −1.2 bp (se 10.6) | −34.8 bp (se 2.8) |
| 2020Q1-2021Q4 | −2.2 bp (se 13.3) | −53.1 bp (se 8.4) |
| 2022Q1-2026Q2 | −8.8 bp (se 5.9) | −29.8 bp (se 4.6) |

Every step across the line has the sign the large scorecard's extra term points
to. The cells on either side of it hold 5 to 61 filers, and a before-and-after
reading around April 2011 would rest on 5 and 9. The gradient that reads is
among banks one rule treats as one class.

**The Board's own classes.** The 13 to 17 basis points compare the fifteen
largest holders of reserve balances each day with the rest of the FR 2420
domestic panel, November 2015 to March 2017, on rates that pool overnight fed
funds with Eurodollar borrowing. Rebuilt quarter by quarter on the quarter-end
balance due from Federal Reserve Banks (`RCFD`/`RCON 0090`), the larger class
has no filer carrying fed funds with no repo at either quarter end in four of
the six quarters, and one in each of the other two. Pooled, its repo share at quarter
ends has a median of 1.00 and falls below one half on 5 percent of rows, so a
fed funds price for that class is an extrapolation of the repo-weight fit across
most of its range: the fitted gap to the rest is −32 bp with filer standard
errors of 44.5 and 249.0 under two seeds. A bank books Eurodollar borrowing as
deposits in foreign offices, whose interest the archive files as `RIAD4172`,
apart from the `RIAD4180` read here. The Board's comparison is not rebuilt on
this instrument.

**The class rule text names on the lending side.** 12 CFR 327.5(b) lets a
banker's bank exclude from its assessment base the reserve balances it passes
through to the Federal Reserve, those it holds there for its own account and its
fed funds sold, up to its deposits of depository institutions plus its fed funds
purchased, and has it certify each quarter. Schedule RC-O files the
certification (`RCFD`/`RCON K656`, the word true or false in either case), the
deduction (`K657`) and the limit (`K658`) from 2011Q2. 16 filers certify and
deduct in the same quarter, 12 to 15 in any one quarter; 9 more certify in some quarter and never deduct. The class's lending price is
the RC-K arm on the asset leg: the quarter's income on fed funds sold and
reverse repo (`RIAD4020`, INCOME&FEES-FED FUNDS SOLD & SEC PUR) over their
quarterly average (`3365`), with reverse repo absent at both quarter ends. Against
EFFR in basis points, next to the filers outside the class whose assets fall
inside its range that quarter, filer standard error in brackets:

| era | class borrowing | others borrowing | class lending | others lending | class lending minus borrowing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2011Q2-2015Q4 | +4.6 | +65.1 | +51.5 | +12.3 | +47.2 (17.5) |
| 2016Q1-2019Q4 | +2.2 | +55.2 | +48.3 | +6.9 | +52.8 (10.3) |
| 2020Q1-2021Q4 | −1.1 | +56.0 | +36.4 | +2.2 | +44.5 (10.3) |
| 2022Q1-2026Q2 | +2.4 | +59.6 | +71.6 | +5.7 | +78.5 (20.2) |

The deduction sits below its limit on all 779 class rows (median 0.357 of it,
largest 0.958), so the exclusion covers all of those balances the class holds. That
term is written on the class's own assessment base: at one gross rate the class
keeps the assessment it would otherwise pay on what it holds and lends, so the
term can lower, and cannot raise, what a bank borrowing from the class pays,
while the step that reads is that smaller filers pay more. What the prices place
the class as is a node between the two ends: it buys at about EFFR and lends
36 to 72 basis points above it, and in 2022Q1-2026Q2 its margin of 78.5 basis
points is above the highest total rate the assessment schedule has set for any
small institution since 2023, 32 basis points. What a correspondent charges each respondent is
agreed between the two, and no public source reports it.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

## B60 — how far a level travels before a market sets its own, read on Indian pulse markets

`commodity` in `Lentil (Masur)`, `Cowpea (Lobia-Karamani)`, `White Peas`;
`near_districts=6`, `min_days=150`, `shifts_days=[180, 365, 545, 730, 1095]` on the
daily reading and `shifts_months=[6, 12, 18, 24, 36]` on the monthly one,
`min_overlap=100` on levels and `24` on monthly changes, `floor_rows=matched`.

Registered 2026-08-31, before this data was touched, and the registered sentence
is conditional: a signal travels one matrix at a time, and **where no broadcast
tops it up**, a distant node grows a local fixed point out of what is left and
becomes its own anchor, at which point two distant regions conditional on the
middle segment are close to independent.

**The floor is measured, not declared.** Shifting one end's series by whole
seasons destroys the real alignment and keeps the autocorrelation, which is what
manufactures a partial correlation on series this persistent: the lag-60-day
autocorrelation of the two thickest states is `0.899` and `0.940`. Every arm is
read against its own shifted-placebo floor.

**Two code faults were found on 2026-09-10 and both are fixed here, with the
figures they change kept beside the corrected ones.** First, a monthly change is
stamped on the first of its month, and a shift in days does not land there: of
113 month keys, the declared 180-day and 545-day shifts found a partner for
**none** of them, because no run of six consecutive months is 180 days and no run
of eighteen is 545, while 365, 730 and 1095 found 76, 48 and 24, the shortfalls
being leap days. The declared five-shift placebo was a two-shift placebo on
windows selected by where February 29 fell. The monthly reading now shifts by
calendar months. Second, a shifted series does not cover the same dates as the
unshifted one, so each placebo was being compared against a fit computed on rows
it does not reach; each placebo is now read against the fit restricted to its own
rows. Both faults ran in the same direction on the two cells that sat below their
floors, and both of those cells were artefacts: they are the only two sub-1.0
entries the station ever printed.

| reading | commodity | far / its floor | near / its floor | before the fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| levels | Lentil | 1.50 | **2.70** | far 1.67, near 3.05 |
| monthly changes | Lentil | 1.88 | **3.45** | far 1.69, near 2.34 |
| levels | Cowpea | 1.75 | 1.77 | far 2.02, near 1.73 |
| monthly changes | Cowpea | 1.35 | **1.54** | far 0.83, near 1.57 |
| levels | White Peas | 1.39 | no floor | far 0.73 |
| monthly changes | White Peas | no triple cleared the overlap | | |

**A cell whose sign turns over on the station's own knobs is not read at all.**
The two knobs are `min_days` and `near_districts`, and the grid is the values the
station already named when it set them. Lentil is unanimous at 9 of 9 points on
both readings. Cowpea's levels cell is not: 4 of 9 points put the near arm above
the far one and 5 put it below, and at the default point the two sit at 1.77 and
1.75, a margin of six parts in a thousand. That cell is therefore undetermined
rather than scored, in either direction. Without this gate it would have scored a
pass, in this framework's favour, on that margin.

**The premise of the registered sentence does not hold on this carrier, and that
is what the carrier settles.** Two facts, both about the world: this data is
itself a national daily publication of every market's price, and lentil is among
the five pulses whose support price the central government announces before the
sowing season on its costs commission's recommendation. The far end is topped up
by broadcast here. So the conditional-independence reading has no object on this
carrier, and the far arm's level is reported rather than scored.

**What the carrier does carry** is the graded reading: on each instrument and
against each arm's own floor, the near arm stands further above its floor than
the far arm, 2.70x against 1.50x in levels and 3.45x against 1.88x in monthly
changes on Lentil, and 1.54x against 1.35x in monthly changes on Cowpea. That is
decay with distance in the residual after conditioning. What survives at
distance, on a carrier with a broadcast, is the broadcast channel. Both are named
by this framework and neither is named by a single scalar price field on
positions.

**What the third market in a triple is.** It is any other unit of the same kind,
not a unit checked for lying between the two ends, and no propagation link among
the three is verified, because no adjacency or routing data for these markets is
on disk. So what the two arms compare is residual association after conditioning
on one other market of the same kind, at two distances, with both arms built the
same way. Betweenness is what the conditional-independence reading would need,
and that reading is withdrawn on the premise above.

| | criterion | detail |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B60-1 the near arm clears its own measured floor (`instrument`), Lentil and Cowpea | within-state triples sit at 2.70x and 3.45x, and 1.77x and 1.54x, of their own shifted-placebo floors |
| ---- | B60-1 (`instrument`), White Peas | no near cell has a measured floor; three states and six districts clear the observation count and no shifted placebo keeps enough overlap |
| FAIL | B60-2 premise: no broadcast reaches the far end of this carrier (`premise`), all three | it does. A premise that does not hold leaves the readings depending on it with nothing to judge, and says nothing about the framework |
| PASS | B60-3 graded form: the residual is smaller between distant regions (`own_reading`), Lentil | 2 of 2 readings have near above far, and both are unanimous across the knob grid |
| PASS | B60-3 (`own_reading`), Cowpea | 1 of 1 read: monthly changes, near 1.54x far 1.35x, unanimous at 9 of 9 grid points. The levels cell is not read, its sign turning over on the knobs |
| ---- | B60-3 (`own_reading`), White Peas | not adjudicable: the positive control B60-1 did not clear on this commodity, so an arm reading cannot be told from what a statistic with no resolution returns. The reading is kept in the record |
| ---- | B60-4 WITHDRAWN (`bookkeeping`) | it scored spatial arbitrage as an opposing account. Arbitrage is this framework's own projection operator, which only removes and never creates a value and so cannot supply a level. Reading kept in the record |
| PASS | B60-5 the triple count is presentation, not evidence (`bookkeeping`), all three | 252 far triples come from 9 states and 348 near triples from 101 districts; triples sharing a series are not independent |

**No rival criterion.** The account this framework generalises is a single scalar
price field on positions, and it places no bet on the partial correlation of two
distant markets given a third. That is what makes this reading one of the
quantities only this framework has a reason to compute.

**What would make the registered sentence adjudicable** is a second carrier where
the premise holds: a commodity or a country with no national price publication
and no centrally announced support price.


## B61 — a market's deviation against its branch, and against its own conditions

`source="csv"` with `commodity` in `Lentil (Masur)`, `Cowpea (Lobia-Karamani)`,
`White Peas` and `variety` in `Other`, `Masur Dal`, `Masoor Gola`, `Kala Masoor New`;
`source="api"` with `commodity="262_Sponge_gourd"` and `variety` in `Sponge gourd`,
`Other`, `Organic`. `min_state_markets=3`, `month_window_days=[25, 35]`,
`shifts_days=[180, 365, 730]`, `cluster="state"`.
`experiments/b61_branch_loading.py`, records `results/b61_branch_loading_*.json`,
nine of them.

**What this adds to B30-5.** The criterion as registered asks for regional
deviation regressed on **the propagation branch** and on **the region's own
conditions**. The cross-sectional run of 2026-09-01 put in only the second, city
income. Rule 34: the coarse version passing does not make the fine version pass,
so the branch regressor was still open, and it is the limb the source sentence is
about, "correlate with the intermediary's own deviation and not with the region's
own conditions". The prereg had blocked it on timing. That family of instruments
shares one assumption, that separating inheritance from a common cause needs to
see who moved first, and this instrument does not use it: it asks what the
deviation correlates with, which needs an intermediary's identity and not a clock.

**Construction.** `p = log(modal)`; `nat(t)` is the median over every market
quoting that day; `dev = p - nat`; the branch is the leave-one-out median of the
market's own state minus `nat`, taken where at least three of that state's
markets quote that day; own conditions are `log(arrivals)` for that market that
day. Monthly changes pair a quote with the nearest earlier quote from the same
market 25 to 35 days back. Levels carry day and market fixed effects, monthly
changes the day effect only. `variety` is a stratum and not noise, per rule 49: a
price gap between varieties is not a price gap between markets.

**The floor is measured, and each comparison is paired.** For each shift, the
rows that shift reaches are taken and **both** the real branch series and the
shifted one are fitted on exactly those rows, so the two standard errors share a
sample and a cluster count. A shift also has to carry at least as many clusters
as the fit has coefficients, since a cluster-robust meat matrix is a sum of one
outer product per cluster and is singular below that; that is arithmetic and not
a threshold. The reading is real minus placebo over the two standard errors
combined, and a verdict needs every surviving shift on the same side.

**The yearly per-commodity files, which carry state, district and market.**

| B61-1 the carrier parses and the branch exists | instrument | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| B61-2 the shared subtraction is absorbed | instrument | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| B61-3 monthly changes, branch loading | own_reading | undetermined | **FAIL** | no floor | no floor | no floor | no floor |
| B61-4 the rival's regressor | rival | undetermined | undetermined | no floor | no floor | no floor | no floor |
| B61-5 levels, the same pair | own_reading | undetermined | **FAIL** | **PASS** | **FAIL** | no floor | no floor |
| B61-6 what the counts are not | bookkeeping | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| B61-7 what each shift reaches | instrument | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS |

**Lentil, the main stratum, three paired comparisons.**

**The two readings, written apart per rule 0b.** This framework's reading of
reality: on the main stratum the branch loading on monthly changes clears its
floor on the two shorter shifts and does not on the longest, and the registered
reading needs all three, so the criterion returns its middle cell. The rival's
reading of reality: a distance-weighted equilibrium predicts the loading sits on
the region's own conditions, and that coefficient matches its own placebo to the
printed digit on all three shifts, so **the rival's prediction is not supported
here, which per rule 31 is a different state from refuted**. Neither side
produced a reading, so no cell is claimed.

**Why the 730-day shift does not clear, and it is a statement about the
instrument.** The three figures are `+2.87`, `+2.13`, `+0.79` and they fall
monotonically with what each shift reaches, `68.4%`, `64.9%`, `52.3%` of the
monthly pairs, while the real arm's standard error rises from `0.0706` to
`0.1254` and its clusters fall from 6 to 5. A spurious reading's figure moves
with the sample at random rather than down with `n`. This changes no verdict.

**How many of the six states carry it, one left out at a time (B61-8).** A
cluster count says six and cannot say how many of the six the reading rests on.

| dropped | pairs held | 180d | 365d | 730d |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| *(none)* | | `+2.87` | `+2.13` | `+0.79` |
| Madhya Pradesh | 34,027 of 47,751 | `+0.73` | `+0.64` | `-0.60` |
| **Uttar Pradesh** | **12,111** | **`+0.71`** | **`-0.04`** | **`-1.80`** |
| Maharashtra | 959 | `+3.05` | `+2.08` | `+0.98` |
| Manipur | 352 | `+2.61` | `+1.54` | `+0.77` |
| West Bengal | 202 | `+2.83` | `+1.90` | not built |
| Rajasthan | 100 | `+2.78` | `+2.04` | `+0.66` |

**Madhya Pradesh holds 71% of the pairs, so its column says nothing**: dropping
most of a sample weakens most readings. **Uttar Pradesh holds 25% and its column
moves the figure past zero on two shifts.** The two together hold `96.6%` of the
pairs and they are the same central belt.

**So the reading rests on two states, and the middle cell has a reason that is
not the one first written down.** It is not that a longer shift has too little
power to be read; it is that this carrier's branch varies across two independent
units and not six. That is a scope statement about the carrier rather than a
shortfall a longer panel would close, and it is what makes "a carrier with more
states" the next thing rather than "more years of this one".

**Levels carry a persistent term and the placebo keeps it.** A state's price
level relative to the country holds across years, so shifting a year leaves most
of the real loading in the placebo, `+0.43`, `+0.44` and `+0.21` against a real
`+0.55`, `+0.52` and `+0.40`. Differencing removes that term and the placebo
falls to `+0.011`, `+0.041` and `+0.005`. Both arms are reported with their own
floors and neither is picked over the other.

**Cowpea reads the other way, and what it stands on is printed beside it.** The
branch loading is negative on all three shifts and below each floor by more than
the combined error, `-1.73`, `-1.04`, `-2.13`, which is the criterion's third
state and a FAIL. B61-7 prints what that stands on: the shifts reach `7.7%`,
`23.1%` and `24.4%` of the monthly pairs against Lentil's `68.4%`, `64.9%` and
`52.3%`; three clusters against six; and subsample coefficients `-0.5893`,
`-0.1752`, `-0.3547` against a full-sample `-0.0727`. A shift reaches only the
rows where the same state kept quoting that many days later, which is not a
random draw.

**The three minor strata are not the same markets under another name, and that
is what they turned out to be about.** They were run as a replication and the
records say otherwise: `Masoor Gola` sits in Chattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and
Uttar Pradesh, `Masur Dal` in Assam, Jharkhand and West Bengal, `Kala Masoor New`
in two states with 1,448 rows. **The strata are different regions, so they are
not one propagation graph read twice.** On monthly changes none of them keeps a
shift with enough clusters, so B61-3 has no floor on all three. On levels:

| stratum | states | shift | real | placebo | n / clusters | combined se |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Masoor Gola | CG, MP, UP | 365d | `+0.8501` (se `0.0523`) | `+0.6378` (se `0.0266`) | 3,528 / 3 | `+3.62` |
| Masur Dal | AS, JH, WB | 180d | `-0.2341` (se `0.2398`) | `+0.2095` (se `0.1456`) | 7,135 / 3 | `-1.58` |
| | | 365d | `-0.1985` (se `0.2044`) | `+0.0970` (se `0.0958`) | 5,633 / 3 | `-1.31` |

**Sponge gourd, where the branch loading is not there.** On the main stratum the
real coefficient sits **below** its own placebo on both readable shifts, `365d`
real `-0.0422` against a placebo `+0.1225`, `730d` real `+0.0092` against
`+0.1292`, which is `-1.14` and `-0.76` combined se and lands in the middle cell.
On the `Other` stratum it sits below on all three, `-41.23`, `-1.76`, `-2.25`,
and is a FAIL. The `180d` shift on the main stratum reaches only two states and
is dropped by the cluster-rank check.

**And the rival's regressor is an order of magnitude larger here than on the
pulses, while still matching its own placebo.** `b_arr` on Sponge gourd is
`-0.10` against Lentil's `+0.008`, with the sign a fuller market carries: more
arrivals, lower price. Its placebos sit on the same figure to the printed digit
(`-0.1001`, `-0.1023`), so what it measures is a standing cross-sectional
relation that a shift does not disturb, and not a shock arriving down a branch.
The criterion stays undetermined on that reading.

**One reading after the fact, recorded as an observation and not as a criterion,
and it replaces the one written here earlier the same day.** The earlier version
said the sign of the monthly branch loading follows geography rather than
commodity, on four carriers: the central belt positive (`+0.2337` Lentil `Other`
on Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, `+0.7519` Masoor Gola on the same belt plus
Chattisgarh) and the eastern and southern sets negative (`-0.1172` Masur Dal,
`-0.0727` Cowpea). **Sponge gourd breaks it**: three of its four states are on
that same central belt and its loading is `+0.1342` at full sample but negative
or at zero on every readable shift, below its own placebo throughout. The reading
that survives the sixth carrier is about the good rather than the place: **the
pulses store and the gourd does not**, and a branch loading is a claim that a
level travelled, which needs something that can wait. It is registered nowhere,
seen after the run, on six carriers, and **not scored**.

**White Peas and Kala Masoor New have no object.** 112 and 1,448 rows keep a
branch, over two states each, and no shift survives both the coverage and the
cluster-rank check on either arm. The full-sample coefficients in those records
are two-cluster artefacts and carry nothing; they are printed because B61-7
prints coverage either way.

**Three implementation corrections, all inside this run, and none moved a
coefficient.** The first comparison ran the real fit on the whole sample and each
placebo on whatever rows its shift reached, giving standard errors on two scales
and a difference with no referent; that version returned `2.83` combined se and
is withdrawn. The second took the intersection of the three shifts, fixing the
scale by throwing away two thirds of the sample and five of eight clusters, and
tying the 180-day comparison to the 730-day one for no reason; also withdrawn.
The third, per shift, is what is on disk. Separately the cell function was first
written as `all(real > placebo)`, a zero-width strict inequality, which fired the
same day on a coefficient whose real value and 730-day placebo agree to four
decimals; the width is now the comparison's own combined standard error. And
B61-2 was first coded as an assertion that three correlations fall monotonically,
which nothing had registered and which fired on two thin carriers; it prints the
three numbers and judges their computability instead. **Every correction moved
verdicts and left every coefficient and standard error where it was.**

Data: Agmarknet market-level daily arrivals and prices, the top-level CSVs, which
carry state, district and market alongside arrivals and the three prices; the
JSON API rows do not, which is failure mode 153. Lentil 115,905 lines across four
varieties: `Other` 90,894 of which 80,117 rows keep a branch across 9 states, 291
markets and 3,283 days; `Masur Dal` 11,338 with 9,838; `Masoor Gola` 10,159 with
8,557; `Kala Masoor New` 2,337 with 1,448. Cowpea 28,236 lines, 9,658 rows with a
branch across 6 states and 121 markets. White Peas 3,337 lines, 112 rows.
