## B33 arm one again — two classes that take the same cell in every number a tax code prints

Second scored carrier for arm one, and the configuration the criterion was
written for. The Internal Revenue Code writes five filing statuses and states
their mutual exclusions in its own text. Two of them, a joint return and a
surviving spouse, take the same cell in every provision of that Code that prints
a number, and are separated only by provisions that print no number at all.

Positions are (taxpayer, taxable year). Ten dimensions, each one published
provision, each carrying a section number and a phrase quoted from that section.
No estimate anywhere: every value is a cell of a statute. Script
`experiments/b33_filing_status.py`, record `results/b33_filing_status.json`,
`--selftest` seeds four worlds.

**Addresses are section numbers and quotes, not offsets.** This Code is amended
every year, so any byte or line offset into it is void at the next amendment
while still looking like a perfectly good integer.

**Why this carrier can be asked at all.** Two shape gates, both pure reading.
The first wants two optional identities for one position rather than two entries
on a list of who qualifies, and the discriminant is exclusivity: can one position
hold both at once. Here it cannot, and the Code says so four times, at `1(c)`
(`every individual (other than a surviving`), at `2(b)(1)` (`is not married at the
close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse`), at `2(a)(2)(A)` (`the
taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year`), and at
`6013(a)` (`A husband and wife may make a single return jointly`), which needs a
living spouse where `2(a)(1)(A)` needs a dead one. The second gate wants the
document delivering the vectors not to be the price list itself, since a
value-indexed table carries one row per distinct vector by construction and so
could never put two classes in one cell. Five cells of this price list hold two
statuses at once, which settles the gate by counting rather than by assertion.

**The three provisions that print numbers.**

| provision | joint | surviving spouse | head of household | single | married filing separately |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rate table, `1` | `1(a)` | `1(a)` | `1(b)` | `1(c)` | `1(d)` |
| basic standard deduction, `63(c)(2)` | `(A)` | `(A)` | `(B)` | `(C)` | `(C)` |
| alternative minimum tax exemption, `55(d)(1)` | `(A)` | `(A)` | `(B)` | `(B)` | `(C)` |

**The six provisions that separate the pair, none of which prints a number.**
Whose income is aggregated and who is liable, both from the one sentence at
`6013(d)(3)` (`the tax shall be computed on the aggregate income and the liability
with respect to the tax shall be joint and several`); the relief election at
`6015(a)`, open to `an individual who has made a joint return`; the two-year
window at `2(a)(1)(A)`; the remarriage bar at `2(a)(2)(A)`; and the household
test at `2(a)(1)(B)`. A seventh term provision, `63(c)(6)(A)`, separates married
filing separately from everyone else and leaves this pair together.

**Three partitions, and the middle line is the reading.**

```
written by the Code            5 blocks   each status alone
over the numbers alone         4 blocks   joint and surviving spouse merge
over the terms alone           5 blocks   each status alone
over every provision           5 blocks   equal to what is written
```

The numbers merge two classes and the terms separate them; read the other way,
the terms alone already recover the whole written partition, so on this table the
numbers are the redundant half. Of the ten pairs, exactly one is separated by
terms alone and none by numbers alone. Two pairs coincide on part of the numbers:
head of household with single at `55(d)(1)(B)`, and single with married filing
separately at `63(c)(2)(C)`. That is a second thing the run did not go looking
for: different provisions of one Code write different partitions, so what is
written is a family of partitions, one per provision, and the clause vector is
their common refinement.

| criterion | kind | reading | |
|---|---|---|---|
| B33-6 both shape gates clear | instrument | four exclusion clauses quoted; five cells of the price list hold two statuses | PASS |
| B33-7 the pair takes the same cell in every number, and is the only pair that does | own_reading | 0 of 3 number-bearing provisions differ; 1 of 10 pairs coincides on every number | PASS |
| B33-8 the scalar field's point prediction does not hold here | rival | it holds on 4 of 10 dimensions and fails on 6, every one of the 6 term-bearing | PASS |
| B33-9 written partition against delivered partition | own_reading | 5 blocks against 5 blocks, equal | PASS |
| B33-10 pairs known to differ on numbers read as differing; all ten named | known_answer | four known-answer checks, none missed | PASS |
| B33-11 every dimension carries a section and a quote | bookkeeping | 10 of 10, across six sections | PASS |

**The rival and the cell.** The premise attacked is that a position carries a
scalar and every term at that position is generated by it, which is to say the
object has one index and no class index. The entailment is immediate: terms are
then a function of that scalar, so two classes reading the same scalar at the
same position must receive identical terms, and one differing provision falsifies
it. Per rule 11e the polarity is that PASS means the rival was wrong. The retreat
that legal liability is not a price moves the question onto the scalar assumption
rather than away from it, and this carrier closes that move harder than most: the
scalar cost of moving between these two classes is zero, since they share every
number the Code prints for them, so no price difference is available to absorb
the six differences. Both accounts were asked against the same reality; this
framework says a class-indexed term exists and it does, the rival says the two
are interchangeable and they are not. Cell B.

**What the PASS is and is not.** Arm one's PASS gets cheaper as dimensions are
added, because another dimension only makes identity on all of them harder and so
makes a failure harder to reach. So the load-bearing reading is not the PASS but
where the separation lives, and that is the four blocks against five above: had
the reading stopped at the price list, this criterion would have failed here. The
first selftest seed runs exactly that world and the criterion fails in it.

**What the run does not claim.** Not that these two statuses should be merged or
split, not that the rate table is wrong anywhere, not that the federal income tax
is price discrimination, and not that ten dimensions are all of them: the Code
branches on filing status in far more places, and adding them can only add
separation, while B33-8 needs one. Nothing here is a tax burden; no tax amount was
computed at any point.

**Sources.** The load-bearing sentence, `6013(d)(3)`, was read in the official
text and in a mirror, word for word the same. The remaining sections were read in
that mirror of the same Code. Level and reading date are in the record's `config`
block.

**One thing the control caught, and it was itself.** B33-10 failed on its first
run, on a pair that does differ, because the known-answer list named that pair in
one order and the pairs are generated in another, so the lookup missed. The same
output printed, one column over, the provision that separates them. Looked up by
members rather than by order afterwards. A control that can fail because of how it
looks something up is still a control that fires.

## B33 arm three — whether a graduated per-person tax ever arrives before the register

**Restated 2026-09-11, and the restatement is about what this arm carries rather
than about any number in it. Nothing below is withdrawn and nothing is changed.**
Arm two of this station requires a register that pre-dates the tax and was not
built for it, which is its definition of a qualifying register. That definition
contains the ordering this arm reads, so finding a qualifying register settles the
sign without looking at a date, and the two arms fail together: a tax preceding
every qualifying register is exactly a graduated tax running with no qualifying
register. **So this arm is not a third claim. Its six cells reading after are arm
two surviving on six more polities, written a different way.** The station had
already diagnosed this shape one arm over, where the loose reading of arm two is
recorded as non-scoring because any per-person tax necessarily has collection
machinery; that one is near-tautological by mechanism and this one by definition,
and only the first was written down.

**What this arm still carries on its own, none of it touched by the restatement.**
The gap is a quantity rather than a test, and it separates two different situations:
nineteen years in Qin says the register and the tax are adjacent, two hundred and
fifty-six in France says the register is merely older. Arm two cannot read that.
The two readings that came out of the run, the overrun rule and the axis alignment,
owe nothing to arm two and both have live failure branches; England came within one
outcome of killing the first. And the carriers do not overlap: arm two was read on
whether one country's taxes of 1377 to 1381 collected, this arm on seven polities'
dates. One claim, two disjoint bodies of material, which is worth what a second
instrument is worth rather than what a third claim would be.


The claim was written on 2026-08-31, in the corpus block that first read a tax
schedule as a price list, and before any date below was looked at: a tax graduated
by person has to arrive after the registration machine and cannot come before it,
with the kill condition next to it, find one polity with no household register, no
tax register and no population register at all that ran a graduated per-person tax
and this dies. The discipline that says a hypothesis's timing carries evidence and
a criterion's does not applies here in the first direction: these seven cells are
out of sample.

Script `experiments/b33_registration_order.py`, record
`results/b33_registration_order.json`, `--selftest` seeds five worlds. No
collection, no estimate, date floor of one year.

**The frame was fixed before the first date was read**, because if the polities
were chosen after the dates were seen this arm would be reading the hand that
chose them: six families named in the design's gate zero, one named polity and
levy per family, plus one slot for a kill candidate. Every cell is reported,
including the ones whose dates cannot be pinned. The register has to clear the
definition this station tightened in its first round: it binds a liability to a
living person at the moment of assessment, it is a maintained list rather than a
record of past events, it pre-dates the tax, and it was not built for it.

| polity | classes | register | established | graduated per-person tax | levied | sign | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Roman Republic | 5 | the census, taken by tribe, recording rank, household, property and income | 578–534 BCE | tributum ex censu | 406 BCE | after | 128–172 y |
| Qin and Han | 5 | household registers compiled annually after the harvest, name and age per person | 375 BCE | suanfu and koufu, banded by age and status | 356 / 203 BCE | after | **19**–172 y |
| England | 7 | tithing membership, viewed twice a year | **not pinned** | the graduated poll tax of 1379 | 1379 | undated | — |
| France | 22 | the parish rolls of the taille | 1439 | the capitation of 18 January 1695, twenty-two classes | 1695 | after | 256 y |
| Uganda Protectorate | ≥2 | the per-person rolls of adult males kept for the 1905 poll tax | 1905 | the Graduated Personal Tax, on assessed income | 1950s | after | 45–54 y |
| Great Britain | 3 | the parish assessment books of the land and assessed taxes | 1692 / 1696 | the income tax of 1799 | 1799 | after | 103–107 y |
| **Athens (was the kill candidate)** | 3 | the deme citizen-lists, enrolment in one being the requirement for citizenship | 508/507 BCE | the eisphora, banded on the Solonian classes | 500–428 BCE | after | 7–80 y |

```
after 6      same act 0      before 0      undated 1
```

**The informative cell is Qin, not France.** A gap of 256 years says the register
is older than the tax. A gap of 19 says the two are adjacent: the 375 BCE order
grouped households in fives for mutual surety, which is not a fiscal device, and
nineteen years later a poll tax banded by age and status was opened on the same
books.

**The kill candidate, and how it closed.** Athens is the cell the design sent this
arm to hunt for, and on the first run it was left with no verdict, hanging on one
narrow question: was Solon's wealth census a maintained list. It was not, and the
constitutional history says so about its own century, four hundred years later:
`when the presiding official asks a man who is about to draw lots for some office
what rate he pays`. The class was asked of the man at the moment he needed it and
the answer was checked against nothing. That is the shape the tightened definition
excludes, and the tightening was written ten days before this cell was looked at,
for an unrelated reason: to stop English parish baptism registers from making one
of this station's other arms pass automatically. It cost the most convenient
reading available here, that the register and the classes came out of one reform.
What replaces it is the deme citizen-lists of 508/507, eighty-odd years later, and
they are still earlier than the tax. Solon's four classes are not themselves a tax:
they governed office and military obligation, and the money levy founded on them is
the eisphora, whose basis is described by the same source that dates its abolition,
`the tax system founded on Solon's property classes was abolished, in 378/7 B.C.`
Liturgies do not count either, on the same ground as the two controls: assigning a
duty to a named man writes no distinct class values. **So the arm now has no live
kill candidate.** That is a statement about the state of the hunt, not a
strengthening of the pass: zero cells reading before is not the same claim as
before being ruled out, and it is not written as one. One cell is still unpinned,
England, because tithing has no establishment year to read and the datable English
list, the poll rolls of 1377, was built for this family of taxes.

**A second reading the same cells give for free, and this one has a live failure
branch.** Where the class count exceeds what the prior list can tell apart, either
the state extends the list or the tax does not run. Five states, mapped per cell in
the record: fits, extended and ran, overran and collapsed, **overran and ran anyway
which is the failure**, and resolution unknown which carries no verdict. A sixth state was added when Athens landed between two of them: overran first and
was extended later. Read: fits 3, extended 1, overran then extended 1, overran and
collapsed 1, failure 0, unknown 1.

| | England 1379 | France 1695 |
|---|---|---|
| classes written | 7, by social rank | 22, from 2,000 livres to 1 |
| what the prior list could tell apart | one bit, in a tithing or not, and no property at all | the parish taille rolls, from which nobles and clergy were exempt and so absent |
| what the state did | nothing | put the nobility on a roll of its own |
| outcome | 37 per cent of expectation, and the next attempt met by refusal to register | ran, and went on running to the end of the old regime |

The third is Uganda, and being one polity's own sequence it is immune to the
choice of polities: 1900 a tax on huts, which can be counted without naming
anyone; 1905 a flat tax per adult male, which is the step that builds the
per-person roll; the 1950s a tax graduated on assessed income, last, half a
century behind. That is the predicted order inside one colonial administration.


**What closing that cell exposed, which is worth more than the sign.** The sign asks
whether the list can find the person. It does not ask whether the list can tell the
classes apart, and those are two questions. The deme lists satisfy every word of the
tightened definition and record citizenship and deme, not property, while the
eisphora's bands are cut on property: the sign passes on a list that cannot resolve
the classes it is being asked to carry. So each cell now records a second field,
whether the register carries the axis the classes are cut on, and the registered
reading is two-sided: carries it means the count fits, does not carry it means the
count is in some state other than fitting. Carries 3, does not 2, partly 1, unknown
1, and the six decided cells align with none misaligned. The seventh, Uganda, was
downgraded the same day from fitting to unknown, because its class count is a lower
bound taken from a source that gives no band table and no assessment mechanism;
recording it as fitting would have written an unchecked thing as a checked one. The
downgrade changes no verdict and Uganda still carries the reading it was brought in
for, its own three-step sequence.

| criterion | kind | reading | |
|---|---|---|---|
| B33-12 frame fixed before any date, every cell reported | instrument | 7 of 7 reported, 1 unpinned and named, 0 written signs disagreeing with the computed ones | PASS |
| B33-13 no tax arrives before a qualifying register | own_reading | after 6, same act 0, before 0, undated 1 | PASS |
| B33-14 an overrun is met by extending the list or by the tax not running | own_reading | fits 3, extended 1, overran then extended 1, overran 1, failure 0, unknown 1 | PASS |
| B33-17 whether the list carries the axis lines up with whether the count fits it | own_reading | carries 3, does not 2, partly 1, unknown 1; 0 misaligned, the unknown cell left out | PASS |
| B33-15 control: a levy keyed to an object or a place is not a per-person graduated tax | known_answer | 2 controls, 0 miscounted | PASS |
| B33-16 every cell carries quoted evidence, unpinned cells named too | bookkeeping | 7 of 7, 30 quotes | PASS |

**No rival criterion here, deliberately, and the record says so in its config.** A
scalar field on positions makes no claim about when a fiscal instrument appears in
history, so this is a cell where nobody on that side had a reason to answer:
new facts, no score. Registering a rival where the other side has no object is the
machine that turns a win into a shared cell and manufactures a loss out of nothing,
which this repository did once and reversed the same day.

**What the run does not claim.** Not that these seven are a random sample: they are
one per family, and the frame being written first says only that the choosing
happened before the looking. Not that the resolution reading has been tested: it
was added after the run, on three instances, one of which carries no verdict. Not
that any date is exact; Rome and Athens are traditional datings, taken as ranges,
and a sign is read only when both ends fall on the same side.

## B33 — where the fold is: collection, price list, publication

Arm one read a tax code against itself, which leaves an obvious question open:
two filing statuses take the same cell in every provision that prints a number, so
is that fold a property of the price list alone or does the whole administrative
system behind it carry the same fold. It turns out to be answerable by reading
documents, because the agencies say how their own classifications are built. No
amount was pulled and nothing was estimated. Script
`experiments/b33_three_layers.py`, record `results/b33_three_layers.json`,
`--selftest` seeds three worlds.

| layer | classes written | separates the two | document, and the phrase that carries it |
|---|---|---|---|
| collection | 5 | **yes** | Instructions for Form 1040, Filing Status: `Qualifying surviving spouse` is a checkbox of its own |
| price list | 4 | **no** | the heading of the rate section itself, `Married individuals filing joint returns and surviving spouses` |
| publication, the count series | not counted | **yes** | the revenue service publishes `Individual Income Tax Filing: Returns of Surviving Spouses` as a series of its own |
| publication, the table with money | 4 | **no** | `Returns of married persons filing jointly and returns of surviving spouses`, almost the rate section's own heading word for word |

```
fold at: the price list, and again in the published table that carries money
```

**The last row was added on 2026-09-11 and it corrects this section's first
version, which read the publication layer off the count series alone and said in
as many words that the unopened stub could not affect whether that layer separates
the two.** It could and it did: the publication layer is not one layer. Where the
table carries money the pair is folded; where it carries only a count of returns
they are apart. The measured version is in the observed-side section below.

The taxpayer states which of the two they are at the moment of filing, and a count
of returns is published for each. **So the class index exists, is recorded, and is
reported; what does not carry it is anything with money attached.** The reply that
the distinction does not really exist is closed by the form at one end and the
count series at the other. Where it is dropped is the rate section and every
published table of amounts that follows it.

**The middle number is not typed into this run.** It is read out of arm one's own
record, so editing arm one's dimension table moves it: 4 classes over the
number-bearing provisions against 5 written, the folded cell being the pair. That
is the positive use of the rule about sentinels: have the sentinel count something
that grows with the content.

**What was not read, named rather than skipped.** The stub of the current basic
table classified by size of adjusted gross income and marital status was not
opened, so that layer's category names and class count are not read here; what the
published series already settles is whether the layer separates the two, which is
what this reading turns on. Separately, the mirror consulted carries values to
2016 while the basic tables classify by marital status through tax year 2023;
whether that stop is the mirror's or that particular historical table's is not
checked.

| criterion | kind | reading | |
|---|---|---|---|
| B33-18 both ends separate and the middle folds, so the fold belongs to the price list | own_reading | collection yes, price list no, publication yes; fold at price_list | PASS |
| B33-19 the middle count is read from arm one's record, not retyped | instrument | 4 against 5, folded cell the pair | PASS |
| B33-20 every layer names a document and quotes it; the layer not read in full says so | bookkeeping | 3 of 3 quoted, 2 of 3 read in full, the third named | PASS |

**What this does not claim, and the first one matters most.** Not that the two
classes pay the same amount: no amount was pulled, so this says nothing about
effective rates at equal income. That is the next cut and it now needs one table
rather than a project. Not that the publication layer writes five classes, only
that it reports these two apart. Not that the five boxes on the return correspond
one to one with the five statuses in the code; the shapes match and this run did
not check the correspondence.

## B33 arm one, observed side — the published table carries the price list's partition

The registered reading for this cut was an ordering rather than a line, and it was
written into the design before the file was obtained: the pair that shares every
printed number should show a far smaller gap in effective rate than pairs that
differ on printed numbers. It registered a third outcome as well, that the table
might not report the pair apart at all, in which case the reading is recorded as
the published aggregate being out of reach rather than the quantity being absent.
**That third outcome is the one that fired, in all three years.**

Source: the Statistics of Income basic table classified by size of adjusted gross
income and marital status, tax years 2021, 2022 and 2023, `data/b33/*in12ms.xls`,
official, fetched by hand on the project's own machine because the gateway in
front of both sandboxes denies that host by policy. Script
`experiments/b33_observed_partition.py`, record
`results/b33_observed_partition.json`, `--selftest` seeded.

**The table's own column blocks, identical across all three years.**

```
All returns
Returns of married persons filing jointly and returns of surviving spouses
Returns of married persons filing separately
Returns of heads of households
Returns of single persons
```

Four statuses in four blocks, and the merged one is the pair. The rate section of
the code is headed `Married individuals filing joint returns and surviving
spouses`; the table is headed almost word for word the same. **The partition the
published table carries is the partition the price list writes, cell for cell**,
and that partition is read out of arm one's record rather than retyped here:
`[[HOH], [MFJ, QSS], [MFS], [SINGLE]]`.

**The fold is exact rather than broad.** Every status that differs from the others
on a printed number sits in a block of its own; exactly one block is merged, in
each year, and it is the one the statute also declines to separate. So this is not
an agency that combines categories freely.

**What could not be read, and how large it could have been.** The within-pair gap
is what this cut was registered to measure and no published table of amounts
carries it. The other half of the ordering is computable and is printed so the
size of the missing comparison is on the record: across the four published
statuses, effective rate being total income tax over adjusted gross income less
deficit with both taken from the same block, the spread within an income band runs
0.09 to 6.98 percentage points over 54 band-years, median 2.83.

| band, tax year 2023 | HOH | **MFJ+QSS** | MFS | single | spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $30,000 under $40,000 | 0.0028 | **0.0067** | 0.0479 | 0.0565 | 5.38 pp |
| $75,000 under $100,000 | 0.0644 | **0.0534** | 0.1186 | 0.1189 | 6.55 pp |
| $200,000 under $500,000 | 0.1945 | **0.1543** | 0.1986 | 0.2037 | 4.94 pp |
| $2,000,000 under $5,000,000 | 0.2816 | **0.2804** | 0.2715 | 0.2751 | 1.02 pp |

So the gap inside the merged block sits somewhere in nought to about seven
percentage points and nothing published narrows it.

| criterion | kind | reading | |
|---|---|---|---|
| B33-21 the table with money carries the price list's partition, and the merged block is the pair | own_reading | 3 of 3 years, 4 blocks, merged MFJ+QSS | PASS |
| B33-22 the within-pair gap in effective rate | own_reading | **not adjudicable**: 0 of 3 years report the pair apart; recorded as out of reach, not absent | no verdict |
| B33-23 control: the fold is exact, and the benchmark half is computed | known_answer | one merged block and four in total each year; 54 band-years, 0.09 to 6.98 pp, median 2.83 | PASS |
| B33-24 the price list partition is read from arm one's record | instrument | `[[HOH],[MFJ,QSS],[MFS],[SINGLE]]` | PASS |
| B33-25 each year named with shape, headings and bands read | bookkeeping | 3 years, identical headings, 18 bands each | PASS |

**A sentinel of this run's own was broken and it is worth naming.** The script that
describes the layout held a label list containing `head of household` while the
table says `heads of households`, so that entire column block was invisible to it;
what caught it was the block count not matching the labels found. Same family as
the rule about tools failing on a particular literal, and it fails silently, by
seeing one block fewer rather than by raising.

**What this does not claim.** Not that the two classes pay the same or differ: this
section records that it cannot be read. Not that the table's wording was copied
from the statute; the near-identity is an observation and no source here says why
the blocks are cut as they are. Not that the published spreads are price
differences; they carry composition as well and nothing here decomposes them, they
are printed to give the missing comparison a scale.

## B33 — the granularity chain, and what it does to the observed side

Nothing was fetched for this. It falls out of three readings already on record and
it is the reason the observed-side cut is worth more than the comparison it could
not make.

```
registration point   five checkboxes on the return        5 classes, the pair apart
class values         the three provisions printing numbers 4 cells, the pair merged
publication, money   the basic table by income and status  4 cells, matching exactly
publication, counts  the published count of those returns  5, matching the register
```

**Published statistics are not one granularity.** The side carrying money is
capped by the price list; the side carrying only a count of returns keeps the
register's. So the question "does this source separate the two" has two answers
inside one source, which is exactly what the earlier three-layer section got wrong
by reading one of them and saying in as many words that the unopened table could
not change the answer.

**This tightens an equation.** The project's price-theory note states that the
granularity of class values equals that of the registration point. Here the
registration point has five and the class values have four, the difference being
precisely the one merge, so a program can decline to use resolution it already
holds and the equality should be read as a cap: class values at most as fine as
the registration point. The earlier carrier behind that equation was a cap too, a
continuous payroll book against a two-region function of it, but with neither side
countable the inequality was invisible. This carrier makes it visible, and that is
the whole of what is new here.

**What it does to the outstanding debt on arm one.** The debt was recorded as: arm
one reads a document against itself and owes an observed clause field. The shape
of that debt changes. On this carrier, at the layer where money appears, the
observed granularity is set by the object under test, so an independent observed
partition cannot be had there by construction rather than by difficulty. Getting
one means going where the granularity is not set by the price list: microdata,
administrative records, or a jurisdiction that reports money for the two
separately. The debt stands; the queue entry now names that shape instead of
saying find another table.

**What this does not claim.** Not that money-bearing statistics are always capped
this way: one carrier, one table, three years. What is claimed is that one source
can answer the separation question two different ways, and a single counterexample
establishes that. Not that the effective-rate difference between the merged block
and single filers is a price difference; it carries composition, one-earner
against two-earner households, which is the half the framework says is not priced.

## FAIL census — what the failing criteria were asking, counted by kind

**RUN: 2026-09-15.** `scripts/fail_census.py`, record `results/fail_census.json`.
No record was rewritten: discipline 11d is not retroactive, so this assigns a kind
by station and criterion name and prints the assignment's reason rather than
editing anything on disk.

**Every number below moves when a station is added, and three of them moved
inside the session that first wrote them here.** Rule 15a says not to pickle a
count into a document, so they are quoted with the run above and the script lands
its own record: to have them now, run it, do not read them off this page. The
script skips that record when it counts, since a tool inside what it measures
grows the thing it is measuring.

**Why this exists.** A FAIL is not a number. Most criteria in a station's table
ask about this run's tooling and its inputs, and adding their failures to "the
rival said something true once" produces a figure with no referent. The figure
worth quoting is the `rival` one.

**Scope, stated because three different correct counts of the same thing
disagree without it.** The scope here is the worktree under `results/` minus
what git ignores minus `.expired`, which is the scope the push check uses. **The count itself is
not quoted here**, because it is the size of a set that grows whenever any station writes a
record, so it has no correct moment, only a correct run: `scripts/fail_census.py --write` puts
it in `results/fail_census.json` with everything else it counts. The scope includes the records
in subdirectories
that a top-level listing misses, and excludes `results/_baseline/`, a snapshot of
283 older copies of the records above it.

**The counts are not written here.** Every one of them is the size of a set that
grows whenever any station writes a record, and on 2026-09-15 they went stale
twice in one day: once because this session added criteria, and once because
another session did while this one was writing. A figure with no correct moment
does not belong in a document; it belongs in a run. So:

```
scripts/fail_census.py            prints them
scripts/fail_census.py --write    lands them in results/fail_census.json
```

**What the census separates, which is the part that does not move.** Objects
carrying `passed = false` are not all criteria: some sit outside a criteria array
entirely. Of the ones that are criteria, some say — in their detail or on a
`void`, `undecidable` or `withdrawn` field — that they were never evaluated, and
by the rule that an undecided criterion is not a failure those come out before
anything is counted. What remains are readings that came out false, and those are
split by what the criterion was asking:

| kind | what a failure there says |
|---|---|
| own_reading | one reading this station registered is withdrawn |
| instrument | this run's reading is unusable; go fix the code or the input |
| bookkeeping | something that should have been printed was not |
| known_answer | a placebo or a check with a known answer caught something |
| premise | an external fact the station rested on does not hold |
| **rival** | **the rival's point prediction held somewhere** |

**One number is quoted, because it is the one that speaks to a theory and because
it has not moved: `rival` is zero.**

**Zero uncovered**: every one of them is matched by a rule that says in a
sentence what that criterion asks, and the script exits non-zero if any is not.

**The one figure: `rival` is zero.** Across every record in the repository, no
criterion registered against a rival's point prediction has failed. Per rule
11e's first clause the polarity of such a criterion is that PASS means the rival
was wrong, so a zero here is a statement about what has been scored and not a
claim that no rival was ever right: the C cell of the four-cell table is empty
and this is the count behind that.

**Three screens matter and each cost an error before it was written.**
The first is scope: a plain directory walk counts the baseline snapshot too,
returning 231 against 137 on the run that caught it, and nothing reports it
because those copies are valid JSON with the same structure and the same
criterion names. The second is
the void screen: a criterion whose detail says it was not evaluated is not a
reading that came out false, and the word has to be looked for anywhere in the
detail rather than at its front. The two sharpest cases in the repository, a
pair of complementary criteria where the one that holds was banked and the other
recorded as a failure, put their reading first and the word after it.

**The third screen is what the second one was reading the shadow of.** A
criterion can say it was not evaluated in two places, the wording of its
`detail` and a field on the criterion itself, and the field is the primary
place: 461 criteria carry `void`, against a word screen that reads prose.
Reading only the prose counted three criteria as readings that came out false
while their own record says the opposite, and one of the three is the criterion
the rules file holds void by name. Both places are read now, and a criterion
counts as not evaluated when either says so. The three are `A1-7` (its two
readings of the registration disagree, so it is gated on neither), `A3-8`
(unstable, and held void for want of a registered threshold), and `A7-B-1` (a
quantity with no sign has no magnitude to trend). **None is a `rival`, so the
one figure worth quoting does not move.**

## B63: the impossible trinity, as Theorem 1 read on the currency × date product

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Statement and proof in `docs/b63_trilemma.md`. Structural checks
in `experiments/b63_trilemma_check.py`, record `results/b63_trilemma_check.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

A position is one unit of a currency's short claim at a date. The short rate sits on
the edge from one date to the next, the spot rate on the edge from one currency to
another, and a forward or a credible peg supplies a locked edge that fixes the next
date's conversion today. The four-cycle through `(k,t)`, `(k,t+1)`, `(l,t+1)` and
`(l,t)` then sums to `r_k - r_l + lam - e` less the frictions, and a peg sets
`lam = e`, so the sum is the rate difference itself. **Theorem 8: a credible peg, a
plaquette some class can walk in both orientations, no frictions and finite
steady-state flows give `r_k = r_l`.** The peg closes the loop, openness makes it
walkable, and the rate is what is left to adjust. After a change of units by the
parities, the pegged part of the graph has the shape of Theorem 1's `G □ H`, with
currencies standing where classes stood, so Theorem 8 is Theorem 1's across-slices
step on a second product, and **the three corners of the trinity are the three cases
of that theorem's §8**: the edge present with its weight fixed, the edge absent, the
edge present with its weight moving. Only closed loops enter, so nothing here rests
on uncovered parity or on a premium.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 5 proved, 1 proved as restated · `bookkeeping` 2 written · `instrument` 4 pass

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| **proved** | B63-1 `own_reading` Theorem 8 | The premise has three parts: no-arbitrage reaches walkable cycles only; flows are finite at the steady state; the short claim is the issuer's own liability, so holding it one period carries no default term. A walk may pass through agent edges, executed as a chain of trades between classes |
| **proved** | B63-2 `own_reading` how many rates a system of pegs leaves, Corollary 8.1 | Rates are equal across each component of the graph of two-way pegs, and the number left free is the number of components, when every pegged conversion is open both ways at both dates or not at all. **One-way pegs chain too, around a directed cycle**: in general rates are forced equal within each strongly connected component of the directed graph of open pegged conversions, and two different components are unrelated. **A consistent system of pegs is a potential on the peg graph**: around a triangle of pegs the parities sum to zero, and a star of pegs to one anchor meets that trivially. On a connected graph of `m` currencies over `T` date steps the first Betti number is `b_1(C)·(T+1) + (m-1)·T`, the second term counting `m - 1` plaquettes per step |
| **proved** | B63-3 `own_reading` the three corners, Corollary 8.2 | Weight fixed: one rate. Edge absent: no cycle crosses, and the two currencies sit in different components, so a peg that keeps its own rate is a peg with the conversion edge removed. Weight moving: under a float the locked edge is absent, and with a forward the rate difference is carried by the forward premium, the covered-parity object of B3 |
| **proved** | B63-4 `own_reading` the friction band, Corollary 8.3 | `-(sigma_bar + beta_k) <= r_k - r_l <= sigma_bar + beta_l` for a pair with no route through a third currency, `sigma_bar` the mean of the spot and locked conversion spreads and `beta` the borrowing spreads. **Closed at `t+1` only, the lower bound survives**: money brought in cannot leave at the parity, so nothing arbitrages a domestic rate above the anchor's, while residents can still leave and come back, so a rate below the anchor's is arbitraged to within the friction. Closed at every date: no cycle crosses and neither bound survives. The band is the directed-edge theorem's friction split read on the plaquette |
| **proved as restated** | B63-5 `own_reading` access split by holder class, Corollary 8.4 | One class holds `k -> l`, another `l -> k`. Agent edges at par compose the two one-way conversions into both orientations and the band holds; agent edges with a price or a cost move the bounds by it, and where a market sets that price it absorbs the rate difference; agent edges removed by a rule leave the rates unrelated. **What bears the load is whatever keeps both directions out of reach of any one class, alone or through a chain of trades**, and the record holds two instruments: closing the reverse edge for the class that holds the forward one (Argentina, Comunicación A 8336, September 2025: buyers of official dollars barred from the financial-dollar market for 90 days), and voiding trades between classes (Germany 1990, *"Umgehungsgeschäfte sind nichtig"*, stage B30-22) |
| **proved** | B63-6 `own_reading` what a peg pins and what it leaves free, Corollary 8.5 | A peg adds constraints only on walkable cycles that cross between the two currencies. Every cycle inside one currency's positions, including every square between two domestic classes on a domestic edge, is constrained exactly as it would be without the peg. **The plaquette pins only the difference `r_k - r_l`**; which side moves is decided by who stands on the conversion and which way its capacity runs |
| **written** | B63-7 `bookkeeping` the capacity side, handed to the A track, Corollary 8.6 | With every walking class bounded, a non-zero sum persists while the flow runs at the bound, for capacity over flow. **Sterilization is capacity with a running cost**, the loop sum times the stock absorbed, per period. **Capacity is directed**: bounded by reserves against outflow, and against inflow only by the cost the authority accepts to carry, so a forced exit runs toward depreciation. The round in which a boundary ceiling first binds is stage A25's object |
| PASS | B63-8a `instrument` the plaquette sum is invariant under a change of units and equals its closed form | 1,000 draws, each with a random change of units at the four positions; both orientations within `1e-12` of the closed form |
| PASS | B63-8b `instrument` Corollary 8.1 on random currency graphs | 400 graphs of 3 to 10 currencies. Rates constant on components: no positive cycle in 400 of 400, and the rank count equals the component count in 400 of 400. One rate moved by `0.001`, every forward re-priced: a positive cycle in 327 of the 327 graphs where that currency shares a component, in 0 of the 73 where it is alone. One-way: a directed 3-cycle forces equal rates, and two strongly connected components joined one way stay unrelated in either direction |
| PASS | B63-8c `instrument` Corollary 8.3's band | 20 spread draws, the first with none. The endpoints found by bisection lie within `1e-9` of the closed form, and the draw with no spreads collapses to `r_k = r_l` |

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: with a peg, access both ways
and no bound on capacity, the rate difference lies inside the round-trip friction
band; under a float the covered loop is carried by the forward premium, and one
covered loop returns different net amounts to different holder classes; a control
regime keeps a difference by keeping both directions out of reach of any one class,
and the difference then sits on a square. What the scalar price field reads of it:
`i = i*` under an open peg, zero on the covered loop under a float, and no class
index anywhere.

| cell | content |
|---|---|
| **A** | The open, pegged corner. Both say `r_k = r_l`, and at this locus the enlarged object is the single-price account (Corollary 5.4), so the agreement is an identity |
| **B** | The covered loop under a float. The rival predicts zero, and B3 reads 30.9 to 45.6 bp against a floor of 2.8 to 3.7, nine of nine tenors over eighteen years. Already on the books |
| **D2** | The class-indexed conversion terms of Corollary 8.4. The trilemma literature measures openness with one number per country, built from the IMF's annual report on exchange arrangements, whose categories include multiple exchange rates, so the question lies inside the rival's own scope, and a country scalar has no slot for which class holds which direction |
| **C** | Empty |

**Readings already in this repository that sit under the corollaries**, zero new
data: B3-8, the covered loop between the offshore and onshore renminbi codes, 66.2 to
169.0 bp across seven tenors and largest at three months, under Corollary 8.4 on a single
currency; B24, path against hole on equity lines (16.4 bp median over 465 pairings of
thirty-one companies where a receipt can be cancelled into its home line; 196 times
that where the two lines cannot be exchanged), under Corollaries 8.2 and 8.3; B5 and B17,
Argentina's legal conversion tracks as squares in five of five over 1,457 dates,
under Corollary 8.4's priced agent edge; B30-22 and B32, Germany 1990, a merger done
as a square on the conversion edge at one date, after which the edge is an
identity; B27, the two ways units are kept consistent, deletion and commutation,
which are the control regime and the open peg bloc; A25, the boundary ceiling where
Corollary 8.6's flow side goes.

## A29: a sovereign drawn outside the graph, whose bonds bring parked claims back into it

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Script `experiments/a29_sovereign.py`, record `results/a29_sovereign.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 768 cells, three seeds, nothing fetched.**

The sovereign sets the edge set, so it is drawn outside the graph (ruled 2026-09-11). A
financial-layer node that buys its bonds is parking, which A18 already builds. The proceeds
leave the graph for a pool, and what the pool passes down enters the graph at the receiving
nodes as an in-edge from outside, which the subsistence floor counts as their inflow. Two
knobs: `bond_share`, the share of each round's parking that buys bonds, and `pass_rate`, the
share of the pool passed down each round. In steady state the flow passed down is
`bond_share` times the parking whatever `pass_rate` is, and `pass_rate` sets only the lag. No
bond matures in this round. Registered design: the criteria are written in the script that
produced the record, the record carries their text, and every quantity this run produced is
reported.

**Default off is the module before it, checked and not argued.** The module before the switch
and the module with it ran 23 configurations in one process, among them A18's exit arm with
and without write-off, A18_E, A23, A18_F and every control cell of this grid, and all 27
recorded series agreed bit for bit in all 23. The parking grid's record (430 cells, sha256
`4341f6c2…`) and A23's three-seed record (sha256 `1ec7d927…`) regenerated byte for byte. Both
sides of each comparison ran on the same machine. Both books close in 720 of 720 treated
cells, to 1e-9 of the opening stock and asserted in the round loop: what lands in the graph is
what the pool passed down, and the pool is the bonds bought less everything passed down.

**Passing down and issuance are two exits from one gap, and they trade one for one.** With the
authority issuing, a pass-down of everything the bonds raise takes the authority's issuance to
nothing: 41.5 to 0.0 over 300 rounds at a parking rate of 0.002, 417.7 to 0.1 at 0.02, while
the circulating stock ends slightly higher (97.1 to 99.9, and 91.6 to 98.7). Bonds taking half
the parking halve the issuance, and a quarter cut it by a quarter. The share of the claims
created to keep circulation going that arrives as debt is `bond_share` when the pass-down is
prompt (1.00, 0.53 and 0.27 at 0.002; 1.00, 0.51 and 0.25 at 0.02), and 0.69 to 0.72 at a
mean lag of a hundred rounds, where the authority issues what is still sitting in the pool.
Issuance falls in 120 of 120 groups.

**Without issuance, what keeps the graph alive is the part of the parking that comes back.** At
a parking rate of 0.02 the control drains to a circulating stock of 1.5 out of 100, with all
200 nodes below the floor. A full pass-down holds it at 98.5, 1.08 times what issuance brings
back on the same cells. A tenth of the pool a round gives 86.9 and a hundredth 39.2; bonds
taking half the parking give 11.9 and a quarter give 4.1, because the part that never comes
back keeps draining at its own rate. At 0.002 the order is the same on a smaller scale: a
control of 65.7, then 99.9, 98.5, 87.4, 81.1 and 73.0. Circulation rises in 120 of 120 groups.

**The bond stock is the cumulative parking, and against circulation it climbs in a straight
line.** With every bond's proceeds passed down, bonds over the circulating stock read 0.077,
0.153, 0.229, 0.305, 0.380 and 0.455 at rounds 50, 100, 150, 200, 250 and 299 for a parking
rate of 0.002, and 0.760 to 4.475 for 0.02. That is the parking rate times the number of rounds
times 0.758 and 0.746, the financial layer's share of the circulating stock, at every horizon
and with issuance on or off. Nothing matures, so nothing bends it. With issuance off and bonds
taking a quarter of the parking, the ratio reaches 10.4, since circulation drains and the
bonds stay.

**Where the money lands moves circulation little and decides one thing: whether a block of
nodes below the floor comes back.** The same cell and seed under two landings differ in
circulating stock by a median of 0.05 at wage elasticity 0 and 0.11 at 0.5. At a floor of 0.20
and a parking rate of 0.02 this carrier sits on a two-state edge, with controls at about 75 or
about 150 nodes below the floor depending on the seed. There, with the authority issuing, a
landing on the production side or on every node moves 22 cell-seeds from the upper state to
the lower, some 75 nodes at once, and a landing on the nodes that parked moves none. That
landing ends with more in the accounts (circulating stock +2.90 against +1.27 and +1.43 on
average) and with the same count below the floor (−0.15 against −7.64 and −6.40). No treated
group ends with less circulation than its control.

## A29, second round: bonds that fall due, and who pays for them

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Script `experiments/a29_maturity.py`, record `results/a29_maturity.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 2,112 cells, three seeds, nothing fetched.**

The first round let the sovereign's bonds roll over for ever. On its fullest pass-down the
circulating stock held and the bond stock against it climbed in a straight line. This round
adds the other side of the sovereign's book: a share of the bonds falls due each round
(`maturity_rate`), interest accrues on what is outstanding (`coupon_rate`), and one of three
routes pays. The holders roll it over; the nodes still trading are taxed, either the same share
each (A18_B's levy rule) or in proportion to what they hold above the mean (A6's progressive
base); or claims are created. What a holder is paid enters the graph as an in-edge from outside
and the floor counts it; a levy leaves the graph. Registered design: the criteria are written
in the script that produced the record, the record carries their text, and every quantity this
run produced is reported.

**Default off is the first round, checked and not argued.** The first round's module and this
one ran 41 configurations in one process, and all 31 recorded series agreed bit for bit. The
first round's 96 cells, rerun on this module, match its record exactly, and a rollover at a
zero coupon matches the cell without debt service in 96 of 96. The three books close in 2,112
of 2,112 cells.

**A rollover with interest snowballs, exactly.** At a coupon of 0.02 a round the bond stock
reaches 286 times the circulating stock by round 299, against a closed form of 287.6, and 6.2
times at 0.002 against 6.2. The cash side does not move in any of its 96 groups: the whole cost
sits on the debt ledger.

**A progressive levy bends the line onto its closed-form plateau, and it is close to the
creditors paying themselves.** It collects everything that falls due, and the bond stock settles
at the parking rate times the financial layer's share over the maturity rate: 0.153 of
circulation at a maturity rate of 0.1 and parking 0.02, against 4.55 when bonds never mature,
with measured over closed form between 1.000 and 1.002. 86% of the tax is paid by the financial
layer, which is the layer the bonds are owed to. Circulation moves by a ten-thousandth.

**A levy of the same share on every node does not collect.** Nodes below the floor have nothing
to pay: it collects 84% of maturing principal where fewer than 100 nodes sit below the floor and
58% where more than 150 do, and 25% to 29% of a perpetual coupon of 0.02. Unpaid principal keeps
rolling, so the plateau sits 1.2 to 1.9 times above the closed form; unpaid coupon is added to
the bonds, so a perpetual coupon snowballs anyway, to 40 times circulation, 8 to 10 times the
closed form. Between 62% and 84% of it is paid outside the financial layer, and on this
carrier's two-state edge 27 cell-seeds have a block of about 75 nodes pushed below the floor.

**Issuance turns the debt into money.** The bond stock comes down, and the circulating stock
grows to as much as 65 times the reference's by round 299, because the created money is paid to
holders who park it again and the sovereign passes it down again. 264 of 576 cell-seeds move a
block of nodes back above the floor. This model has no price layer, so what reads here as more
circulation is a larger money stock.

**The authority does not refill what a levy takes.** Its issuance above the reference cell's is
at most 3.8% of what a levy collects, because the pass-down has already returned the money to
the production side and the authority reads that side's inflow.

## B64: the two-tier gold market, and the classes that could still walk the conversion

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Statement and readings in `docs/b64_gold_two_tier.md`. Script
`experiments/b64_gold_two_tier.py`, records `results/b64_checks.json` and
`results/b64_gold_two_tier.json`, each carrying the configuration it ran under.**

The conversion of dollars into gold at 35 was open to monetary authorities at the US
window, and from 1961 the private class reached it through the Gold Pool's sales in
London. Corollary 8.6 of B63 gives the time such an edge can hold as its capacity over
the flow of the classes that can still walk it, and the restrictions of 1967 and 1968
took classes off it one at a time. **On the total gold stock, the Exchange Stabilization
Fund's gold included, the outflow was 207.3 a month in the year before the split of
1968-03-17; the stock then took in gold for the 21 months to the South African
arrangement, and lost 74.0 a month from there to July 1971.** By customer, from the
replication package of Bordo, Monnet and Naef, the United Kingdom's line, through which
the Pool's sales reached US gold, went from -148.5 to +7.2 a month across the split,
while official non-members bought more and France turned seller. The stock stood below
the dollar claims of foreign official holders from the end of 1965, and the window
closed in August 1971.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: the conversion edge carried the
flow of the classes that could still walk it, the flow fell on the class each
restriction cut, and after the window closed the official price moved only up. What a
single price for gold reads of it: the free price at 35 at all times, where it stood as
much as 25.5 percent above 35 with the window open and below 35 by more than a cent on
24 days in 1970. Triffin's condition, the other account on the table, says the system
cannot last once dollar claims exceed the gold stock and gives no date.

The question sits inside Triffin's argument, which gives no time; Corollary 8.6 gives it as capacity over the flow of the classes that can still walk the edge |

## A30: the same shock on structures under different strain

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Script `experiments/a30_shock.py`, record `results/a30_shock.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 1,800 cells, five seeds, nothing fetched.**

One shock, applied at round 150 to three strains, five floors and two wage elasticities,
with the endogenous authority on and off. A freeze moves a share of every live node's
balance out of the trading accounts at the close of round 149 and returns the same amounts
at the close of round 150; a destruction makes the same removal and returns nothing.
Strain uses the model's own quantities: the floor, where 0.20 is this carrier's two-state
edge, and whether a chronic leak is there and recycled (parking at 0.02, and A29's
pass-down onto the production side). Every shocked cell is read against its twin, the same
configuration and seed with no shock. The model is not changed: a driver advances the round
loop and acts only between rounds. Registered design: the criteria are written in the
script that produced the record, the record carries their text, and every quantity this run
produced is reported.

**The driver is the model, checked and not argued.** With no shock it reproduces
`Network.run()` bit for bit on 61 configurations, every recorded series and the closing
state. Every shocked cell's random streams end where its twin's end, so the two runs draw
the same numbers and their difference is the shock's alone. The claim total equals held
plus parked after every round in 1,800 of 1,800 cells, and every freeze comes back node for
node.

**A one-round cut in circulation is gone within two rounds.** With no authority issuing,
435 of 450 frozen cell-seeds are back inside their twin's floor (twice the dispersion across
seeds) within two rounds: 143 of 150 on the healthy structure, 142 on the recycled leak, 150
on the leak. On the healthy structure a freeze of three tenths reads −27.0% at the shock
round, −0.97% the next and −0.09% the one after. The 15 that take longer are almost all
cells where a block of about 75 nodes went below the floor for a round, and there too the
block came back.

**An authority that issues into the dip, and never takes back, leaves a healthy economy
permanently larger.** With the authority on, the same freeze reads +4.0% the round after
and settles at +6.0% for good; freezes of one, three and five tenths settle at +1.6%, +6.0%
and +10.7% in flow. The extra is what the authority issued after the shock, 0.18 to 0.23 of
the amount frozen: the rule issues the shortfall of the Layer 2 inflow below its round-0
level and has no branch that takes anything back, and the frozen claims return on top of
it. On the leaking structure, where the authority issues every round anyway, a freeze of
three or five tenths is worked off in 6 to 9 rounds and the tail reads 1.000.

**A destruction of claims stays, in proportion, unless something issues it back.** With no
authority the healthy structure's circulating stock settles at 0.900 and 0.700 of its
twin's after a destruction of one and three tenths, exactly what was left, and the gap
never closes: nothing in the model rebuilds a destroyed claim. With the authority on, the
loss is issued back only down to the authority's target, and the part of it above the
target is not issued back at all. Of a one-tenth loss, 0.73 comes back on the healthy
structure at wage elasticity 0, whose twin stood 3.0% above the target when the shock hit,
and 0.98 at 0.5 (0.9% above); 0.24 and 0.48 on the recycled leak, whose pass-down onto
the production side had lifted the Layer 2 inflow 7.1% and 5.7% above it; 0.97 on the
leak, whose twin sat 4.6% below it and which is refilled back to the twin's own path.

**One shock knocks a block under only on the edge, and only where the good state is held
up by recycling.** Of 1,500 shocked cell-seeds, 15 end with a block of 50 or more nodes more
below the floor than the twin, and 14 of them are in one cell: floor 0.20, the recycled
leak, wage elasticity 0.5. Its twins sit at 75 to 78 nodes below the floor; the healthy
twins on the same floor and elasticity sit at 150 to 153, so the good state there is the
pass-down's. A destruction of one or three tenths sends about 75 nodes under in the shock
round or the next: 10 of 10 stay under with no authority, 4 of 10 with it, where the other
6 are issued back after 2 to 8 rounds. A freeze sends the same block under for 1 to 3
rounds, and it comes back in 30 of 30. On floors of 0.05, 0.10 and 0.50 no block ends up
moved. The fifteenth is on the floor of 0.15 and flickers between the two states for about
ten rounds before it settles under; and one freeze of five tenths, with the authority
issuing, lifts a block the other way, out of a twin in the lower state.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`instrument` 2 pass · `own_reading` 3 printed · `bookkeeping` 1 pass

## B65: the post-Keynesian core, as a special case of the enlarged graph

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Statement and proof in `docs/b65_post_keynesian.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b65_pk_flow_side.py`, record `results/b65_pk_flow_side.json`, which carries
the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

Three objects carry the post-Keynesian account of demand and distribution, and each is a
case of an object this repository already uses. **Stock-flow consistency is Kirchhoff's
current law** for a flow on the enlarged graph of sectors by instruments, with stocks on the
time edges and the sovereign as an outside node. **Theorem 1 is its dual**: a field is exact
exactly when it pairs to zero with every circulation, so under a single price vector a
stock-flow-consistent circuit creates no value, and what any circuit creates is bounded by
the distance of Theorem 5, which one such circuit therefore bounds from below (Theorem 9).
**A sectoral model is a quotient of the graph.** The projection keeps Kirchhoff's law for
any partition, and with connected blocks it loses exactly the circulations inside the
blocks, a number that can be counted; take the blocks to be the manuscript's layers and
spending by the financial layer on the financial layer is one of them, which is the precise
form of Volume One's statement that spending inside a layer is functionally saving
(Lemma 9.1). **The markup is the sum of the production cycle**, money to hours to goods and
back, a slice cycle of the producing class: free entry with no bound on quantity puts it at
zero, a bound on quantity lets it persist, and a cost of entry caps it at the limit price
(Theorem 10). **Kalecki's profit equation is Kirchhoff's law on a four-block quotient**, and
the profits it names are the value the production cycle creates on the cost bill
(Corollaries 10.1 and 10.2). Godley and Lavoie's redundant equation, the one their models
leave out of the solution and check afterwards, is the equation at the last node, one per
component (Proposition 9.0).

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 3 proved, 2 proved as restated · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 4 pass ·
`bookkeeping` 1 written

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: stock-flow consistency is Kirchhoff's
law on the enlarged graph, and the value any consistent circuit creates is the pairing of the
field with it, zero exactly when the field has a single price vector; a sectoral model sees
every flow between sectors and none of the cycles inside them; the markup is the sum of the
production cycle, persistent under a bound on quantity and capped by the cost of entry. What
the scalar price field reads of it: every cycle sums to zero, the production cycle included,
so there is no profit over full unit cost. What the post-Keynesian account reads of it: the
accounting identities, the profit equation, and markup pricing with the degree of monopoly
limited by the barriers to entry, with sectors as the units of account.

| cell | content |
|---|---|
| **A** | The three balances, Kalecki's equation and the redundant equation: identities on both sides, and on this side consequences of Kirchhoff's law on a quotient. The limit price: Theorem 10(c) gives the same cap as Bain and Sylos Labini |
| **B** | The production cycle against the scalar price field, which sets every cycle to zero. This station measures no markup, so the cell is registered and left out of the count |
| **D** | Two quantities no account asks for: the cycles a sectoral model loses, `Σ_r b₁(Γ[B_r])` by Lemma 9.1, and the lower bound on `ρ(ω)` that one consistent circuit gives, `\|⟨ω, x⟩\| / ‖x‖` by Theorem 9 |
| **C** | Empty |

**What this station places, and what it leaves where it found it.** It places the accounting
and the price side: the identities, the sectoral aggregation, the markup and the profit
equation. The behavioural half stays behavioural on both sides. What sets consumption out of
income and wealth, what sets investment, what sets the bound `D` that effective demand puts
on the cycle, and how a portfolio is split between instruments are functions the modeller
supplies, here as there; the enlarged graph says where those flows live and what a circuit
made of them can create, and it does not say how large they are.

## A31: the issuance rule's other side, and whose accounts it comes out of

**RUN: 2026-09-11. Script `experiments/a31_withdrawal.py`, record
`results/a31_withdrawal.json`, which carries the configuration it ran under. 3,850 cells,
five seeds, nothing fetched.**

A30 read a one-round freeze settling a structure without a chronic gap permanently larger,
and a destruction of claims issued back only down to the level the endogenous rule aims at,
because that rule issues the Layer 2 inflow's shortfall below its round-0 level and has no
branch that takes anything back. This station gives it that branch, and asks what the branch
opens: the rule pins one aggregate while the subsistence floor is read per node, so whose
accounts the claims come out of could decide who ends up below the floor with the aggregate
pinned either way. Three positions, each a set this model already names: the financial
layer, which is where the issuance lands; every live node; and every live node outside the
financial layer, which is the set the sovereign's pass-down pays into. Each takes pro rata
to what an account holds, capped at it, at two gains. Four shocks at round 150 on A30's
driver and carrier: a freeze, a destruction, and, where the parked stock is latent claims
and nothing else, a release of it. Registered design: the criteria are written in the script
that produced the record, the record carries their text, and every quantity this run
produced is reported.

**Off is the module before it, and A30's record comes back out of it.** The module before
the switch and the module now ran 85 configurations in one process, among them A18's exit
arms, A18_E, A23, A18_F, A29 with its debt served, and every base cell of A30's grid: 46
fields including the closing state compared bit for bit, 0 differ, and the three new columns
are None in every run. The driver with no shock is `Network.run()` on the same 85. A30's 360
recorded rows, recomputed through this module and this driver, agree in all eight fields.
The withdrawal's own ledger closes in 3,850 of 3,850 cells, with nothing uncollected and no
account taken below zero.

**The aggregate is pinned whichever accounts it comes out of.** The Layer 2 inflow over the
rule's target in the tail: one-sided, +1.9% on the healthy structure and +6.5% on the
recycled leak; two-sided, −0.0001 at gain 1.0 and +0.0009 at 0.5. What the pinning costs the
circulating stock against the one-sided twin: 0.979 healthy, 0.930 on the recycled leak, and
1.000 on the leak, whose inflow sits below the target and has nothing to take back.

**Who pays does not change who ends up below the floor.** Of 60 carrier-and-gain cells, 58
leave the same block state under all three positions, and two are split across seeds with
the three positions splitting the same way. Over all 300 seed-by-seed comparisons the
positions never differ: they return the same integer difference in the count below the
floor. Inside a cell the three differ by a median of 0.0016 in the circulating stock ratio
and 0.20 in what they take. A block moves in one cell only, floor 0.20 on the recycled leak
at wage elasticity 0.5, where 2 of 5 seeds lose about 75 nodes under every position and both
gains.

**What washes the position out is the trade.** A side probe on that cell and seed, script
`experiments/a31_mixing_probe.py` and record `results/a31_mixing_probe.json`, prints the
closing distribution under each position: the per-node shares of the tail stock differ
between the production position and the financial position by at most 1.26e-04 and between
the proportional and the financial by 2.2e-05, at correlations of 0.999999 and above, and
the Layer 2 share of the stock reads 0.2548, 0.2552 and 0.2553 against the one-sided rule's
0.2598. Spending is pro rata to what an account holds and so is the withdrawal, so a
position changes the level and the graph mixes the shape back within rounds. The level is
what moves the block: the one-sided stock is 1.06205 times the two-sided one there, and the
per-node shares of those two differ by 7.95e-04.

**The overshoot goes back, and the refill becomes whole.** Under the one-sided rule a freeze
of three tenths settles above its twin in 100 of 150 cells, at 1.0496 of it. Under all six
two-sided rules it is back inside the floor in 150 of 150, at 1.000, with 0.205 to 0.230 of
what was frozen taken back, which is what A30 measured the rule issuing into the dip. A
destruction of one tenth settles below its twin in 80 of 150 one-sided cells, at 0.9865,
recovering 0.85 and leaving two blocks under; under every two-sided rule it is back at
1.000, recovering 1.000, with no block under anywhere. A30's partial refill was the twin's
headroom over the target, so taking that headroom back leaves a refill nothing to miss.

**A rule that moves both ways rings, at a tenth of the gap it removes.** On the twins the
gap against the target changes sign 137 to 159 times over 299 rounds and the rule withdraws
in 144 to 185 of them, while the mean absolute gap reads 0.0032 against the one-sided rule's
steady 0.0488. At gain 0.5 it rings less often, withdraws in more rounds, takes back less
(10.8 against 15.7) and leaves the tail gap slightly wider.

**A latent pool coming back is absorbed either way, and the position sets the speed.** On
the leak, releasing a tenth of the parked stock is back inside the floor in 13 rounds under
the one-sided rule, which answers it by issuing 0.90 of the released amount less. The
two-sided rules take back 0.19 to 0.42 of it and are back in 7 to 10 rounds, fastest where
the claims came back, which is the financial layer. At three tenths the one-sided rule takes
33 rounds and the two-sided 8.5 to 18. No block moves in any of the 700 release cells, and
every tail reads 1.000.

## B66: the edges a sovereign posts, and where two mechanisms of modern monetary theory live

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b66_mmt.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b66_mmt_check.py`, record `results/b66_mmt_check.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

A sovereign is drawn outside the graph as the party that sets its edges (stage A29), and it
posts three kinds of edge: an obligation payable in the unit it names, an enforcement that
says what leaving the obligation costs, and a price at which it offers to trade a position.
**Theorem 11.** Summed over the nodes dated at or before `t`, Kirchhoff's law leaves the stock
of the unit held inside the graph equal to the sovereign's cumulative spending less its
cumulative receipts; with no class inside able to issue it, that stock cannot be negative, so
**the unit is issued before it is collected**. The two routes for discharging one unit of the
obligation, buying the unit at its goods price `p` or paying the enforcement `κ`, close a
square of sum `log(κ / p)`; **both point into the obligation, which is a sink, so no class can
walk it**: (NA) says nothing and the sign of the sum decides which route carries the flow. A
tax therefore makes a demand the size of the bill for the unit it is payable in, at any price
below the enforcement and none above it, and with two acceptable units it drives the cheaper.
**Corollary 11.1.** A job guarantee is a price posted one way on labour hours. Where hours do
not pass between classes its edge lies on no cycle and the guarantee acts on the flow side, so
hours reach an employer below its wage only from classes it does not admit or beyond what it
can take; where an agent edge passes hours at a cost `c`, the square closes in one orientation
and gives one side of a band, `W ≥ W_JG / (1 + c)` with no upper bound; and where the
programme is bounded, Corollary 8.6 returns the gap on the hours it cannot take.
**Corollary 11.2.** An edge bears on the field only through the walkable cycles that contain
it, **which is a question about the cycle and not about the direction**: one-way edges chain
into directed cycles and pin terms there, while an edge open both ways pins nothing if it
hangs on no cycle. **Corollary 11.3.** A posted wage reaches goods prices through the
production cycle of Theorem 10, `p ≥ (1 + μ)·W_JG·l`, so it carries the markup with it and
moves goods prices by different amounts according to whether that markup is pinned.

**Four further claims of that literature are readings of stations already on the books**, and
§2 of the file points at them rather than proving them again: the sectoral balance identity is
Corollary 10.1 of B65; bonds trading one for one against issuance is A29's first round, and
what falls due is its second; the floor paid on balances is B59, a posted price that reaches
the classes on one regulation's list; and monetary sovereignty is what B63's corollaries leave
free.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: a tax makes a demand for the unit it is
payable in, of the size of the bill and only below the enforcement, and it drives whichever
acceptable unit is cheapest to obtain; the issuer's cumulative deficit is the stock of its unit
held by everyone else and cannot be negative; a guarantee posted one way floors the wage of
those it admits on the flow side, gives one side of a band on the field only where hours pass
between classes, and reaches exactly the cycles that cross it. What that literature reads of
it: a tax liability creates sellers against the state's unit, the issuer spends first and
collects afterwards, the deficit is the other sectors' surplus, and the source of the price
level is the prices the government pays. What the scalar price field reads of it: it has no
place for the tax edge or for the class that holds it, and a guarantee is a floor in one
labour market.

This station measures no wage, so the cell is registered and left out of the count |
| **D2** | The two bounds on what a tax can do: the bill sizes the demand, the enforcement caps the price at which it exists. The question is that literature's own central mechanism, and it names the enforcement without pricing it |
