**What the station leaves where it found it.** The behavioural half stays behavioural on both
sides: what sets consumption, what sets investment, how large the bound on a programme is, and
what any enforcement is worth are inputs here as there. **The registered carrier for the
one-sided band was gated on 2026-09-12 and no station was opened**, because the two programmes
registered for it fail on opposite gates. **India's MGNREGA has the gradient and not the
object**: its statutory wage is notified by state and by year, so the treatment varies widely,
but Schedule I paragraph 11 of the 2005 Act reads `The Scheme shall not permit engaging any
contractor for implementation of the projects under it`, which puts it on the side of this
station's own switch where hours do not pass between classes, and there Corollary 11.1 says the
edge lies on no cycle and there is no band to read. **Argentina's Jefes de Hogar has the object
and not the gradient**: beneficiaries could take employment in a private company on a wage
subsidy, so the hours did pass and the edge composes into a cycle, but the benefit was a
uniform 150 pesos a month nationally, so the treatment takes one value. **The registration is
therefore rewritten as a specification**: a programme whose hours a private employer can obtain
at the posted wage, **and** whose posted wage varies across units. Both are needed. **The same reading raised and then closed a second
question**: MGNREGA was replaced by the VB-G RAM G Act of 2025, and whether that Act kept the
contractor prohibition decided whether this switch flipped on a dated boundary. **It kept it.**
Schedule I paragraph 21(1) of the new Act reads `No contractor shall be engaged for the
execution of any work or component financed through expenditure under this Act`, and section 10
still has the Central Government notify wage rates with `different wage rates may be notified by
the Central Government for different areas`. **So India sits on the same side of the switch
before and after, the dated boundary does not exist, and that line is closed by an answer rather
than left open for want of one.**

## B67: prices of production, as the configuration in which every production cycle carries the same sum

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b67_prices_of_production.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b67_prices_of_production.py`, record `results/b67_prices_of_production.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B65's Theorem 10 puts the markup on a cycle and leaves every class its own. **The classical
theory of prices adds one equation: all of those sums are equal**, and that equation, written
out, is Sraffa's price system. **Theorem 12.** With one class per industry and one set of
commodity prices, the condition `∮ C_j = c` for every industry is
`p_j = (1 + r)·Σ_i p_i a_ij + w l_j` with `1 + r = e^c` when wages are paid out of the
product, and `p_j = (1 + r)(Σ_i p_i a_ij + w l_j)` when they are advanced: **the convention is
which edges lie on the loop.** The solutions are a one-parameter family in `r` with the wage
falling, ending at `1 + R = 1/λ_PF(A)` where the wage is zero and `p` is the left
Perron-Frobenius eigenvector; with the standard system scaled to one unit of labour and its net
product as the unit of account the wage is exactly `1 − r/R`. **Against the potential the
prices themselves give, the field departs by `log(1 + r)` on every production edge and by
nothing anywhere else**, so `ρ(ω) = c_Γ·log(1 + r)` with `c_Γ` a number of the graph, `√(n/3)`
for the graph drawn here: **the invariant is the sum on one cycle, and the distance aggregates
it, so it counts how the graph was drawn.** **Corollary 12.1**: Kalecki and Sraffa are that one
equation apart. **Corollary 12.2**: with the cycles walkable and unbounded, (NA) forces the
rate to zero, and with every producer bounded it reaches none of them, so **a uniform positive
rate of profits is not a no-arbitrage conclusion**; it needs a bound and a flow that moves to
the higher sum, which is what the classical postulate has to deliver. **Corollary 12.3**: the
value advanced is read off the field and the field moves with `r`, so no quantity read off
prices orders techniques independently of the rate. **Corollary 12.4**: the standard commodity
is the right eigenvector and the prices at `R` the left one, so at the top of the family the
field side and the flow side are the two eigenvectors of one matrix.

**This is the third station in a row to land on the same shape.** The tax and the job guarantee
of B66 act on flows because their edges lie on no walkable cycle; here the cycles exist and a
bound takes (NA) off them. What decides in every case is Corollary 11.2's test: an edge bears
on the terms only through the walkable cycles that contain it.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: prices of production are the
configuration in which every production cycle carries the same sum; the configurations form a
one-parameter family ending where the wage vanishes; the whole departure from a single price
vector sits on the production edges; a uniform positive rate needs a bound and a flow that
responds; and any ordering of techniques by a quantity read off prices moves with the rate.
What the classical account reads of it: the price equations, the maximum rate, the standard
commodity, the linear frontier in standard units, and reswitching. What the scalar price field
reads of it: every cycle sums to zero, so no profit over full unit cost and a rate of zero.

## A31, second round: the same pinned aggregate, taken in three shapes

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Script `experiments/a31_shape.py`, record `results/a31_shape.json`, which

The first round moved the position the claims come out of and read no difference at all: the
three positions left the same integer below the floor in 300 seed comparisons, because all
three take pro rata to what a node holds while spending is pro rata to what a node holds as
well, so trading puts the distribution back within a few rounds. This round moves the shape
instead. `WithdrawSpec.base` splits the same amount inside the same position three ways: pro
rata to holdings, the same amount from every node inside the position that holds something, or
in proportion to the part above the mean, which is A6's progressive base. The gain is fixed at
1.0, since the first round read it as a speed knob. Registered design: the criteria are written
in the script that produced the record, the record carries their text, and every quantity this
run produced is reported.

**Default off is the first round, checked and not argued.** The module before this field and the
module with it ran 103 configurations in one process, among them the library default, A18's exit
arm with and without write-off, A18_E, A23, A18_F, A29's control and treated cells, every base
cell of A30's grid, and the first round's own two-sided cells with the base at its default: 46
history fields and the closing state compared bit for bit, 0 differ, and the generators end in
the same place. The driver with no shock against `Network.run()`: 0 differ. The first round's 770
recorded rows recomputed on this module: 17 fields each, 0 differ. The books close in 5,500 of
5,500 cells to 1e-9 of the opening stock, asserted in the round loop; the Layer 2 share of what
was taken is 0 in every financial cell and 1 in every production cell, 0 out of place.

**The three shapes take from visibly different people, and that is measured before the reading
rather than assumed.** Layer 2's share of what was taken has a median of 0.251 pro rata, 0.824
in equal amounts and 0.148 above the mean, a factor of 5.6 between the last two. Equal amounts
leave 3.4% of what the rule asked for uncollected, where the other two leave nothing. At one

layer, 50/50/40 across every node and 30/30/28 on the production side, and the per-node take
share differs from pro rata by up to 0.063 to 0.113. The first round's three positions differed

**The count below the floor is the same integer in all of it.** 450 comparisons of three bases
at a fixed carrier, position and seed: 0 differ. Nine one-application probes, with the history
identical behind them and the amount asked identical in all three: 0 differ.

**And the instrument does move a block, which is what makes that zero a reading.** Over 1,350
two-sided cell-seeds read against the one-sided twin, the difference in the count below the
floor takes three values: 0 in 1,287 of them, 1 in 45, and 75 in 18. So a block of 75 nodes goes
under in 18 cell-seeds, and in all 18 the three shapes move it on the same seeds. The three

**What is pinned is the setpoint, not the amount collected and not the incidence.** The Layer 2
inflow over the rule's own target, averaged over the last 50 rounds: the one-sided reference
sits at +0.0271 and the three bases at -0.000115, -9.1e-05 and -0.000116. Meanwhile the

per round collects for longer, and the state it holds is the same. So the first round's wording,
that the aggregate decides, is better read as the setpoint decides, and the first round's
section carries that pointer.

**The two rounds wash out their variable for different reasons, and the difference is the
result.** The first round washed out the position because trading returns the distribution
within a few rounds. This round washes out the shape because the rule's setpoint is the same

## B68: the labour values as the member of that family at a zero rate, and the transformation as the move along it

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b68_value_field.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b68_value_field.py`, record `results/b68_value_field.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B67 left the classical price system as a one-parameter family in the rate of profits. **This
station names two members of it and asks what holds still on the way between them.**
**Theorem 13.** The price equations at `r = 0` and `w = 1` are the labour value equations
`v = v A + l`, term for term, so the values are the member of the family at a zero rate with
labour as the unit of account. On that member every production cycle sums to zero, so the field
is exact and `ρ(ω) = 0`; at every positive rate the cycles sum to `log(1 + r) ≠ 0` and `ρ > 0`,
so **the value scheme is the one member of the family with a potential**. The map from the
values to the prices at a rate is `p(r) = w(r)·l (I − (1 + r) A)^{-1}`, explicit and single
valued on `0 ≤ r < R`: **whether a transformation exists is answered by a formula, and what is
at issue is which magnitudes hold still along it.** **Corollary 13.1**: an aggregate is a
pairing of the field with a flow, in the sense of Theorem 9, so which aggregates hold still is
fixed by which flow is paired. The total value of the net product is the labour employed;
pricing the net product at its value is a choice of unit and asserts nothing; and with that
unit `Π − S = L (v·b − p·b)`, so **the total profits equal the total surplus value exactly when
the wage basket costs what it is worth**, which a basket in the net product's proportions does.
Prices stay proportional to values along the family exactly under equal composition, which is
`v` proportional to `l`. **Corollary 13.2**: with the wage advanced, `1 + r = 1/λ_PF(A + b l)`
and `r > 0` exactly when `v·b < 1`, which is the Fundamental Marxian Theorem of Okishio (1963)
and Morishima (1973) read on the cycles: **every production cycle carries a positive sum exactly
when the wage basket is worth less than the labour that buys it.** The step it turns on is
`v (A + b l) = v − (1 − v·b) l`: the augmented matrix moves the value vector down by the
surplus and by nothing else. **Corollary 13.3**: buy the normal return on the advance along
with the inputs and the bundle costs exactly what the product sells for, so every cycle sums to
zero at every rate, while `p`, `w` and `r` are the same numbers. **So "no profit over full
cost" and "every cycle carries log(1 + r)" are two drawings of one configuration**, and the
rate is what does not move when the drawing does. **It follows that `ρ` is not a measure of the
gap between values and prices: the gap is the family's parameter.** That freedom exists exactly
where an edge weight is imputed by whoever keeps the accounts, and not where both legs are
posted, which is why the empirical arm reads posted terms. **Corollary 13.4**: the value
scheme, the price scheme and the long-run competitive scheme each carry one number per
commodity, that is, each takes the class graph to a single vertex, so there are no squares and
the whole disagreement among them lies in `H¹(G)`.

**This is the fourth station in a row to land on the same shape.** B65 put the markup on a
cycle, B66 found that an edge bears on terms only through the walkable cycles containing it,
B67 added the one equation that makes those sums equal, and here the family that equation
defines turns out to contain the labour values at one end. **What separates the accounts is
which equation is imposed and where the edges are drawn, and what is invariant under both is
the sum on one cycle.**

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: the labour values are the member of the
classical family at a zero rate and the only exact one; the transformation is the move along a
family with one parameter; an aggregate is a pairing of the field with a flow, so which
aggregates hold still is fixed by which flow is paired; and whether the normal return is a cost
or a profit is a choice of drawing, under which the rate is invariant and the distance is not.
What the Marxian account reads of it: the value equations, the two aggregate equalities, and
the Fundamental Marxian Theorem in its modern form. What the Sraffian account reads of it: the
price equations, the family, the standard commodity, and the demonstration that the two
aggregate equalities do not hold together in general.

| **D2** | **What type of statement each aggregate equality is.** That dispute asks which of the two is the true invariant and treats it as a question about the price transformation; here the first is a choice of unit and the second a statement about one number, and invariance is a property of the flow that is paired. The question is the tradition's own and the flow side is not in it |
| **D** | `ρ` as a function of the rate, the reading that the value scheme is the unique exact member, and the reading that the cost-or-profit question is answered by a drawing. No account asks for these |
| **C** | Empty, and this station cannot produce it: it reads no data, so no point prediction of any other account is scored here |

**Where a specialisation and an account's own statement of itself come apart.** Drawing an
established account out of this framework term for term is what a more general statement owes a
narrower one, and each such derivation is recorded above as a common answer. Where the two come
apart, the place to look first is the explanation the narrower account gives of its own result:
which causal claim carries the weight, whether a term keeps one sense from the premise to the
conclusion, and whether the instrument applied takes the object the claim is about. **The
phenomena those accounts report are carried by large literatures; their explanations are
written by each account separately and contradict one another.**

**Registered, not scheduled.** The falling rate of profits is a movement of `(A, l)` over
time, that is, the family itself moving, so it needs a mechanism for the direction of technical
change, which this framework does not supply: outside scope rather than queued. **Okishio's
theorem, registered here as algebra of the same kind as Corollary 13.2, was done on 2026-09-12
as B69 below, where it turns out to be the same bound at a second member of this family.

where the sign turns out to be a statement about the cone of feasible net outputs.**

## B69: Okishio's theorem as the same bound evaluated at a second member of the same family

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b69_okishio.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b69_okishio.py`, record `results/b69_okishio.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B68 proved the Fundamental Marxian Theorem by putting the labour value vector into the
Collatz-Wielandt bound on the augmented matrix `M = A + b l`. **That vector is one member of
the family of Theorem 13; this station puts in a second one.** **Theorem 14.** With the real
wage basket held fixed in kind and one industry's method replaced, `M` and `M'` agree off the
changed column, so `(p M')_j = λ p_j` for every other `j`, and the two-sided bound gives
`r' > r` when the new column is cheaper at the prevailing prices, `r' < r` when it is dearer,
and `r' = r` when the cost is equal. **The sign of the change in the general rate of profit is
the sign of the cost saving on the one column that changed, read at the prices in force: an
equivalence, of which Okishio's 1961 theorem is one half.** Strictness needs `M'` irreducible,
which holds automatically when the basket contains every commodity, since then `b l' > 0`
entrywise. Read on the cycles, the cost criterion is exactly the statement that **the new
method's production cycle shows an excess over the `log(1 + r)` every other cycle is
carrying**, and the theorem says that excess survives the re-solving of the whole field rather
than turning negative. Third clause: `r'` is continuous and strictly decreasing in a
proportional rise of the basket, so **every cost-reducing substitution has exactly one rise in
the wage basket that cancels its gain**, and that number is computed here rather than asserted.
**Corollary 14.1**: for any positive row vector `u`, `λ_PF(M) ≤ max_j (u M)_j / u_j`; the
family `u(r₀) = l (I − (1 + r₀) A)^{-1}` supplies the test vectors; `u(0)` is the labour value
vector and gives the Fundamental Marxian Theorem, and `p = (1 + r)(p·b)·u(r)` is the family's
member at the actual rate and gives Theorem 14. **The two theorems are one inequality
evaluated at two points of one family**, and the members between them give bounds no account
has asked for. **Corollary 14.2**: put dates in the positions, as in B63's product with dates,
and a production cycle's two legs sit at different vertices, so its sum takes both `p_t` and
`p_{t+1}` and is not a function of the technique and the basket alone; the stationary case is
the quotient by the date shift. **So the long dispute about this theorem is a question about
which graph is drawn**, and which graph fits an economy is a fact about that economy: were the
inputs bought at other dates, and at other prices, than the outputs were sold. This station
does not adjudicate it and implements neither side's valuation rule.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 4 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 4 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

All five computed criteria are read off one shared sample of **1,800 draws**: a system of 3 to
8 industries from stage A19's generator, a wage basket whose labour value is `0.3`, `0.5` or
`0.7`, and a substitution in one industry drawn by scaling that column entrywise in
`[0.6, 1.4]`, which preserves the zero pattern and so the irreducibility.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| **proved** | B69-1 `own_reading` the sign of the change is the sign of the saving, Theorem 14(1) and (2) | The two matrices agree off the changed column, so both extrema of `(p M')_j / p_j` are still attained at `λ`, and the upper bound gives Okishio's half while the lower one gives its converse. **Stated here as an equivalence rather than an implication**, with strictness automatic when the basket contains every commodity. The criterion read on the cycles is an excess sum in the field in force |
| **proved** | B69-2 `own_reading` the basket carries the conclusion, Theorem 14(3) | `M'(g) = A' + (1 + g) b l'` rises entrywise, so `r'(g)` falls strictly and continuously to `−1`: **every cost-reducing substitution has exactly one basket rise that cancels its gain.** The direction the rate moves is fixed by the technique and the basket together, and this framework supplies no law for how either moves |
| **proved** | B69-3 `own_reading` one bound, a family of test vectors, Corollary 14.1 | `p = (1 + r)(p·b)·u(r)` follows from the price equation, so the price vector is the family's member at the actual rate up to the unit of account. **The Fundamental Marxian Theorem is that bound at `u(0)` and this station's theorem is that bound at `u(r)`** |

| PASS | B69-6a `instrument` the cost criterion is a cycle sum | The old field's cycle for the changed industry carries `log(1 + r)` to `4.3e-15`, and the same cycle with the new method carries more **exactly when** the new column is cheaper, 1,800 of 1,800, cheaper and dearer alike; smallest excess in absolute value `1.7e-5` |

The tightest member is `0.25 R` on 594 draws, `0.5 R` on 552 and `0.1 R` on 254: **usually neither of the two ends that carry a named theorem** |
| PASS | B69-6d `instrument` the cancelling rise in the basket | Found by bisection for all 915 cheaper substitutions inside a window of 20 times the basket: median `0.0541` of the basket, range `0.0000` to `1.6163`. **A technical change that raises the rate a little is cancelled by a wage rise of a few per cent** |

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: the sign of the change in the general
rate of profit is the sign of the cost saving on the changed column at the prevailing prices,
in both directions; that criterion is an excess cycle sum in the field in force; the conclusion
is carried by the fixed basket and the cancelling rise is computable; the theorem is one bound
at a second member of the price family; and the dispute about the theorem is a question about
whether positions carry dates. What the Marxian account reads of it: the theorem as an
implication, and a long literature disputing what it settles about the tendency of the rate of
profit to fall.

The question is both sides' own and the discriminant is in neither |
| **D** | The equivalence in both directions rather than the published implication; the cost criterion read as an excess cycle sum; the cancelling basket rise as a computed number; and the family of test vectors, of which two members are named theorems and the rest are bounds nobody asks for |
| **C** | Empty, and this station cannot produce it: it reads no data, so no point prediction of any other account is scored here |

**Registered, not scheduled.** A carrier where Corollary 14.2 can be measured, which needs the

## B70: joint production, where the cycles and the commodities stop being the same index set

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b70_joint_production.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b70_joint_production.py`, record `results/b70_joint_production.json`, which
carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B67 drew one production cycle per industry, and under single production that is also one cycle
per commodity. **Joint production separates those two index sets, and every difficulty this
literature reports follows from that.** **Theorem 15.** With `n` processes and `m` commodities,
input matrix `A` and output matrix `B`, the cycle's sale leg carries the whole output bundle:
`(p B)_j − w l_j` against a bundle costing `(p A)_j`. (1) **The `n` cycle sums are all equal to
one number if and only if `p B = (1 + r) p A + w l`**, and nothing in that proof used single
production; the identity between the legs is algebraic and holds at any signs, while the cycle
sum is a logarithm only where both legs are positive, which under joint production is a
restriction with content because a price can come out negative. (2) **The drawn graph has
`b₁ = n`, one independent cycle per process, and that number never mentions `m`.** The price
equations are `n` equations in `m` unknowns, so `n = m` gives one price vector per rate, `n < m`
leaves it undetermined on a subspace of dimension `m − n`, and `n > m` leaves no exact solution
at all. **The classical square system is the coincidence of two index sets, which here reads
`b₁ = m`, and the inequality methods are what one does when they come apart.** Under single
production each commodity has a cycle of its own; in general the per-commodity price is a
coordinate obtained from the cycle data rather than a primitive of the graph. (3) With
`v (B − A) = l` and `x_i = (B − A)^{-1} e_i` the activity delivering one net unit of commodity
`i` and nothing else, `v_i = l · x_i`, so **`v_i < 0` forces a negative component in `x_i`: one
unit of that commodity on its own is not a feasible net output, and the number called its value
is the labour of an activity nobody can run**; conversely a non-negative inverse gives strictly
positive values. **Corollary 15.1**: a machine of constant efficiency lasting `T` periods is
this system with the machine's age as a position, exactly as the date is in B69's Corollary
14.2, so **the value of a part-worn machine is a coordinate of the price field and the
depreciation schedule falls out of the price equations**: at `r = 0` the recursion makes the
price fall by the same amount every period, so the schedule is straight-line, and at `r > 0` the
solution is `C(1 + r)^j − K/r`, which is linear in `j` only if the schedule is constant, which
`p_T = 0` with `p_0 > 0` forbids. **Straight-line depreciation is the zero-rate member of a
family, as the labour values are in B68.** **Corollary 15.2**: every construction here writes
one number per commodity, or per commodity and age, so the class graph is still a point and the
square summand is still empty. **Negative values, several rates or none, undetermined or
inconsistent price systems: all of it is on the position side, and it arrives while the class
index is still absent.**

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 4 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 5 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| **proved** | B70-1 `own_reading` the characterisation survives, Theorem 15(1) | Equal cycle sums are the price equations with the sale leg carrying the bundle, and single production is nowhere in the proof. **Added to the design**: the identity between the legs is algebraic at any signs, while the cycle sum needs both legs positive, and joint production can push a price below zero |
| **proved** | B70-2 `own_reading` one cycle per process, Theorem 15(2) | `b₁ = E − V + 1 = n`, which never mentions the commodity count. `n = m` is the square assumption read as `b₁ = m`; below it the price vector is undetermined on a subspace, above it there is no exact solution. **The per-commodity price is a coordinate, not a primitive** |
| **proved** | B70-3 `own_reading` a negative value is about the feasible cone, Theorem 15(3) | `v_i = l · x_i` with `x_i` the activity delivering one net unit of `i` alone, so a negative value forces a negative activity level: **that unit cannot be produced at all, and the sign is a fact about what the technique can deliver** |
| **proved** | B70-4 `own_reading` fixed capital and the depreciation schedule, Corollary 15.1 | The machine's age is a position, and the schedule is a coordinate of the field: straight-line exactly at `r = 0`, and at no positive rate, since the recursion's multiplier is `1 + r` |
| PASS | B70-5 `known_answer` Steedman's example | Two processes, `5` of commodity 1 and one labour giving `6` and `1`, and `10` of commodity 2 and one labour giving `3` and `12`. **Ten published numbers read back with a worst gap of exactly zero**: values `(−1, 2)`, activity `(5, 1)` for the net product `(8, 7)`, labour `6`, the workers' bundle `(3, 5)` needing `(9, −2)` so `V = 7`, the capitalists' bundle `(5, 2)` needing `(−4, 3)` so `S = −1`, and `L − V = −1`. **The rate comes out at exactly `0.20` with prices `(1, 3)` and a wage of `3`** |
| PASS | B70-6a `instrument` the legs and the cycle sums | 400 systems at five rates, 2,000 solvable points: the sale leg is `(1 + r)` times the bundle's cost within `4.7e-16` everywhere; where both legs are positive the cycle sums are all `log(1 + r)` within `7.1e-14`, 1,969 of 1,969. **The other 31 points have a non-positive leg**, where the logarithmic field is undefined on that edge and the identity still holds |
| PASS | B70-6b `instrument` the two index sets | `b₁ = n` on 400 of 400 and `B − A` full rank on 400 of 400; dropping a process leaves an undetermined subspace of dimension exactly one, 326 of 326; adding one leaves no exact solution, 326 of 326, smallest residual `2.4` |
| PASS | B70-6c `instrument` negative values and the cone | 153 of 400 systems carry a negative labour value, and **on every one of them the activity delivering that unit alone has a negative component**, 153 of 153; the 37 systems with a non-negative inverse have strictly positive values, 37 of 37; most negative value `−2.98` |
| PASS | B70-6d `instrument` how many rates carry positive prices | **Under single production exactly one stretch, beginning at zero, on 400 of 400.** Under joint production **52 of 400 have no such rate at all** and 348 have one. So on these draws joint production removes the rate rather than multiplying it. Several disjoint stretches are possible and did not occur here, which is reported rather than claimed either way |
| PASS | B70-6e `instrument` the depreciation schedule | A machine lasting five periods: at `r = 0` the schedule `1.8125, 1.45, 1.0875, 0.725, 0.3625` is straight-line to `1e-10`; the departure grows monotonically with the rate, `0.0119` at `0.02` through `0.1109` at `0.20`, as a fraction of the new machine's price |
| **written** | B70-7 `bookkeeping` placement | below |

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: the characterisation needs no single
production; one independent cycle per process, so the square system is the coincidence of two
index sets and the per-commodity price is a derived coordinate; a negative labour value is a
statement about which net outputs the technique can deliver; and fixed capital is the position
graph carrying an age, with straight-line depreciation as the zero-rate member of a family.
What the classical account reads of it: the price equations under joint production, negative
values and their connection to inferior processes and separability, the possibility that no
positive price system exists, the inequality formulation, and depreciation as an annuity.

| **D2** | **What kind of object a per-commodity number is.** That debate asks which redefinition of labour value is right and each proposal answers with a new definition; here the primitive is the field on edges and the per-commodity number is a coordinate that exists when the index sets coincide. The question is that tradition's own and the typing is not in it |

| **C** | Empty, and this station cannot produce it: it reads no data, so no point prediction of any other account is scored here |

## A32: what sets the amount, for every switch that moves claims

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Script `experiments/a32_switch_census.py`, record
`results/a32_switch_census.json`. No model is run: the census is parsed out of `network.py`
and every reading comes off a record already on disk.**

A31 read that a collection's incidence does not change who falls below the subsistence floor.
That reading belongs to one switch, and asking whether it is a rule across the track costs
nothing, because the criteria are in the records. The claim, written before the check:
incidence changes who falls below the floor exactly when neither absorber is present, absorber
one being a controller whose amount is whatever closes a gap in the very quantity the floor is
read against, absorber two being mixing, since spending is pro rata to holdings and the graph
carries claims away from wherever they arrived. Registered design: the criteria are written in
the script that produced the record, the record carries their text, and every quantity this run
produced is reported.

**The census is read out of the module rather than remembered.** Every line that adds to or
subtracts from the claim total, with the function it sits in: seven lines in five functions,
and a line that only reads the total is excluded by requiring an augmented assignment. A
function present in the module and absent from the table fails the criterion, as does a table
entry with no such line, as does a table entry whose quoted line is not unique. The third of
those has now fired twice. On the first run the pass-down was quoted by
`self._total_claims += amount`, which also occurs in the recapitalisation. On the second the
write-off's quoted line had been wrapped by a later edit to the module and no longer occurred at
all. **The first catch was an ambiguous address and the second a dead one**, and neither was
noticed by anything except this criterion.

**Six mechanisms, and two of them are controllers on different quantities.** Issuance and
withdrawal both close a gap in the Layer 2 inflow, which is the quantity the floor is read
against. The pass-down is a fraction of a stock with no target. Debt service and
recapitalisation are set outside that loop, by maturity and coupon rates on the bond stock and
by last round's realised lender losses. **The write-off is a controller too, and on a different
quantity**: it fires when the claim total runs past a trigger against the resources offered.

**One absorber holds and the other does not, and one verdict would have hidden it.**

| | mixing dead | mixing live |
|---|---|---|
| **a controller on the floor's quantity** | 2 of 400 differ, 0 beyond one node | 4 of 477 differ, 0 beyond one node |
| **no such controller** | 159 of 797 (19.9%), 74 beyond, largest gap 80 | 199 of 872 (22.8%), 116 beyond, largest gap 119 |

With such a controller present, 6 of 877 paired cells differ at all and **none differs by more
than one node**, which is the discrete jitter this carrier family carries and which A18_C
measured and attributed to A18_B6. Nothing turns a block anywhere on that side, against an
instrument that moves 42 to 125 nodes when it moves. With none present, mixing does not lower
the rate: it is 19.9% with the wage channel dead and 22.8% with it live, and the largest gap
rises from 80 nodes to 119. Every cell the survey flags against the claim has that one shape, no
controller and mixing live and incidence deciding anyway. The recapitalisation's own three
elasticities are not monotone, which is not new here: A18_C reported the wage channel's effect
on the count as non-monotone, and this survey recomputes it independently and reaches the same
shape.

**A cell's movement is read in three states, not two.** Still is no pair differing at all;
inside the jitter band is some pair differing and none by more than one node; moves is at least
one pair differing by more than that. **The middle state is adjudicated as neither**, because
the alternative is a threshold of zero width where a gap of one node and a gap of a hundred
trigger the same verdict. Three cells sit there: the issuance at both elasticities and the
recapitalisation at an elasticity of one.

**Which row a cell lands in is a property of the mechanism being dialled, not of the run.** A
controller on the floor's quantity is running in every cell of this survey, the authority being
on by default, so the row does not ask whether such a controller is anywhere in the run; it asks
whether the mechanism whose incidence is being turned is itself one. The write-off is the case
that makes the difference visible: it ran with the authority live throughout and its shape
decided anyway. **A controller absorbs its own incidence and does not absorb everybody else's.**

**What that costs the earlier reading.** A31's second round attributed its first round's zero to
mixing and its own to the controller. The first half no longer has support: the controller was on
in the first round too, and across this survey mixing absorbs nothing. What the first round's
side probe measured is still true, that the distribution reconverges to 1.26e-04 per node, and
what it shows is that the perturbation from one round's collection is wiped out, not that a
landing point fails to decide who is below. The survey separates those because it has a whole row
with no controller, where the distribution mixes just as hard and the landing decides anyway.

**The surviving absorber now rests on two mechanisms, and they are the two halves of one
controller.** The withdrawal supplies 825 of those comparisons and the issuance 52. The second
was a gap when this station first ran: `injection_target` was already swept, in A2d, A4 and A9,
and read there against concentration, the support size and the wage share, while no record
carried a reading of it against the count below the floor. A33 supplied that reading. **The
claim is about that count and about nothing else**, and the landing does move other readouts:
A33's own grid has the tail circulating stock and the financial layer's share differing in 52 of
52 pairs and the top one per cent share in 50 of 52 at a median of 8.3%.

**Both of this station's queued dials are now read, and the count of them is zero.** The other

## B71: von Neumann's equality as the field side and the flow side of one pencil

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b71_von_neumann.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b71_von_neumann.py`, record `results/b71_von_neumann.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B70 left the price equations overdetermined whenever the processes outnumber the commodities,
and registered the inequality formulation as what one does instead. **That formulation is von
Neumann's, and it comes with a theorem: the coefficient of expansion and the interest factor
are the same number.** **Theorem 16.** Write `C = B^{-1}A`, the input matrix per unit of output
bundle, and suppose it is non-negative and irreducible. (1) `B x = α A x` is `C x = x/α` and
`p B = β p A`, with `u = p B`, is `u C = u/β`; a non-negative irreducible matrix carries a
positive eigenvector at its Perron root and at no other eigenvalue, so both are forced to that
root and **`α = β = 1/λ_PF(C)`, with the intensity vector the right Perron vector and the price
vector `u B^{-1}`**. So the equality is not a fixed point here: **it is the pairing of Theorem 9
of B65, the field side and the flow side being the two Perron vectors of one pencil.** The
condition `C ≥ 0` is stronger than von Neumann's own assumption, and the trade is visible:
**assume the pencil into Perron-Frobenius's reach and the equality is an eigenvalue fact; do
not, and it is a fixed point.** (2) `p B = β p A` read column by column says **every production
cycle carries `log β`**, so the equality says the number the field puts on every cycle is the
logarithm of the number the flow grows by. (3) His (8) says no cycle carries more than `log β`
and (8') that one carrying less is idle; his (7) says no commodity is in deficit and (7') that
one in strict excess is priced at zero. **A cycle whose sum falls short is idle, and free
disposal is the statement that a commodity off the binding constraint carries no term.** **The
converse is not in the conditions**: a cycle can reach the common value and still carry no
intensity, which is a degenerate vertex, and B75 reads that case. Published as "exactly" and
corrected 2026-09-13. (4) `p = u B^{-1}` and `B^{-1}` need not be non-negative, so **the equality system
does not deliver positive prices**, which is what the inequalities and free disposal are for,
and B70-6d is the other side of it. **Corollary 16.1**: with `B = I` and no wage, `C = A` and
`α = β = 1/λ_PF(A) = 1 + R`, the right vector being Sraffa's standard proportions and the left
one his prices where the wage vanishes, so **the standard system is the von Neumann ray of that
economy and B67's Corollary 12.4 is this said twice**. **Corollary 16.2**: fold the wage basket
in, `M = A + b l`, and the same root is the `1 + r` of B68 and B69, so **an economy reinvesting
every profit grows at the profit factor**.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 4 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 4 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

(a) and (b) are the same numbers off the same solve, so they are one function here. The names
are not renumbered, because renumbering would break the correspondence with the design's (c),
(d) and (e).

| **proved** | B71-2 `own_reading` the interest factor is the common cycle sum, Theorem 16(2) | `p B = β p A` column by column is one sentence per process: its cycle carries `log β` |
| **proved** | B71-3 `own_reading` slackness read on cycles, Theorem 16(3) | A process runs only if its cycle carries the common sum; a commodity is priced only if it is not in excess. **Free disposal is not an assumption about behaviour but a statement that a commodity off the binding constraint carries no term** |
| **proved** | B71-4 `own_reading` two degenerate pencils, Corollaries 16.1 and 16.2 | `B = I` with no wage gives Sraffa's standard system as the von Neumann ray; `M = A + b l` gives the rate of profit of the Marxian theorems. **One root, read on two degenerations** |

interest factor is the common cycle sum; the slackness conditions are sentences about cycles;
and one root, read on two degenerate pencils, is Sraffa's maximum rate and the Marxian rate of
profit. What the classical account reads of it: the equality, its uniqueness, the four
conditions, and the von Neumann ray's connection to the standard system, which is worked out at
length in that literature.

## B72: rent, as a term on an edge into a position no cycle produces

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b72_land_and_rent.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b72_land_and_rent.py`, record `results/b72_land_and_rent.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B70 registered land as the other half of Sraffa's Part II and B71 read the complementary
slackness conditions as sentences about cycles. **Rent is where the two meet.** **Theorem 17.**
With `n` produced commodities, `k` qualities of land in use and one method per land: (1) each
land vertex is bought by the one bundle that uses it and produced by nothing, so it is a
pendant vertex and `b₁ = k + n − 1`, the number of operated methods. **A rent is a term on an
edge into a position no cycle produces.** (2) Setting every cycle's sum to `log(1 + r)`
requires `ρ_i = p₁ q_i − (1 + r) p a_i − w l_i`, **the amount that land's cycle carries over
the common value**, so the rent is not a further price to be determined alongside the others:
it is the excess, taken off. (3) In the corn model, land `i` alone would support the wage
`w_i(r) = (1 − (1 + r)α_i)/λ_i`, and every rent is non-negative exactly when `w ≤ min_i w_i(r)`;
with all `k` lands in use the wage is that minimum, **so the land attaining the lower envelope
pays no rent and every other rent is positive**. Take any other land as the marginal one and
some rent goes negative. **The zero is forced by non-negativity: it is von Neumann's condition
(7') of B71 read on an input no process produces, not a separate postulate.** (4) Each `w_i` is
a straight line in `r`, so the envelope's argmin changes wherever two lines cross: **the order
of cultivation varies with distribution and is not a physical datum**, which is Sraffa's
section 86, and a reversal is the same object as a switch point in B67-6b. **Corollary 17.1**:
put two methods on one land, which is intensive rent, and that land's vertex is bought by two
bundles, so it closes a cycle and `b₁` rises by one. **The extra equation intensive rent is
known to need is that extra cycle: the two kinds of rent are one graph with a land vertex of
degree one or of degree two.**

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 4 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 3 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

are both counting, so they are one function here; the names are not renumbered.

zero on the marginal land is B71's slackness condition; the order of cultivation moves with
distribution because the envelope's argmin moves; and the two kinds of rent differ by one in
`b₁`. What the classical account reads of it: differential rent, the no-rent margin, and the
dependence of the order of cultivation on distribution.

## A33: the same controller's other half, and where its claims land

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Script `experiments/a33_injection_landing.py`, record
`results/a33_injection_landing.json`, which carries the configuration it ran under. 450 cells,
five seeds, nothing fetched. No module change: `injection_target` is a field the module already
carries, so rule 19 has no object here. The record was rewritten later the same day, after a
wording correction in one criterion, and every one of its 450 rows and 150 pairs came back
identical under a module that had changed in between.**

A32 read that a controller absorbs incidence, and that the reading stood on one mechanism, the
withdrawal, because it was the only one whose incidence had been swept while such a controller
ran. This station supplies the second, and it is the other half of the same controller: the
issuance, whose landing is `injection_target`. That dial is swept already in A2d, A4 and A9 and
read there against concentration, the support size and the wage share; what no record carried is
a reading of it against the count below the floor, and that count is what the claim is about. The withdrawal supplies
825 of the comparisons that side of the claim rests on, counted one seed at a time.
Registered design: the criteria are written in the script that produced the record, the record
carries their text, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

**Of 150 pairs, 52 are read and 98 are held out, each for a stated reason.** In 81 the rule
asked for nothing at all, so the dial placed nothing: that is every cell of the recycled leak,
where the pass-down already fills the gap, and the deeper floors of the healthy graph. In
another 17 the rule issued something so small that by the close the two landings leave the same
share on the injection node to six figures. The two groups part at about five thousandths of the
circulating stock on what was issued over what circulates, and the bands abut rather than stand
apart: the lowest two that keep a trace read 0.005166 and 0.005170 against a highest traceless
0.005250, while the other fifty issue more than four times the stock over the run.

**The landing does not change who is below the floor.** Of the 52 read, 46 leave the same
count. The six that differ all differ by exactly one node, four in one direction and two in the
other, and none by two or more. One node is the discrete jitter this carrier family already
carries, which A18_C measured and attributed to A18_B6. Against that, the same grid moves the
count by 42 to 125 nodes when the authority is switched off: 100 of 300 comparisons are
non-zero and 68 of them move a block of 50 or more.

**And the landing moves plenty else, on this station's own grid rather than a borrowed one.**
Across the same 52 pairs the tail circulating stock differs in 52 of 52, median 4.9%; the
financial layer's share of the closing stock in 52 of 52, median 1.7%; the top one per cent
share in 50 of 52, median 8.3%; the Gini in 50 of 52; total wages paid in 52 of 52. **A
controller absorbing a landing's effect on the count below the floor is not a claim that it
absorbs that landing anywhere else**, and that sentence now rests on this station's numbers.

**One structural thing the earlier station did not have to face.** Moving the landing moves how
much the controller has to issue: the two landings' issued totals differ by a median of 9.6%,
and by 2.8% at the closest. So the 1.91% spread A31 measured as one that changes no block state
marks every differing cell here as not adjudicated, and not by luck: no cell on this grid comes
within that line, and the reading leans on the one-node jitter line
instead. The withdrawal got away with that line because its collected totals differed by 0.7% to
1.9%; the issuing half does not, and for a controller the amount cannot be held fixed while the
landing moves, since the amount is the loop's output.

## B73: two registered extensions, one costing nothing in the graph and one costing a cycle

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b73_two_extensions.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b73_two_extensions.py`, record `results/b73_two_extensions.json`, which carries
the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

A machine of declining efficiency was registered by B70 and the arithmetic of intensive rent by
B72. **They are done together because their costs in the graph are opposite, and that is the
point.** **Theorem 18.** (1) A profile of output coefficients changes weights and no edge, so
`b₁` is unchanged; at `r = 0` the machine's price falls each period by `q_j − a − w l₁`, so
**the schedule is straight-line exactly when the profile is constant** and B70's Corollary
15.1(3) needs constant efficiency as well as a zero rate. **The sign of the fall is the sign of
that expression**, so a period whose output falls short of that period's own non-machine cost
makes the price rise with age; a merely rising profile does not do it. (2) With two methods on
one land the land vertex has degree two, so `b₁` rises by one and deleting the vertex lowers it
again: **the land lies on a cycle rather than hanging off one.** Charge the two users `ρ₁` and
`ρ₂` for the same acre and that cycle carries `log(ρ₂/ρ₁)`, **so it closes exactly when the two
rates agree**, and with one rent the two price equations are square in `(w, ρ)` with **no
zero-rent condition anywhere**: the second method is the second equation. (3) Both equations
give the same `ρ`, so `C₂/q₂ − C₁/q₁ = ρ(1/q₁ − 1/q₂)`: **the rent and the unit-cost gap are
the same number up to a positive factor**, and with `q₂ > q₁` the rent is positive exactly when
the method yielding more per acre carries the higher cost per unit of product. **That is
Sraffa's section 87, and here it is an identity rather than a condition to be imposed.** (4) At
a position with one user, the assumption that everyone pays the same rate for it is vacuous and
the system is closed by a boundary condition, which under extensive rent is the zero rent on
the marginal land; at a position with two users it is the closure of a cycle, and that closure
is an equation. **Extensive and intensive rent are the two sides of that line.**

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 4 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 2 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

**The name B73-6c is not used**, as with B71-6b and B72-6d: the design's (b) and (c) are one
construction and are checked by one function.

| **proved** | B73-2 `own_reading` a second user costs a cycle, Theorem 18(2) | Degree two raises `b₁` by one and deleting the vertex lowers it again; the added cycle carries `log(ρ₂/ρ₁)`, so **one rent per acre is that cycle closing**, and the system is then square with no zero-rent condition |
| **proved** | B73-3 `own_reading` the rent is the unit-cost gap, Theorem 18(3) | `ρ(1/q₁ − 1/q₂) = C₂/q₂ − C₁/q₁`, two lines of algebra. **Sraffa's section 87 is an identity here, not a restriction to impose** |
| **proved** | B73-4 `own_reading` what one price per position costs, Theorem 18(4) | Vacuous at degree one, an equation at degree two. **Extensive and intensive rent are the two sides of that line** |

## B74: roundaboutness is a degree, and how often the order can reverse is a sign count

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b74_roundaboutness.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b74_roundaboutness.py`, record `results/b74_roundaboutness.json`, which carries
the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B67's Corollary 12.3 already says that no quantity read off the field orders techniques
independently of the rate, so **this station does not prove that again**. It does the three
things that were left. **Theorem 19.** A technique is a list of dated labour inputs `l_t` with
cost `C(x) = Σ l_t x^t`, `x = 1 + r`. (1) In the dated position graph of B69's Corollary 14.2 a
cycle crosses one date edge per period of lag and each date edge carries `log(1 + r)`, so the
longest cycle of a technique crosses `T = deg C` of them: **roundaboutness is a degree, and it
is the one quantity here with no price in it and no dependence on `r`.** (2) Two techniques are
equally costly exactly where `D = C₁ − C₂` vanishes, so switch points are the roots of `D` with
`x > 1`, and between consecutive roots one technique is strictly the cheaper. (3) By Descartes'
rule the number of positive roots of `D` is at most the number `s` of sign changes in its
coefficients and differs from it by an even number; switch points are positive roots, so
**their number is bounded by `s` as well, and `s` is read off two labour profiles with no rate
of profit in it**. (4) With `s = 1` there is exactly one positive root, so the ordering reverses
at most once and **one number does order those two techniques**; with `s ≥ 2` two switch points
occur. **That is the exact domain of the Austrian intuition: the two dated labour profiles
cross once.** (5) Writing `APP = N/M` and differentiating, `APP'(x) = Var(t)/x` under the
discounted weights `w_t = l_t x^t / M`: **the average period rises exactly as fast as the
variance of the date**, and is constant only for a profile on a single date. Its ordering
between two techniques can reverse, and **the rate where it reverses need not be a switch point
at all**.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 5 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 3 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

**Two numberings meet here.** The five clauses of Theorem 19 are the five `own_reading`
entries; in the script `B74-5` is the known answer and `B74-6a/6b/6c` the structural checks.
The correspondence is in the table and neither is renumbered, as with B71-6b, B72-6d and
B73-6c.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| **proved** | Theorem 19(1) `own_reading` roundaboutness is a degree | One date edge per period of lag, each carrying `log(1 + r)`, so the longest cycle crosses `deg C` of them. **The profile is a list of labour quantities, so no price enters and the degree does not move with `r`** |
| **proved** | Theorem 19(2) `own_reading` switch points are roots | Equal cost is `D(x) = 0`; `D` is a polynomial, so it keeps its sign between consecutive roots and one technique is strictly the cheaper over that whole interval |
| **proved** | Theorem 19(3) `own_reading` Descartes bounds the reversals | At most `s` positive roots, same parity. **Switch points need `x > 1` and positive roots need `x > 0`, so the former are a subset and inherit the bound**; the parity clause belongs to the positive roots |
| **proved** | Theorem 19(4) `own_reading` the domain of the intuition | `s = 1` gives exactly one positive root, so at most one reversal and a single number orders the pair; `s ≥ 2` permits two and §5 attains it. **The intuition is not false, its domain was never written down** |
| **proved** | Theorem 19(5) `own_reading` the average period moves, and not where the cost moves | `APP' = Var(t)/x`, so it is non-decreasing and constant only on a single-date profile. **The reversal of its ordering is a different function's zero from `D`'s**, and the run exhibits reversals where `D` has no root |
| PASS | B74-5 `known_answer` Samuelson's two switch points, by factoring | `D(x) = −6x + 7x² − 2x³` factors as `−x(2x − 3)(x − 2)`, so the switch points are exactly `3/2` and `2`: **50 and 100 per cent matched to `0.0e+00`**, costs 15.75 and 28.00 matched to `0.0e+00`. **Descartes' bound is attained**, two sign changes and two switch points. B67-6b read the same pair by bisection; **here the roots are rational** |
| PASS | B74-6a `instrument` the bound and its parity | 600 drawn pairs: **positive roots never exceed sign changes**, 600 of 600, **and always have the same parity**, 600 of 600; the bound is attained on 288. Joint distribution of (sign changes, switch points) printed in full, including `(2,2)` on 5, `(4,2)` on 1 and `(5,2)` on 1 |
| PASS | B74-6b `instrument` where one number does order the techniques | Of the 169 pairs whose difference changes sign once, **all 169 have at most one switch point and at most one reversal of the cost ordering**. Of the 374 changing sign twice or more, 7 carry two switch points. **The domain is neither empty nor everything** |
| PASS | B74-6c `instrument` the average period against the cost ordering | 601 rates from zero to 3. **The average period moves on 598 of 600 pairs**, largest movement 4.6240 periods; **its ordering reverses on 133, and on all 133 the reversal is at no switch point**. An instance reverses at `r = 0.3775` in a pair with no switch point at all. The two non-moving pairs were inspected: both legs of both sit on a single date, which is clause 5's equality case |
| **written** | placement `bookkeeping` | below |

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: roundaboutness is the number of date
edges the longest cycle crosses, which is the degree of the cost polynomial; switch points are
the positive roots of the difference of two such polynomials; their number is bounded, with
matching parity, by the sign changes of that difference; ordering by a single number is valid
exactly where the profiles cross once; and the average period rises at a speed equal to the
variance of the date under the discounted weights. What the Austrian and Cambridge accounts
read of it: that production takes time and techniques differ in how much; that the
Hicks-Malinvaud average period depends on the rate of interest and gives opposite rankings at
two successive switch points, so it does not express a degree of roundaboutness; and
Samuelson's pair at 50 and 100 per cent.

| cell | content |
|---|---|
| **A** | That the average period moves with distribution, does not express roundaboutness, and has its ranking reversed between two switch points. Fratini's (2012) reading of Hicks-Malinvaud has it; here the first half comes out as `APP' = Var(t)/x`, which says the same thing and says how fast |
| **D2** | **How many switch points a given pair can have.** "How often can the ordering reverse" falls inside a theory of the choice of technique, and that literature answers it with examples rather than with a bound. Descartes on the difference of two profiles gives the bound and its parity in one line, and the framework's dated positions are what put the profiles into a form a sign count applies to |
| **D** | That roundaboutness is a degree in the dated position graph; that the bound and its parity are read off labour quantities with no price in them; that the domain of the Austrian ordering is "the profiles cross once"; that the measure's speed is a variance; and that its ordering can reverse where there is no switch point at all, a case outside a reading that takes the reversal between two switch points. No account asks for these |
| **C** | Empty, and this station cannot produce it: it reads no data, so no point prediction of any other account is scored here |

**Corollary 12.3 and this station do not conflict.** That corollary rules out quantities read
off the field; the degree is not read off the field, and it does not order the techniques
either. **It bounds how often the order can change.**

**Registered, not scheduled.** **The lower envelope of three or more techniques and the total
number of switch points on it were done on 2026-09-12 as B76 below**: the owner sequence is a
Davenport-Schinzel sequence whose order is this station's sign-change count, so the total is
linear in the number of techniques where the pair count is quadratic, and this station's domain
condition becomes the condition for no reswitching anywhere. Tying roundaboutness to `ρ` on the
dated graph, which needs a dated carrier first, is still registered.

## A34: the write-off's shape, and the one place the claim predicted a difference

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Script `experiments/a34_writeoff_shape.py`, record
`results/a34_writeoff_shape.json`, which carries the configuration it ran under. 1,050 cells,
five seeds, nothing fetched.**

A32's claim was that a collection's incidence changes who falls below the subsistence floor
exactly when neither absorber is present, the first absorber being a controller whose amount is
whatever closes a gap in the very quantity the floor is read against. A31 and A33 swept the two
halves of the one controller that does close that gap and found nothing. **The write-off is a
controller on a different quantity**, the claim total against the resources offered, so the
claim predicts its shape decides, and this is the only station in the family where a null counts
against the claim. `WriteOffSpec.base` was opened for it and reuses the withdrawal's splitter, so
the default is bit for bit the one multiplication the module has always had. Registered design:
the criteria are written in the script that produced the record, the record carries their text,
and every quantity this run produced is reported.

**The shape decides, and it moves whole blocks.** Of 300 pairs, 238 had the trigger fire; the
other 62 are held out. Among the 238 the count below the floor differs by 0 in 162, by 1 in 33,
by 2 to 4 in 30, and **by 75 to 79 in 13**. The block turns both ways: one cell of the leak at a
floor of 0.15 reads 75, 150 and 75 under the three shapes, and another at 0.20 reads 150, 75 and
150, so the shape settles which side of the edge the block lands on rather than favouring anyone.
Taking the same amount off every account holding something is both the best shape in 16 of the 36
deciding cells and the worst in 17.

**Beside the two stations that swept the other controller, that is the reading.**

| | what gap the controller closes | comparisons | differing | largest gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A31, the taking half | the quantity the floor reads | 825 | 0 | 0 |
| A33, the issuing half | the same | 52 | 6 | 1 |
| **A34, the write-off** | the claim total over the resources | 238 | 76 | **79** |

Same family of dial, same carrier family, same readout, and the largest gap goes from one node
to seventy-nine. The one thing that changes is whether the controller's setpoint is the quantity
the floor is read against.

**And the other half of the claim does not survive, which is worth saying plainly.** The claim
was an "exactly when". The "only" direction holds: with such a controller present, 877
comparisons across two mechanisms leave a largest gap of one node. The "whenever" direction does
not: with no such controller, 162 of 238 cells move nobody at all. So the claim narrows to
something usable and smaller. **A controller closing a gap in the quantity the floor reads
guarantees that incidence changes nobody's place. Its absence guarantees nothing**, and 162
cells say so against an instrument that moves a block of 50 or more in 51 of 900 comparisons on
the same grid.

**One criterion here was a day old and load-bearing.** Until 2026-09-12 the write-off destroyed
on the claim total, which counts parked claims, while reducing only the held side, so the
conservation identity broke as soon as anything was parked. No record on disk had ever carried
both switches; this is the first station to put them in one grid, and its 1,050 cells all close.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`instrument` 3 pass · `own_reading` 2 printed · `bookkeeping` 1 printed

### Void: A34-4's firing rounds, and A34-0's sentence about them

**Corrected 2026-09-12 from this station's own record, and re-run 2026-09-13 so the record itself
carries the corrected line.**

`a34_writeoff_shape.py` reported the firing rounds inside the per-base loop **without indexing by
base**, while every other quantity in that loop was indexed. It therefore printed one number three
times, and A34-4 read `holdings / equal / threshold` as **`173.0` each**. A34-0's sentence "the
rounds the trigger fires in do not move with the shape" rests on that line.

**The record's per-base rows say the opposite, and by a wide margin.** Over the 238 cells where
the trigger fired:

| shape | firing rounds, median | against pro rata, per cell |
|---|---|---|
| `holdings` (pro rata) | **98**, a lower bound | — |
| `equal` (per head) | **173**, a lower bound | **higher in 233, lower in 0, tied in 5** |
| `threshold` | **97**, a lower bound | lower in 211, higher in 0 |

**The three medians are lower bounds rather than estimates**, which A35 established by running the
same grid to twice the horizon: they go to `198 / 298.5 / 197`, because over half the live cells are
still firing when the run stops. **The per-cell comparisons in the third column are not affected**,
since both sides of each are censored the same way, and the within-cell ratio of per head to pro
rata reads `1.510204` at the short horizon and `1.505051` at the long one. Over all 300 cells the
medians are `97 / 148 / 84`. The largest per-cell spread is **106 rounds**,
and two cells tie at it, both seed 3 on the leak at rate `0.2` and elasticity `0.5`, at floors of
`0.05` and `0.10`, each reading `98 / 203 / 97`.

**So the registration below was already answered by this station's own data and nobody read it**,
because the pair record collapsed the three bases with `max` and the criterion that would have
printed them was the line with the missing index. **A per-head write-off prolongs the condition it
fires on: 233 cells to 0, on this grid.**

The figures in this section that do not involve firing rounds are unaffected: they were each
indexed by base. The script now carries `rounds_by_base` on the pair and reads it, and the station
was re-run on 2026-09-13 so that the record carries the corrected line rather than pointing at a
correction made outside it. **That re-run is also the check on the correction**: the three medians
and the 233-to-0 tally were read back along two independent paths, the new per-base field and an
independent regrouping of the rows, and they agree to the digit. A34-0's sentence has been replaced
in the script as well, so the claim it used to make no longer reaches anyone reading the record.

**`threshold` running shorter than pro rata is the other half of the mechanism, and it points at
what A35 has to measure.** Pro rata touches every account holding anything, which collects little
from the small ones and pushes them toward zero; taking only from the accounts above the mean
leaves the small ones alone. If a drained account leaves the paying set, then each remaining payer
carries a larger share of a per-head levy, which is a cap that bites harder the longer it runs.
**That is a mechanism with two candidate carriers**, the shortfall a cap leaves uncollected and the
paying set shrinking, and neither is recorded on this grid.

2026-09-12.** What is left is the mechanism rather than the fact: whether the prolongation is
carried by accounts drained to zero, which is a count this grid does not record, and whether the
effect has a ceiling or runs to the end of every horizon. **That is A35.**


## A35: what carries the prolongation a per-head write-off causes

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Script `experiments/a35_writeoff_prolongation.py`, record
`results/a35_writeoff_prolongation.json`, which carries the configuration it ran under. 1,800
cells across two horizons, five seeds, nothing fetched.**

A34 found that a per-head write-off fires for longer than a pro rata one, 233 cells to 0, and left
the fact without a mechanism. Two candidates were available and neither was recorded. **One is the
cap**: a per-head levy aims the same amount at every account holding something, so an account
holding less pays what it has and the rest is not collected and not carried forward, while pro rata
aims a fraction of each account's own balance, which no account can fail to meet. **The other is the
paying set**: an account emptied by the levy is one the levy can no longer draw on, so the per-head
share rises and the cap bites harder. Four counters go on the history behind a switch that is off by
default. Registered design: the criteria are written in the script that produced the record, the
record carries their text, and every quantity this run produced is reported.

**The cap carries it and the paying set does not.** Paired within the cell over the 238 where all
three shapes fired, the extra rounds correlate with the shortfall the cap left at `+0.561` and with
the extra accounts emptied at `+0.037`, a factor of fifteen. The per-head shape leaves a shortfall
in 234 of its 238 live cells, a median of **50.3% of what it aimed at**, while the other two sit at
the arithmetic floor around `1e-14` relative, thirteen orders of magnitude below.

**The paying set does not shrink, and the reason is worth stating because the counters look like it
should.** The per-head share is the rate times the held stock over the payers, so its ratio over a
run factors exactly into a stock term and a paying-set term, and the factorisation closes to
`4.4e-16`. **The paying-set term is 1.000 under all three shapes.** Accounts are emptied 11,245
times per cell under the per-head levy, across 148 rounds, and they receive inflow again before the
next levy, so the count of emptyings is large while the number of payers at the levy ends where it
started. **Emptying an account and keeping it empty are two different things, and this grid does the
first constantly without doing the second.**

**Neither candidate is necessary, which the third shape settles.** Taking only from accounts above
the mean differs from pro rata in 211 of 238 cells while its shortfall stays below the floor and it
empties nobody at all. That difference runs through the amount rather than the shape — it destroys
`0.983` times as much per firing round, so the ratio it fires on falls faster — and it is registered
open rather than attributed to either candidate.

**The firing-round medians are lower bounds, not estimates.** Run to twice the horizon the same grid
reads `198 / 298.5 / 197` against `98 / 173 / 97`, because over half the live cells are still firing
when the run stops: 126, 160 and 137 of 238 at the short horizon. **What survives the doubling is
the within-cell ratio**, `1.510204` against `1.505051`, a drift of 0.3%, and the direction counts, 233
of 238 against 236 of 244 with no reversal at either horizon. So the comparison A34 made stands and
the absolute figures it quoted are bounds; both write-ups now say which is which.

**Rule 19 here is not the usual check, because the counters only record.** Comparing the switch off
against the module before the fields existed is nearly free to satisfy: a field nobody allocates
cannot change anything. So every configuration is run twice, once off and once **on**, against that
baseline, over every field of the history plus the closing state plus the generator digest. Both
groups: 193 configurations, 50 fields each, nothing differing. **An observer that changes the run is
not an observer.**

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`instrument` 2 pass · `known_answer` 1 pass · `own_reading` 4 printed · `bookkeeping` 1 printed

No criterion on this station is a rival's point prediction. Nobody has asked any theory whether the
shape of a write-off prolongs the condition it fires on, so this reads as a quantity the framework
has and the alternatives have no object for, not as a contest.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| **pass** | A35-1 `instrument` the books close on every cell | 1,800 of 1,800 |
| **pass** | A35-2 `instrument` rule 19, the counters do not change the run | 193 configurations with the switch off and 193 with it on, 50 fields each, 0 differ |
| **pass** | A35-3 `known_answer` A34's firing rounds come back | 714 shared cells, 0 differing |
| **printed** | A35-4 `own_reading` what each shape failed to collect | per head leaves 50.3% of what it aimed at, in 234 of 238 cells; the other two are at the arithmetic floor |
| **printed** | A35-5 `own_reading` which candidate carries it | the shortfall at `+0.561`, the emptying at `+0.037`; and neither is necessary, since above-the-mean differs in 211 cells with both counters at the floor |
| **printed** | A35-6 `own_reading` does the paying set shrink | the paying-set term of the share is 1.000 under all three shapes, the factorisation exact to `4.4e-16` |

**Two registrations, and one of them is not about this station.** The small difference between
above-the-mean and pro rata runs through the amount and has no criterion here. And
`Criterion.as_dict()` does not write the flag that distinguishes a criterion that could not be
evaluated from one that failed, so an unevaluated criterion lands in a record as `passed: false` and
reads as a failure; that is the same source as the unevaluated entries the failure census counts,
and changing it touches every record on this track.

## B75: choice of technique is complementary slackness read cycle by cycle

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b75_rectangular_programme.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b75_rectangular_programme.py`, record `results/b75_rectangular_programme.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. Needs `scipy`.**

B71 did von Neumann's equality half and left the rectangular case registered, because it needs
a linear programme. **This station solves it and asks what shape the solution has.**
**Theorem 20.** With `n` processes, `m` goods, inputs `A`, outputs `B`, intensities `x ≥ 0`
and prices `p ≥ 0`: (1) under `Bp ≤ βAp` and `x(B − βA)p = 0`, every term of
`Σ_j x_j[(Bp)_j − β(Ap)_j]` is non-positive, so the sum vanishes only if each does, and
`x_j > 0` forces `(Bp)_j = β(Ap)_j`. In logarithms: **a process runs only if its cycle
carries the common sum, and at a non-degenerate solution exactly then.** The step gives that
direction and no more: a cycle can carry the common sum with no intensity, which is a degenerate
vertex. Published as "exactly when" and corrected 2026-09-13. So the classical question of
which techniques are in use is answered by a condition the field already carries, **not by a
comparison laid on top of it**. (2) A basic optimal solution of the programme for `x` has at
most `m + 1` basic variables including the value, so at most `m` processes run, and dually at
most `n` goods are priced; at a non-degenerate solution of a connected economy the active block
has a strictly positive left null vector and a strictly positive right null vector, both null
spaces are one-dimensional, and its rank is both `|J| − 1` and `|I| − 1`, so **`|J| = |I|`**.
Deleting the idle processes and the free goods changes none of the conditions, so **`α` solves
the block's own problem: the rectangular case needs no theorem of its own, B71's square one
holds on the active subgraph.** The bound belongs to the `D22` family: **however many processes
are written down, the number that can run is held down by the number of positions.** (3)
Enlarging the process set only enlarges the feasible set, and by (2) the solution is unchanged
by deleting idle processes, so **`α` is the upper envelope of the sub-economies' own factors**
and an idle cycle contributes nothing at all rather than a little; where the maximiser changes,
two sub-economies attain it, so by (1) **two cycles carry the common sum at once**. That tie is
B74's switch point and the programme's degenerate vertex: **one object seen three ways**, and
B72's lower envelope of wage curves is the same shape with the extremum reversed. (4) When the
economy is not in one piece, `α` and `β` are determined on different parts and need not agree,
**and the counting identity of (2) fails with them**: the common cycle sum is a connectivity
condition, which is what Kemeny, Morgenstern and Thompson's irreducibility assumption buys.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

`own_reading` 4 proved · `known_answer` 1 pass · `instrument` 4 pass · `bookkeeping` 1 written

**The instrument's floor decides how three of these are stated.** Anything read through the
bisection carries the linear programme's accuracy, not the bisection's depth: the solver's
feasibility tolerance is `1e-7` and the game value's slope in `γ` measures about `0.13`, so a
root is pinned to roughly `8e-7` however many times the bracket is halved. **200 halvings buy
nothing over 60.** The bound used is `1e-6`, taken from that division and not from any run's
worst case; the worst gap actually seen is printed each time.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| **proved** | Theorem 20(1) `own_reading` choice of technique is the slackness condition | A sum of non-positive terms vanishes only if each term does, **so the operated processes are among the cycles attaining the common sum** and at a non-degenerate solution they are all of them; a cycle can attain the sum and carry no intensity, which is the degenerate vertex this station reads elsewhere. Nothing is added to the field in order to choose. **Published as "exactly the set" and corrected 2026-09-13**, the proof giving one direction |
| **proved** | Theorem 20(2) `own_reading` the solution sits on a square block | `\|J\| ≤ m` from the basic-solution count; `\|J\| = \|I\|` at a non-degenerate solution of a connected economy; `α` solves the block's own problem. **The hypotheses are not decoration**: the published reducible example has `\|J\| = 3` against `\|I\| = 4` |
| **proved** | Theorem 20(3) `own_reading` an upper envelope whose kink is a tie | `α` is the largest factor among available sub-economies; an idle cycle contributes nothing; at the crossover two cycles carry the common sum. **The envelope's kink, B74's switch point and the degenerate vertex are the same parameter value** |
| **proved** | Theorem 20(4) `own_reading` the common sum is a connectivity condition | Both factors involve only the part a positive vector is supported on, so disjoint supports determine them independently. **What irreducibility buys is that the graph is in one piece** |
| PASS | B75-5 `known_answer` two published rectangular examples, and the one that breaks both halves at once | Example one, irreducible, 3 × 4: `α = β` and **the exact value is the cube root of two**, within `1e-12`; the lecture's printed figures agree within `1e-8`, its own bisection tolerance; `x` and `p` match the printed vectors within `0.005`; **3 run and 3 priced, equal**. Example two, reducible, 5 × 6: `α` is again `2^(1/3)` while **`β` is one**, and **3 run against 4 priced, not equal**. **One instance breaks clause 4 and clause 2's counting identity together** |
