## B76: the envelope of k techniques, linear in k where the pairs are quadratic

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b76_envelope.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b76_envelope.py`, record `results/b76_envelope.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

Two registrations asked for the same object: B74 left the envelope of three or more techniques
open, and B75 left the relation between its growth-factor envelope and B74's cost envelope
open. **They are one curve.** **Theorem 21.** (1) The cost of a unit of the numeraire under
technique `i` is `1/w_i(r)` and the reciprocal is strictly decreasing, so the lower envelope of
costs and the upper envelope of wages pick the same technique everywhere: **choosing the
cheapest and choosing the highest-paying are one instruction, not two that agree.** (2) Write
down which technique owns each maximal stretch of the envelope. **If that owner sequence
contained an alternation `a … b … a … b …` of length `s + 2`, the two curves would have to meet
in each of its `s + 1` gaps**, so with pairwise meetings bounded by `s` it is a
Davenport-Schinzel sequence of order `s` and has at most `λ_s(k)` terms. **`λ_1(k) = k` and
`λ_2(k) = 2k − 1`, both linear, while the number of pairs is `k(k−1)/2`**: the naive count that
every pair contributes its own crossings is quadratic and wrong, because most pairwise
crossings lie under some third curve. **`s` is B74's Theorem 19(3)**, the sign-change count of
the pairwise difference, so the bound on the whole envelope is read off labour profiles with no
rate of profit in it. (3) At `s = 1` the sequence forbids `a … b … a`, and with no two equal
terms adjacent that means no symbol twice: **no technique leaves the envelope and returns,
however many techniques are in the book.** **B74's domain condition, stated there for one pair,
is here the condition for no reswitching anywhere.** (4) `w_i(r) > 0` exactly for `r < R_i`, so
the envelope vanishes at `max_i R_i` and the technique owning the right end is the one attaining
it, while the left end is owned by `argmax_i w_i(0)`, a different technique in general. **So
B75's expansion factor is this envelope's right-hand endpoint, and the kink in B75's sweep is a
switch point of this envelope at that end. The two were never two objects.**

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

## B77: what a continuum changes, and what it does not

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b77_continuum.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b77_continuum.py`, record `results/b77_continuum.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. Needs `scipy`.**

B72 registered a continuum of land qualities and B76 a continuum of techniques, each noting the
two were the same object. **This station makes the index set a continuum and asks what
survives.** **Theorem 22.** (1) B75's bound on the active set counts the programme's **rows**,
`m` inequalities and one normalisation, and adding columns does not add rows, so **at most `m`
processes run at a basic optimum whatever the cardinality of the index set**; in the limit an
optimal measure is supported on at most `m` atoms. **The qualifier is the programme's**: a
degenerate optimum can spread the same activity over more processes, so this bounds the solution a
vertex solver returns rather than every optimal one. **This is not that a continuum approximates a large finite book:
the two give the same exact answer to "how many run", at every size.** (2) The switch count
grows without bound under refinement, so B76's `λ_s(k)`, true at every `k`, has no limiting
content; what survives is the envelope theorem, `E'(x) = ∂C_θ/∂x` at the owner, the term in
`dθ*/dx` vanishing because `∂C_θ/∂θ` does at an interior minimiser. **Under one and the same
refinement the two counts move in opposite directions**: how many run is a property of the
economy, how many switches is a property of how finely the book was written. (3) With affine
costs the envelope is a minimum of affine functions, hence concave, so the slope carried by the
owner never rises; **but the owner's index need not be monotone**, since `θ ↦ b(θ)` need not be.
**So "a technique leaves and returns", well posed with finitely many, is a statement about names,
and names are dense.** A single index has measure zero and its exact optimality at two separated
rates is not stable under refinement. **The continuum does not inherit the question; it inherits
the invariant, which is the coefficient and not the name.** (4) A land quality bought by one
method and produced by nothing hangs off by a single edge, adding a vertex and an edge, so `b₁`
is unchanged at every discretisation and therefore in the limit; what the limit changes is that
the marginal quality has measure zero, **contributing nothing to total rent while still pinning
the wage**.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

## B78: a machine's life is an envelope owner, and one age of it is one land with two users

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b78_scrapping.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b78_scrapping.py`, record `results/b78_scrapping.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B73 registered an endogenous scrapping date, noting it "needs a criterion for when a machine
stops being worth running", and a system carrying fixed capital and land at once. **Both are
done here, and the first registration's own wording turns out to be the answer: the criterion
was already in the framework.** **Theorem 23.** (1) Running the machine `T` times is a complete
production system, so B76's Theorem 21(1) applies verbatim and the chosen `T` is the one paying
the highest wage; which truncation runs is then B75's Theorem 20(1). **So the economic life is
not a parameter but the owner of `max_T w_T(r)`, and everything B76 proved about envelopes
transfers to it with no new argument.** (2) The wage-maximising truncation is exactly the
longest `T` whose **own** system has all old-machine prices non-negative. **The qualification is
load-bearing**: the untruncated system's first negative age is a different number, and a dense
sweep separates the two readings where four spot rates did not. (3) The number of times the life
changes as `r` runs is at most B76's `λ_s(k) − 1` with `k` the candidate truncations, and the
life may skip an age. **No direction is implied, and that is structural**: an owner sequence is
fixed by where curves cross, so there is no general direction to be had, which is why the
literature's examples fall on both sides. (4) An age position is delivered by one process and
bought by the next, so its degree is two and it closes a cycle, exactly as a land used by two
methods does in B72's Corollary 17.1; a land under extensive rent has degree one and closes
none. **Fixed capital and intensive rent are the same graph move and extensive rent is the other
one**, and the extra cycle per age is the extra machine price to determine.

**Criteria are counted by kind. A total across kinds would name nothing.**

## B79: the circular test is exactness, and GEKS is the projection

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b79_index_numbers.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b79_index_numbers.py`, record `results/b79_index_numbers.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

`b1_theorem.md` §2 says that `d¹ ∘ d⁰ = 0` on a graph is elementary, because a coboundary
telescopes. **In index number theory that sentence is Fisher's circular test (1922), and its
failure is chain drift**, which the scanner data literature measures directly. This station reads
the standard repair.

**Theorem 24.** Put `omega(j,k) = log P(j,k)` on the graph of comparisons actually computed;
`omega` is antisymmetric exactly when the bilateral index passes the time reversal test.
(1) A system of indexes is transitive if and only if `omega` is a coboundary, which is Theorem 1
read on that graph, and the potential is the log price level up to the choice of base.
(2) On the complete graph the normal equations give `psi(k) = (1/n) Σ_l omega(l,k)`, so
`psi(k) − psi(j) = (1/n) Σ_l [omega(j,l) + omega(l,k)]`, which exponentiates to
`∏_l [P(j,l) P(l,k)]^(1/n)` — **the GEKS index exactly as published**. So a transitive index is
the coboundary nearest the data and what it discards is the non-exact part.
(3) A chain drift is the sum along one closed walk, so it is **one** reading of that residual and
it moves with the chain; `rho` of Theorem 5 is the whole residual and does not depend on a path.
The number of independent readings is `b₁ = |E| − |V| + 1`, on the complete graph
`(n−1)(n−2)/2`. (4) A rolling window restricts to a subgraph, so it changes the cycle space: it
is a different projection, not the same one on less data. (5) Regions × periods is a product
graph, so Theorem 2 splits the obstruction into slice, agent and square, and
**the square part has dimension `(|V_G| − 1)(|V_H| − 1)`** — by the two vertex counts alone.
Computing more comparisons raises `b₁` and the other two parts and does not move it by one.

**Known answer.** Diewert (2021) Table 1 is four periods and two commodities with period 4
repeating period 1; Table 2 reports about two per cent downward for the chained Fisher and close
to three for the chained Törnqvist. Recomputed: **chained Fisher `0.979436` (`−2.06%`), chained
Törnqvist `0.972315` (`−2.77%`)**, both signs and both magnitudes read back.

## B80: a reducible economy, and why its two factors are read off two different parts

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b80_reducible.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b80_reducible.py`, record `results/b80_reducible.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. The solver is B75's, imported rather than
rewritten.**

Three registrations asked for one object: B75's "which component `α` and which `β` are read off
in a reducible system", B71's Kemeny-Morgenstern-Thompson generalisation, and B77's joining of
the continuum's active set to that decomposition. **All three turn on which part of a
disconnected economy a factor lives on, and the answer is that the two factors do not live on
the same family of parts.**

**Theorem 25.** A set `S` of goods is **independent** when some processes consume nothing
outside `S` and together produce every good in `S`; the economy is irreducible when it has no
proper independent subset. On a simple economy (`B = I`) that is closure under the out-edges of
`i → j when A[i,j] > 0`. (1) **Closure is not strong connectivity**: an SCC may consume from
outside and still be strongly connected, so the two families differ in every economy that is not
one piece. (2) **The two factors are read off the two families, one each**:

```
alpha_0 = max over S closed under consumption of 1 / lambda_S
beta_0  = 1 / lambda_PF(A) = min over all strongly connected components of 1 / lambda_S
```

**Proof.** A feasible `x` with support `S` must satisfy `0 ≥ alpha (x'A)_j` for every good `j`
outside `S`, so `(x'A)_j = 0` and no row indexed in `S` touches `j`: **the support of a quantity
vector is forced closed**. A feasible `p` with support `S` must satisfy `p_j ≤ beta (Ap)_j`
outside `S`, and `p_j = 0` satisfies that whatever `A` does: **the support of a price vector is
under no closure constraint**, so the minimum runs over every subset and is attained at the whole
matrix's Perron root. **The asymmetry is the direction of the edges**: a quantity programme
cannot expand on inputs drawn from a part that is not expanding with it, a price programme can
put a zero anywhere. (3) Irreducible collapses both families to the whole matrix, so
`alpha_0 = beta_0`, which is Theorem II, and **the gap is an `H⁰` quantity** in the directed
sense of `b4_directed_edges.md`. (4) The intensity support lies inside the part attaining
`alpha_0`, and the constraint is on the support and not on the count, so it survives whatever the
cardinality of the process set. (5) The gap and the spread of the cycle sums are two objects,
and both off-diagonal cells exist.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `--seed 80 --reps 10`.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B80-1 `known_answer` both published economies | example 1 irreducible, `alpha = beta = 1.259921050 = 2^(1/3)`; example 2 reducible, `alpha = 1.259921050`, `beta = 1.000000000`. Both inside `1e-8` of the published pair |
| PASS | B80-2 `instrument` the independence relation, two enumerations | 17 economies, one enumeration over subsets of goods and one over subsets of processes, **17 agree**; 14 reducible and 3 irreducible, so both branches occur. **The first version of the second route failed at 6 of 17**: it recorded only `produced(T)` where the definition admits every `S` between `consumed(T)` and `produced(T)`. The criterion caught a wrong translation, which is what it was for |
| PASS | B80-3 `own_reading` **the two families** | `alpha_0` is the max over the closed parts in **10 of 10**; `beta_0` is `1/lambda_PF` of the whole matrix, equivalently the min over all strongly connected components, in **10 of 10**. **Both cross readings fail**: `beta_0` off the closed family wrong in **7 of 10**, `alpha_0` off the all-components family wrong in **3 of 10**. So no single family carries both halves |
| PASS | B80-4 `own_reading` where the active set lives | the intensity support is closed under consumption and inside the part attaining `alpha_0` in 10 of 10; the price support sits outside that part in 3 of 10, which is the asymmetry stated as a count |
| PASS | B80-5 `own_reading` the gap is connectivity | 11 irreducible economies, every one with `\|alpha − beta\|` below `1e-6`, **zero exceptions**; 11 reducible, of which 5 carry a gap above `1e-4`, largest `1.511786`. **Stated one way**: reducible permits a gap and does not force one |
| PASS | B80-6 `own_reading` `H⁰` against `H¹` | both off-diagonal cells exhibited. Irreducible with a spread: gap `1.3e-14`, cycle sums spanning `0.0427` over 5 processes on 4 goods, one idle. On **20** irreducible simple economies the worst spread was `3.9e-14`, so that cell is structurally empty there: with `B = I` and `A` irreducible the Perron vector is strictly positive and nothing is idle. It opens exactly where B75's bound on the active set bites. Reducible with no spread inside a part: gap `0.259921` while each of the two parts carries one common sum |
| PASS | B80-7 `bookkeeping` the three registrations | B75 → B80-3 and B80-4; B71 → B80-1, B80-2 and B80-5; B77 → B80-4 |

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: which part of a disconnected economy each
factor is read off, and that the difference between the two parts is the direction of the edges.
What the von Neumann literature reads of it: the model, the two theorems, the two examples, and a
one-line summary of the reducible case.

| cell | content |
|---|---|
| **A** | Theorem I, Theorem II, both example economies and their factors. **Recorded as this framework being right, not as a debt** |
| **D** | Separating the two families, saying which factor is read off which, and giving the reason as a direction on the graph. The published line `alpha_0 = max_i alpha_i, beta_0 = min_i beta_i` is right on each half under a different reading of "part" and **no single reading carries both**, which is measured here in both directions. That literature states the line and does not split it |
| **D2** | Empty |
| **B** | Old reading on the scalar price field, not counted again. Nothing is scored against it here |
| **C** | Empty, and this station cannot produce it: it reads no data, so no point prediction of any other account is scored here |

## B81: the country-product-dummy method is the same projection on a second graph

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b81_cpd.md`. Checks in `experiments/b81_cpd.py`,
record `results/b81_cpd.json`, which carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero
data.**

B79 registered the other standard multilateral method as "a regression rather than a projection
and therefore a different loss". **A regression onto dummies is a projection, the loss is the
same sum of squares, and what differs is the graph.**

**Theorem 26.** The CPD equation is `log p[j,r] = z_j + beta_r + e[j,r]`, least squares, and the
parities are read off `beta` (Coondoo, Majumder and Ray 2004, eq. 1). Draw the bipartite graph:
a vertex per product, a vertex per country, an edge per observed cell.
(1) Put `psi(product j) = −z_j` and `psi(country r) = beta_r`; then `psi(r) − psi(j)` is the
fitted value on edge `(j,r)`, so **the fit is a coboundary and every cycle sums to zero**. That
is why the parities are transitive, and it is B79's Theorem 24(1) on a second graph. That paper
attributes the circularity to "the properties of the dummy variables regression model", which
names no mechanism; this is the mechanism.
(2) What CPD discards is the non-exact part, of dimension `b₁ = MR − (M+R) + 1 = (M−1)(R−1)` on a
complete tableau, **the same closed form as B79's square part, for the same reason: both graphs
are products**.
(3) **Two methods, one operation, two graphs**: GEKS on the complete country graph with the log
bilateral index on its edges, `b₁ = (R−1)(R−2)/2`; CPD on the bipartite graph with the log
individual price on its edges, `b₁ = (M−1)(R−1)`.
(4) On a complete equal-weight tableau the two return the same parities. **They part on the
incomplete tableau**: a bilateral index needs two countries to price something in common, so GEKS
needs that of every pair, while CPD needs only that the bipartite graph is connected.
(5) **Identification is connectivity**: with `c` components the design matrix's rank deficiency
is `c` and `b₁ = E − V + c`. Two components are two parities that cannot be compared at any
sample size. A missing cell is a missing edge, and the question is whether the graph stays in one
piece rather than how many cells are missing.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `--seed 81 --reps 10`.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B81-1 `known_answer` transitivity and base invariance | worst triple sum `2.2e-16`, worst shift on changing the base country `2.2e-16`, worst residual-design inner product `2.1e-15` |
| PASS | B81-2 `own_reading` **why they hold** | every cycle of the bipartite graph sums to `2.2e-16` on the fitted values and to **`2.207` or more on the raw log prices**. The cycle basis comes from the incidence pattern and never sees the regression; the cycle count matches the closed form and the incidence rank. **The second clause had to be able to fail**: if the raw prices were transitive too this would be reading an identity |
| PASS | B81-3 `own_reading` **two graphs** | `(M−1)(R−1)` against its incidence rank in 10 of 10, running 8 to 36; the country graph's `(R−1)(R−2)/2` running 3 to 15 |
| PASS | B81-4 `own_reading` do they agree | worst gap `2.0e-15` on complete equal-weight tableaux, two routes sharing no code: an OLS on dummies, and products averaged then multiplied out through the GEKS formula |
| PASS | B81-5 `own_reading` **identification is connectivity** | 40 sparse tableaux, **13 disconnected**; rank deficiency equals the component count in 40 of 40, `b₁ = E − V + c` matching the incidence rank throughout |
| PASS | B81-6 `instrument` the gauge | dropping each dummy in turn moves the fitted values by at most `2.4e-15` and the coefficients by up to `1.139`. **Both halves are required**: unchanged coefficients would mean the gauge was never exercised |
| PASS | B81-7 `bookkeeping` B79's registration | named, with the correction to its wording |

**The two methods are not an academic pairing.** The International Comparison Program runs both
at the same level of the same round: basic-heading parities by the Jevons index made transitive by
GEKS **and** by the country-product-dummy method, each with a weighted version, aggregated with
GEKS again. **The two graphs of Theorem 26(3) are two graphs the same round draws over the same
prices.**

**Placement.** What this framework reads of the world: that the fit is a difference of a
potential, which is why the parities are transitive; that the two standard multilateral methods
are one operation on two graphs; and that whether the parities exist at all is connectivity. What
that literature reads of it: the equation, the estimator, the transitivity, the base invariance.

| cell | content |

| **A** | The equation, the estimator, transitivity and base-region invariance. **Recorded as this framework being right, not as a debt** |
| **D** | The mechanism behind the circularity, which that paper attributes to "the properties of the dummy variables regression model"; the two graphs and the two counts of what each discards; and identification read as connectivity rather than as missing data |
| **D2** | Empty |
| **B** | Old reading on the scalar price field, not counted again. Nothing is scored against it here |
| **C** | Empty, and this station cannot produce it: it reads no data, so no point prediction of any other account is scored here |

## B82: the two families on a rectangular economy, and they are two index sets

**RUN: 2026-09-12. Statement and proof in `docs/b82_rectangular_parts.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b82_rectangular_parts.py`, record `results/b82_rectangular_parts.json`, which carries
the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. The solver is B75's and the independence
machinery is B80's; both are imported rather than rewritten.**

B80 proved the two-factor split for a simple economy and registered the general rectangular case.
**The support argument holds, and the general statement is sharper than the registration expected.**

**Theorem 27.** Write `produced(T)` and `consumed(T)` for the goods a process set makes and uses.
(1) Let `T = supp(x)`. For a good outside `produced(T)` the quantity constraint reads
`0 ≥ alpha (x'A)_j`, so `(x'A)_j = 0`: **the support of `x` is a process set that produces
everything it consumes**, `consumed(T) ⊆ produced(T)`. (2) Let `S = supp(p)`. A process consuming
nothing in `S` has `(Ap)_i = 0`, so its constraint reads `(Bp)_i ≤ 0`: **no process produces into
`S` without consuming from `S`**. (3) Hence

```
alpha_0 = max over admissible process sets T of alpha(T, produced(T))
beta_0  = min over admissible good sets S    of beta(rows touching S, S)
```

**two extrema over two families over two different index sets.** (4) `B = I` makes a process
produce exactly its own good, so `produced(T) = T` and the first family's image is a family of
goods, which is B80's family of independent subsets. **That identification is a property of the
simple case, not of the model**, which is why B80's version could not be read off as the general
one.

**Six criteria, all passing** at `--seed 82 --reps 8`.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B82-1 `known_answer` both published economies | `3 × 4`: `alpha = beta = 1.259921050`; `5 × 6`: `alpha = 1.259921050`, `beta = 1.000000000`, both inside `1e-8` |
| PASS | B82-2 `instrument` **it specialises to B80** | on 8 simple economies the image of the process family under `T → produced(T)` is B80's family of independent good sets, **8 of 8**. A disagreement would mean one of the two stations has the condition wrong |
| PASS | B82-3 `own_reading` **the two families** | 9 rectangular economies: `alpha_0` is the max over admissible process sets in **9 of 9**, worst departure `1.3e-14`; `beta_0` is the min over admissible good sets in **9 of 9**, worst `3.8e-15` |
| PASS | B82-5 `own_reading` **two index sets** | the image of the process family and the good family are different families in **15 of 16** rectangular economies |
| PASS | B82-6 `own_reading` the solution's own supports | the intensity support satisfies the process condition and the price support the good condition in 9 of 9. **Neither condition is imposed anywhere in the solver; both are read off what it returns** |
| PASS | B82-7 `bookkeeping` B80's registration | named, with the way the answer is sharper than it |

**`B82-4` is not a hole left by a withdrawn reading**: the two halves are checked in one sweep
because they share the economies they run on, and the numbering was left as it stood after the
merge rather than renumbered.

## B83: the space-and-time square on the ICP, which is the number the World Bank sets by hand

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and readings in `docs/b83_icp_square.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b83_icp_square.py`, record `results/b83_icp_square.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Two published benchmark rounds and two published price indices;
nothing is estimated. Fetching needs a machine that can reach the source: the sandbox and the
bridge both get 403.**

B79 registered a question, whether any published space-and-time comparison has links dense enough
to identify the square part on its own. **The International Comparison Program does.** Each round
publishes a benchmark parity per economy and the World Bank extrapolates between rounds with a
price index, so two rounds and two years close a loop per economy:

```
loop(a) = log P1(a) - log[ P0(a) * rel(a) ],   rel(a) = (I(a,t1)/I(a,t0)) / (I(base,t1)/I(base,t0))
```

**A scalar price field on the published figures predicts every one of these is exactly zero**,
with nothing free to fit: if the number on each (economy, year) is the difference of a potential, carrying an old benchmark
forward by relative inflation returns the new one exactly.

**The two benchmarks must be the two rounds as each published them.** They are served as separate
sources stamped 2020-10-21 and 2024-08-04, so the earlier figures predate the later round. The
filled annual series is not usable: its earlier value sits on the later basis and closes part of
the loop by construction.

**The floor is measured, and counting printed digits would have measured the serialiser instead.**
One source prints `1` for the base economy and `4.18381118774414` for China; a digit-counted floor
differs by five orders of magnitude for two figures from the same batch. All 2,333 published values
round-trip to within `5.94e-08` of a float32, below half a unit, so storage is uniform and over six
legs contributes `7.14e-07`. **What binds is the choice of index**: the same square computed with
the GDP deflator and with the consumer price index differs by up to `0.6484`, median `0.0344`,
about 48,000 times storage, and that gap touches neither benchmark, being
`log(rel_cpi / rel_deflator)`.

**Nine criteria, all passing.**

**Scope, added 2026-09-13.** The object measured is the published index, which is what the point
prediction is about. An aggregate can break transitivity on its own, a Fisher or Tornqvist index
over commodities whose underlying prices did come from one potential needing no zero loop, **so a
non-zero loop here refutes a potential on the published figures and does not by itself place the
non-exactness in the underlying per-commodity prices.** This station's own binding floor is the
choice of index, `0` to `0.6484`, which is that same effect measured. **And the float32
round-trip shows storage granularity and not the accuracy of what was measured**, so the `7.14e-07`
it gives is used only as a lower bound on the noise, four orders below the binding floor.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B83-1 `instrument` coverage closes | 181 carry all four legs, 38 named with a reason, 219 in the universe; none dropped silently, none counted twice, every absence carrying its reason |
| PASS | B83-2 `premise` two rounds, not one back-revised | separate sources, stamps 2020-10-21 and 2024-08-04. Failing this stops the station rather than downgrading it |
| PASS | B83-3 `instrument` **the floor is measured** | storage `7.14e-07` over six legs from 2,333 values, worst printing gap `5.94e-08`; index spread `0` to `0.6484`, median `0.0344`. 15 economies have no second index and take no verdict |
| PASS | B83-4 `rival` a scalar potential predicts exactly zero | **77 of 164 countable squares stand at two floors or more**, median multiple 4.2, largest `-4.1460` at Zimbabwe. 87 cannot be separated from zero, 15 have no floor, 2 sit across a currency changeover; all three take no verdict |
| PASS | B83-5 `own_reading` the count is `(T-1)(R-1)` | closed form 180; the graph built from the legs has 387 nodes, 566 edges, one component, so `b1 = 180`. Built from the legs and not from the rows, so a filter that admits a different set shows up instead of agreeing by construction |
| PASS | B83-6 `own_reading` the squares as objects | each printed with its floor and multiple. 60 of the 77 are negative: the new benchmark comes in below the extrapolation more often than not |
| PASS | B83-7 `instrument` the degenerate square | base against itself reads `0.00e+00` |
| PASS | B83-9 `instrument` **a conversion is not a reading** | 2 of 166 ratios sit near one. Mauritania's ouguiya went ten new for one old in 2018 and the kuna became the euro at 7.53450; net of those the squares are `-0.0553` and `-0.0517` against a median of `0.0643`, which is the check |
| PASS | B83-8 `bookkeeping` the record carries what the table says | 181 rows at 12 fields, 38 reasons, 2 stamps |

**Zimbabwe is the mechanism in the open.** Its two benchmarks are `0.5112` and `0.5414`, nearly the
same, while relative inflation over the window is 66.9, so the extrapolation predicts `34.21`.
Under a hyperinflation the index and the benchmark stop being two views of one thing.

**The kinds are not added.** Only `B83-4` is about a theory; the rest are about this run's
instrument, its premise or its bookkeeping.

component and needs two vintages of the deflator.
## B84: weighting the country-product-dummy method changes the metric and not the topology

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b84_weighted_cpd.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b84_weighted_cpd.py`, record `results/b84_weighted_cpd.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B81's tableau generator, design matrix,
incidence matrix and cycle basis are imported rather than rewritten, so a disagreement between the
two stations is a real one.**

B81 section 6 stated, and said plainly that it did not check, that the weighted CPD the
International Comparison Program actually runs is the same projection in a weighted inner product.
**It is, and the sentence was missing a boundary.**

**Theorem 28.** With `W = diag(w_e)`, `w_e > 0`, the weighted fit is
`psi_W = argmin sum_e w_e (y_e − (d⁰psi)_e)²`, which is B81's problem in the inner product
`<a,b>_W = a'Wb`. (1) The fitted value is `d⁰psi_W`, a coboundary by construction, so **the weights
cannot break transitivity**: the design's column space is the exact subspace either way and only
which element of it is nearest depends on `W`. (2) The normal equations are a weighted graph
Laplacian `L_W psi = d⁰'Wy`, whose null space for `w > 0` is the constants on each component, so
identification is exactly B81's Theorem 26(5). (3) `b₁ = E − V + c` contains no weight: **the
weights change which coboundary is nearest, not how much is discarded in dimension.** (4) **Zero is
not a small weight.** As `w_e → 0` the parities converge to the fit with `e` deleted, linearly in
`w_e`, while `b₁` and `c` jump only at zero: an edge in a cycle drops `b₁` by one, a bridge raises
`c` by one and two parities stop being comparable at any weight. (5) The unweighted case is the
member at `w = 1`, and the fit is invariant to `w → λw`.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `--seed 84 --reps 10`.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B84-1 `known_answer` unit weights are B81, the scale does nothing, the gauge is sound | fitted values agree to `0.00e+00` using B81's own solver; scaling every weight by 7.3 moves the parities by `2.2e-15`; re-gauging to each other base moves no pairwise difference by more than `2.2e-16`, **while the raw coefficients move by at least `0.163` when the weights change** |
| PASS | B84-2 `own_reading` coboundary, and the prices are not | 98 cycles: at most `2.2e-16` on the weighted fitted values, at least `0.928` on the raw log prices |
| PASS | B84-3 `own_reading` **metric, not topology** | six dispersions on ten tableaux: `b₁` and the rank deficiency hold at every dispersion and equal the closed form and the component count, **while the parities move by up to `1.819`** |
| PASS | B84-4 `own_reading` **zero is an edge leaving** | ten cycle edges converge to the deleted-edge solution, `1.1e-12` at the bottom of the ladder, and the distance tracks the weight to a ratio of `0.85` to `1.00`; ten bridges raise the component count and leave `b₁` alone |
| PASS | B84-5 `own_reading` how far the two get | largest change in any pairwise comparison, median by dispersion of log weight: `0.25 → 0.15`, `0.5 → 0.36`, `1.0 → 0.68`, `2.0 → 0.81`, `4.0 → 1.60`. The spread of the difference, so the number is the same under any gauge |
| PASS | B84-6 `instrument` two ways to solve it | `6.3e-15`. **An implementation check and not a second route**: the normal equations make the two equal by a theorem |
| PASS | B84-7 `bookkeeping` B81's section 6 | discharged, and that section's wording corrected in the same round |

**Two things the checks found that the statement did not contain.** At the density the rest of the
station uses, the bipartite graphs come back **two-edge-connected**, so no bridge exists and no
vanishing weight can disconnect anything; the bridges had to be drawn from sparser tableaux. That
sharpens B81's Theorem 26(5) from "connectivity decides" to "connectivity decides, and on a
well-covered round it is not close". And the approach to the deleted-edge solution is **linear in
the weight**, so a small weight is a small perturbation rather than a partial deletion.

**Sharpened 2026-09-15 by B103** (`docs/b103_time_reachability.md`, Corollary 41.1).
The distance to the deleted-edge solution is exactly `|D| · s · w/(1 + wR)`, with `R` the
effective resistance between the edge's ends in the deleted tableau, so the ratio printed for
`B84-4` is `(1 + w_b R)/(1 + w_a R)`: its low end `0.85` is that curvature on the first step at
`R = 1.8`, the second steps sit within `1.8e-3` of one, and its high end is float noise on the
last step. The linear reading holds as the weight goes to zero.

**Three criteria carry a clause whose job is to be able to fail**: `B84-1` needs the raw
coefficients to move, or its gauge clause reports that a gauge nobody exercised is harmless;
`B84-2` needs the raw log prices not to telescope and counts the cycles it tested, since a tableau
with no cycle passes both halves for nothing; `B84-3` needs the parities to move, since an
unchanged topology is also what a weight that never reached the solve looks like.
## B85: several columns at once, where Okishio's equivalence becomes an implication

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b85_simultaneous.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b85_simultaneous.py`, record `results/b85_simultaneous.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B69's system generator, Perron solver,
basket and substitution form are imported rather than rewritten, so a disagreement between the two
stations is a real one.**

B69's Theorem 14(1) is an equivalence on the one column that changed, and its scope section
registered the several-column case as "the same argument with `p M' ≤ λ p` holding on a set of
columns". **Half of that is right.**

**Theorem 29.** (1) **The forward implication carries over unchanged**: every column in `S` no
dearer at the prices in force and one strictly cheaper gives `p M' ≤ λ p` with strict inequality
somewhere, so `λ' < λ` and `r' > r` by the same Collatz-Wielandt step. (2) **The converse does
not.** A set with some columns dearer and others cheaper can raise the rate, and **1,461 of 4,092
drawn several-column substitutions do**, the largest lifting the rate from `0.257` to `0.623` on
four columns of which one got dearer. So the equivalence is **not the `|S| = 1` case of a
several-column equivalence, it is a property of `|S| = 1`**: with one column the prices in force
see everything that moved. (3) What survives is a bracket over the moved columns,
`sigma = min_{k∈S} (pM')_k/p_k` and `rho = max`, computable with no re-solving: `rho ≤ λ` gives
`r' > r`, `sigma ≥ λ` gives `r' < r`, and `sigma < λ < rho` **does not decide**. At `|S| = 1` the
ends coincide and that third cell is empty, which is Theorem 14(1). (4) **The bracket over every
column is true and useless**: an unchanged column sits at `λ` exactly, so it contains `λ` whenever
one column is left alone. (5) Irreducibility comes from the basket: `b > 0` and `l' > 0` make
`b l'` strictly positive, so `M'` is positive whatever the substitution did to `A`.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `--seed 85 --systems 120`, 5,532 substitutions, one second.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B85-1 `known_answer` it reduces to B69 at one column | the sign of the change is the sign of the saving on `1440 / 1440`, on B69's own systems and baskets with B69's solver |
| PASS | B85-2 `own_reading` the forward half | `601` draws have every changed column cheaper and the rate rises on all `601`. **The premise count is in the verdict**: zero counterexamples is free on zero cases |
| PASS | B85-3 `own_reading` **the converse fails** | `1461` of `4092`, found rather than assumed. Had none been found it would read "not found", not "does not exist" |
| PASS | B85-4 `own_reading` the three cells | below `λ`: `1306` draws, rate rises `1306`. Above: `1360`, rises `0`. **Straddling: `2866`, rises `1461` and falls `1405`** — both outcomes inside the undecided cell. **No single-column draw straddles**, which is the clause that tells this bracket from the all-column one |
| PASS | B85-5 `own_reading` **how often the old prices decide** | 1 column `1440/1440`, 2 columns `705/1440`, 3 columns `375/1440`, 4 columns `146/1212` |
| PASS | B85-6 `instrument` the hypothesis | basket and labour vector strictly positive on `5532/5532`, so `M'` is positive. **The irreducibility computation cannot fail while that holds**, so it is a check on the test rather than a third reading (`D35` second clause), guarded by a hand-made reducible matrix |
| PASS | B85-7 `bookkeeping` B69's registration | discharged and written back the same round; this criterion failed on the first run, which is what it is for |

**The first version of the discriminant took the bracket over every column and reported that the
prices decide nothing even at one column**, contradicting Theorem 14(1). The contradiction is what
showed the object was wrong, and it was visible only because `B85-5` prints the counts by set
size. **A discriminant that contradicts a known answer on the cell where the answer is known is a
wrong discriminant, not a new finding.**

**Both registrations were done on 2026-09-13 as B91 below**, and they turn out to be one
question. This station's hypothesis was supplied by its generator; removing that, `M'` is
reducible on 466 of 1,200 draws, **the forward implication survives it and the strict positivity
of prices does not**, and one power iteration decides a quarter of the undecided cell where the
prices in force decide none of it.
## B86: the non-substitution theorem, or demand cannot move this field

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b86_non_substitution.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b86_non_substitution.py`, record `results/b86_non_substitution.json`, which carries
the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data.**

B85 holds the real wage basket fixed and reads the rate: a cheaper column raises it. **Hold the
rate fixed and read the prices instead and the same Perron monotonicity gives the non-substitution
theorem** of Samuelson, Georgescu-Roegen and Arrow. With one primary factor, no joint production
and constant returns, the cost-minimising technique and the whole price field depend on the rate
and the available methods only, not on the composition of final demand.

```
B85   basket fixed, rate read      a cheaper column raises r
B86   rate fixed, prices read      a cheaper column lowers every price
```

**Theorem 30.** With `p_T(r) = l_T[I − (1+r)A_T]^{-1}` over the techniques that pick one method
per good: (1) the expression has no demand in it, which is true by inspection and is not the
theorem, since it leaves open which technique is in use. (2) **The componentwise minimum over
techniques is attained by a single technique**, which is the substantive half and **is what makes
"the cheapest technique" definable without naming a demand vector**: without it one would have to
say cheapest for whom. (3) Hence the technique and the field are demand-free and demand moves only
`x = [I − A_{T*}]^{-1} d`. (4) **Cohomologically, demand can neither create nor destroy an
obstruction**: every square, `rho` and `b₁` is a function of the field, which is a function of the
methods and the rate. (5) It is B85's monotonicity with the other thing held fixed.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `--seed 86 --systems 60`: 240 (system, rate) pairs, 5,512
techniques enumerated, under a second.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B86-1 `known_answer` a hand-checked case | one good: `l/(1−(1+r)a) = 1.2820512821`, solver `1.2820512821`. Two goods with two methods each, built so the cheaper method for the first good carries more labour and less input and cannot be read off either column alone |
| PASS | B86-2 `own_reading` **the componentwise minimum is attained** | by a single technique on `240 / 240` systems |
| PASS | B86-3 `own_reading` demand moves quantities, not the field | over `1200` demand pairs the field moves by `0.00e+00` **while the quantity vector moves by at least `0.1576`**. Both halves required: a field that did not move is also what a demand that never reached the solve looks like |
| PASS | B86-4 `own_reading` **a second primary factor breaks it** | the technique changes on `53 / 60` drawn method sets when a second factor is repriced, **against `0 / 60` for the same search with one factor**, which is the control |
| PASS | B86-5 `own_reading` **joint production breaks it** | the componentwise minimum is attained by no technique on `180 / 199` viable systems. **B70 already showed joint production parts the cycles from the commodities**, so this failure is derived rather than newly assumed: without one good per method there is no lattice of columns for the monotonicity to run on |
| PASS | B86-6 `instrument` the enumeration is complete | the technique count equals the product of the per-good method counts on `240 / 240`. Everything above is a statement about a minimum over a set, and a set short by one member would make all of it a statement about a different set |
| PASS | B86-7 `bookkeeping` the pair with B85 | written into B85's own file, so a reader of either finds the other; it failed on the first run, which is what it is for |

**Both failure modes are measured and each carries its control.** A search that switched under one
primary factor too would be finding its own noise rather than the failure of a hypothesis, and
`B86-5` had to find its cases and would have recorded "not found on this family" rather than "does
not exist".

**The continuum registration was done on 2026-09-13 as B93 below**, together with B77's
continuum on the other index: the minimum survives exactly when the per-good minimum is attained,
Theorem 30(2) being indifferent to cardinality, **and when it fails it fails by the infimum
escaping rather than by two goods wanting different techniques**.

**The second registration is done, 2026-09-13, at B87, and the guess in it was wrong.** It read
"a second primary factor is a second potential, so the field stops being one function". The field
stays one function: B72's Theorem 17(3) pins the wage to the lower envelope because rents have to
be non-negative. **What demand fixes is which lands are in use, a combinatorial object**, so its
action is a step function with at most `k` values rather than a continuum.

## B87: demand's grip on the field is combinatorial, and it is one dimension per land

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b87_demand_grip.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b87_demand_grip.py`, record `results/b87_demand_grip.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B72's envelope solver, land generator, graph
builder and Betti number are imported rather than rewritten, so a disagreement between the two
stations is a real one.**

B86 proved that with one primary factor demand moves nothing on the price side, then registered
the two-factor case with a guess: a second potential. **The guess is wrong and B72 already had the
shape.** Land is a position no cycle produces, a pendant vertex under extensive rent (Theorem
17(1)), and non-negative rents pin the wage to the lower envelope of the lands' own wage curves
(Theorem 17(3)). The second factor's price is not a free dimension. **What is not pinned is which
lands are in use, and Theorem 17(3) assumes all `k` are, which is exactly where demand enters.**

**Theorem 31.** With `k` lands of unit capacity ordered by their own wage curves, `n` other
produced goods, the rate fixed, and `S` the best `ceil(d)` lands: (1) demand acts on the field only
through `S`; (2) so that action is a step function with at most `k` values, constant between
thresholds and jumping at them; (3) `b₁ = |S| + n`, the number of operated methods, because a land
under extensive rent raises the vertex and edge counts together; (4) **hence each extensive step
costs exactly one dimension**, which is Theorem 30(4) turned over: with one primary factor demand
can neither create nor destroy an obstruction, with a scarce second factor it moves the dimension
one method at a time; (5) **the intensive margin costs two**, since a land taking a second method
stops being pendant and the second edge closes a cycle by B72's Corollary 17.1, so **intensive rent
arrives as a step of the demand sweep rather than as a separate model**; (6) what is claimed is the
dimension, and whether any particular cycle sum is non-zero is a different question.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `seed 87`, 200 systems, `k` from 2 to 6, 985 steps.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B87-1 `known_answer` full cultivation is B72's Theorem 17(3) | on `200 / 200` systems the last extensive step returns B72's wage and B72's marginal land, worst wage gap `0.00e+00` |
| PASS | B87-2 `own_reading` the cultivated set is nested and takes at most `k` values | nested at every step on `200 / 200` with exactly `k` distinct values, `k` running 2 to 6. **Counted rather than argued from the way the sweep is built**: the order comes from the envelope, and a different order would break nesting |
| PASS | B87-3 `own_reading` `b₁ = \|S\| + n`, from the drawn graph | agrees on `985 / 985` steps, computed from B72's incidence matrix rather than from the formula. **Its control is one land worked by two processes**, where the builder returns `4` against `3` for the extensive case, so the measurement is live rather than a closed form handed back to itself. The closed form first written down carried `\|S\| + n − 1` and the measurement is what said it was wrong by one |
| PASS | B87-4 `own_reading` the field is still inside a step and moves across one | `1570` demand pairs inside a step move the wage by at most `0.00e+00`; `585` adjacent pairs across a step move it by at least `2.16e-04`. **Both halves required**: a field that never moved is also what a demand that never reached the solve looks like |
| PASS | B87-5 `own_reading` the ladder, printed rather than counted | `[3,4,5,6,7,9]`, `[3,4,5,6,8]`, `[3,4,5,7]`, `[3,4,6]` and 196 more. **`+1` at every extensive step and `+2` at the intensive one**, on `200 / 200` |
| PASS | B87-6 `instrument` the thresholds are where they are computed to be | each of `585` is probed at `±1e-06` in demand and the cultivated set has `m` lands below and one more above, on `585 / 585`. **Checked rather than declared**, which is what gate six asks of a floor |
| PASS | B87-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B86's file names this station against the registration it opened, including why its guess was the wrong shape |

**At the intensive step this station claims the graph and not the field.** Two methods on one land
need the extra equation of B72's Corollary 17.1, which neither station carries, so B87-4 and B87-6
are restricted to extensive steps and say so in their own detail lines. B87-3 and B87-5 cover it
because the graph is drawn there and the Betti number is read off it.

**Registered, not scheduled.** Heterogeneous land capacities, where the thresholds stop being
integers and the step widths change while the ladder's shape does not; and a second rate, which
reorders the envelope and therefore the cultivated set, which is the interface to reswitching.

**The field at the intensive step was done on 2026-09-13 as B88 below, and it corrects this
station on a second point.** The cycle does not only add a dimension, it replaces the boundary
condition, so the land that was marginal starts paying rent. And **putting the second method on
the best land was a fiat**: with one intensification technology per system the acre that takes
it is the most fertile on 558 of 1,762 systems and the marginal one on 406. This station's graph
reading survives because any acre with two users closes a cycle whichever acre it is.

## B88: the two margins cannot both be open, because they supply the same missing equation

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b88_two_margins.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b88_two_margins.py`, record `results/b88_two_margins.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B72's envelope solver and land generator and
B73's intensive pair are imported rather than rewritten, so a disagreement between the three
stations is a real one.**

B87 swept demand over a set of lands, found that the step past full extensive cultivation puts a
second method on one acre and raises `b₁` by two, **drew the graph there and did not solve it**,
because two methods on one acre need B73's Corollary 17.1. B73 has it, and joining the two gives a
constraint neither station could state alone.

**Theorem 32.** With `k` lands of unit capacity, corn the unit of account and the rate fixed:
(1) **the extensive system is short by one and the mixed system is square**, `k` equations in `k+1`
unknowns against `k+1` in `k+1`; (2) **so the boundary condition is displaced rather than dropped
by choice**, since a square system carrying it as well is over-determined by exactly one, and
B73's Theorem 18(4) had a boundary condition and a cycle closure as the two ways of closing two
different systems, while on one system they are alternatives; (3) **hence free land disappears at
the intensive margin**, as a matter of counting rather than of bargaining; (4) **viability is
B72's envelope rule applied to a closure rather than to a land**, `w_int ≤ w_ext` if and only if
every rent is non-negative; (5) three thresholds give four cells and **the third is new**, in
which the second method earns a non-negative rent on its own acre and still drives another land's
rent below zero, because what it moves is the whole system's wage; (6) **which acre takes it is
decided by the closure and not by fertility**, the two being different orders.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `seed 88`, 3,000 systems, `k` from 2 to 6, 12,009 mixed
configurations.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B88-1 `known_answer` the imported pieces are the imported pieces | the rent written on a land not being intensified reproduces B72's own to `0.00e+00` over 3,000 systems; a pair solved by hand at `q = (1, 1.5)`, `a = (0.2, 0.5)`, `l = (0.4, 0.9)`, `r = 0` gives `w = 0.4` and `rho = 0.64`, and the solver agrees to machine precision |
| PASS | B88-2 `own_reading` **the counting, and the over-determination** | shapes printed rather than counted: extensive `k` equations by `k+1` unknowns at every `k` from 2 to 6, mixed `k+1` by `k+1`. **The rent the boundary condition would set to zero comes out at least `8.0e-05` from zero over 12,009 configurations, against `1.1e-16` on the extensive control**, which is what separates two closures disagreeing from a solver tolerance |
| PASS | B88-3 `own_reading` four cells, all occupied | not worth operating on its own acre `2478`; **profitable on its own acre and infeasible for the system `1703`**; viable `3917`; wage non-positive `3911` |
| PASS | B88-4 `instrument` the equivalence | `w_int ≤ w_ext` and `every rent ≥ 0` agree on `8098 / 8098`. **An implementation check and not a reading** per D35's second clause: a rent falls in the wage and the marginal one is zero exactly at the envelope, so the two statements are one statement |
| PASS | B88-5 `own_reading` **no free land** | the formerly marginal land pays a strictly positive rent on `3917 / 3917` viable configurations, the smallest `1.5e-04`. **Not implied by viability**, which would be satisfied by a rent of exactly zero, and exactly zero is what a boundary condition surviving the step would look like |
| PASS | B88-6 `own_reading` **which acre, and B87's fiat** | one intensification technology per system, so the choice is a reading rather than a draw. The acre taken is the most fertile on `558 / 1762` and the marginal one on `406`; the two orders differ on `599 / 1498`; **both choosing rules run over the same candidates part on `305 / 1762`** |
| PASS | B88-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B87, B73 and B72 each name this station |

**B88-6 counts where two rules part rather than where one rule lands**, and the first version did
not. Reporting only that the fertile acre is taken 558 times of 1,762 does not separate "the
closure chooses" from "the closure agrees with fertility and the fertile acre is often not a
candidate", since both rules run over the viable set. A mutation that switched the choice to
fertility passed the first version and is caught by this one.

**The second-rate registration was done on 2026-09-13 as B90 below**, and it carries the
reswitching it expected plus two things it did not: the intensive margin closes below the
extensive one, leaving a band in which demand above capacity cannot be met at all, and the viable
set of rates need not be an interval.

**The other two were done on 2026-09-13 as B89 below.** A separate intensification technology on
each acre does not make fertility the choosing rule: on 234 systems the acre taken is the most
fertile on 38 and the two rules part on 61. **Two acres intensified at the same time is not a
configuration at all**: it is over-determined, which falls out of a counting identity that has
this station and B72 as its only two square cells.

## B89: one identity covers every configuration of the two margins, and it has four cells

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b89_degrees_of_freedom.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b89_degrees_of_freedom.py`, record `results/b89_degrees_of_freedom.json`, which
carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B72's envelope solver and land
generator and B73's intensive pair are imported rather than rewritten.**

B88 counted two configurations. Counting all of them at once turns that into an identity, and the
identity says which configurations exist at all. Write `c` for the cultivated lands, `j` for how
many are worked by two methods, and `f = 1` when some cultivated land still has spare capacity so
that a boundary condition applies. **The station builds the rows itself and knows neither
imported solver**, so the solvers have to agree with the rows.

**Theorem 33.** (1) `equations − unknowns = j + f − 1`. (2) **So the system is square exactly
when `j + f = 1`, and the two solutions of that are the two stations already on the board**:
`(0, 1)` is B72's extensive rent with a free margin and `(1, 0)` is B88's mixed system with none.
(3) **Two classical facts are corollaries of the arithmetic, in general position**: `j ≥ 1` with
`f = 1` is over-determined, so intensive cultivation does not coexist with spare capacity, and
`j ≥ 2` is over-determined, so at most one acre is worked by two methods. (3a) **General position
is where that corollary lives**: over-determined rows can still be consistent when the technical
coefficients coincide exactly, which a random draw misses with probability one, **so the sweep
cannot meet an exception however large it grows**. They are built instead, one line of recipe per
cell, and the identity is untouched by them. (4) The remaining cell
`(0, 0)` is short by one, and **the wage is then not determined by cost**. (5) **That family has
a direction and the direction is the labour vector**, `(1, −λ₁, …, −λ_c)`: raise the wage by one
and every rent falls by that land's labour input, so the missing equation is the one that says
where on the wage-rent frontier the economy sits. (6) Hence the demand ladder walks along the
square cells and nowhere else, and **B87's step of `+2` in `b₁` is one dimension for the added
process and one for the cycle that replaces the boundary condition**: the graph gains a cycle
exactly where the price system loses a degree of freedom.

**Clause (3) was published on 2026-09-13 without its general-position qualifier and carries it the
same day**, no measured quantity having moved; `docs/b89_degrees_of_freedom.md` §1 has it.

All criteria pass at `seed 89`, 300 systems, `c` from 2 to 6, 6,276 configurations, and 40
constructed systems in each of the two excluded cells.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B89-1 `known_answer` the two square cells are the two solvers' own answers | `(0, 1)` matches B72's envelope wage to `2.2e-15` over 1,046 cases and `(1, 0)` matches B73's pair to `4.5e-11`. **It caught a real fault**: the first version put the boundary condition on the last land in the list rather than on the marginal one, which disagrees with B72 whenever the list is not sorted by fertility, and it read `3.2483` before the fix |
| PASS | B89-2 `own_reading` the identity | holds on all 30 distinct shapes drawn, `c` from 2 to 6, **shapes printed rather than counted** |
| PASS | B89-3 `own_reading` **three states over the grid** | `(0,0)` a family of solutions on 1,046; `(0,1)` and `(1,0)` one solution on 1,046 each; `(1,1)`, `(2,0)` and `(2,1)` no solution on 1,046 each. **No cell is ever mixed** |
| PASS | B89-4 `own_reading` **the frontier** | the family is one-dimensional and its direction is `(1, −λ)` to `1.3e-15` over 1,046 cases |
| PASS | B89-5 `own_reading` a separate second method per acre | on 234 systems with a viable acre, a mean of `1.72` acres are viable, the acre taken is the most fertile on `38`, and **the two choosing rules part on `61`**. Giving each acre its own technology does not make fertility the rule; it adds a second source of difference between them |
| PASS | B89-6 `instrument` **the line is measured** | the largest residual among cases with a solution is `4.4e-13`, the smallest among those without is `3.0e-04`, a ratio of `7.0e+08`. A tolerance chosen in advance would be a number this station made up |
| PASS | B89-8 `own_reading` **the excluded cells, built rather than drawn** | `(1, 1)`: `36 / 36` built are over-determined and consistent, worst residual `5.6e-15`, all with non-negative rents. `(2, 0)`: `35 / 35`, worst `2.2e-15`, `34` with non-negative rents. One instance returns a wage of `0.5693` with rents `[0.5611, 0.5668]` on four rows in three unknowns |
| PASS | B89-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B88 and B72 each name this station |

**Every mutation seeded was caught but one, which is an equivalent implementation rather than a
fault.**
It reads the residual off the solver's own output instead of recomputing it; that output is empty
exactly where the true residual is zero and non-empty exactly where it is the true residual, so it
returns the same verdict in every cell. **A mutation that changes no verdict is not a miss**, and
saying so is cheaper than adding a probe for a fault that is not there.

**Two gaps in the self-test rather than in the criteria, both fixed.** A fixture built so the
closure order matches the fertility order trips both of B89-5's clauses at once and so cannot say
which is load-bearing; making the most fertile acre unviable as well trips only the clause that
counts where the two rules part. And B89-3 did not require every `(j, f)` cell to be present, so a
grid missing the two-acre cases would have reported the cells it happened to have.

**Registered, not scheduled.** `j ≥ 3` and more than two methods on one acre, where the identity
is stated for any `j` and the grid stops one past the point where squareness fails; heterogeneous
land capacities, where the thresholds stop being integers and `f` needs restating; and whether the
consistent over-determined systems of B89-8 are economically reachable, which asks whether anything
would choose that configuration rather than whether it solves.

## B90: the rate moves two orders on one system, and they switch at different rates

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b90_two_switch_structures.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b90_two_switch_structures.py`, record `results/b90_two_switch_structures.json`, which
carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B72's envelope solver and land
generator, B73's intensive pair and B89's row builder are imported rather than rewritten.**

B88 and B89 both run at one rate, and B88 registered a second rate as the interface to
reswitching. Sweeping it turns up three things and only the third is the one the registration
expected. **Every switch reported is bisected from the grid interval it was spotted in**, so the
grid finds candidates and does not decide them.

**Theorem 34.** (1) **The intensive margin closes below the extensive one.** Every land is
workable up to the rate at which the worst land's own wage curve reaches zero, and the intensive
closure stops lying under the envelope strictly below that. (2) **So there is a band of rates in
which demand above capacity cannot be met at all**: every land is workable and no acre can take a
second method, so by Theorem 33 the configuration is `(j, f) = (0, 0)`, the rows are consistent,
the extra output is not produced and the wage is not determined by cost. (3) **The viable set of
rates need not be an interval**: the margin can close as the rate rises and open again above it,
which is reswitching of a margin rather than of a technique. (4) **Which land owns the extensive
envelope and which acre takes the second method are two orders that almost never switch at the
same rate**, so neither is a reparametrisation of the other.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `seed 90`, 500 systems, `k` from 3 to 5, a rate grid of 601
points to `3.0`, 50 bisection steps.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B90-1 `known_answer` the state function is B72's answer at B88's rate | at `r = 0.05` the envelope wage and the marginal land agree with B72's own solver on `500 / 500`, worst gap `0.00e+00` |
| PASS | B90-2 `own_reading` **the band** | the intensive margin closes strictly below the extensive one on `357 / 362` systems where both open, median `0.295` in the rate, within one grid step on `5`. **Checked rate by rate and not inferred from two endpoints**: `0` of the 357 bands contain a rate at which some acre is viable |
| PASS | B90-3 `own_reading` **the viable set need not be an interval** | `326` systems with one block, `28` with two, `5` with three, `3` with four, `138` with none. **Printed as intervals**: `[[0.0, 0.365], [0.4, 0.535]]`, `[[0.0, 0.135], [0.31, 0.64], [0.875, 0.905]]`, `[[0.0, 0.175], [0.625, 0.705]]` |
| PASS | B90-4 `own_reading` **two switch structures** | both switch on `100` systems and **share a grid interval on `1`**; only the envelope owner on `164`, **only the intensified acre on `79`**, neither on `157` |
| PASS | B90-5 `instrument` **located, not read off the grid** | `557` switches bisected, widest remaining bracket `4.4e-16` against a grid step of `0.005`, a factor of `1.1e+13` |
| PASS | B90-6 `own_reading` the band is B89's cell | at a rate inside the band, B89's own row builder returns its indeterminate cell on `357 / 357` |
| PASS | B90-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B88 and B89 each name this station |

**B90-4's load-bearing count is the 79 and not the 1.** A shared-interval count of one in a
hundred could be read as the two orders switching together and this station missing it; the 79
systems on which the acre switches while the envelope never does cannot be that, since there is no
envelope switch there to be seen through another variable. A mutation that shadowed every acre
switch with an envelope switch one interval along passed the first version and is caught by this
one.

**B90-2 is checked rate by rate for the same reason.** Subtracting two upper endpoints gives a
band even when the viable set has holes, so a system whose margin reopens would report a band
containing viable rates. **Eight mutations, all eight caught**, two of them only after the
criteria were strengthened.

**Registered, not scheduled.** Whether the four-block systems have further blocks above `3.0`;
one intensification technology per acre rather than per system, which is B89-5's setting carried
into the rate sweep; and how the switch density depends on the number of lands, which is read here
only at three, four and five.

## B91: what the irreducibility hypothesis buys, and how much more than the old prices decides

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b91_thin_basket_and_iteration.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b91_thin_basket_and_iteration.py`, record
`results/b91_thin_basket_and_iteration.json`, which carries the configuration it ran under. Paper
station: zero data. B69's generator, Perron solver, basket and augmented matrix and B85's cell
discriminant are imported rather than rewritten.**

B85 left two registrations and they turn out to be one question: how much of Theorem 14 survives
when its hypothesis stops being free. **B85's hypothesis was supplied by its own generator**, a
strictly positive basket against a strictly positive labour vector making `b l'` positive and `M'`
positive whatever the substitution did. This station removes both, with a bundle that does not
contain every intermediate good and a substitution allowed to set entries of `A` to zero.

**Theorem 35.** (1) **The hypothesis is not free once the basket has zeros**: `M'` is reducible on
a large minority of drawn systems that were irreducible before. (2) **What irreducibility buys is
the price vector and not the direction of the rate**: on the reducible systems the forward
implication holds without exception while the left Perron vector loses strict positivity on a
minority. **Reducibility permits a zero rather than producing one**, `386` of `466` reducible draws
carrying a strictly positive vector, and where one appears depends on which block dominates; a
comparison of Perron roots needs the vector not at all. (3) **The prices in force decide none of the undecided cell, and that is
structural**: an unchanged column returns exactly `λ`, so the bracket contains it. (4) Iteration
decides it and the curve is the answer. (5) **The bracket is never wrong at any iteration**, which
is Collatz-Wielandt, so the iteration is a safe early exit rather than an approximation. (6) What
sets the number of iterations is how far the bracket has to travel and how fast it travels.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `seed 91`, 1,200 thin-basket draws and 1,368 iteration draws.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B91-1 `known_answer` the imported pieces, and the vector used as prices | that vector is a left eigenvector of `M` to under `1e-9` relative; B85's own generator gives a strictly positive basket, an unchanged zero pattern and an irreducible `M'` on every draw, all three cells occupied |
| PASS | B91-2 `own_reading` **the hypothesis stops being free** | `M'` reducible on `466 / 1200` draws against `0 / 1200` before the substitution, a median of `2` entries of `A` newly zero |
| PASS | B91-3 `own_reading` **the rate survives and the prices do not** | on the 466 reducible draws the premise is met on `398` and the root falls on `398 / 398`; the left Perron vector is strictly positive on `386 / 466` reducible against `734 / 734` irreducible. **Both halves counted on the same draws**, so the contrast is not between two samples |
| PASS | B91-4 `own_reading` **the curve** | of `678` straddling draws one iteration decides `173` (`25.5%`), two `333`, three `457`, five `588` (`86.7%`), ten `661`, and all `678` within `46`. **No threshold is placed on the curve, which is the reading itself** |
| PASS | B91-5 `instrument` never wrong, never decided at zero | verdicts agree with the recomputed root on `1368 / 1368` and `0` of `678` straddling draws are decided at zero iterations. **Both implementation checks** per D35's second clause |
| PASS | B91-6 `own_reading` what sets the count | iterations fall with the size of the move in the root, Spearman `-0.566`, and rise with the ratio of the second modulus to the first, Spearman `+0.421`, median `3`, **on average ranks**: `661` of `678` counts are tied, so a double `argsort` would order ties by array position. **Rank correlations rather than a fit** |
| PASS | B91-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B85's file names this station against both registrations |

**B91-3 caught a real fault in this station before it caught anything about the theorem.** The
first version took the Perron routine's vector as prices, and that is the right eigenvector. The
forward clause then failed on one irreducible draw in about five hundred, which is exactly what a
violation of Theorem 14(1) would look like and is not one. **A fixture of 220 draws cannot hold a
one-in-five-hundred fault**, so the check was moved onto the residual of the vector each draw
actually used and stored in the draw, which catches the swap on the first one. A criterion that
builds its own vector cannot catch a draw that built a different one.

**B91-4 carries no threshold and the first version did.** It asserted that one iteration decides
less than a fifth, a line drawn against numbers the swapped vector had produced; the corrected
figure is a quarter. **Moving that line to fit the corrected numbers would have been worse than
removing it**, and rule 11 forbids the shape either way. What is asserted now is that the cell is
exhausted and that the curve has somewhere to go.

**Eight mutations, all eight caught**, two only after the criteria were strengthened. One
candidate was dropped as an equivalent implementation rather than a fault: the bracket is
invariant under rescaling the iterate, so not renormalising changes no verdict short of underflow.

**Registered, not scheduled.** How thin a bundle has to be before reducibility appears, which is
fixed here at a third of the goods; which goods carry the zero prices, counted here but not named;
and how the iteration count depends on the number of industries, not separated here.

## B92: capital reversing, and why two techniques cannot produce it without reswitching

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b92_capital_reversing.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b92_capital_reversing.py`, record `results/b92_capital_reversing.json`, which carries
the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B74's technique generator, Samuelson's
1966 pair and its root finder are imported rather than rewritten.**

Capital reversing is the half of the Cambridge controversy that says a lower rate of profit can go
with a less capital-intensive technique, so the rate does not measure a scarcity of capital. **B67's
Corollary 12.3 already contains it in general form**: the value advanced is read off the field and
the field moves with the rate, so no quantity read off prices orders techniques independently of
the rate. This station names it, measures it, and finds where the two-technique case stops short of
the general one.

A technique is a dated-labour profile, B74's object: `c(x) = Σ_t l_t x^t` with `x = 1 + r`, wage
`w = 1/c(x)`, net output per worker `1/L` with `L = Σ_t l_t`, and capital per worker
`k = (1/L − w)/r`. **At a crossing the wage is shared**, so `k_A > k_B` exactly when `L_A < L_B`.

**Theorem 36.** (1) **`k` is two-valued at every switch between techniques of different total
labour**: both techniques are in use at one wage and one rate and their capital per worker differs, **so `k` is not a coordinate on the field** and
asking it for a direction is a category error rather than an anomaly. (2) **With two techniques,
reversing requires reswitching, and it is arithmetic**: `c_i(1) = L_i`, so a single crossing above
`x = 1` leaves the technique cheaper below it cheaper all the way down, hence carrying the smaller
`L`, which is the opposite of what reversing needs. (3) **With three or more it does not**, since
the pair meeting on the envelope need not include the technique that owns `x = 1`. (4) Reswitching
brings reversing with it, at one of the two switches and not at both.

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `seed 92`, 1,145 two-technique draws that cross and 1,878
families of three to five whose envelope switches.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B92-1 `known_answer` **Samuelson's 1966 pair** | the crossings come back at `r = 0.5` and `r = 1.0` against the published pair, the wage is equal at each to `0.00e+00`, and **capital reverses at the second and not the first**; `L_A = 7` against `L_B = 8` is what decides it |
| PASS | B92-2 `own_reading` **two techniques** | `0` of the `1102` single-crossing draws reverse and `43` of `43` that cross twice or more do, counted on the same draws |
| PASS | B92-3 `own_reading` why that half is arithmetic | on `1102 / 1102` single-crossing draws the technique taken at the higher rate carries the larger `L`, without exception, which is `c_i(1) = L_i` read back |
| PASS | B92-4 `own_reading` **three techniques break it** | `12` of `1878` families reverse with no owner returning anywhere, at sizes 3, 4 and 5, against `52` that do reswitch; on all `12` neither side of the reversing switch is the technique that owns a zero rate, which is exactly the condition the two-technique argument needs |
| PASS | B92-5 `own_reading` **`k` is two-valued, and what makes it two** | the two capital values differ on all `3399` switches drawn, median `0.562` of the smaller, tenth percentile `0.222`, smallest `9.8e-04`. **Every drawn switch has different total labour on its two sides, `3399 / 3399`**, so the other case is constructed: `C_A = 3 + x + 2x²` and `C_B = 1 + 4x + x²` change places at `x = 2` with `L = 6` on both sides and one value of `k`, `7/78` |
| PASS | B92-6 `instrument` crossings, tangencies and direction | switches bisected to `4.4e-16` against a grid step of `7.5e-04`; a technique against itself yields `0` crossings, where counting roots rather than changes would report one everywhere; and **the envelope is checked to run the right way up**, the owner at the lowest rate being the technique with the least total labour, `0` exceptions |
| PASS | B92-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B67 and B74 each name this station |

**B92-6's direction check exists because a mutation needed it.** Reading the envelope owner as the
dearest rather than the cheapest technique still produces switches and still produces reversing
counts, and nothing else in the station noticed. **An instrument that reads the envelope upside
down still hands back readings of the right shape.** The check that kills it is free and
structural: `c_i(1) = L_i`, so the owner at the lowest rate is the technique with the least labour.

**Eight mutations, all eight caught**, one only after that check was added.

**Registered, not scheduled.** How often reversing without reswitching occurs by family size,
reported here only as existence; whether the same argument survives in a system with produced
means of production, where the reduction to dated labour keeps `c(1) = L` but that has not been
checked; and how the size of the two-valued gap depends on where the switch sits.
