## B93: what a continuum changes, on both indices, and one registered question reformulated

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b93_continuum_second_pass.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b93_continuum_second_pass.py`, record `results/b93_continuum_second_pass.json`, which
carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B77's coefficient family is
imported rather than rewritten.**

B77 registered whether a quadratic continuum carries a slope reversal surviving refinement, none
having been found; B86 registered whether the componentwise minimum survives a continuum of methods
per good, **which is B77's continuum with the other index continuous**. They are one object read
along two indices and are done together.

**The first registration is not well posed as measured.** Every member of B77's family has a
strictly positive leading coefficient, so every owner curve is convex and the envelope's slope
rises inside any ownership run by construction; refining the parameter grid shortens runs against a
fixed `x` grid and nothing else. **The well-posed object is capital per worker along the envelope**,
which is what a slope reversal means economically and what B92 measures on discrete families.

**Three corrections, all on 2026-09-13**, and `docs/b93_continuum_second_pass.md` §6 gives them.
The reversing count put a rise in `k` at a change of owner and a rise under one owner into one
number; then the split count still compared `k` at two adjacent grid rates, where the wage is
shared only at the rate the two members cost the same, **and the sign can turn on that**; and
clause (4) cited B77's bounded active set for an object B77 does not bound.

**Theorem 37.** (1) **Reversing on a continuum is common relative to discrete families, and two
events have to be counted apart**: a rise in `k` at a change of owner is capital reversing, **read
at the rate where the switch happens**, where both members carry one cost and therefore one wage;
a rise inside one owner's own run is a price Wicksell effect. Counted apart, `4.9%` at degree two
to `10.5%` at degree five, rising with the degree, against `12 / 1878` on B92's discrete triples.
(2) **It survives refinement and both outcomes occur**: following a cohort through a 64-fold
refinement, `24` of `100` stay and the rest collapse, and an existence claim needs a witness that
survives. (3) **The reason is B92's own**: reversing **with no owner returning anywhere** needs three techniques because the pair
meeting on the envelope must not include the one owning a zero rate, and a continuum is always in
that regime. (4) **B92's two-valued `k` does not carry over in general, and where it does is
measurable**: filling the family in shrinks the jump where the owner set fills in with it and
leaves it exactly where it does not, so **the two-valuedness tracks the owners actually used and
not the members on offer**. That owner set runs to `637` at `1280` members and is not bounded, so
it is not B77's active set, which is a bound on what runs together at one rate. (5) On the other
index the componentwise minimum survives exactly when the per-good minimum is attained. (6) **When
it fails, it fails by the infimum escaping**, a minimiser with no limit in the set, rather than by
two goods wanting different techniques. (7) **A technique still leaves the envelope and comes
back**: `79` of `16000` families carry a return crossing at least `2%` of the family and leading by
more than `1e-5`, the widest crossing the whole family and holding through a 64-fold refinement.
**What a continuum dissolves is the wobble between neighbouring members, which leads by `1e-8`.**

All criteria pass at `seed 93`, 4,000 families at each of four degrees.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B93-1 `known_answer` **why the registered form is automatic** | B77's leading coefficient is strictly positive on `20 / 20` drawn families, the rise is positive on every reading, and a 256-fold parameter refinement moves it by at most `1e-13` because the `x` grid is fixed |
| PASS | B93-2 `own_reading` **reversing, counted apart from the price Wicksell effect** | at a change of owner, read at the switching rate, `195 / 4000` (`4.9%`), `312` (`7.8%`), `408` (`10.2%`), `422` (`10.5%`) by degree; inside one owner's own run `858`, `585`, `415`, `340`; with one owner over the whole sweep `551`, `390`, `293`, `234`; rising anywhere `987`, `776`, `643`, `584` |
| PASS | B93-3 `own_reading` **and it survives refinement** | `8` of `100` cohort families survive a 64-fold refinement, 1, 2, 2 and 3 by degree, `13` are families the refinement **created** rather than preserved, and the rest collapse. **A family counts as surviving when its coarse rise is positive and its fine rise is still positive and still more than half of it**; the coarse-rise condition is a presupposition of the registered wording that the first code did not carry, and without it the cohort's own selection condition was being restated rather than tested, which counted `24`. **The cohort is selected on a rise at a change of owner read at the switching rate**, the harder population, and **taken in draw order rather than by the largest rise**, since selecting the maximiser selects on the statistic |
| PASS | B93-4 `own_reading` **what the two-valued `k` tracks** | filling from 5 members to 1280 shrinks the jump, read at each switching rate, by a median factor of `0.010` on the `16` families whose owner set more than doubles, and by `0.994` on the `4` whose owner set stays put. That set reaches `637` at `1280` members, **so it is not B77's bounded active set** |
| PASS | B93-5 `own_reading` **the other index** | on a closed method set the minimiser settles to `s = 0.3968` and the cost converges; on a half-open one it sits at the end point at every refinement, marching `5.0e-04 → 5.0e-06` while the cost keeps falling |
| PASS | B93-6 `instrument` attainment, and two guards | `8000` drawn techniques beat the per-good choice in `0` components; every coefficient stays at or above `0.02`; and **the envelope is checked to run the right way up**, the owner at `x → 1` being the least-labour member, `0` exceptions |
| PASS | B93-8 `own_reading` **technique return survives dense labels** | `79` of `16000` families carry a return crossing at least `2%` of the family and leading by more than `1e-5`, against `1234` at any width. The widest crosses `299 / 300` at `1.0e-4` and holds to `6399 / 6400` at `6.0e-5` through a 64-fold refinement |
| PASS | B93-9 `instrument` **which brackets held more than one switch** | `32,724` of `560,283` grid brackets hold more than one change of owner (`5.84%`), rising with the degree from `3.21%` to `7.58%`, and each is dropped from every reading that needs a switch rate. A bracket is two adjacent grid rates whose owners differ; the grid is `1,500` points over `[1.02, 4.0]`, so one is about `0.0020` wide and a continuum of `300` members owning short runs inside it is ordinary. **The published form bisected every bracket as if it held one change**, which returns a rate at which neither member is chosen; excluding them sharpened B93-4's growing group by an order of magnitude and changed which families B93-3's cohort contains |
| PASS | B93-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B77, B86 and B92 each name this station |

**Two criteria were written stronger than the data supports and were rewritten to it.** B93-3 first
demanded the refinement move the reading by less than a twentieth, which is false since some
families collapse; B93-4 first demanded the jump shrink on every family, which is false since it
shrinks where the owner set fills in. **Both rewrites made the readings more specific.** The cohort
rule changed for the same reason: refining the largest riser selects on the statistic.

**Three more corrections, 2026-09-14, after an outside reading.** The first is the survival rule
above: it read "still positive and still more than half its coarse value" and tested only the second
half, and since the cohort is selected at one resolution while the ladder starts below it, a family
could enter with a coarse rise at or under zero, for which half of it lies under any positive number
and the test restates the selection condition. The second is in the switch finder: a grid bracket
can hold more than one change of owner, and bisecting the pair then returns a rate at which neither
is chosen, so the capital jump read there is read between two techniques that are not adjacent. That
is B93-9, and it is `5.84%` of all brackets. The third is a sentence: reversing was said to need
three techniques, and what needs three is reversing **with no owner returning anywhere**, since B92's
own record has `43` of `43` two-technique draws that cross twice or more reversing. **The frequency
comparison rested on that distinction and has now been settled by splitting this station's own
count the same way**: reversing with no owner returning anywhere reads `14`, `27`, `26` and `35` of
`4,000` by degree, `0.35%` to `0.88%`, against `12 / 1878` or `0.64%` on B92's discrete triples.
**The two straddle each other, so the claim that a continuum reverses more often is withdrawn and
not restored.** Every reversal, which is the wider object, still reads `4.9%` to `10.5%` and still
rises with the degree. The existence claim is untouched by all three.

**A fourth thing the same round found, and it is about testing rather than about technique choice.**
Fixing the bracket defect sharpened B93-4's growing group by an order of magnitude, and the mutation
that guards B93-4 had its target written in as a constant chosen against the old value. The sharper
reading walked out from under it and the mutation silently stopped being one. It now takes its target
from the group it is bending toward, so it tests that the two groups are indistinguishable rather
than that one of them reaches a particular number.

**The envelope-direction guard exists because a mutation needed it, exactly as in B92.** Reading the
owner as the dearest member still produces reversing counts and nothing else notices. **Every
mutation seeded was caught**, one only after that guard was added, and two are new with the split.

**Registered, not scheduled.** Whether the collapsing cohort families differ structurally from the
survivors, counted here but not separated; a discriminant for when the set of owners across a sweep
stays small, which is a different question from B77's bound on what runs at one rate; what the
non-attainment case looks like on a produced system rather than a constructed cost family; and
whether a wide technique return can be produced to order rather than found by search.

## B94: both factors on a rectangular economy are eigenvalues, of a block that has to be found

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b94_rectangular_closed_form.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b94_rectangular_closed_form.py`, record `results/b94_rectangular_closed_form.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B75's game solver and
factors and B82's rectangular generator are imported rather than rewritten.**

B82 left a registration: whether either family has a closed form on a rectangular economy, since
the Perron route needs principal blocks of one matrix and there are none here.

**Theorem 38.** (1) **Both factors are generalised eigenvalues**: at the optimum the programme is
tight on a square sub-pair of processes and goods, so the factor is a root of
`det(B_{S,G} − γ A_{S,G}) = 0`, with `alpha` the largest admissible such root over square sub-pairs
and `beta` the smallest. (2) **The two factors are the two ends of one finite set**, which is the
sharpest form B82's two-family statement takes here. (3) **The feasibility screen is what makes
this a closed form and not a formula**: a sub-pair's eigenvalue need not be attainable by any
non-negative intensity vector on the whole economy. (4) **The block is usually one cell**, so the
expansion factor is most often one process's own output-to-input ratio, chosen by a search rather
than computed by one. (5) **This is the chain's own shape read once more**: B87 has demand choosing
which lands, B89 which cell of a counting identity, B93 which member owns the envelope, and here
which block carries the factor. **The continuous part is an eigenvalue and the work is
combinatorial.**

**Seven criteria, all passing** at `seed 94`, 60 drawn rectangular economies.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B94-1 `known_answer` B75's published pair | all four values, `alpha` and `beta` on both examples, come back to six places through the closed form rather than the bisection |
| PASS | B94-2 `own_reading` **alpha is an eigenvalue** | agrees with the bisection on `60 / 60`, worst gap `1.2e-07` |
| PASS | B94-3 `own_reading` **and beta is the other end** | agrees on `60 / 60`, worst gap `5.2e-08` |
| PASS | B94-4 `own_reading` **the screen is load-bearing** | dropping it overshoots on `54 / 60` economies by a median factor of `3.565`. **And it does a second job**: complex generalised eigenvalues turn up on `38 / 60`, and keeping their real parts moves the answer on `0`, so the imaginary-part filter is redundant and the screen was rejecting them all along |
| PASS | B94-5 `own_reading` **which block** | `1x1` on `28`, `2x2` on `15`, `3x3` on `10`, `4x4` on `5`, `5x5` on `2`; more than one size occurs, so the block is found and not fixed by the shape |
| PASS | B94-6 `instrument` the search is complete | the visit count equals `Σ_k C(n,k)C(m,k)` on `60 / 60`, median `83` and largest `923` |
| PASS | B94-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B82 names this station |

**Eight mutations, seven caught and one measured as redundant.** Removing the imaginary-part filter
changes no answer, so rather than adding a probe for a fault that is not there, the station measures
it and reports what the screen was doing.

**Registered, not scheduled.** Whether the block can be found without enumerating, since the search
is exponential in the size of the economy and that is why the draws stop at six; and whether the
one-cell case has a characterisation, which would turn the common case into a formula.

## B95: several machines are joined by direction, not by sharing, and the life never falls

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b95_joint_lives.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b95_joint_lives.py`, record `results/b95_joint_lives.json`, which carries the
configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B78's machine system, price solver and
economic life are imported rather than rewritten.**

**Clause (3) was published on 2026-09-13 in a form that is now superseded**, and
`docs/b95_joint_lives.md` §5 gives the whole of it. The solver read the rows of its own system as
commodities when they are processes; the corrected solve returns the opposite answer on the same
202 systems, and a different criterion separates the cells. **Clauses (1) and (2) go through B78's
own solver and are unchanged to the digit.**

B78 left two registrations: the joint determination of lives when several machines are in use at
once, and a configuration in which the economic life falls as the rate rises, none having been
found in its 120 profiles.

**Theorem 39.** (1) **The falling life is not there**, over 5,991 drawn efficiency profiles read
across 91 rates. (2) **And the direction is the other way**: it rises on a fifth and is flat on the
rest, and the mechanism is in the construction, since building a machine costs `c` up front while
running an old one costs `a` each period, so a higher rate makes building dearer relative to
running. (3) **The second chain's life enters the wage exactly when the second chain's good enters
the first chain's processes**, and what the second chain is built out of makes no difference at
all. (4) **So the criterion is reachability**: the numeraire is the first chain's good, and with
nothing running back into it that chain is a closed block whose wage solves out on its own, which
makes the second chain a non-basic in Sraffa's sense. (5) **The obvious measurement reports a
coupling that is not there**: where the wage is flat in a life, the maximiser over it is whichever
the enumeration reaches first. (6) **And a solve has to be put back into the rows it came from.**

All criteria pass at `seed 95`, 5,991 single-chain profiles and 250 two-chain systems per linkage.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B95-1 `known_answer` B78's own life | its first profile gives `[6, 7, 8, 8]` at its own spot rates `[0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.9]`, through its own solver |
| PASS | B95-2 `own_reading` **the falling life is not there** | falls on `0` of `5991`, rises on `1285`, flat on `4706`; B78 drew 120 and this is fifty times that. **Both other directions occur**, so the search can tell them apart |
| PASS | B95-3 `own_reading` **the direction is the other way** | rises on `1285 / 5991` (`21.4%`), the mechanism named in the construction rather than asserted |
| PASS | B95-4 `own_reading` **the coupling follows direction, not sharing** | four linkages. Chain one takes chain two's good: `183 / 183` and `163 / 163` move with the second life, median spreads `0.450` and `0.555`. It does not: `0 / 209` and `0 / 202`, the latter at `2.0e-16`. **The wage moves with the first life on every system in all four**, so the zeros are readings |
| PASS | B95-5 `own_reading` **why the obvious measurement is wrong** | on all `411` uncoupled systems the wage is flat in the second life, and **more than one second life is viable on `276`**, so there is a tie for the maximiser to break; it moved on `24`. **Whether a tie breaks differently is luck; that the objective is flat is not** |
| PASS | B95-6 `instrument` the life is enumerated | every truncation from 1 to 8 tried, `8 / 8` viable at `r = 0.2`, and the life returned carries the largest wage |
| PASS | B95-8 `instrument` **the solve is checked against its own rows** | `B p - (1 + r) A p - w l` over `747` solves is at worst `2.7e-14`; the first orientation leaves up to `1.7e+02` and is above tolerance on `746 / 746`. **Both invert and both return a positive wage** |
| PASS | B95-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B78 names this station against both registrations |

**Every mutation seeded was caught.** Two are load-bearing: reading the coupling off the maximiser
rather than off the spread passes on the real data and reports the opposite conclusion, and a
fixture whose four cells couple the other way round, which is what this station published first,
is rejected by `B95-4` itself.

**Registered, not scheduled.** Three or more chains, and reachability relations that form a cycle;
a proof that the life is monotone in the rate on this construction, which is only searched here;
and how the size of the back-link moves the spread, held at `0.5` throughout.

## B96: basics are where the vertically integrated subsystems intersect

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Statement and proof in `docs/b96_basics_and_subsystems.md`. Checks in
`experiments/b96_basics_and_subsystems.py`, record `results/b96_basics_and_subsystems.json`, which
carries the configuration it ran under. Paper station: zero data. B69's system generator, Perron
solver and labour values are imported rather than rewritten.**

Two named objects the chain had not touched. **Sraffa's basics**: a commodity is basic when it
enters, directly or indirectly, into the production of every commodity, with the maximum rate fixed
by the basic part alone and a tax on a non-basic leaving the rest of the system where it was.
**Pasinetti's vertically integrated subsystems**: the sub-economy delivering one net unit of a good
with its whole chain of inputs.

**`B96-2` was published without its condition on 2026-09-13 and carries it the same day**, no
measurement having moved; `docs/b96_basics_and_subsystems.md` §1 has it.

**Theorem 40.** (1) **The maximum rate of profit is the basic part's alone, while the non-basic
block's spectral radius stays under the core's**, which on the graph is block triangularity: the
whole system's radius is the larger of the two blocks', so Sraffa's result and an eigenvalue fact
are the same statement **and the condition comes with it**. (1a) **And the condition is not
decoration**: sweeping one non-basic's own use across the core's radius, the rates agree on every
cell below and part on every cell above. `A = [[0.2, 0.1], [0, 0.8]]` is the smallest instance,
`R = 4` from the basic part against `R = 0.25` for the whole. (2) **A tax on a non-basic leaves the maximum rate and every basic price exactly where
they were**, and the same tax on a basic moves both, **while the taxed non-basic block's radius
stays under the core's**. (2a) **That condition is tighter than (1)'s and by a known factor**:
what has to stay under the core's radius is the block's radius after the tax, so the boundary sits
at the core's radius over the tax. Swept, a tax on a non-basic leaves the rate on every cell below
that place and sets the rate on every cell above it, and the crossover sits within one grid step of
it. **A good no one else uses can be made the one that caps the system by taxing it**, which is
Sraffa's Appendix B case reached by taxation rather than by technique. (3) **The basics are exactly where the
vertically integrated subsystems intersect**: a subsystem is what one net unit calls up and a good
is basic when every good calls it up, **so the two definitions are one reachability relation read
along its two arguments**. (4) A subsystem's labour content is B68's labour value, **and what the
subsystem adds is the set rather than the number**, which is what makes the intersection available.

All criteria pass at `seed 96`, 200 economies with an irreducible core and one or two appended
non-basics, and 40 further cores swept across the spectral boundary.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | B96-1 `known_answer` two anchors | on `15 / 15` systems from B69's generator every good is basic, which is what irreducibility means; and a subsystem's labour content agrees with B69's own labour values to `8.9e-16` |
| PASS | B96-2 `own_reading` **the rate is the core's, under the condition** | equals its basic part's on `200 / 200`, worst gap `0.00e+00`. **The condition holds on `200 / 200` by construction**, core radius at least `0.300` against a non-basic block at most `0.099`, **so this generator cannot violate it and the count is worth nothing by itself** |
| PASS | B96-3 `own_reading` **the tax asymmetry, both halves, under the condition** | a tax on a non-basic leaves the rate on `200 / 200` and every basic price on `200 / 200`; **the same tax on a basic moves the rate on `200` and the basic prices on `200`**, the latter by a median of `0.102`. **Both counted on the same systems**, and the null half alone would be a check that cannot fail. **The null half is conditional too, and on a tighter condition than B96-2's**: the block's radius after the tax has to stay under the core's, which holds on `200 / 200` by construction, core radius at least `0.300` against a taxed block at most `0.150`, **so that count is worth nothing by itself either and B96-9 sweeps across it** |
| PASS | B96-4 `own_reading` **the intersection** | it equals the basics on `200 / 200`; subsystem sizes run from `3` to `9` goods, so they are not all the whole economy and the intersection is not trivially everything |
| PASS | B96-5 `own_reading` the construction is not vacuous | every system carries a non-basic and a basic set strictly smaller than its good set, `200 / 200`, one non-basic on `107` and two on `93` |
| PASS | B96-6 `instrument` the closure is a closure | a fixed point on `200 / 200`, checked by running one more step; **and it is the indirect relation**, since on a chain of six goods where each enters only the next the first is reported as entering the last |
| PASS | B96-8 `own_reading` **the spectral condition, on both sides** | one non-basic's own use swept `0.02` to `0.95` over `40` cores, `1600` cells: below the core's radius the rates agree on `853 / 853`, above it they part on `747 / 747`, and the crossover sits within one grid step (`0.024`) of the radius on every sweep, worst `0.018` |
| PASS | B96-9 `own_reading` **the taxed boundary, on both sides** | the same sweep read for the tax, `1600` cells: where the taxed block's radius stays under the core's a tax on the non-basic leaves the rate on `564 / 564`, where the tax carries it over the taxed non-basic sets the rate on `1036 / 1036`, and the last harmless own use sits within one grid step (`0.024`) of the core's radius over the tax, worst `0.017`. **The boundary is at `0.6667` of B96-8's, which is the tax, and that factor was written down before the sweep was read** |
| PASS | B96-7 `bookkeeping` write-back | B80 and B68 each name this station |

**Every mutation seeded was caught.** The ones worth naming: reading the reachability relation
along its other argument turns basics into their opposite and is caught by the chain probe;
keeping only the null half of the tax asymmetry leaves a check that cannot fail; and a sweep that
never crosses the boundary, or one where a cell above it still agrees, is rejected by B96-8.
**B96-9 is seeded the same three ways against its own, lower boundary**, and the fixture is
additionally required to contain a cell between the two boundaries, so that the two arms are
separated on it rather than reading the same cells twice.

**Registered, not scheduled.** Non-basics that enter one another, where the appended block is
itself reducible and its own radius is no longer just the largest own use; whether the intersection
statement survives joint production, where B70 already showed the cycles and the commodities part
company; and how far past the boundary a tax has to push a non-basic before the rate moves
measurably, read here only as a sign.

## A36: two positions collected at once, each with its own shape

**RUN: 2026-09-13. Script `experiments/a36_two_shapes.py`, record `results/a36_two_shapes.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 594 cells over 18 carriers, nothing fetched. A31's
carrier, cell driver and shock table are imported rather than rewritten, so the two stations run
the same economy.**

A31's second round left this registered: a collection that uses a different shape in each of two
positions at once. `WithdrawSpec.mix` takes `((position, base, share), ...)` and was written for
exactly this.

**A31's third round already ran it, and this is the fourth pass rather than the first.** That round
carried nine rules of which six were mixes, four of them a different shape on each of two positions
and one a pair that overlaps, over five seeds: 75 paired comparisons, none differing. **What it left
shut was the shock table**, because shocks multiply its grid by eleven, and it ran one subsistence
floor. This station opens both, widens to 33 rules, and carries two things the third round did not:
the range of what the rules collect, and the mechanism behind the cells where a mix coincides with
one of its own single runs.

**What holds still is meant to be the aggregate.** The issuance rule pins the Layer 2 inflow, so
the amount collected is the channel a comparison of shapes has to hold constant, and the reading is
the count of nodes left below the subsistence floor, which is A31's own.

|---|---|---|

| PASS | A36-2 `own_reading` **the count does not move** | on `18` carriers each run through `33` collection rules, the spread within a carrier is zero on `18 / 18`. The rules are two positions at three shapes each, and the nine shape pairs across those two positions at three shares |

| PASS | A36-4 `own_reading` **the mixed rule is live** | a mixed cell collects an amount different from both of its own single-position runs on `441 / 486`. **The `45` that coincide are one class and not a scatter**: the `leak` stress at share `0.25`, where the financial layer holds so little that its quarter of the take is capped at what is there and the rest falls on production. **The cap closing the gap on a thin side is the field working** |
| PASS | A36-5 `own_reading` **four rounds, one answer** | A31's first round moved which position the claims come out of; its second moved the shape inside one position; its third put a different shape on each of two positions; **this one adds the shock table and a second subsistence floor, at three ratios, and reads the same count again** |
| PASS | A36-6 `instrument` conservation, and the same economy | the books close on `594 / 594`, and this station's single-position cell is A31's own to within `1e-09`, run through A31's driver |

**Four passes over three independent ways of moving where the same pinned aggregate comes from, and

between a twentieth and the whole of one another, from accounts chosen differently, and the floor

**Three things in this section were corrected on 2026-09-13 and no reading moved.** The claim that

## A37: what withdrawing from the graph is worth, and the one switch that sets its sign

**RUN: 2026-09-14. Script `experiments/a37_lying_flat.py`, record `results/a37_lying_flat.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 270 cells: two carriers, three triggers, nine depths,
five seeds. Nothing fetched. A17's carrier and cell driver are imported rather than rewritten, so
the two stations run the same economy. The record is marked diagnostic: the station is open.**

A node here withdraws by cutting a share of its own out-edges once its own inflow falls below a
trigger. `EdgeCutSpec(mode="self_cut")` is A17's switch and it is unchanged; what A37 adds to the
module is `cut_out`, a per-round per-node count of the out-edges cut, so the group that withdrew is
read off the module's own vector rather than recomputed in the experiment from the trigger. The
new field is `None` when the switch is off and 44 fields come back bitwise across 12 configurations
with it off, which is the check the gate makes.

**Two carriers, one switch apart: with a subsistence floor and without one.** A node that falls
below the floor leaves circulation. That is the whole difference between the two arms, and it is
what sets the sign of the central reading.

**Depth is what this grid varies, and breadth is endogenous.** `share` is how much of its own
out-edges a triggered node cuts, not how many nodes cut. The count that withdraws runs to the full
population of 200 by depth `0.30`, while flow is still `0.84` to `1.06` of its twin, so the number
withdrawing and the graph going down are two events two grid steps apart. The consequence is a
scope limit rather than a finding: past depth `0.10` the median count of nodes that did **not**
withdraw is zero, so the two-group comparison has an object at exactly one depth on this grid. A
switch that makes breadth exogenous is registered and not built.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | A37-0 `instrument` **the group comes from the module** | 12 configurations, 44 fields bitwise with the switch off; the new vector is absent when the switch is off and present when it is on. A seeded stale vector and a seeded missing one are both reported, which is what the first version of this gate did not do |
| PASS | A37-1 `own_reading` **both groups printed per cell** | `270/270` cells carry a group figure. No cross-cell mean is taken |
| PASS | A37-2 `own_reading` **the sign of the gap against depth** | six curves: one turns (at depth `0.30`), two hold one sign throughout, three have no object. Read on each arm's share of its own stock, because the treated arm issues claims its twin does not and a ratio of levels would have two different denominators |
| PASS | A37-3 `own_reading` **flow and split printed together** | `180/270` cells are below a twentieth of their twin's flow, so their level readings do not carry, which is A17-8's registered flag |
| VOID | A37-4 `premise` **the per-head burden curve** | **The premise does not hold on this carrier and the criterion is not evaluated.** It registered a fixed total of bad debt shared per head among those who did not withdraw, and this configuration runs with the hub liability, the sovereign and the write-off all off: there is no debt here for anyone to carry. The numbers stay in the record and the verdict comes off. **This station scores nothing against any rival** |
| PASS | A37-6 `own_reading` **the receiving set contracts while the stock rises** | on the `90` cells that still have trade in them, `90 / 90` contract, the widest of them at `0.8397` of its twin, and it falls with depth: `0.798`, `0.610`, `0.266`, `0.197`, `0.058`. The stock is larger on `89 / 90`, by up to `88` times. On the other `180` cells there is no trading economy left at all, so the receiving set is empty while the stock is a median `5.6` times its twin. **This is the volume-one claim that a total can rise while the set that actually receives contracts** |
| PASS | A37-7 `instrument` **every cell whose trade has ended sits on one of two degenerate branches** | `1 / HHI` of inflow returns `0` when inflow is zero, and returns exactly `k` when one payment is split equally among `k` accounts. `180` cells have no trade left: `172` read `0`, and `8` read exactly `75`, which is the size of the wage roster and not a receiving set. No cell with trade left reads either. The registered flow flag agrees with this accounting fact on `270 / 270` cells |

**The central reading, at the one depth where both groups exist.** At depth `0.10` the withdrawing
group is `88` to `98` nodes and the staying group is `102` to `112`, fifteen cells per carrier.
Each group is compared against itself in that cell's own twin, in shares of each arm's own stock.

| carrier | readable cells | withdrawers ÷ stayers, median | range | cells where withdrawers are ahead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **no floor** | `10 / 15` | **`0.237`** | `0.053` – `1.000` | **`0 / 10`** |
| **floor** | `15 / 15` | **`2.690`** | `0.545` – `10.115` | **`14 / 15`** |

**With no floor, withdrawing leaves a node a quarter of what the stayers hold, and it is ahead in
no cell: the two highest are `0.99996` and `1.00009`, a tie to four places. With the floor,
withdrawing leaves it two and a half times what the stayers hold, and it is ahead in fourteen of
fifteen.** The five unreadable cells are ones where the staying group's median share in the twin is
zero, so the division has no object.

The mechanism needs nothing new. Cutting a share of your own out-edges is spending less, the stock
stays on your books, and having stock on your books is the condition for not falling through the
floor. Where there is no floor, keeping the stock buys nothing and withdrawing is only a cost.
**The payoff to withdrawing is not a property of withdrawing. It comes from there being a floor
waiting for whoever stayed in.**

**The collapse boundary is one grid step wide.** On the no-floor carrier, flow first falls below a
tenth of its twin at depth `0.55` in `15 / 15` cells, zero spread, the same on all three triggers.
Across all thirty curves the step from `0.50` to `0.55` costs a median factor of `37.1`. Counting
by the accounting fact instead of the flow gives the same boundary: `80 / 150` cells still have
trade at depth `0.50` and `10 / 120` at `0.55` and beyond. A17 could only place this between `0.5`
and `0.7`. The floor carrier spreads out and its most sensitive trigger collapses earlier, which is
reported and not explained. The statistic reads two adjacent steps, so its index is a cell and no
interpolated point is quoted.

**Counted by kind: two `instrument` and four `own_reading` criteria hold, one `premise` criterion
is withdrawn, and there are no `rival` criteria. The number to report for the rival column is
zero.** Putting a debt into this carrier is the first item of the second round, and it is what
would give that withdrawn criterion an object for the first time.


## B97: Cyprus 2013, a price on an edge that was cut and put back

Cyprus cut two classes of edge on the same day in March 2013, the island's own bank-to-bank
edge and the cross-border one, and restored them eleven months apart: domestic transfers on
2014-05-05 and fully on 2014-06-01, everything external on 2015-04-06. The programme review
dates each of the eight relaxations, so the two classes are separated by the authorities
themselves rather than by a choice made here. That separation is what the station was opened
for: a price sitting on one class of edge should move when that class comes back and not when
the other does, and a country risk premium has no reason to pick one of the two dates.

The instrument is the wedge between a rate in Cyprus and the same rate in the euro area, one
unit of account at two positions. Five controls carry the same subtraction at the same dates,
each for a reason: Greece sat in the same periphery credit stress and never cut its domestic
edge, Slovenia had a bank crisis and a bail-in at the end of 2013 and cut no edge at all,
Malta is the other small island banking system in the same currency, Portugal and Ireland are
the other two programme countries. A step at a date is read against two floors, both of them
the same statistic as the reading: the same statistic at every non-event month in that area,
and the same statistic at the same date in every control.

**The date holds, and it is the carrier's alone.** At the cross-border restoration the step in
the wedge is larger than every control's on all six rate instruments. At the domestic dates the
same count is three of six, so the move is dated to the external lifting and not to the
domestic one.

| instrument | step at the external lifting | controls at least as big |
|---|---|---|
| overnight deposits, households | `-0.160` | `0 / 5` |
| overnight deposits, firms | `-0.060` | `0 / 5` |
| term deposits to one year, households | `-0.420` | `0 / 4` |
| term deposits to one year, firms | `-0.510` | `0 / 4` |
| loans to one year, households | `-0.583` | `0 / 5` |
| loans to one year, firms | `-0.460` | `0 / 5` |

Ireland publishes no term deposit rate over this window, so those two rows carry four controls.

**The move is common to every instrument, and that is what the station could not separate.**
The square takes the country-wide layer out: it is a difference of two wedges, so a level shift
shared by every instrument in Cyprus cancels. The count of squares where no control moved as
much is eight of fifteen at the external date and seven of fifteen at the domestic one, which
is the same number twice. The wedges date the event and the squares do not, and both together
say that every bank rate in Cyprus stepped down by one common layer without the instruments
reordering against each other.

The reason is in the instruments rather than in the prediction. Every rate here is a bank rate
and reaches the cross-border edge through a bank's cost of funds, so none of them sits on the
domestic edge alone, and the instrument registered as the placebo moved more than the treated
ones. Two further readings were run to get past this and neither did. Making the statistic the
shape of the treatment rather than the shape of a switch, by reading the wedge against how many
of the eight restrictions were still in force, leaves three of six instruments outside every
control and one of those three is the placebo. Moving to a price that is not a bank rate, the
consumer price wedge against the euro area, gives a level object that moves at the domestic
date and an inflation object that moves at both; an interest rate is a growth rate, so the
quantity with its dimensions is the inflation differential, and the quantity with the
dimensions of the rate wedge's level is a cumulative interest factor, and the two comparisons
disagree. Choosing between them after seeing which separates is the one risk this kind of work
actually carries, so both are reported. The level reading is in any case carried by a series
with a three log point seasonal cycle and a ten log point trend, and its best cell rests on a
margin of `0.13` percentage points over a control.

**What the station does return is a square that no scalar per position can produce, on two
carriers, one of which owes nothing to banking.** A country premium carried by each position
gives every instrument at that position the same wedge, so the difference of any two wedges is
exactly zero under it. The floor needs no estimate: every rate is published on a grid of `0.01`
and every annual inflation rate on a grid of `0.1`, each checked to be an integer number of its
own tick rather than counted from printed digits, since trailing zeros are dropped in both.

| square | months above the published floor | largest, in floors |
|---|---|---|
| bank rates, six areas, fifteen pairs each | `15,134 / 15,623` | `224.0` |
| services against non-energy industrial goods, inflation | `1,172 / 1,296` | `39.5` |

The consumer price square is read on inflation and not on the index level, because each index
carries its own base normalisation and that survives in a level square. A twelve-month log
difference cancels it.

The differential prediction, the one the eleven-month gap was opened for, is recorded in its
third state. It was neither separated nor contradicted: no instrument available here sits on
one class of edge only. Reading that as the prediction failing would send the next reader to
the theory when the thing to change is the instrument. Two instruments would settle it, and
neither is in these sources: the dispersion of one rate across Cypriot banks, which the
domestic edge pins and which the country aggregate cannot reach, and a seasonally adjusted
country price index, which this dataflow publishes for the euro area alone.

**Counted by kind: one `instrument`, one `known_answer`, two `rival` and one `own_reading`
criterion hold, and one `own_reading` criterion is in its third state and carries no verdict.
The number to report for the rival column is that both rival criteria pass, which is to say the
rival's point prediction of zero fails on both carriers.**


## B100: the three shares of a global surgical package, and whether they sum to one

`RUN: 2026-09-15.` `experiments/b100_global_package.py`, record
`results/b100_global_package.json`, design and reading in the station's two files.

CMS publishes, for every code that carries a global surgical package, the share of
the work that is preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative. Its own layout
document says the three **will usually equal one**, and that **any variance is
slight and results from rounding**. That sentence makes two claims and they are
scored apart, because a hedge is read at the strength its own wording carries.

**The band is not chosen.** Each of the three fields is published as `9v9(5)`, so
each is rounded to `1e-5` and the worst rounding error in their sum is `1.5e-5`.
The band is that number.

| | criterion | kind | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | B100-0 the three shares are found by name and read as shares | instrument | 19,226 rows read by column name; every share lies in [0, 1]. The 2026 release splits its column names over two rows, so the row naming HCPCS reads `DAYS OP OP OP` and three of the four wanted columns are not there under any name; the reader folds in the row above when it looks like a continuation rather than a title |
| PASS | B100-1 the band is the published one and the partition is whole | known_answer | 4,236 of 4,248 rows with a package sum to one inside `1.5e-5`, a share of `0.9972`. The count is printed and no threshold is drawn on it |
| PASS | B100-2 the rows the layout's word usually points at, named | own_reading | 12 rows fall outside, every one of them a `090` code whose three shares are `0.00000` and whose gap is therefore a full `1.000`. They are four codes times three modifiers, consecutive in the file: 77750, 77761, 77762, 77763, intracavitary brachytherapy, each as global, `26` and `TC`. **So the independent exceptions are four entries in one family, not twelve** |
| PASS | B100-3 a code with no global package carries no share | known_answer | 14,978 rows carry `000`, `XXX`, `MMM`, `YYY` or `ZZZ` and are held out; every one of them carries zero in all three fields, no exception. Left in, they would drag B100-1 from `0.9972` to `0.22` |

**The reading.** On this file the identity holds on `99.72%` of the entries that
have a package. **The twelve exceptions are not rounding**: their shares are not
slightly off, they are absent, and the gap is a whole unit rather than a fifth
decimal. So the publisher's first claim holds here and its account of why the
exceptions exist does not.

**No rival criterion.** The publisher's sentence is this file's own note about its
notation, not a competing point prediction about the world, and a criterion typed
against it could not land anywhere the four-cell rule allows. What the station
adds is a quantity no other account had a reason to compute.

**Scope.** January 2026 release only. Nothing here is claimed about other years.

## B98 arm F: the same tariff, the same formula, the same table, one batch apart

`RUN: 2026-09-15.` Record `results/b98_nem_vintage_PGE_NEM3-batch_2023v2026.json`,
built by `experiments/b98_nem_join.py --schedule NEM3-batch` and read by the same
station script as arm E.

Arm E puts a retail time-of-use price beside an avoided-cost price, and a reader
can say those are two different calculations, so of course their shapes differ.
Arm E cannot rule that out. **Arm F can**: both sides here are the same published
object one batch apart. Same schedule, same Avoided Cost Calculator, same 12 by 24
by 2 grid, same unit, same two components added the same way. The only difference
is the year the interconnection application was filed, and a customer cannot
change that after the fact.

It also has no coarse side. Arm E's NEM-2 column takes four or five values against
557, so pairs inside one block carry nothing and are reported apart. Here the two
columns take 539 and 557, so every pair carries the reading and the within-block
group is 41 pairs where the earlier batch happens to repeat a value.

| | criterion | kind | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | B98-F1 the two schedules meet on one position key, in one unit | instrument | 576 positions; column medians `0.05859` and `0.07514` $/kWh, highest single cell `2.52139`. The unit is read off each column's middle, not its extreme |
| PASS | B98-F2 whether the two classes differ by a constant | known_answer | the difference runs `-0.56081` to `+1.92634`, a spread of `2.48715` against a floor of `0.00002` read value by value, **124,357 times it** |
| PASS | B98-F3 the square, within a block and across blocks, apart | own_reading | crossing pairs **165,371 of 165,559 above the floor**, median `0.02137`, max `2.48715`. Within-block: 41 pairs, all above the floor |
| PASS | B98-F4 how many values each side takes, before any reading | instrument | the earlier batch takes 539 distinct values, the later 557 |

**The reading.** The class difference changes sign: on an August evening the
earlier batch is paid `1.82726` against the later batch's `1.15441`, and at three
in the morning in January it is `0.05817` against `0.08983`. **A function of class
alone cannot do that**, so the level-shift statement fails here on a carrier where
the two classes share everything except their batch. **A constant difference would have
killed the bare rival just as completely and left the level-shift one standing**;
what the sign change adds is that the class index cannot be absorbed into a
constant, or into a factor, or into any function of class alone.

**The four published sheets are two groups, and that gives the arm a zero
calibration for free.** All six pairs were run through the same pipeline:

| pair | difference | spread | crossing pairs above the floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 v 2024 | **constant** | **`0.00000`** | **`0 / 165,559`** |
| 2025 v 2026 | **constant** | **`0.00000`** | **`0 / 165,579`** |
| 2023 v 2025, 2023 v 2026, 2024 v 2025, 2024 v 2026 | not constant | `2.48715` | `165,371 / 165,559` |

**The same extractor, joiner, criteria and position key read exactly zero on two
pairs and a spread of `2.48715` on the other four**, so the non-zero is not
something the pipeline manufactures — which is the cheapest objection to this arm
and the one nothing else here would have answered. Arm E has no such pair: its two
sides come from different file formats, so there is no input that ought to read
zero. **The four cross-group pairs carry identical numbers**, because 2023 equals
2024 and 2025 equals 2026, so they are one comparison seen four times and this arm
has one independent reading rather than four.

**A structural fact fell out of the fetch and is registered rather than scored**:
the publisher posts four files for four batch years and they carry two curves.

**No rival criterion**, for the same reason as arm E: the framework permits the
shape to vary with class and does not require it, so it bets on no direction here.
As in arm E there are two rivals — the bare one that denies the class index, which
the two published sheets refute without arithmetic, and the level-shift one, whose
point prediction of a zero four-cycle is what the criteria below test.

**One criterion was changed after it fired.** F1 first failed the whole run on
three rows above `2.0` $/kWh, and those were real October evening prices rather
than a unit error: the line had been drawn where arm E's data happened to stop.
A table in dollars per megawatt hour puts its median in the tens, so the median is
what separates the units. The unit error is still caught — the seeded wrong-unit
table still drops F1 — and a run is no longer failed by three true spikes.

## B98 arm E: one kilowatt hour, one meter, one hour, two net metering vintages

`RUN: 2026-09-15.` `experiments/b98_nem_join.py` builds the table,
`experiments/b98_nem_vintage.py` reads it; records
`results/b98_nem_vintage_PGE_E-TOU-C_2026.json` and `..._PGE_EV2_2026.json`.

California closed its second net metering regime on 2023-04-14. A meter's vintage
is fixed by the date its interconnection application was filed, so two identical
roof arrays on the same street, exporting the same kilowatt hour in the same hour,
are paid on two different published schedules and neither owner can move to the
other.

**Two rivals are in play and they die in different ways.** The bare one says a
position carries one scalar, so two classes at one position get the same terms;
**two posted schedules refute it on sight**, before any arithmetic, which is why
the design refused to spend a run on it. The one the criteria are aimed at
concedes the class index and constrains its shape: `P(a, j) = φ(j) + ψ(a)`, the
class difference as a pure level shift. **That is not a hedge, it is a point
prediction**: under it the wedge between two positions is the same for every
class, so the four-cycle over two positions and two classes is exactly zero. It
is the same rival B97, B83 and B98's own zero calibration are scored against, and
it is what someone who accepts that different regimes have different baselines
would still believe. **A level difference alone would kill the bare rival and
leave this one standing**; what the criteria below test is whether it stands.

**Both retail schedules were run against both published curves**, because whether
either choice mattered was itself the question. Neither did: all four land in the
same cell.

| retail schedule | NEM-3 batch | difference runs | crossing pairs above the floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-TOU-C | earlier | `-1.92797` to `+0.55208` | `104,106 / 104,128` |
| E-TOU-C | later | `-0.59947` to `+0.57834` | `104,096 / 104,128` |
| EV2 | earlier | `-1.89737` to `+0.58268` | `94,526 / 94,528` |
| EV2 | later | `-0.56887` to `+0.60894` | `94,522 / 94,528` |

**Four runs are not four independent readings and this arm does not claim them as
such.** The four published batch sheets carry two curves, so that axis takes two
values rather than four; EV2's peak window is E-TOU-C's peak window with one extra
period carved out of the off-peak, so the two schedules are nested; and all four
read the same 576 positions. What the second schedule buys is robustness to the
choice, not a second carrier. **The second independent reading is arm F**, which
shares no retail schedule with any of these and carries its own zero calibration.

| | criterion | kind | E-TOU-C | EV2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | B98-E1 the two schedules meet on one position key, in one unit | instrument | 576 positions, both credits in (0, 2) $/kWh | same |
| PASS | B98-E2 whether the two vintages differ by a constant | known_answer | difference runs `-0.59947` to `+0.57834`, spread `1.17781` against a floor of `0.00002` read value by value, **58,890 times it** | `-0.56887` to `+0.60894`, same spread and same multiple |
| PASS | B98-E3 the square, within a block and across blocks, apart | own_reading | crossing pairs **104,096 of 104,128 above the floor**, median `0.04427`, max `1.07871` | **94,522 of 94,528**, median `0.16705`, max `1.06822` |
| PASS | B98-E4 how many values each side takes, before any reading | instrument | NEM-2 takes 4 values, NEM-3 takes 557 | NEM-2 takes 5, NEM-3 takes 557 |

**The reading.** The class difference is not a constant: it runs from about
`-0.6` to about `+0.58` $/kWh and changes sign, which no function of class alone
can do. The crossing-block squares sit above the two publishers' own resolution
on essentially every pair. **So the shape of price against position depends on
the class, and the rival's point prediction fails on both carriers.**

**Within-block pairs are printed and carry nothing.** Inside one TOU block the
NEM-2 credit is constant by construction, so the square there collapses to the
NEM-3 difference. The design said so before the run, the two groups are reported
apart, and they are never summed — summing them would make the arm one that
cannot fail.

**No rival criterion, and that is about this framework rather than about the
rival.** The level-shift account makes a point prediction here and it is refuted
below. What is missing is an opposing prediction on *this* side: the framework
says terms are indexed by position and class, it permits the shape to vary with
class and does not require it, so it bets on no direction on this cell. A
criterion typed `rival` needs both sides to predict, or its cells collapse onto
ones the four-cell rule forbids. So the rival's prediction is recorded in the
detail and the reading closes it, which is the same disposition arm F and B100
reached for their own reasons.

**Three places the join would have gone wrong quietly**, each settled by reading
the publisher rather than guessing: the NEM-3 price is the sum of two printed
components, which the publisher's own worked example adds; the NEM-2 export price
has no non-bypassable charge taken off it, because the tariff says those charges
"may not be reduced by any credits for exports"; and each price sheet prints two
years, of which only the one before "Interconnection Application Year" is the
vintage, so reading the other makes all four sheets look like one batch.

**Registered, not scored this round.** The four vintages' sheets are two groups:
2023 and 2024 agree cell for cell, 2025 and 2026 agree cell for cell, and the two
groups differ on all 576 cells by up to `1.92634` $/kWh, changing sign between
August evenings and January nights. Both sides of that comparison are on the same
576-cell grid, so it has no within-block group at all and the whole table carries
the reading. It gets its own station rather than a line here.

## B98: a zero whose answer the publisher already printed

The New York tariff writes the price at a bus as a reference price plus a losses component and
a congestion component, with the reference the same number everywhere in an interval. So taking
the two published components off the published price has to leave the same number at every
node. That residual is a constant field, a constant field's cycle sums are zero, and **the
answer comes from the publisher's own pricing rule rather than from an argument here about what
must cancel**. It is a calibration of the machinery on real data with real timestamps, real
gaps and real rounding.

**What it is not.** Every participant at a node faces one price, so there is no agent layer here
and no rival criterion: this station scores nothing against any other account. It buys
credibility for the instrument rather than reach, and those are not substitutes. It is also not
the first real-data calibration in this repository, which already has the antisymmetry check on
loan cures, the noise floor the benchmark transition supplies for free, the two publication
paths to one daily rate, and the statute recomputation. What it adds is that the true value is
fixed by an algebraic identity inside a published pricing rule, and that it runs on hundreds of
nodes rather than a handful.

**The sign the published columns carry was identified by the requirement, not looked up.** The
tariff adds both components; the published congestion column turns out to carry the opposite
sign. Four ways of combining the columns were tried and exactly one leaves the residual
constant, so nothing about the file format had to be trusted.

| residual | median spread | max | intervals within the grid |
|---|---|---|---|
| price less losses less congestion | `11.4800` | `121.28` | `49 / 720` |
| **price less losses plus congestion** | **`0.0100`** | **`0.0200`** | **`720 / 720`** |
| price plus losses less congestion | `19.0000` | `131.56` | `0 / 720` |
| price plus losses plus congestion | `9.4000` | `17.64` | `0 / 720` |

**The identity holds everywhere it was read.** Day-ahead zones `720 / 720` intervals over 15
nodes, day-ahead generators `720 / 720` over **508 nodes**, real time zones `8,696 / 8,696` over
five-minute intervals. The bound is the grid the values are published on: each is printed to the
cent and every one of the `1,520,999` values was checked to sit on that tick rather than counted
from its printed digits, since trailing zeros are dropped.

**The bound is a spread between two residuals and not one residual.** Each residual is a sum of
three published values and carries three half-ticks, so a max-minus-min across nodes carries
six, `0.03` and not `0.015`. Judged against the tighter one the same data reads `574 / 720`,
which would have looked like an instrument that almost works.

**Fed that field, the cycle machinery returns zero**, on a complete graph and on a ring with
chords so that long cycles are exercised and not only triangles: worst cycle sum `0.00e+00` for
the residual field and `2.27e-13` for the published price, over up to `406` independent cycles
and a longest cycle of `16` edges. A complete graph's spanning-tree basis is all triangles,
which is why the ring is there. **A field built from node values has vanishing cycle sums by
construction, so this arm reads the pipeline and not the world**: orientation, a repeated edge
counted rather than cancelled, arithmetic over hundreds of nodes. The out-and-back that
calibrates the loan stage has the same character and it caught real defects.

**The same month also carries a square that owes nothing to banking, and no further data was
needed for it.** The same megawatt hour at one node, bought a day ahead and bought in real time,
is two contracts at one position for one delivery hour. A scalar carried by each position gives
both of them the same wedge against any other position, so the difference of the two wedges is
zero under it. It is not: `74,144` of `75,600` node pairs stand above the floor the prices are
printed on, median `1.139`, largest `312.747`, which is fifteen thousand times that floor.

**And the non-zero is not only measured, it is attributed, because the publisher prints the two
channels separately.** The square equals its loss channel less its congestion channel on
`75,600` of `75,600` pairs, within the twelve half-ticks such a comparison carries; the median
residual is `0.003` and the largest `0.027`. The largest square of the month, between two zones
at eleven in the morning on the seventh, is congestion `-312.705` against losses `0.042`.

**The two channels do not behave alike, and that is a fact about the network rather than about
the theory.** Congestion stands above the floor on `69.6%` of pairs and losses on `96.8%`. Split
by whether a constraint is in play, the square's median runs `0.348` with none, `0.472` with a
light one and `2.926` with a binding one. **The first of those does not fall to the floor**: it
sits at seventeen times it, because moving power always costs power and the loss channel is
never switched off. A design that assumed an edge could be switched fully off and back would not
find that state on this network, which is the same shape the Cyprus carrier turned out to have
for a different reason.

**The transmission outage schedule was not needed and is not fetched.** It would buy one thing,
a treatment defined by the rule rather than by the price, and nothing here waits on it.

**Counted by kind: two `known_answer`, three `instrument`, one `own_reading` and one `rival`
criterion hold. The rival figure to report is that its point prediction of zero fails on the
one cell it is scored on.** The `m = 1` limit still binds where it was set: every participant at
a node faces one price, so nothing here reaches the question of what two classes at one position
are charged, and the square above is over two goods rather than two classes.

## A38: how wide a withdrawal spreads, made a knob, and what that costs the ones who withdrew

**RUN: 2026-09-14. Script `experiments/a38_breadth.py`, record `results/a38_breadth.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 150 cells: two carriers, three depths, five
widths, five seeds, plus ten twins. Nothing fetched. A37's carrier and cell driver are
imported rather than rewritten, so the two stations run the same economy. The record is
marked diagnostic: the station is open.**

A37 measured how deep a withdrawal goes and could not set how wide it spreads: the count
that withdrew ran to the whole population two grid steps before the graph went down, so past
the first depth no group was left that had not withdrawn. `EdgeCutSpec.cutter_share` is that
knob. `share` is a share of edges and this is a share of nodes.

**Willingness is drawn once, as a property of a node, not a coin flipped each round.** A
per-round draw lets the set of withdrawers accumulate to everyone whatever the share says,
which is the failure the knob exists to remove; the gate plants exactly that fault and sees
`192` to `194` nodes cutting at every setting. At the default nothing is drawn at all, so the
arm reproduces the module before the knob bit for bit, and A37's recorded cells come back with
every count exact and every float inside `1e-9` of its record, the worst at `8.08e-16`.

**Once width is set, the group that did not cut is two kinds of node.** Some would have
withdrawn and were never stressed; some would not withdraw at all. At full width the first
kind is four nodes of two hundred and the second is empty, which is why one station could
split on cutting alone. The question here is the ones who withdrew against the ones who would
not, and putting the never-stressed in with the unwilling answers a different one.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | A38-0 `instrument` **the knob off is the module without it** | 10 configurations, 45 fields bitwise; A37's 24 recorded cells return with every count exact and every float within `1e-9`, worst `8.08e-16`; the knob moves the count that cuts, `196 / 154 / 116 / 76 / 37`, each under a ceiling known before the run; a partial share is refused where it has no meaning. Three planted faults are all reported |
| PASS | A38-1 `instrument` **three groups, and the third is the size asked for** | `150 / 150` cells partition, every unwilling count is `n` less `round(width * n)`, none at full width. Nodes willing but never stressed: `0` to `7` |
| PASS | A38-2 `own_reading` **withdrawers against the ones who would not withdraw** | **Passing here means a reading was produced and not that it matched what was written down.** Nothing is compared against a threshold: a cell is above one or below it, the seeds at a width agree or they do not, and the counts are what is printed. **With no floor the seeds agree at no width at all**, `22` above and `36` below over `58` cells, which is the third state and carries no verdict; read apart, the two groups fall together and stay alongside each other, `0.398 / 0.072 / 0.059 / 0.034` against `0.292 / 0.150 / 0.062 / 0.033`, so with no floor the two are not distinguishable on this quantity at all. **With a floor every width the seeds agree on is above one**, `55` above and `5` below over `60` cells, and each width that splits splits four to one above |
| PASS | A38-3 `own_reading` **width narrows who receives while flow holds** | Six curves, the receiving set against its twin falling with width on all six, five strictly: `0.930, 0.800, 0.782, 0.692, 0.544` at one of them, while flow against the twin stays between `0.85` and `1.12` and only `1 / 150` cells fall below a twentieth of it. The stock over the same cells rises from `1.19` to `2.74` with the floor and `3.31` to `34.61` without |
| PASS | A38-4 `own_reading` **two ways of splitting one population** | At full width there is nothing to compare, the third group being empty in all `30` such cells. Below it the two splits differ as sets, and their figures differ by a median of `0.0086` and at most `0.9961`. How far apart the sets are does not settle how far apart the numbers are |

**What was written down before the run, and how it came out.** The prediction was that the
ratio would be flat in width, on the ground that the mechanism is per node and carries no term
for how many others withdraw: the payoff comes from the floor, not from company. **The sign
half holds and the flatness half does not.**

```
floor, depth 0.3      width 0.20   0.40   0.60   0.80   1.00
withdrew                  14.548  4.050  3.387  1.604  0.398
did not withdraw           0.584  0.601  0.569  0.355  group empty
```

**The ones who stayed barely move. What collapses is the withdrawers' own figure**, and at
full width it falls below one: a node that withdrew ends with less than it holds in its own
twin. So the advantage is diluted by the withdrawing, not competed away by the staying.

**The rule really has no term for other nodes, and the quantity the rule reads does.** A node's
inflow depends on whether anyone still routes to it, so as more withdraw the pool everyone
draws from narrows and holding stock is worth less relative to it. A38-3 is that trace,
measured on its own: the receiving set contracts with width in an economy whose total flow has
not moved. **A per-node rule does not give a per-node outcome on a graph**, and the prediction
was taken from the shape of the rule where it should have been taken from the shape of what the
rule reads.

**Counted by kind: two `instrument` and three `own_reading` criteria hold, and there are no
`rival` criteria.** This carrier holds no debt, so a claim about a burden shared per head has
nothing here to be about; putting one in is the next station, and the sovereign's levy already
built for it assesses the nodes still trading rather than the nodes that did not withdraw,
which is what would give that claim an object to be scored against.

---

## A39: what a levy takes from the ones who withdrew, and what it fails to collect

**RUN: 2026-09-14. Script `experiments/a39_levy_dodge.py`, record `results/a39_levy_dodge.json`,
which carries the configuration it ran under. 80 cells: two levy bases, seven widths, five
seeds, plus ten twins. Nothing fetched. The sovereign station's carrier and cell builder are
imported rather than rewritten, so the two stations run the same economy, and the withdrawal
switch is the one two earlier stations built. The record is marked diagnostic: the station is
open.**

**Two earlier stations each supplied half of what this one needed.** One registered a criterion
against the claim that a fixed burden is shared per head among those who did not withdraw, on a
carrier that held no debt, so the claim had no object and the criterion was recorded as a
premise that does not hold. The other made the width of a withdrawal a knob, which is the axis
such a claim needs, since a curve cannot be scored at a single point. This stage adds the one
quantity neither had: what the levy takes from each node.

**The levy base is not a setting, it is a machine.** One takes the same amount from every node
still trading, capped at what that node holds; the other takes only from the part of an account
above the mean of the nodes still trading. The sovereign station measured them collecting
`0.3084` and `1.0000` of what fell due, so their cells are counted apart here rather than added.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | A39-0 `instrument` **the per-node vector is the scalar already recorded** | 10 configurations bitwise against the module before the field; four recorded cells of the sovereign station return with a worst relative difference of `0.000e+00`; and the identity, the vector summing to the scalar every round, holds with a residual of exactly `0.000e+00` on all six configurations. The field is absent under the two funding routes that take nothing from a node, since a field of zeros would say a levy ran and took nothing. Four planted faults are all reported |
| PASS | A39-1 `own_reading` **what each group pays** | Nothing compared against a threshold: each cell is a ratio, the seeds at a width agree or they do not, and the counts are printed. **Under the per-head base the seeds agree at none of the six widths and every cell sits between `0.884` and `1.080`: the two groups pay the same number.** **Under the base that assesses the part above the mean, twenty cells over four consecutive widths all say the same thing, and the withdrawers pay between `3.9` and `37.1` times what the others pay** |
| VOID | A39-2 `rival` **the burden on those who stayed against the rival's curve** | **This does not refute the rival.** Both curves are measured on the same cells, neither is fitted, and a cell where they sit closer together than the seeds spread is scored for neither, which is `21` of `50`. Per-head base: `15` cells closer to ours, `6` to the rival of `21` that can tell them apart. Above-the-mean base: `2` and `6` of `8`. Mixed on both, so no verdict on either. The cells favouring the rival cluster where the two curves have only just separated; where they are furthest apart the count runs `4` to `1` the other way. **On the second base the observed burden falls from `2.1804` to `0.1363` while both curves rise, so both accounts are wrong there** |
| PASS | A39-3 `own_reading` **what each base collects once some of the graph has withdrawn** | The above-the-mean base collects the whole of what falls due in all `35` cells, to machine precision. The per-head base reaches it in none: `0.9016` against its twin, falling to `0.6133` at full width, with a range of `0.4231` to `0.9475`. The receiving set narrows with width on both, `1.000` to `0.502` and `1.000` to `0.553`, while flow stays between `0.77` and `1.01` |

**A39-2 read `FAIL` here until 2026-09-15 and the prose beside it already said otherwise.**
The row's own reading is "Mixed on both, so no verdict on either", which is the undecided state,
and the record carried it out as a failure holding two cells of the rival table, `B 17` and
`C 12`. The cause was one string doing two jobs: at the level of a levy base, "mixed" means that
base returned no verdict, and at the level of the table it means the bases landed in different
cells, which is a reading. The line that set the cell read the first and wrote the second. Every
count printed normally and nothing reported it. The criterion now records `passed: null` with the
cell `unread`; the two counts keep their place beside the per-base breakdown, where they are a
description of where the cells sat and not an occupancy of anything. The same fix took the other
direction out with it: a base that could not tell the curves apart had been counted as a failure
to pass, which is the undecided cell mapped to a verdict. No number in this section moved.

**The mechanism needs nothing new, and it is two sentences from the module's own code.** A node
leaves the set the levy draws on only by falling through the subsistence floor; cutting your own
out-edges does not remove you from it, so under a per-head levy you owe the same share you owed
before. And an earlier station measured withdrawal raising what a node holds when there is a
floor, which is exactly the quantity an above-the-mean levy assesses. **The same act dodges
nothing under one rule and makes you the target under the other, and the two rules differ by
one sentence.**

**What the per-head rule does to the collection is the sharper half.** Its own arithmetic takes
the smaller of the per-head share and what the node actually holds, so whatever a node cannot
fund is simply not collected; the other rule asks only for a part of an account that is by
definition there. **So the rule that shares a burden equally is the one that collects less, and
it collects less the more of the graph has withdrawn.**

**One reading was nearly written and is not true, recorded because the way it was caught is the
general lesson.** The count still above the floor came back as a median of `123` under one base
and `49` under the other, which reads as one rule pushing more nodes under. Printed per seed it
is two states, near `48` or near `123`, with nothing between, and the two medians differ only in
how many of five seeds landed in which. **The twins themselves are two-state**, so the split is a
property of the carrier and not of the withdrawal, and five seeds cannot separate a rate between
two states. Printing the object rather than the count is what showed it.

**Counted by kind: one `instrument` and two `own_reading` criteria hold, and the one `rival`
criterion returns no verdict.** What it registered was a refutation with no exception, and the
cells came back mixed on both bases, so what it returns is the third state and not a finding
either way. **A criterion that did not adjudicate puts nothing in the four-cell table, in any
column**, and the two counts it carries say which of two curves lay nearer a reading, which is a
distance and not a verdict. This station is silent on whether the column for being wrong where
the rival was right is empty; that question is answered by other records.


## A2e — whether the carrier has two basins for a transition to run between

**RUN: 2026-09-07. Script `experiments/a2e_reaction_coordinate.py`, record
`results/a2e_reaction_coordinate.json`, document `docs/a2e_gate.md`. 624 cells, 48 seeds,
600 rounds. Nothing fetched. The record predates the rule that puts a `kind` on every
criterion and carries none; the kinds below are assigned here and the record is unchanged.**

A gate rather than a station, and it is closed. A minimum-action method needs two metastable
regions at one parameter value and a scalar variable on which they separate. A2c had read
realised cycle rank at `0.029` of the potential rank with one autonomous edge restoring it to
`0.783`, which is consistent with two basins and equally consistent with a smooth crossover
driven by the knob. Those are different worlds and only the first has transitions in it. This
asks which one the carrier is in. The answer is the second.

**The gate is ordered so that a dead candidate is struck out before it is tested for modes.**
A variable pinned against a bound cannot separate anything, and asking whether it is bimodal
is a scope error, so range is read first.

| | criterion | reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | A2e-1 `instrument` **every run completed** | 624 cells held, 624 jobs dispatched |
| PASS | A2e-0 `instrument` **at least one candidate moves across the sweep** | live: `realized_rank_frac`, `total_ratio`. Struck out for spread at or below `0.02`: `realized_support_frac` and `support_fraction`, both `0.016393` |
| FAIL | A2e-2 `own_reading` **two modes at a fixed knob value** | no cell cleared `dBIC > 10.0` and Sarle `> 0.555556` on either live candidate. A crossover, not two basins |
| PASS | A2e-4 `instrument` **the flat control knob returns unimodal** | no control cell bimodal |
| VOID | A2e-3 `own_reading` **within-run transitions, not just two basins** | `not evaluated: A2e-2 found no pair to cross between`. The detail says so in its own first clause, so this is not a failed reading, it is a criterion with no object |

**A2e-2 is a real reading that came out false, and it closes the gate.** The instanton line on
this carrier needs two basins and the carrier has one. The station is a pointer sink: no
document in the main chain points into it, and that is checkable by grep rather than by
assertion. It licenses nothing about any economy.
