| FAIL | `B120-1` `known_answer` every locked price read sits within a tick of 80% of VWAP20 on a base date of its plan, or falls in a named class that says why not | 875 plans whose documents read a price: at the floor 716, the floor of another market day of the plan's life 60, above the floor with a document naming 每股净资产 31, within a tick of the offering table's issue price carried to the issue day 34, not confirmed 34. The 34 are named in the record and stay out of every table below; 16 of them sit more than 100 ticks off and read as a misread price or a plan wrongly joined. Not objects here: 67 plans whose documents read no price and take the rule's price, whose gap is zero by construction, and 7 on the Beijing exchange with no bars |
| FAIL | `B120-2` `instrument` every plan holds one end dated after its first document and not after the data end, no announcement sits in two plans, and every completed locked cash placement finds the plan it came from | 949 plans, each with one end after its first document and not after the data end; announcements in two plans 0, and 116 held by one plan both as an agreement and as a plan document. Of the 370 cash placements the offering table reads as priced in advance from 2020-09-01, the pricing text reads 23 as the matching funds of an asset deal and 10 as priced on the first day; of the 337 it reads as locked, one more is the cash beside an asset deal by B110's own reading, leaving 336: linked to a plan 334, no verdict 1 (920198, whose exchange the census does not cover), no plan found 1 (600029) |

The share that issued, by M bin: 0.000, 0.259, 0.339, 0.462, 0.517, 0.547, 0.648. The rank correlation between M and issuing is +0.2509 against a floor of 0.1727, 1.45 times it, the floor being the largest any of 2000 label shuffles reached on either of two seeds, taking the stricter of a plain shuffle and one that moves labels inside a start year and length bucket alone. Not one of the 45 plans at M below 0.70 issued at its locked price; the lowest M at which one did is 0.736 |

A plan is the run of announcements one company's locked placement leaves: the subscription agreement announcements and
their supplements, the placement filings assigned to them, and the first announcement that ends the run. The base date
and the price are the candidate pair nearest the floor, the candidates being the plan's first locked document, each
calendar base date its documents write, and each filing assigned to it, against each price per share its documents
print. Where a plan's documents read no price the rule's price is used and the plan is named apart. A price is
confirmed when it falls in one of the five named classes above. The size n is the money cap over the price where the
documents print one, since the cap on the shares is usually the 30% of the shares before that the rules set: the two
are more than half apart in 20 of the 909 plans printing a cap, and where they are, the share cap is named beside the
band. `B120-3`'s floor is measured and not declared, and measured twice: the two seeds put the floor 0.0088 apart
against 0.0782 between the reading and the floor. The stratified floor stands above the plain one, which is what it is
there for: plans at low M ran longest, 1,118 days at the median in the lowest bin against 272 to 436 in the others, so
a gradient that were only the passage of time would not clear a shuffle that keeps each start year and length bucket
intact.

**What the reading does not cover.** The three classes the rules name are not told apart beyond one marker, whether a
document's title names a related-party transaction; the subscribers' names are in the offering table for the plans that
issued alone. The acceptance and registration announcements were not fetched, so nothing here reads the stage a plan
had reached when it ended, and the station says nothing about whether a subscriber who leaves before the registration
takes effect owes anything. The 115 plans with no cap read leave `B120-4`'s total a floor over the plans that print a
cap rather than a total over all of them.

**Where the plans ended, by M.** M is the close of the last day the stock traded before the end over the locked price
carried to that day. The 908 plans whose price is confirmed, with the median days from the first document to the end.

## B26 — a headline number that did not move while three of the four fields around it did

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-19. The station was read on 2026-08-30 and its result file was never
carried into this ledger. Criteria in `docs/b26_prereg.md`, readings in `docs/b26_results.md`,
sources and their calibers in `docs/b26_focal_price_availability.md`. All four arms read; the
station is not void.**

A seller announces one number for a class of its products and commits to it in public. The
station asks what that seller does when its input cost rises far enough that a passthrough
account predicts the number moves. The object is not the number alone but the offer: the price
field, the set of eligible products, the set of participating stores, and how often the offer can
be taken. The four fields were fixed in the design before anything was read.

**The prereg registers no assignment to the six criterion kinds**, so the arms are printed here as
the station wrote them rather than sorted into kinds this ledger would have had to invent.

| | Arm | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| third state | `B26-1` the headline scalar | the announced number never changed; it was preserved while its scope was emptied |
| PASS | `B26-2` the margin count | three of four fields moved: eligible drinks, participating stores, frequency; the price field did not |
| PASS | `B26-3` the shock magnitude | unit cost +35.9% to +46.2% against a 20% threshold fixed before the reading |
| PASS | `B26-4` the positive control | non-focal posted prices at the same seller moved in the same window |

**The third state was registered as a distinct prediction, not as a fallback, and it is what
occurred.** `9.9` was announced nationally in June 2023 and committed to at the second-quarter
results call in August 2023: 郭谨一, 瑞幸咖啡董事长兼CEO, *"当年6月开始的9.9元感恩回馈活动反响
超预期，因此决定将这一优惠活动常态化进行下去，至少持续两年。"* The firm had the ordinary
alternative available and did not take it. By 2025 the named zone was gone, replaced by a
"from `9.9`" framing that keeps the digits and drops the commitment.

**Reproduced at a second seller that was not part of the design.** The competitor ended its own
all-items `9.9` from February 2026 by the same route: the number kept for a special zone of three
to seven products while everything else reverted to `11.9` to `16.9`. At the time of the report a
single product carried `9.9` and it was out of stock; on the first seller's side most products had
returned to `10.9` to `13.9`. Two sellers, same market, same shock, neither moved the number, and
both withdrew the offer by narrowing what it covered.

**The two axes moved in opposite directions inside one announcement**, which is a sharper
observation than any single field moving. On 2024-04-22 customer service stated both the outward
move of the store field and the inward move of the drink field: *"之前是天天券，指的是部分门店可以
参与，现在是全国券，它是两种不同的券。"* and *"活动内容有所更改，之前的天天券已升级为全国门店
可使用，目前全国券只能选择6款饮品，具体以使用规则为准。"* The drink field ran all freshly made
coffee (2023-06) → ten named (2024-02-19) → six named (2024-04-22) → eight (early 2025) → zone
removed; the frequency field ran daily → one coupon per week → an afternoon-tea slot.

**The shock, and what the arithmetic is allowed to carry.** Arabica rose about 70% over 2024, the
C-type contract close to 90% over six months, reaching 429.95 US cents per pound. A published unit
cost decomposition for a comparable operator in the same market puts raw material at 5.7 of 11.1
yuan, a share of 0.5135, giving 0.70 × 0.5135 = +35.9% and 0.90 × 0.5135 = +46.2%. **The share is
used only as a share and never as a level**: the reading is that the shock is large relative to
unit cost in this business, not that any seller's unit cost took a particular value.

**Where this sits.** Against a cost passthrough account the pair `B26-1` with `B26-3` is
distinguishing: a 36 to 46 per cent unit cost increase with no move in the price field is not what
that account predicts. Against short-run price stickiness `B26-4` separates it, since other posted
prices at the same seller moved in the same window, so the constancy is a property of that number
and not of this seller's prices in general. `B26-2`'s four-field count is a quantity no competing
account has a reason to assemble.

**The premise this station establishes is already established elsewhere, on tighter carriers, and
that is the reason to cite rather than to compete.** DellaVigna and Gentzkow (2019), *Uniform
Pricing in U.S. Retail Chains*, QJE 134(4), 2011–2084, find near-uniform prices across stores of
one chain despite wide variation in demographics and competition, the median chain forgoing about
16 million dollars a year against store-level optimal pricing, and record that uniform pricing
raises what poorer households pay relative to richer ones. Their design shares cost as well as
converging it. Snir, Levy, Gotler and Chen, and Levy, Lee, Chen, Kauffman and Bergen, *Price Points
and Price Rigidity*, find nine-ending prices more common and more rigid, consumers less likely to
notice a larger price ending in nine, and the rigidity asymmetric. **Both records were read from
abstracts and working-paper pages; neither full text has been read**, and page-level claims must be
checked against the version of record before use.

**What is still unclaimed, and it is the whole of what remains.** That literature presents uniform
pricing as a puzzle and explains it by managerial simplicity, inattention and fairness. The step
from "posted prices are conventional and rigid" to "convention propagated around a cycle admits no
global potential" is not taken there, is not taken by this station, and is where the framework's
claim lives.

**What this station does not settle.** It does not establish which individual items sat at the
focal number on any given date: no unified menu state exists to read and the design excludes the
claim. It does not establish anything about the cost shock's own effect, since there is one shock
in the window and identification is across margins inside it. It does not establish that the number
is rigid in general or at other sellers; two sellers behaved the same way, one of them outside the
design, and that is reported as suggestive. It does not establish a mechanism for why the number is
the rigid object.

**Two gaps stated rather than left to be found.** The 2025 states of the zone, its replacement by
the "from `9.9`" framing and the afternoon-tea slot are recorded from reading and **no original is
held for them**. The two individual non-focal item moves cited under `B26-4` are the weakest source
in the file, a single trade report, one of them hard to reconcile with a broker report giving that
drink a list price of 18 in 2023; the arm rests on the separately reported range-wide reversion
instead.

## B27 — how the consistency of conventional conversion systems is held together, and the one number in it that was withdrawn

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. The station was read over 2026-08-30 and its result file was never
carried into this ledger. Design and screening decisions in `docs/b27_prereg.md`, readings and
the audit in `docs/b27_results.md`. The station's preregistered arm `B27-0` sought a first
cohomology reading and failed on every carrier screened; what the station returned instead is a
classification, and one quantitative reading that its own audit later withdrew.**

Corollary 5.4 puts the single-price account on the zero set: every class agreeing, the common
field exact. That locus has measure zero in the field space, which leaves a question the theorem
does not answer. If no potential exists, why does the world look so much like a world where one
does? This station reads thirteen independently documented systems in which parties publish
factors converting between units of account and asks, of each, what keeps it consistent.

**Twelve of the thirteen are classified, and in every one of those the absence or the closure of
a loop is an act by a party with an interest in the outcome.** Two mechanisms cover all twelve.
Where the edge that would close a loop can be removed, the party bearing the loss removes it.
Where it cannot be removed, that party sets the factor so the loop closes. The thirteenth admits
a closable loop with no single party over it and is not read here; it is `b28`.

**Deletion, and the proof that it is a choice.** A loyalty issuer's trade statement is one-way:
the units transfer out and cannot come back. A platform's currency terms say it twice, that the
currency has no cash value and is not redeemable for any sum of money, and that it may not be
sold, transferred, assigned, redeemed or exchanged for cash. **The edge returns exactly where a
legislature puts it back, and only up to the amount the legislature names.** Ten US states
require cash refunds of small stored-value balances at thresholds fixed by statute rather than by
any economic quantity: Rhode Island and Vermont under one dollar, Colorado, Maine,
Massachusetts, Montana, New Jersey, Oregon and Washington under five, California under ten and
since raised to fifteen by Senate Bill 22. **Source: Connecticut General Assembly, Office of
Legislative Research, *States that Provide Cash Refunds for Gift Card Balances*, report
2019-R-0185, updating 2015-R-0095**, official tier, with each state's citation carried in the
station's file.

**A precision error this ledger carries deliberately.** The station first described those
thresholds as `$0.99`, `$4.99` and `$9.99`. Those are the highest qualifying balances, not the
statutory numbers, which are written as *under one dollar*, *under five dollars* and *under ten
dollars*. **The distinction matters more here than it usually would**, because this station's
subject is posted numbers, and attributing a nine-ending price point to a legislature would have
been the framework finding its own object in a place that does not contain it.

**Commutation, sourced verbatim.** Where the edge cannot be deleted, the factor is chosen. A
merger compelled an absorbed programme's balances into the surviving one and no party could
decline to publish the ratio. Three factors then stood in public, and the diagram commutes
exactly:

```
absorbed  -> airline     20,000 -> 25,000
absorbed  -> surviving   1 : 3
surviving -> airline     60,000 -> 25,000
```

Quoted at third-party tier: *"Starpoints were tripled into rewards points. So, the same transfer
ratio applies: 20,000 Starpoints = 60,000 rewards points = 25,000 airline miles."* **Three is not
a number the merger discovered; it is the number that makes the two routes agree given the two
pre-existing charts.** The holding was renamed and its magnitude multiplied by three while what
it buys did not move, and the redefinition is posted rather than hidden.

**What could not form a loop, and why that is itself a reading.** Of the thirteen carriers, all
but two cannot form a loop at all, and three of those are prevented by an act rather than by
structure. Consumer electronics price bands and prepared beverage price points are stars
maintained by hierarchy. Rating agency notching is a star from the issuer rating. Airline partner
mileage earning is not composable. Course credit articulation carries a factor that is not
multiplicative; professional licensing reciprocity carries a condition rather than a factor;
administered exchange rates derive every factor from one scalar at lags. **Successive generations
of one product name is the row worth reading twice**: the releases might have been independent
anchors, one per name, and they are not. Over fourteen releases on one line the modal move is
exactly zero, five of thirteen transitions leave the list price unchanged to the yuan, and the
whole series' dispersion equals its generation-to-generation dispersion, `0.0805` against
`0.0825`, so nothing accumulates. Each name inherits from the one before, which makes the
reference structure a path, and a path is a tree. **Hierarchy in the first two rows was across
sellers at one time; here it is across time within one seller. Both are trees, and neither can
carry a holonomy.**

| | criterion | kind | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| FAIL | `B27-0` a first cohomology reading on any screened carrier | own_reading | fails on every carrier; twelve of thirteen are acyclic and three of those deliberately so |
| PASS | `B27` deletion is an act rather than a structural feature | known_answer | reversed by statute in ten states, at thresholds set by legislatures rather than by any economic quantity |
| PASS | `B27` commutation where deletion is unavailable | known_answer | the merger's three factors commute exactly, quoted verbatim, and the ratio was fixed before any trade |
| **withdrawn** | `B27` the round-trip spread across partners on the hotel-to-airline carrier | own_reading | reported as `2.40` with log sd `0.3125`; **the audit established it cannot be a cross-partner spread and the number is withdrawn**, see below |

**The withdrawal, and it is the most useful thing in the file.** The station read ten round trips
out of one hotel programme into ten airline programmes and back, none returning to its start,
with loop products spanning `0.2083` to `0.5000`, a factor of `2.40`. Chasing the citations found
the forward leg official: Marriott Bonvoy, *How to Transfer Points to Miles*, read 2026-08-30,
gives United at `0.5000` (3:1 plus 10,000 bonus per 60,000) and the standard partner at `0.4167`
(3:1 plus 5,000 bonus per 60,000), both landing on the file's values to four decimal places. The
five values then decompose exactly as `0.4167` or `0.5000` times a return leg of 1, 1, 3/4, 2/3
or 1/2, and only United's 1:1 return leg is sourced, at third-party tier. **But the same source
shows the chart turns over**: it records United at `0.4583` in an earlier vintage against
`0.5000` now, and JetBlue's six-points-to-one-mile term at a time when JetBlue is no longer among
the thirty-eight partners at all. Dated against the chart as it stood on 2026-08-30, the complete
set of distinct rates is `0.5000`, `0.4167`, `0.3333` (American AAdvantage, Avianca LifeMiles,
Delta SkyMiles, 3:1 with no bonus) and `0.0050` (Air New Zealand, 200:1), with thirty-five
partners on the standard ratio. **Two of the file's five values are on that chart and three are
not, and a rate that is on it, `0.3333`, is absent from the file's table.** A one-day cross
section of partners would contain `0.3333` and would not contain the other three, so the
cross-partner reading is dead. The remaining possibilities are loop products with undocumented
return legs, which the exact decomposition supports and no document confirms, or a mix of
vintages of a chart that demonstrably changes. **A spread across time is a different object from
a spread across partners, and this station is about the second**, so the quantitative result
stands withdrawn until the panel is rebuilt from one dated chart plus documented return legs.

**What that reading was registered as, for whoever rebuilds it.** The graph is a star with ten
spokes, so `b1 = 10 - 11 + 1 = 0` and it was never a first cohomology reading. Every closed walk
goes out and back on one spoke, which is `omega-bar` in the directed decomposition of
`b4_directed_edges` §5, and Theorem 6(2) makes a non-zero symmetric part exactly what prevents a
sub-potential with zero slacks. The `rho` column is Theorem 6(4)'s registered quantity, the same
one B13 reads on live exchange quotes, **so a rebuilt version would be a second reading of `rho`
on posted terms rather than on quotes.**

**Where this sits.** Against a no-arbitrage account the station is distinguishing, and that is the
objection that matters most: no-arbitrage says traders compete a gap away, so the gap shrinks
toward zero through trading, while this account says the gap never appears, because the
rule-setter removed the edge or chose the factor. **The merger case separates them, since the
ratio was fixed at the point of merger, before any trade, with no trader participating in closing
it.** Against a bid-ask reading of the round-trip loss the station is not separated and says so:
one party publishes both directions there. The quantity no competing account has a reason to
compute is the classification itself, of conversion systems by how their consistency is
maintained.

**What this station does not settle.** It establishes no first cohomology result. It does not
establish that the two mechanisms exhaust the possibilities: the population defined in
`b27_prereg.md` §4a has not been enumerated, the carriers were nominated before that population
existed, and the count is therefore a count over nominations. It does not establish that the
round-trip loss is not a posted spread. **And it does not establish that maintained consistency
is inefficient, unfair or anyone's fault**; the finding is that it is maintained, and by whom, and
by which of two methods.

**Closed against reopening on the original question.** `b27_prereg.md` is retained as the design
record and as the account of what the search was for. It is not superseded and it is not to be
re-run on these carriers: their acyclicity is established and, in three cases, deliberate. The
next screen is named instead, and it is `b28`: a carrier whose two directions are set by
different parties, which the three-price structure of a durable good has, since the maker posts a
sale price and a trade-in price while the secondary market clears at neither.

**Locator debt still open on this station.** Four of the five return-leg ratios are not attached
to a named programme, and each of the thirteen screening decisions in `b27_prereg.md` §5a rests
on a programme document that is not cited. **Nothing in this station quotes a non-English source**,
so the original-text half of rule 109 does not arise; the locator half is unmet on those two
lists. The 2023 successor report to the gift card compilation, 2023-R-0195, exists and its PDF
was refused by this project's fetch path, so the 2019 compilation is used and California's change
is carried from its own source; a run needing current thresholds for all ten states must read
each statute directly.

## B28 — the posted number is defended, and which margin gives way depends on the tier

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. Read over 2026-08-29 and 2026-08-30 and never carried into this ledger.
Criteria in `docs/b28_prereg.md`, readings in `docs/b28_results.md`, scripts
`experiments/b28_5a_sale_life.py` and `experiments/b28_6_generational_anchor.py`. `B28-1`, `B28-5a`,
`B28-5b` and `B28-6` are read. `B28-2`, `B28-3` and `B28-4` are not run, so this is a station in
part and is entered as one.**

This is the carrier B27 named as its next screen: a durable good whose two directions are set by
different parties, since the maker posts a sale price and a trade-in price while the secondary
market clears at neither. What the station found first is that one of those legs is arithmetic.

**`B28-1`, and the correction that makes it weaker and better supported.** Seven items carrying
both a refurbished and an original price on the maker's own listing, across two categories and a
`3.42` factor in list price, fit one rule exactly: take fifteen per cent off the list price, then
round down to the nearest price ending in nine. `P4/P1` spans `0.84656` to `0.84995`, a range of
`0.40` per cent, log sd `0.00177`. **A twenty-three item panel from a third product family then
broke it**: `P4/P1` from `0.8189` to `0.8874`, log sd `0.0203`, eleven times the seven-item
figure, and the rounding rule fits three of the twenty-three. **The dispersion sorts by product
line**, entry `0.8448`, small `0.8551`, mid `0.8544`, professional `0.8769`, with every one of the
professional line's ten items above the entry line's whole range. So the discount is still a
posted convention carrying no information about the item, and it is one convention per line rather
than one for the firm.

| | criterion | kind | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | `B28-1` the refurbished discount is a posted rule rather than an assessment of the object | own_reading | first state; seven of seven on the exact rule, then stratified by line on a larger panel, log sd `0.0203` with a monotone tier ordering |
| PASS | `B28-5a` which margin absorbs a mismatch, by tier | own_reading | nine price steps of exactly `$100` on retained non-professional models against six professional withdrawals taking no step, on the same three dates |
| PASS | `B28-5b` whether the withdrawal is technical rather than commercial | known_answer | two matched cohorts: sale life differs by `2.99` and `2.98`, support life by `1.024` and `0.984`, OS generations six and six, seven and seven |
| second branch | `B28-6` whether a new name resets the anchor | own_reading | median transition ratio exactly `1.0000`, six of fourteen exactly flat, log sd `0.0825`: the name does not reset the anchor and the independence reading fails |
| not run | `B28-2`, `B28-3`, `B28-4` | | no market price `P2` collected; nothing here compares to it |

**`B28-5a`, and the cleanest cut in the station.** On three dates the maker acted on both tiers at
once, in the same product family. Retained non-professional models took **nine price steps, every
one of them exactly `$100`, with no other step size observed**: iPhone 12, 13 and 13 mini on
2022-09-07, iPhone 14, 14 Plus, 15 and 15 Plus on 2024-09-09, iPhone 16 and 16 Plus on 2025-09-09.
On those same days six professional models took no step of any size and were withdrawn instead. Six
consecutive professional generations have sale lives of 12.78, 10.71, 11.43, 11.86, 11.60 and 11.63
months, range ratio `1.193`, log sd `0.0572`, and **overlap positive zero times out of six**, each
going off sale about ten days before its successor ships. **One maker, one day, one product family,
two tiers, a different adjustment margin on each: where the number moves it moves in a fixed step
and the object stays; where the number does not move the object goes.**

**The supply story does not survive the within-generation cut.** The 13 Pro was withdrawn at 11.4
months while the iPhone 13, launched the same day, from the same generation, on the same supply
chain, stayed on sale 35.5 months and was cut to `$699` in 2022 and `$599` in 2023. A supply or
demand account predicts the same treatment for both and does not predict a split by tier. The
tablet panel says it more weakly over more cases: the professional line's log dispersion in sale
life is `0.1242` against `0.4381` to `0.5388` for the other three lines of the same family, three
and a half to four times tighter, and its overlap is never positive across seven transitions. The
five models kept past their own successor are all outside the professional line and each was kept
at a reduced number, three of them named in one sentence of the maker's own release, 2014-10-16:
*"iPad Air, iPad mini 2 and iPad mini, available in silver or space gray, are offered at now more
affordable prices."*

**`B28-5b` is the arm that could have destroyed `B28-5a`, and it is the reason the reading holds.**
The maker runs two withdrawal clocks over one object. The commercial clock is set by tier; the
engineering clock is set at a silicon boundary and crosses the tier line. Where support has already
ended there are two cohorts, each containing a matched pair of the same year, maker, family and
chip generation:

| cohort | model | tier | sale life (mo) | last major OS | OS generations | support life (mo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | iPhone X | professional | 10.28 | iOS 16 | 6 | 58.28 |
| 2017 | iPhone 8 | standard | 30.75 | iOS 16 | 6 | 59.66 |
| 2018 | iPhone XS | professional | 11.63 | iOS 18 | 7 | 71.85 |
| 2018 | iPhone XR | standard | 34.63 | iOS 18 | 7 | 70.70 |

**Sale life differs by a factor of almost exactly three; support life differs by about one month,
which is the gap between the two models' own launch dates.** The professional model is withdrawn
while it still has years of support ahead of it, 48 months in the iPhone X's case. That kills the
strongest remaining competing reading, that the professional model is the technically leading
product and is therefore superseded fastest, since its technical life is the same in both cohorts
where the comparison exists. **Two matched pairs, because two is how many exist**; the 2019 and 2020
cohorts will test it when their boundaries land and are recorded as pending rather than as support.

**`B28-6` returns its second branch, and it is a negative result on a hypothesis this project would
have preferred to win.** One maker's base handset, China launch price, fifteen generations,
fourteen transitions: median ratio exactly `1.0000`, six transitions exactly flat, log sd `0.0825`,
first to last `1.2000` over fourteen years. Registered: wide dispersion means each name carries an
independently set anchor, clustering near one means the new name inherits the old and the
independence reading fails. **It clusters. The name is renewed annually and the number is not.**
The one stretch of four consecutive non-zero moves, `+20.62%`, `-15.39%`, `+14.55%`, `-4.76%`, has
strictly alternating signs and strictly decreasing amplitude and is followed by three exact zeros,
**and the station explicitly refuses to test it**, because the window was chosen as the stretch
where the price moved and a stretch selected for having moves is not a random draw.

**Two readings of one series are not two pieces of evidence.** B25 reads this line by year and gets
log sd `0.0805`; `B28-6` reads it by generation and gets `0.0825`. These are two cuts of one
series, and the near-equality is arithmetic rather than corroboration. **Any argument leaning on
both is double counting**, which the prereg required be said here.

**The advertised rate is not the rule.** The listing says *"Apple Certified Refurbished products
include a one-year warranty, full functional testing, and savings up to 15%"* (apple.com/shop/
refurbished, read 2026-08-30, official), and that sentence is what licenses treating the
refurbished and new unit as the same object. But `0.8500` sits inside the measured range rather
than above it: the maximum measured saving is `18.11%` and the entry line's mean saving is `15.52%`,
both past the advertised ceiling, while the professional line's mean saving is `12.31%`. **A reading
that took fifteen per cent as the rule would have been wrong on twenty of twenty-three items.** No
complaint is implied and a saving larger than advertised harms nobody; the point is that the seller
posts one number and prices by another, which is the shape of everything else in the file.

**The two-sided corner, and why only a direction is taken from it.** Every posted-price instance in
this project so far is the too-high corner: coverage and eligibility in B26, storage content in
B25, existence here. A mechanism observed on one side of a mismatch invites the reading that it is
selective observation. **Top-tier handbags supply the other corner**: two resale platforms' annual
reports agree in direction that the secondary market clears above retail, and the maker rations
quantity rather than raising the posted price. **Only the direction is used**, because those
figures come from interested parties' marketing documents disclosing neither sample size nor
coverage, and no retention-level comparison is made. **And the category that retains nothing is a
scope condition rather than a data gap**: high-end tailoring prices each garment individually, so
no name-level number exists for a secondary market to reference, which is why prices there fall
back onto the object.

**Information is a fourth margin, and the discriminating case is inside the station.** The maker
publishes trade-in values per model, which looks like publishing exactly the figure this account
says gets suppressed. **The resolution is in the currency and it is checkable**: the trade-in value
is paid in purchase credit and cannot be taken as cash, so it is a discount on a new purchase
denominated in a unit that spends in one place. **The falsifiable form is that where a maker
publishes its own buy-back number, that number should be payable in a restricted currency far more
often than in cash.**

**What this station does not settle.** Nothing about the market price, since `P2` has not been
collected. Not that existence is the adjustment margin in general; the catalogue observation is one
date and one line, and `B28-5a` replaced catalogue presence with stop of sale precisely because the
maker does not control whether an object goes on trading. Not that the fifteen per cent is unfair
or mispriced; the finding is that it is computed rather than assessed. Not that the rule holds for
other makers or categories. **And the line-level interpretation is labelled as an interpretation**:
anchor protection and absence of room predict opposite signs for the relation between gross margin
and discount depth, a panel spanning sellers of different margin would decide between them, no such
panel exists, and neither is assumed.

**Instrument limits carried forward.** The vintage and obsolete lists are a lower bound on age
rather than a clock: four rows check out exactly against the maker's stated rule and three do not,
all three carried as vintage past the seven-year boundary, with region-dependent handling stated on
the same page. Tablet dates are a third-party compilation checked on those four rows; phone dates
are trade press on the day for 2024 and 2025 and third-party infoboxes for the four earlier
generations; the tablet pricing statements are official. **The twenty-three item refurbished panel
has no per-item capture date** and is bounded to 2026-08-29 to 2026-08-30 from the file's own
backups, recorded as a bound rather than as a timestamp. The two-sided section's secondary-market
figures and the trade-in schedule carry no locator. The `B28-6` series has both endpoints
independently sourced and **its ten intermediate values one source deep**, a compilation dated
2022-10-16, and its line definition excludes the premium model, which is stated rather than
defended.

**What would break `B28-5a`:** a professional model kept on sale by the maker after its successor
launched, at a reduced posted price. None occurs in thirteen professional transitions across two
product families. **What would break `B28-5b`:** a cohort in which the professional model's support
ends materially earlier than its standard sibling's.

## B29 — the cost band cannot destroy the defect, and the statistic that was registered to measure it cannot find it

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. `B29-3` read 2026-08-30 and never carried into this ledger. Readings in
`docs/b29_results.md`, the locality theorem and its verification in `docs/b29_locality_theorem.md`
(§2 for Theorem 7, with 7(4) and 7(5) added 2026-09-11), the two-threshold sweep in
`docs/b30_propagation.md` §12.7. Scripts `experiments/b29c_cost_band.py` and
`experiments/b29b_two_thresholds.py`, cache `results/b29c_cost_band.json` keyed by `(n, r, L, seed)`.
No external source: everything here is computed.**

B29's arbitrage was an exact orthogonal projection, so every visible cycle closes to machine zero.
Real arbitrage has a cost band, and a loop whose discrepancy sits under the round-trip cost is not
worth doing and stays open. **If the band can swallow the defect, a zero read on a real carrier
cannot be told from a defect hidden under cost, and `B29-1` has no interpretation.** That is D24's
resolution floor and it is why this arm ran first. The model is cycle-by-cycle Kaczmarz with a dead
zone `tau`: for each visible cycle `c`, if `|c·w| > tau`, move `w` so `|c·w|` becomes exactly `tau`.
Ring of 20, range 2, horizon 6, so `ceil(n/r) = 10` and the defect survives by Theorem 7; eighty
visible cycles, three seeds, `tau` from 0 to 10 against a largest pre-arbitrage cycle sum of about
3.7.

| | criterion | kind | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | `B29-3` whether a cost band can destroy the defect | own_reading | it cannot: every update is a multiple of some `c` in `V`, so `w` moves only inside `span V` and the component orthogonal to it is exactly conserved. `hol_inv` is identical to four figures at `tau = 0` and `tau = 10` on all three seeds, across twelve values of `tau` each |
| FAIL | the registered statistic `ratio = |hol| / resid` | own_reading | non-monotone in the noise floor; seed 2 reads swallowed, then marginal again, then swallowed |
| PASS | the replacement statistic `|hol_inv| / tau` | own_reading | monotone in every seed with one crossover each, at `tau = |defect| / 3`: `0.0384`, `0.0051`, `0.2890` |

**The structural fact was stated before any number and needs no simulation.** Updates lie in
`span V`, so the defect, which lives in the orthogonal complement, is untouched by any `tau`. **The
cost band cannot destroy the defect; it can only raise the floor until the defect is not
measurable**, and quantifying that floor is the whole point of the arm. Confirmed to the last digit:
`hol_inv` is `0.1152`, `0.0154` and `-0.8671` on the three seeds, identical at both ends of the
sweep. And `resid` equals `tau` exactly while `tau` is below the largest initial cycle sum, since
the iteration drives every visible cycle to the band edge, and stays at its initial value above it.

**The registered statistic fails, and that failure is the arm's result.** `hol`, the sum around the
ring, is not conserved and is not well behaved: it ranges `-5.4116` to `0.1152` on seed 0, `-0.0166`
to `0.4339` on seed 1, `-0.8671` to `4.6268` on seed 2, **wandering up to forty-seven times its
conserved value and changing sign**. The reason is visible once stated: `R` has a large component
inside `span V`, the dead zone leaves `w` anywhere in a feasible set rather than at a point, and the
ring sum mostly reads where in that set the system happens to sit. **A criterion that recovers as
the cost band widens is measuring something other than recoverability.**

**The replacement is a repair rather than a patch**, and it passes failure mode 108's two gates:
`hol_inv` is the exactly conserved component, derivable before any run from the fact that updates
lie in `span V` and fitted to nothing, and it makes a new prediction that can fail.

**The design correction this forces on `B29-1`.** That arm was registered as "measure the cycle-sum
defect as a function of cycle length", and under a cost band that instruction is under-specified and
would produce garbage, because a single loop's sum is dominated by where in the feasible set the
field sits. **Corrected: the defect must be extracted as the component of the observed field
orthogonal to the span of the cycles the traders can actually close**, a Hodge extraction over the
whole field rather than an arithmetic sum around one loop. That is HodgeRank's operation (Jiang,
Lim, Yao and Ye, *Math. Prog. B* 2010, arXiv:0811.1067), and this arm is the reason the project now
needs it rather than merely acknowledging it. Two consequences bind any real reading: **many loops,
not one**, and **the trading graph and the horizon must be known**, because the extraction projects
onto the complement of `span V` and `V` is defined by what traders can reach. A reading that cannot
state who can arbitrage what cannot state a defect.

**The new falsifiable prediction.** On a real carrier the Hodge-extracted defect should be invariant
to the arbitrageurs' cost level while single-loop sums should not: periods of higher trading
friction should leave the extracted defect unchanged and scatter the loop sums. **If the extracted
defect moves with friction, this reading is wrong.**

**The resolution floor, in units a collector can check before collecting.** A cycle defect is
measurable iff the round-trip transaction cost is below `defect / 3`. It also says what to do when
that fails: **look at longer loops**, since by Theorem 7 the defect is carried by the winding class
and does not shrink with loop length, while the cost of the loops an arbitrageur would actually
close does not grow with it either.

**Limits.** One graph family, ring with range 2 and horizon 6: the conservation argument is general
and needs no simulation, but the size of `R`'s component inside `span V`, which is what makes the
ring sum useless, is graph-dependent and has only been seen here. Three seeds, **which is enough
because the conserved quantity is identical to the last digit in all of them and the estimator
failure appears in all of them; a fourth seed would confirm arithmetic that is already proved.** The
dead zone is symmetric and the same for every cycle, while real costs differ by route and direction,
and the asymmetric variant is not run. The soft-threshold rule assumes the arbitrageur takes the
whole profit above cost; closing the gap fully to zero whenever acting is worthwhile was not run and
would give a different `resid` while leaving the conservation fact untouched.

## B37 — a publisher that is still printing a number after the thing it was a number for has been cut off

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. `B37-1` and `B37-2` read 2026-09-01, records `results/b37_runs.json`;
`B37-3` and `B37-4` read 2026-09-01, record `results/b37_freeze.json`. Never carried into this
ledger.**

Argentine peso quotes, several publishers and several rate concepts over seven years. A run is a
stretch of consecutive days on which a published quote does not change. The station asks when a
published series has stopped being about anything, and it gets an instrument sharper than its design
expected, because inflation over this window is high enough that a live peso quote moves almost
every day.

| | criterion | kind | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | `B37-1` a floor exists and is narrow | instrument | Ámbito `mayorista`, independently shown by B5 to track BCRA A3500, has a longest run of `7` days; all five Ámbito series are alive, medians 1, p99 2 to 4 |
| PASS | `B37-2` edges do go sticky, and not rarely | own_reading | five series cross the floor, with longest runs of 57, 71, 47, 19 and 13 days, and the shapes differ by series |
| PASS | `B37-3` whether the world moved while the pipe was frozen | own_reading | bimodal with nothing between: `oficial` at 1.9, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3 against `mayorista` at 11.8, 21.6, 31.2, 539.0 |
| PASS | `B37-4` a cut edge against a noisier one | own_reading | four of four `mayorista` freezes reconnect in one step: `step/gap` of 1.04, 1.02, 1.00, 1.05 |
| no verdict | the `blue` arm | own_reading | the referee froze on the same days at the same value, so the reading is undecidable for referee failure rather than for a zero |

**The station's own control was given by the data rather than designed.** Two of the longest freezes
sit in different worlds. `oficial` froze at `60.4483` from 2019-12-11 to 2020-02-05, when the
official rate was near-pegged after the September 2019 controls, so the world was not moving either.
`mayorista` froze at `937.9988` from 2024-08-13 to 2024-10-22, under a crawling peg of about two per
cent a month, so the world was moving. **One publisher, two series, one still because the world was
still and one still because the pipe was cut.** The discriminant is the referee's movement during
the freeze over that series' own median daily step on non-frozen days, and the criterion was written
before looking.

**The separation is bimodal and nothing draws it.** `oficial`'s largest is 3.3 and `mayorista`'s
smallest is 11.8, with no segment in between. The script's `3.0` line is therefore not load-bearing
and the section reports the two modes rather than the line, under rule 11: print the object, do not
draw a line on the estimator. **`oficial`'s own 1.9 to 3.3 is itself a reading**, since a quote whose
daily step is the same order as the world's movement is what a peg means.

**The headline.** From 2023-12-12, `argentinadatos mayorista` sat at `365.9497` for thirty trading
days while BCRA A3500 moved `+0.7991` in logs, which is the Milei devaluation. Ratio 539. **The
first step after the thaw was `+0.7984`, so `step/gap` is 1.00.** The number stayed alive at full
amplitude for thirty days while it stopped being about anything, and then the edge was reconnected
and the gap closed in one move.

**`B37-4` answers a half-question the price theory outline left open.** Four `mayorista` freezes give
`step/gap` of 1.04, 1.02, 1.00 and 1.05, all near one, so this is freezing and reconnection rather
than drifting on partial information. **A node with only one upstream edge freezes when that edge is
cut, because drifting needs some other input to drift on.** That gives a discriminant between two
kinds of break: a full step on reconnection means the single edge was deleted, a partial step means
other inputs remain and the edge got noisier rather than cut. **`cripto`'s `0.88` is logged as a
possible instance of the second kind and the station does not claim it**, because its referee is a
proxy.

**A defect in this station's own first script, recorded rather than quietly fixed.** The design
registered the discriminant as the referee's movement against the noise floor. The first script used
a percentile of the referee's own same-length window distribution and drew a `0.25` line on it,
which was not in the registration, and it **read three segments backwards**: the 71-day `mayorista`
freeze came out at the 17th percentile and the script printed "the world was still too", while the
referee had moved `+0.0462` over those 71 days. A percentile asks whether a window is unusual for the
referee; the registered criterion asks whether the referee moved enough to make a flat quote a
fault. **Restoring the registered criterion changed no byte of the readings and inverted only the
adjudications.** The percentiles are still printed and carry no verdict.

**Three things read in passing, all printed.** `tarjeta`'s 13 days match digit for digit the 13 days
B5's zero-calibration arm reports, recomputed here on a different statistic with this station's own
run function, which is a clean reproduction of an external number rather than a self-confirmation.
`mayorista`'s three freezes run 30, 50 then 71 days, so once an edge goes sticky the next episode is
longer, logged as a shape with no criterion attached. And two publishers froze on the same start date
at the same four decimal places, `121.8975` from 2020-07-03, with one of them frozen five days
longer, **which is a clue about a shared upstream and is not enough to assert one**, since one
segment is not a distribution.

**Open items.** The `blue` arm needs a referee not sharing Ámbito's upstream and none is claimed. The
documentary source for whether the late-2019 official rate was pegged was searched twice without a
hit, and the station uses BCRA A3500's own series instead, on the ground that it is the source rather
than a publisher. Ámbito's 2011 to 2015 history is not fetched, so the paired half of `blue`'s early
window is missing. `tarjeta` and `cripto` have proxy referees and are printed without entering the
bimodal reading.

## B32 — the German monetary union's conversion, and which side of the balance sheet the exception was written for

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. Read 2026-08-31. Never carried into this ledger. The station is closed.
Six criteria: four PASS, one PASS with figures printed and no verdict, one withdrawn, none
failed.**

**The treaty's own wording puts the burden on the right side.** Article 10(5): *"Alle anderen auf
Mark der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik lautenden Forderungen und Verbindlichkeiten werden
grundsätzlich im Verhältnis 2 zu 1 auf Deutsche Mark umgestellt."*, with *"Löhne, Gehälter,
Stipendien, Renten, Mieten und Pachten sowie weitere wiederkehrende Zahlungen werden im Verhältnis
1 zu 1 umgestellt."* **So 2:1 is the default and 1:1 is the exception**, and the construction is to
halve every claim and liability first and then write a named list back to par, where the list's
defining term is `wiederkehrende Zahlungen`. **That ordering is load-bearing**: the write-down is
the default, par is the exception granted, and the test for the exception is whether the thing is a
recurring flow.

**`B32-4`, and it needs three numbers at once or it writes a false sentence.** Household net money
income ran about 159 billion marks a year, converted at 1:1; household demand and savings deposits
of 165.6 billion converted to 115.2 billion, of which 100.8 billion went at 2:1; **and prices moved
across at 1:1**, so a ten-mark item became a ten-D-mark item. The tempting comparison is that the
flow exception is worth more in its first year (79.5 billion) than the stock write-down is once
(50.4 billion), and **that sentence is arithmetically true and misleading, because it drops the
price leg.** Converting wages at 1:1 while prices move at 1:1 preserves the old relation between
them, which is the neutral setting rather than a benefit; converting the stock at 2:1 under a 1:1
price move is a halving in full. **The circulating side sets the unit of account and the dormant
pool is what gets priced against it.** The station claims nothing about household real welfare,
since subsidies were removed and prices freed, with East German living costs up 26.5 per cent in
1991, and that layer rather than the conversion ratio decides purchasing power.

**Two things the station corrected in itself, and both are worth more than the readings they
replaced.** A reading that the tax-free conversion allowances were filled to about 100 per cent was
**withdrawn in full** on 2026-08-31 once Appendix 4 was obtained, because the 64.8 billion figure it
rested on is an output of the same model computation rather than an observation, and the arithmetic
is kept while the reading is gone. And a **qualification now hangs on every figure taken from
Appendices 4 and 5**: that table opens *"Precise statistical data are not yet available."* and is a
substitute computation made in July 1990 on the consolidated balance sheet of 1990-05-31 to *"gain
some idea of the quantitative implications"*. **Those are projections from May positions, not the
realised conversion of 1 July.** Two further computational conventions are recorded from the same
page: external assets and liabilities were foreign-currency business already and are revalued rather
than converted, and claims on and liabilities to CMEA countries enter at 50 per cent of their mark
value, with the Bundesbank adding *"It remains to be seen whether due account has thereby been taken
of the doubts about the intrinsic value of these claims."*

**The mechanism the station found on the way, and it is this framework's own object.** Footnote 1
sets out the Richtungskoeffizient in full: the old East German credit system **formally maintained a
1:1 relation between the D-mark and the East German mark**, while enterprises actually paid 4.40
East German marks per D-mark on trade; at settlement the 4.40 was split into a foreign-exchange mark
worth one D-mark, cleared through DABA, and a wedge of 3.40 cleared through the state bank. **One
object, two prices, one official and one paid**, with the wedge carrying its own name, its own
settlement institution, and a stock that accumulated, since exports to the West drew 3.40 of subsidy
per mark of export value and fell short of imports, so the coefficient had to be raised as the mark
depreciated, which is to say **external liabilities had to be written up inside domestic
circulation.** A station on that wedge was opened as a candidate and **adjudicated not to be built
on 2026-08-31**, failing gate zero `D22` with `b₁ = 0`: fourteen of the fifteen objects in the
1988-05-04 Politburo document carry only one direction, so no square can be formed. `D26`, `D29` and
`D30` all pass, the unlock condition is recorded, and §R14b's mechanism reading is unaffected because
it is a description rather than a square.

**Open items, written as debts rather than as completions.** Whether settlement figures were ever
published, and in which issue, was not checked. The denominator of the "about 1.6:1" mixed
conversion rate is still undetermined, and it no longer affects any criterion; the load-bearing
figure is `1.8154:1`, which has two independent supports, the division `446.6 → 246.0` and a source
stating *durchschnittlicher Satz von 1,8:1*. External assets and liabilities are provisional at the
1989 year-end booking rate and the 1990-06-30 market-rate final values were not fetched. A second
caliber conflict is open and both numbers are held out of the tables: converted enterprise
liabilities at 115.8 billion DM (APuZ 24/1998) against 167.1 billion (Busch 2010), a ratio of 1.443,
too far apart to be one caliber.

## B20 — a station that the derivation converted from an unmeasured quantity into a zero domain, and was therefore not built

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. Paper derivation dated 2026-08-27. Zero fetch, zero run: everything is
substitution into definitions already in the repository. Never carried into this ledger, and there
is no record file because nothing was run.**

B20 was registered as a D-grid station, an unmeasured closed quantity: a company drops out of the
Russell 1000 and comes back, an agent holding it has walked a closed loop, and a non-zero loop sum
would be non-integrability. **The derivation asked two questions in the order they were set, and
both came back with the same answer, which changed what kind of station this is.**

**Is index membership a position?** No. A company dropped from the index has the same shares, the
same register, the same order book and the same price to every buyer. **What changes is who is
permitted to hold it**, since a fund tracking that index may not hold a non-constituent. Under the
split already made in `a3_asset_channel.md` §2.1, `γ_pay` is the terms paid and enters the cochain,
while `γ_gate` is an admission threshold, which restricts the domain rather than the terms and lives
in `H⁰`. **Index membership is admission, so it is `γ_gate`**, and the framework therefore predicts
this loop sum is zero. A3h and A3i had just measured that on the A arm: over 57 points the gate cell
never once agreed across seeds.

**Does the passive-flow account give a different sign?** No, and the first draft's reason for that
was wrong and is recorded rather than replaced. The draft argued that passive effect is proportional
to index weight change times tracking capital, and that a round trip's two weight changes cancel at
first order. **That route was refuted the same day by a document check**: Madhavan (2003,
*Financial Analysts Journal*) splits the reconstitution effect into permanent and temporary
components and puts the Russell 2000 deletion effect at `3.94%` permanent against `0.16%` temporary.
If cancellation of weight changes were the mechanism, the effect would be temporary, and it is
almost entirely permanent. **The conclusion survives on the repository's own simpler reason**:
`a3_asset_channel.md` §2 says the price cancels entirely and holonomy is a difference in terms,
independent of the price path. Passive money moves the price, the price is the same for every class,
so it cancels out of a class difference whether it is permanent or temporary. **Madhavan's split is
about the price level, which is exactly the thing that cancels.**

**Under §45.3 a B-grid station is not built when no opposing sign can be derived, so B20 was not
built. That is a derived outcome rather than a judgment call**, and the lesson the section keeps for
itself is that the draft's conclusion was right while its route was wrong, and what caught it was a
`D26` document check registered before any run rather than any measurement.

## B99 — a station designed on paper to the point where its zero calibration exists, and not run

**WRITEBACK 2026-09-20. Paper stage done 2026-09-14. No record file:
`experiments/b99_drug_routes.py` and `results/b99_drug_routes.json` are named in the design and not
yet written. Never carried into this ledger.**

The number and the carrier names were checked against every earlier station on 2026-09-14 before
use: `B99` had no earlier holder, with `99` to `107` free on the B arm, and the carrier names
appeared in no station.

**The station exists because a carrier-selection note said the first step was not to fetch anything.**
Negotiated medical prices ranked first among candidates with one gap, the second discriminant, a zero
calibration, and both candidate solutions to it were marked unverified with not one file downloaded.
The note said to write the zero calibration on paper first and change candidate if it could not be
written. **Six candidates were then checked against their publishers' own rule texts, on 2026-09-14,
with zero data files and zero cost, and the discriminant passed, so the candidate stands.**

| candidate | zero by construction | both sides published | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| pure repackaging route | **no** | key published, both prices in NADAC | not a zero calibration; it is an edge |
| bundled code against component codes | the named identity does not hold | | points at the wrong object |
| **NADAC week on week** | **yes** | **yes** | **holds, becomes `B99-1`** |
| Part B payment limit = 106% × ASP | yes, by rule | **no**, ASP not published | dead |
| FUL = 175% × weighted AMP | yes, by statute | **no**, AMP confidential | dead |
| NADAC's corresponding generic | yes | value published, key not | half dead, unused |

**The first candidate died cleanly and its key turned out harder than the original registration
assumed.** 21 CFR 207.53 requires a registrant to report *"The NDC assigned to each finished drug
received by the registrant for repacking or relabeling"*, which *"must be associated with the
corresponding NDC(s) for repacked or relabeled drugs"*, with medical gases the only exception, and
DailyMed prints it: REMEDYREPACK's `70518-4748-0`, a 30-count blister pack, carries source NDC
`52817-254`, with the page stating *"This is a repackaged label. The source NDC Code refers to the
unique number assigned to the original label"*.

**Scope, as the design states it.** This design handles the second discriminant only. The first,
that some agent's opportunity set carries `b₁ ≥ 1`, needs a two-index field `P(a, j)` and therefore
MRF or TiC data, and the station does not touch it. The carrier is the weekly NADAC reference file
plus the NADAC week-on-week comparison file plus FDA NSDE plus DailyMed SPL source NDCs, **all four
free, public and at NDC-11 level.**

## B121: the 2007-09 crisis, which intervention reached which kind of fault, read on the rival's own data

**RUN: 2026-09-17. Scripts `experiments/b121_a2_panel.py` (the panel), `experiments/b121_a2_read.py`
(the level reading, which is not read) and `experiments/b121_a2_events.py` (the event days), records
`results/b121_a2_panel.json`, `results/b121_a2_read.json` and `results/b121_a2_events.json`, each
carrying the configuration it ran under. Main window 2007-01-03 to 2008-08-08.**

The framework separates a fault that lives in the scalar at a position from a fault that lives on an
edge. A change in the policy rate moves the scalar, and the gradient of a scalar integrates to zero
around any closed loop, so a wedge that lives on an edge does not move with it. Opening a facility
adds an edge, and that does move it. The object here is the three-month LIBOR minus the three-month
OIS, and the two doses are the days the target rate changed and the days the Term Auction Facility
was announced, took bids or settled.

The data is the rival's own replication package (openICPSR 114040, Taylor and Williams, *A Black Swan
in the Money Market*, AEJ: Macroeconomics 1(1): 58-83). Every column is read under the name the
workbook's own Notes sheet gives it. The package ends on 2008-08-08, before Lehman; the window past
that is not read yet.

| | Criterion | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | `B121-7` `instrument` each event set is named by the rival's own workbook and marks days that exist, neither none of them nor all | rate 7, announce 7, bid 15, settle 17, of 420 rows |
| no verdict | `B121-8` `own_reading` the days the target rate changed do not move the wedge: those days minus the rest sit inside their own floor | `+2.97` bp, `+1.80` of its own floor, p `0.0680`; the four five-day settings whose windows hold both doses are printed and do not enter the verdict; subtracting the previous day's OIS instead turns the one-day sign to `-1.10`, so the cell is not read |
| no verdict | `B121-9` `rival` the facility's own days do move it: on the day an auction is announced, bid or settled, the object falls past two of its own floor | announce `-3.51` bp on 7 days, `-2.12` floors, p `0.0490`; three sets were looked at, so the floor takes the best of three inside each draw, p `0.0305`; on the Board's own list of TAF releases the same reading is `+0.04` bp (`+0.03` floors), so the list of days turns the sign over and the cell is not read; grid unread |
| FAIL | `B121-10` `instrument` the sign of the facility's reading holds on every declared setting | twenty-four settings; the sign turns over on the Board's list and on the union of the two lists |
| PASS | `B121-11` `instrument` two seeds leave every reading in the same state and each p moves less than its distance to the line | largest move `0.110` floors against `0.256` to the line |

`instrument` 2 pass 1 fail · `own_reading` 1 no verdict · `rival` 1 no verdict

The rival is one price at the position: the spread is counterparty risk, a property of the borrowing
bank, and the facility changes neither total liquidity, nor the expected path of the overnight rate,
nor counterparty risk, so its point prediction for the facility's days is zero. The framework reads
the spread as a property of the edge, so opening the edge narrows it. The two give opposite signs,
which is what lets this criterion hang at all.

**Which days count as announcements sets the sign, so neither dose is read in this window.** The rival's workbook codes its announcement column by content: `+1` on seven days, `-1` on 2008-02-01, and no mark on the releases that only repeat an amount already offered. The Board's TAF page lists every release, eleven in this window, six of them on the workbook's days. On the workbook's `+1` days the object falls `3.51` bp (`-2.12` of its floor); on the Board's list it moves `+0.04` bp (`+0.03`); on the union `-1.30` bp (`-1.07`). Twenty-four settings are swept (the list, the spread's timing, the window's start, one day or five) and the sign of the announcement reading turns over among them, so under `11f` the cell carries no verdict and no grid. The rival's point prediction is neither overturned nor borne out here.

**Coded by what each release says.** Each of the eleven TAF releases in this window was read from the
Board's own text and marked where it raises the amount offered or adds an instrument or a tenor: five
days (2007-12-12, 2008-01-04, 2008-03-07, 2008-05-02, 2008-07-30); the other six repeat an amount already
set or only schedule auctions. The rule was written down after the readings above and before the texts
were read. On those five days the one-day move is `-0.67` bp (`-0.35` of its floor), negative in all eight
settings and past the floor in none; over five days it is `-8.1` bp (`-2.2` to `-2.4` floors), but seven
of those twenty-five windows also hold a rate change. Kept to the three days more than five trading days
from any rate change, the five-day move is `-2.91` bp (`-0.62`). The `-3.51` bp on the workbook's own days
comes mostly from 2007-12-21 (a release saying auctions will continue) and 2008-03-11 (the Term Securities
Lending Facility, a different facility). On the rival's own data, at a daily resolution, the TAF's capacity
days cannot be told from zero: the narrowing the framework reads for them is not seen, and the rival's zero
stands unrefuted. The framework gives no size for the narrowing, so no power can be set against a floor of
about `2` bp a day on three to five events, and `B121-9` carries no verdict.

**What the readings are, in full.** Announcement days `-3.51` bp at `-2.12` of their floor; bid days
`-1.75` at `-1.39`; settlement days `+1.27` at `+1.22`; rate-change days `+2.97` at `+1.80`. Seven
announcement days is a thin object and the reading is stated at that thickness. At a weekly horizon
the same sets read `-8.21` bp (`-2.61`) for announcements and `-4.44` (`-2.14`) for bids, larger on
both counts, but 18 of those weekly windows hold a rate change as well, and a window that holds both
doses cannot say which one moved the object, so those settings are printed and left out of the
verdict.

**A cell that is not read, and why it stays unread.** The first form of this reading regressed the
daily change in the spread on the daily change in the TAF balance. Its sign turns over with one
declared knob, whether the object subtracts the same day's OIS or the previous day's: `+0.071`
against `-0.089`, eight settings each way out of sixteen, while the TAF caliber, the control and the
window start move nothing. The cause is a shared subtrahend: the object carries OIS inside it and the
TAF balance moves with OIS, so which OIS day enters the object decides how much of OIS is left in the
regressor. Under `11f` that cell is not read, and the event-day form above replaces it with a dose
that is a day rather than a level, carrying no OIS variance of its own.

**Free recovery of the LIBOR leg, for the window past the package.** ICE stopped licensing LIBOR for
redistribution and FRED removed the three-month dollar series in January 2022, but `TEDRATE` survives
to 2022-01-21 and `DTB3` is current, and `TEDRATE + DTB3` returns the workbook's own `US0003M` to
within `0.50` bp on all 397 overlapping days, median gap `0.12` bp. `DED3`, the H.15 London eurodollar
deposit rate, does not stand in for it: mean gap `6.4` bp, largest `38.8` bp on the same days.

**Two arms of this station are not run here.** The stigma arm is not measured again: Armantier,
Ghysels, Sarkar and Shrader (2015, *Journal of Financial Economics* 118(2): 317-335) read the premium
banks paid to avoid the window at about `44` bp, and about `126` bp after Lehman, and `B113` above
reads the class difference on the same edge from 2010Q3 on. The repo-haircut arm is dropped: that
gate rations by capital, where this framework and limits to arbitrage are the same object, bilateral
haircuts are contract terms, and tri-party haircuts were stable from 2008-07 to 2010-01 while the
funding volume was not (Copeland, Martin and Walker, NY Fed Staff Report 506), which is an edge that
stopped conducting rather than a threshold that breathes.

**Arm A1: the day a central bank's dollar swap line first pays out.** RUN 2026-09-22, script
`experiments/b121_a1_swaplines.py`, record `results/b121_a1_swaplines.json`. The object is the absolute
three-month covered interest parity gap (`cip_govt`, Du, Keerati and Schreger); the events are each G10
counterparty's first settlement in the Board's swap-line transaction file, eight of them from 2007-12-20
(euro, Swiss franc) to 2008-10-17 (Swedish krona); the controls are the G10 currencies whose line had not
paid out yet.

| | Criterion | Reading |

| PASS | `B121-12` `instrument` every G10 counterparty in the Board's file has a first settlement in the window and the gap is read around it | 8 counterparties, 8 events |
| FAIL | `B121-13` `own_reading` on the day a line first pays out, that currency's gap moves toward zero against the currencies still without one, past two of its own floor | `+8.31` bp, `+2.06` floors, p `0.0545`: it widens |
| PASS | `B121-14` `instrument` the sign holds on every declared setting (horizon, control set, trade or settlement day) | twelve settings, all positive, `+0.56` to `+36.97` bp |
| PASS | `B121-15` `instrument` two seeds leave the reading in one state | `+2.06` and `+2.04` floors |

bank against its own banks' dollar shortfall, so the first one lands in that currency's tightest days,
and the dose is chosen by the object it is read against. The edge this framework speaks of is the line's
existence and size, which the announcements set; the drawing is its use. The reading that is withdrawn is
this one, on this dose.

funding through it; the edge to private buyers came back as the facility left.

**How clean the windows are.** RUN 2026-09-22, script `experiments/b121_calendar.py`, record

from zero.
